articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Cell Reselection Trigger Optimization in Satellite Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to the characteristics of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks, such as high satellite mobility, large network scale, and uneven user distribution, efficient mobility management is crucial to ensure the continuity and stability of user services. Traditional mobility management schemes are specifically designed for terrestrial cellular networks, making it difficult for them to adapt to the large scale and highly dynamic characteristics of LEO satellite networks. This paper focuses on proposing a efficient mobility management for users in non-connected state in LEO satellite networks. It leverages machine learning algorithms to develop a cell reselection evaluation trigger mechanism aimed at reducing reselection frequency and minimizing unnecessary evaluation triggers, thereby ensuring service quality for users while improving system efficiency.

articleTitle: Less Labeling Burden: A SAR Ship Detection Data Selection Method Based on K-means
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In deep learning-based object detection, labeled data is crucial. However, annotating ship targets in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images is challenging because of the distinct characteristics of SAR images, especially when employing Oriented Bounding Boxes (OBB). These challenges arise from factors such as varying ship orientations, complex backgrounds, and the presence of noise, making accurate annotation more difficult. To reduce the labeling burden while minimizing its impact on ship detection performance, we propose a SAR data selection method. This method ensures that, despite limited quantities, the data contains a more representative range of scenarios when constructing a new dataset. By selecting 10 features of SAR images and performing K-means clustering based on these features, we choose the samples closest to the cluster centers as the selected data. We have validated the effectiveness of the proposed method by applying two typical object detection models to both randomly selected and clustering-selected datasets, thereby demonstrating the efficacy of proposed approach.

articleTitle: Doppler Rate Estimation for Passive Synthetic Aperture Localization Based on Discrete Fractional Fourier Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Doppler rate estimation is a critical issue in passive synthetic aperture (PSA) radiation source localization. However, existing Doppler rate estimation algorithms are significantly affected by the residual frequency offset (RFO) between the receiver and emitter. To address this problem, a Doppler rate estimation algorithm for PSA using the discrete fractional Fourier transform (DFRFT) is presented in this paper. The presented algorithm employs a two-step approach, utilizing coarse-to-fine search in the fractional domain, to achieve accurate Doppler rate estimation while also reducing computational complexity. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm exhibits superior estimation accuracy, and its performance is not affected by the RFO.

articleTitle: Modulation Recognition of Underwater Acoustic Signals Using Dynamic Dilated Convolutional Neural Network and Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This study proposes a parallel two-branch Dynamic Dilated Convolutional Neural Network (DDCNN) Transformer model for identifying modulation types of underwater acoustic signals. In the signal preprocessing stage, wavelet transform and instantaneous autocorrelation processing are used to extract the signal's time-frequency and instantaneous autocorrelation characteristics, constructing a joint feature plane for model training. To enable the model to extract more refined feature information, a dynamic dilated convolution (DDConv) module was proposed and combined with traditional convolutional neural networks to form a DDCNN network, enhancing feature extraction capability over the original CNN. By simultaneously combining the transformer model, a parallel dual-channel network model is formed. The DDCNN branch extracts local information, while the transformer branch extracts global information. A weighted sum is used for classification and recognition. Simulation results show that the proposed model achieves a classification accuracy of 95.6% for eight types of modulation signals, demonstrating good classification and recognition ability.

articleTitle: End-to-End Human Pose Reconstruction from Radar Signals Based on Deep Residual Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The reconstruction of human pose using radar primarily focuses on effectively estimating the position and pose of a target based on radar echo signals. Compared to traditional optical methods, radar signals can operate under limited lighting conditions, in the presence of occlusions, or beyond the line of sight. This paper proposes an end-to-end human pose reconstruction method based on a deep residual network. This method bypasses traditional imaging and detection algorithms, directly extracting amplitude and phase features from radar echo signals, and outputs the target's azimuth, distance, and pose information. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Finding Channel-wise Tensor Subspaces in GANs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) can map a latent vector sampled from a random distribution to a photorealistic image. Previous methods attempt to leverage the semantic features embedded in the latent space to enable local editing but encounter challenges in accurately disentangling these features. In this paper, we analyze the redundant characteristics inherent in the deconvolution mechanism and explore the high-order redundant information of feature maps to find channel-wise tensor subspaces in GANs. We propose an architecture-agnostic unsupervised approach, where tensor subspace clustering is used for the first time to disentangle the interpretable semantic features in GANs. Each cluster is regarded as a semantic mask by calculating its mean. The relationship between the latent vector with the selected cluster is established through network gradients to identify the interpretable directions. Note that the proposed method circumvents the demand of manually drawing regions of interest and only computes gradients in the shallow layers rather than the entire network. Experimental results on three GAN-based architectures show that our method can well disentangle the semantic features in GANs and achieves more precise local editing on facial images compared to the state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Emerging Versatile Context Representation on Modulation Recognition with Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Accurate recognition of intra-pulse modulation patterns is essential for enhancing radar system performance. Tranditional recognition algorithms are typically designed under ideal conditions and handcrafted features, the presence of substantial noise interference in complex electromagnetic conditions can significantly degrade the performance of these algorithms. Although Transformers have achieved great success with computer vision tasks, existing vision transformers are lack of capturing long-range dependencies. To remedy these flaws, this paper proposes an accurate automatic modulation recognition algorithm based on vision transformer. First, we utilize traditional image processing techniques to provide position of signal in time-frequency image and introduce a radius basis function to generate the positional embeddings. This procedure enhances the spatial awareness of our model. Second, dynamic scales of 2D patches are embedded as the input to the encoders. Third, inspired by dilated convolutions, vanilla attention is reformed in the cascade encoders. Experiments and ablation studies exhibit the proposed algorithm performs well under conditions of various signal-to-noise ratio conditions. It is worth mentioning that the classification accuracy can be up to 93.4% when SNR is -10 dB, and reach to 94.4% when SNR is 0 dB, which indicates the proposed algorithm demonstrates superior robustness against noise perturbations compared to other methods. The present work provides a sound experimental basis for further studying automatic modulation classification for the sake of future field application in electronic warfare systems.

articleTitle: Distributed MIMO Radar Multi-Target Detection and Localization Method with Time Synchronization Errors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synchronization errors can seriously affect the target detection accuracy of distributed Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar system. In this paper, a method for detecting and localizing multiple targets for distributed MIMO radar in the presence of time synchronization errors is proposed. To address the problem of reduced target detection probability due to time synchronization error, the extended cell Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) detector is proposed. Specifically, this detector increases the search width of each grid cell to ensure the detection probability of the target cell. Additionally, time synchronization errors can lead to the localization of false targets, which is addressed by the proposed Extended Grid Cell Clean (EGCC) algorithm. The EGCC algorithm can adaptively match the cell where the target is located in each channel according to the localization results, thus eliminating false targets and localizing true targets. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively detects and localizes multiple targets with time synchronization errors.

articleTitle: Wall Compensation for Through-Wall Radar Imaging Based on LiDAR Point Cloud Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the advancement of through-wall radar technology, its applications have become increasingly important in many applications such as security monitoring, disaster rescue, etc. To mitigate the impact of irregularities such as doors, windows, pillars, and protrusions on non-uniform building walls during through-wall imaging, this paper proposes a wall compensation method based on LiDAR(Light Detection And Ranging) point cloud data. By integrating measurements from both LiDAR and through-wall radar, and employing the ICP(Iterative Closest Point) algorithm, point cloud preprocessing and contour fitting techniques, accurate wall contour information is obtained, enabling effective wall compensation. Experimental results demonstrate that the accuracy of building interior layout reconstruction is significantly improved by compensating the impact of the external wall extracted by LiDAR.

articleTitle: Multiband Radar Signal Fusion and Extrapolation Method Based on Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The improvement of range resolution is crucial for enhancing the capability of imaging radars to detect small targets, such as drones. However, due to technical and cost limitations, current radars cannot indefinitely increase hardware bandwidth to enhance range resolution. To address this challenge, the multiband fusion and extrapolation technique has emerged. This method uses multiple discrete sub-band radar signals and fuses them to extrapolate the missing frequency bands, effectively achieving a wideband radar signal. Traditional approaches primarily rely on constructing signal models and estimating model parameters to accomplish fusion and extrapolation. This paper is the first to apply machine learning techniques to the field of multiband fusion and extrapolation, proposing a radar multiband signal fusion and extrapolation method based on a Transformer model. By training the Transformer network, the method enables accurate estimation of unknown frequency band signals. The effectiveness of the approach is validated through electromagnetic simulation data of drone echoes, demonstrating significantly improved estimation accuracy compared to traditional signal fusion and extrapolation methods.

articleTitle: Joint Design of Waveforms and Mismatched Filters Considering Correlation and RSM Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Radar agile waveforms and mismatched filters exhibiting good correlation properties can effectively mitigate masking the weak adjacent targets and distinguish different signals from echoes through (mis)matched filtering. However, the Range Sidelobe Modulation (RSM) for agile waveforms stands as a significant factor that leads to performance degradation in radar detection after Pulse-Doppler (PD) processing. To address the sidelobes of auto-correlation, suppress cross correlation and counteract RSM, we jointly design waveforms and mismatched filters, formulating a cost function integrating sidelobes of auto-correlation, cross-correlation and the discrepancy of auto-correlation. Subsequently, we present an algorithm to tackle this issue via Majorization Minimization (MM). Through numerical analysis, our proposed algorithm strikes a better balance in mitigating correlation sidelobes and suppressing RSM compared to previous methods.

articleTitle: LT-1 Differential Tomography: First Results and Comparison between Monostatic and Bistatic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Differential Tomography SAR technology integrates the advantages of Differential Interferometric SAR and Tomographic SAR, enabling four-dimensional imaging in areas with SAR layover to obtain elevation and deformation information of the target area. Compared to the traditional monostatic mode, the space-based bistatic observation mode has the advantages of interference immunity and richer information acquisition. This paper uses Differential Tomography SAR technology to perform deformation inversion on the LuTan-1 monostatic and space-based bistatic data. While obtaining the elevation information and linear deformation rate of the observed scene, it also compares the results and performance of Differential Tomography under the two different modes.The final conclusion is that LuTan-1 demonstrates strong capabilities in differential tomography. Additionally, the differential tomography performance of space-based bistatic systems is superior to that of monostatic systems.

articleTitle: Non-contact Lung Sound Vibration Sensing Based On FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Lung sounds are crucial diagnostic indicator, providing valuable pathological and physiological information about the respiratory system. Traditional lung sound measurement is contact-based, which has various drawbacks such as cross-infection and patient discomfort. In view of the characteristics of weak, time-varying, and wide bandwidth of lung sound vibration, this paper designs and verifies a lung sound auscultation simulator and studies a radar-based non-contact lung sound vibration sensing method based on non-contact vital sign detection. Various experiments based on samples from the ICBHI 2017 database show that lung sound vibration can be sensed using millimeter-wave radar.

articleTitle: Joint Detection of Moving Target Based on Distributed Video SARs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High resolution and high frame-rate radar imaging is of great significance for ground moving target indication (GMTI). However, the traditional video synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is not conducive to detecting high-speed target at long distance due to high frequency and long synthetic aperture. This paper proposes a new moving target multi-dimensional joint detection method for distributed video SARs based on the swarm unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). First, equivalent long synthetic aperture and displaced phase center antenna detection channels can be obtained by using the short synthetic apertures formed by each UAV in different time and spaces, which can realize high frame-rate imaging in the lower frequency and shorter integration time, leading to clear moving target shadow and focused moving target image. Second, the moving target state can be initialized by pre-detection after clutter suppression and velocity matching. Third, a dynamic programming-based track-before-detect (DP-TBD) algorithm is used to realize joint accumulation of multi-dimensional moving target information based on state mapping between shadow and energy. Finally, a shadow-aided radial velocity estimation method is adopted, which can effectively determine the ambiguity number of the interference phase. The proposed approach can significantly improve the detection performance of high-speed targets.

articleTitle: Range and Velocity Estimation in Carrier-Aggregation OFDM ISAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The requirements for high-accuracy sensing in future communication systems and the similarity between communication and sensing systems have given rise to integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveform has been widely considered a suitable waveform for ISAC to provide sensing functionality with little change on the existing communication systems. However, the large bandwidth requirements of high-precision sensing are contradictory to the fragmentation of communication spectrum resources. Based on existing carrier aggregation (CA) communication architecture, this paper considers a multi-band ISAC system and proposes a universal sensing signal processing algorithm for a CA-OFDM communication system. Improved IDFT and DFT factors are proposed to construct a joint multiband matching filter for CA ranging and velocity estimation. Finally, simulation results confirm the superiority of the proposed algorithm over state-of-the-art schemes.

articleTitle: Heuristic Algorithm of Multi-Constraint MHT in Ground-Moving Target Track Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The track detection technology of the ultra-wideband (UWB) radar for ground-moving targets is studied in this paper. A heuristic algorithm based on multi-constraint multi-hypothesis tracking (H-MCMHT) is proposed. Some constraints are added to the initial track generation of multi-hypothesis tracking according to the short-time motion characteristics of ground-moving targets. Then a heuristic track association method is proposed. The aim of the algorithm is to obtain as complete a real track as possible in a short time. Simulation results show that compared with MHT, H-MCMHT can effectively reduce the occurrence of false tracks and ensure the detection rate of real tracks. The physical verification results also confirm the simulation conclusions.

articleTitle: Image homogenization based on gray level co-occurrence matrix and region-growing for spaceborne Martian exploration SAR calibration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Researchers use radar echoes to probe the ionosphere, with synthetic aperture radar (SAR) being one of the current methods for Mars ionosphere detection. The accuracy of radar echoes affects the ionosphere detection results, making radiometric calibration of radar echoes necessary. Due to the size of point targets and the harsh Martian environment, deploying artificial calibrators on Mars is challenging. Thus, there is a need for a distributed SAR target radiometric calibration method suitable for the unique Martian landscape. The antenna pattern is a major influencing factor in radiometric calibration. Homogenized targets are essential for spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) to obtain antenna patterns using flat and uniform areas. Mountainous desert geology is widespread on Mars and can be utilized for radiometric calibration, but these areas are not uniform and require the removal of non-uniform regions. This paper presents a homogenization method that employs the Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) and a region-growing algorithm to generate a mask, effectively achieving the uniformization of non-uniform surface targets. Consequently, the coefficient of variation (CV), a metric used to assess data dispersion, exhibited a reduction of 34%.

articleTitle: A Time-Series Cross-Calibration Method for SAR Data Using Iterative Robust Linear Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Time-series calibration is essential for ensuring consistency and comparability across different Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images, which is critical for long-term sequence analysis tasks. However, traditional time-series calibration methods that rely on artificial calibrators encounter significant challenges due to the labor-intensive and time-consuming nature of deploying these calibrators. Cross-calibration offers a promising alternative by using calibrated satellites to calibrate uncalibrated satellites, providing substantial advantages in calibration frequency and timeliness. This paper proposes an advanced time-series calibration method based on the cross-calibration approach. Moreover, since traditional ordinary least squares (OLS) methods for determining calibration coefficients often struggle with outlier interference in scatter-stable pixels, this paper introduces a calibration coefficient computation method based on iterative robust linear regression (IRLR). It iteratively calculates residual control intervals, excludes outliers, and performs robust regression to derive accurate radiometric calibration coefficients. Experimental results from Sentinel-1 data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared to traditional OLS methods, it offers superior accuracy, and 95.6% of the time-series images show a reduction in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) by 0.01 to 0.156 dB.

articleTitle: Analysis of Composite Human Actions Based on Millimeter-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Radar-based human sensing has emerged as a promising solution for non-contact human-computer intelligent interaction. Current existing works typically preset a set of actions and use deep learning algorithms to extract features for classification. These studies usually focus only on recognizing body activities (such as walking, standing, and sitting) or gestures (such as sliding, pushing, and rotating). When recognizing activities, hand movements are often ignored, while gesture recognition typically requires the body to remain still. However, people often make gestures during body activities to convey additional information. In this paper, we investigate the feasibility of using a millimeter-wave radar sensor to simultaneously recognize human activities and gestures when composite actions involving both body movements and gestures are present in the sensor’s field of view. First, we establish the kinematic model of composite actions. Next, we analyze the Doppler-Range-Angle image features of these composite actions. Experimental results demonstrate that the sensor can simultaneously capture the motion information of both the body and the hand. Additionally, the motion characteristics of the body and hand show a certain degree of spatial distinction.

articleTitle: A Full-Aperture Imaging Algorithm for High Resolution Spaceborne SAR Based on NCS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High-resolution spaceborne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging is constrained by curved orbits, Earth’s rotation, and the curvature of the Earth, leading to significant 2-D spatial variations, particularly in the azimuth dimension. Current approaches to high-resolution spaceborne SAR imaging primarily involve resampling, interpolation, and sub-aperture techniques. However, these methods tend to be computationally intensive and less efficient. Nonlinear Chirp Scaling (NCS) is a relatively effective method for addressing azimuth spatial variations, which could enable full-aperture processing without interpolation. This paper first introduces a two-step distance domain molecular band method that effectively removes range frequency spatial variations. Subsequently, a method combining time-frequency transformation/inverse transformation with NCS is proposed, which effectively eliminates 2-D spatial variations, particularly in the azimuth dimension. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to validate the availability of this algorithm.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Image Segmentation Model for Extracting Migratory Birds and Insects Echoes Using Polarimetric Weather Radar Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Weather radars are essential for monitoring airborne animals, including birds and insects. Despite the potential of dual-polarization radar moments for echo classification, extracting migration echoes from birds and insects at pixel-level remains challenging. In this study, six radar moments were rendered into two RGB images, and a deep learning-based image segmentation model was developed to extract bird and insect echoes at the pixel level. The model uses the typical encoder-decoder architecture. The ResNet-50 model was used to extract the features on different spatial scales, which was modified to accept six input channels, matching the six radar moments of polarimetric weather radar data during the encoding stages. The U-Net model was employed for multiscale feature fusion during the decoding stages. Training and validation on a manually labeled dataset demonstrated that the proposed method performs exceptionally well, achieving a mean intersection over union of 98%. The model's performance was further evaluated using two representative cases.

articleTitle: Evaluation of geological hazard risk in Xiaojin County with time series InSAR deformation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The evaluation of geological hazard risk can provide the scientific basis for regional geological hazard prevention and control. The traditional superposition analysis of model factors fails to fully consider the correlation between factors and the degree of their impact on disasters. In this paper, Xiaojin County is selected as the research area for the evaluation of geological hazard risk. According to Pearson correlation coefficient method, 14 factors containing InSAR deformation value were screened. The evaluation of geological hazard risk in Xiaojin County was carried out based on weighted information content model and weighted evidence weight model using the above factors. Finally, the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC curve) is used to compare and analyze the evaluation accuracy of the two models. The results show that the Area Under Curve (AUC) value of the ROC curve of the weighted information content model is higher, and the accuracy of the evaluation results is better. Better risk assessment results can be obtained by constructing the model after factor screening.

articleTitle: A Polarization Anti-Jamming Method Based On Squint Projection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper presents a practical active suppression jamming suppression scheme to enhance the radar’s capability in detecting and tracking targets under countermeasures, thereby improving its anti-jamming performance. For a horizontal/vertical dual-receiver polarization radar system, we propose a parameter estimation method based on the maximum likelihood of the polarization coherence matrix. This method is capable of simultaneously estimating the polarization parameters of both jamming and target signals. Subsequently, we introduce a polarization domain filtering method utilizing squint projection transformation, which effectively preserves the target echo signal without compromising its amplitude and phase, while suppressing jamming. The efficacy of this jamming suppression technique is verified through field-measured data.

articleTitle: QE-WNet: A Quadratic Encoding-decoding W-shape Network for Road Segmentation based from Optical Remote Sensing Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With advancements in imaging technology, high-resolution remote sensing images are now readily available for applications such as urban planning, resource assessment, and land cover analysis. Roads are a crucial element of infrastructure, and extracting road information from high-resolution remote sensing images is vital for tasks like urban planning and mapping. However, existing road extraction techniques, which rely on traditional encoder-decoder architectures, often struggle to accurately delineate road boundaries and surfaces. As a result, these methods tend to produce subpar outcomes and are challenging to implement in practical systems. To address this issue, we introduce a novel quadratic encoding-decoding W-shaped network, referred to as QE-WNet. This approach recognizes the differing characteristics of road bodies and boundaries—where road boundaries are more stable in semantic representation and road bodies are less so. In the first stage of encoding and decoding, we focus on modeling road boundaries, while the second stage emphasizes road bodies, leveraging the more stable secondary encoding-decoding information. This separation enhances the accuracy of road extraction. We conduct comparative experiments using several established methods on the Deepglobe dataset, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Space-Variant Baseline Error in Micro-Deformation Monitoring Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to external factors or inherent equipment limitation, micro-deformation monitoring radar will introduce the spatial baseline errors phase to the measured results. This paper proposes a method to estimate and compensate the space-variant baseline error phase for this problem. This process mainly uses total differential and singular value decomposition method. The final experiment proves that our method performs well in correcting the phase of space-variant baseline error caused by equipment vibration and helping the accuracy of deformation inversion improved.

articleTitle: Hybrid Integration Method for High-Speed Weak Target Detection with Distributed Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To address the challenge of detecting high-speed weak targets among distributed radar nodes, we propose a longtime hybrid integration method in this paper. Firstly, we establish the distributed radar system model, and the fluctuating signal generated by a target is acquired using this approach. Subsequently, we use the Generalized Radon-Fourier Transform (GRFT) to correct the intra-channel distance walk and Doppler walk caused by the high-speed and high maneuverability characteristics, resulting in coherent integration data. Finally, the Dynamic Programming (DP) method is used to achieve non coherent integration of weak target inter-channel echoes. Simulation results confirm that the proposed hybrid integration approach significantly enhances the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) during extended observation periods, which is beneficial for subsequent detection, tracking, or recognition of the target.

articleTitle: Adaptive Waveform Design for Cognitive Radar Target Detection with Constant Modulus Constraint
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Waveform design is a critical part in cognitive radar to improve the radar performance. In this paper, an adaptive waveform design method based on maximizing the signal to clutter plus noise ratio (SCNR) is proposed, which aims at optimizing the target detection performance. Moreover, to satisfy the practical application, the constant modulus constraint is taken into account. As the first step of the method, the optimal energy spectral density (ESD) of transmit signal is calculated, which suppresses the clutter via the energy allocation. After that, the constant modulus signal is synthesized to approximate the optimal ESD using alternating projection algorithm. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Non-Local Means Filtering based Landslides Coherence Change Detection for Multitemporal SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Landslides often occur in mountains, where the low coherence characteristics result in decreased accuracy of traditional SAR-based change detection algorithms. In this paper, a non-local means filtering based coherence change detection algorithm is proposed for multitemporal SAR images. First, Persistent Scatterers (PSs) and Distributed Scatterers (DSs) are both detected to improve the monitoring density in low coherence area. Then, coherence change detection is adopted based on the multitemporal SAR images to replace traditional amplitude based change detection algorithm. Finally, non-local means filtering is used to improve the change detection accuracy of the whole area. The raw data of landslides occurred in Hong Kong is used to indicate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A Cascade-filtered Adaptive CFAR Detector in Low Small Target Detecting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the context of detecting low-flying small targets in urban high-rise environments, the targets are often obscured by large clutter reflectors or non-uniform clutter regions. This paper proposes a cascaded filtering adaptive constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detector. This method consists of two cascaded detectors. Units judged as "target present" by the first stage are filtered out in the second stage. Compared to single-stage detectors, this method effectively integrates the performance advantages of multiple CFAR techniques. This makes it suitable for more complex detection environments. Based on measured data and Monte Carlo simulation results, the cascaded filtering CFAR detector has a high detection rate in multi-target environments and a low false alarm rate in non-uniform clutter edge environments.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach Combining Decoupling Training with Prototype-based Contrastive Learning for Tracking Long-Tailed Recording in Optical Aerial Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Scene classification is a classical task in optical aerial imagery. In practical applications, it is difficult to obtain a balanced training samples supporting model training. Therefore, the dataset usually follow the Long-Tailed distribution, which is challenge for classification task, especially for multi-categories scene classification. It would make model intend to learn the representation of head classes with majority samples, which lead to under-represent middle and tail classes with minority samples and affect a better classifier construction for long-tailed classification. In this article, a novel Prototypical Supervised Contrastive Learning Based on Decoupling Framework called PSCL-DF is proposed for Long-Tailed Classification in Optical Remote Sensing Imagery to make a better feature learning and better classifier leaning. Finally, extensive tests are performed on the two artificially generated long-tailed datasets, demonstrating the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed methods. Our results show that decoupling feature extraction and classification achieve significant performance gains.

articleTitle: Ultra-Rapid Satellite Clock Offset Boundary Jumps Compensation Method Based on Dynamic Adaptive Weighting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The traditional ultra-rapid satellite clock offset boundary jumps compensation method based on epoch-differenced suffers from error accumulation, which reduces the accuracy of satellite clock offset. In this paper a new compensation method based on dynamic adaptive weighting is proposed. The method makes full use of ultra-rapid satellite clock offset data from adjacent observation window. Calculate prior weights based on satellite offset dynamic characteristics, obtain satellite posterior residual through batch estimation, and compensate the satellite clock offset boundary jumps. The ultra-rapid satellite clock offset products updated 1-hour provided by WHU from DOY 060-062 in 2024 are used to verify the performance of the proposed method. The results show that, contrasted with the traditional compensation method based on epoch-differenced, the accuracy of the satellite clock offset is improved by 36.2%. In addition, the RMS and STD accuracy of PPP are improved by 13.2% and 26.2% within two hours before and after the observation window boundaries, respectively.

articleTitle: Wireless frequency synchronization and delay refinement methods for distributed array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Nowadays, distributed network such as coherent radar system has gained popularity due to better performance, flexibility, and stability. However, the independence of each node presents a significant challenge: clock synchronization, and in long-distance scenarios, we prefer to achieve it wirelessly. Clock synchronization consists of two parts: frequency and time. The traditional methods are mostly based on protocols, and the hardware requirements are very high to achieve high accuracy. So, we propose a novel frequency estimation and correction method based on signal processing for delay estimation, and further improve the accuracy by data refinement. Simulation results show that with a signal frequency of 100MHz and an SNR of 30dB, the accuracy of frequency difference estimation is 10 Hz. When the sampling rate is 1GHz, the accuracy of delay estimation can be improved by about 20 times after refinement.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Optical Remote Sensing Object Detection Based on Shape Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Traditional object detection methods suffer from excessively high false alarm rates in scenarios with scarce training samples. To address this issue, this paper proposes a few-shot optical remote sensing object detection method based on shape matching. This method first obtains the sliced mask image of the object within the predicted bounding box in the pre-detection process. Then, the shape context algorithm is utilized to perform template matching between the template image and the sliced mask image, thereby eliminating false alarm objects and enhancing the object detection performance. To examine the capability of the proposed method, two public datasets, namely FAIR1M datasets and MAR20 datasets, are selected for experimentation. The experimental results show that our method achieves exceptional effectiveness, yielding F1 scores of 0.705 and 0.866 on the FAIR1M and MAR20 datasets, respectively.

articleTitle: The Design and System Implementation of Multi-parameter Joint Agile Coherent Radar Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Advanced deceptive jamming can significantly degrade a radar's detection capabilities and, in severe cases, disable the radar system. Expanding the agility of radar waveform parameters is expected to reduce the effectiveness of jamming parameter reconnaissance, thereby enhancing radar anti-jamming performance. However, complex agile signals pose challenges to the waveform generation of radar systems. Based on this, the paper designs a multi-parameter joint agile radar waveform with low probability of interception. More importantly, it proposes a waveform generation method that meets the real-time requirements of jamming countermeasures. This method involves reading parameters directly from a formatted file, enabling flexible adjustment of waveform parameters and effectively reducing the volume of parameter transmission data. The designed radar signal was implemented on a waveform board card, and test results demonstrate the correctness and effectiveness of the design.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Cooperative Localization Based on Active Radar/Infrared at Different Sites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multi-source perception fusion positioning technology based on heterogeneous sensors is a key research area in the field of target positioning. The heterogeneous sensor positioning system composed of radar and infrared has a wide range of applications. However, existing works mostly use radar measurement to expand the dimension of infrared data to locate target, which will introduce the large angle measurement error of radar into infrared. In this paper, we propose a radar/infrared linear weighted least-squares (WLS) localization algorithm based on target motion model. First, we build linear equations of target position relative to radar and infrared based on the space relationship, respectively. In this manner, the position of target can be solved through a linear optimization problem. Two kinds of equations are combined by deformation and solved by WLS algorithm to achieve the target localization. Simulation results show that the proposed method has better target localization performance than that of single radar, and with the improvement of the measurement accuracy of radar/infrared sensors, the localization effect is better.

articleTitle: Multi-angle Asymmetric Coplanar Analysis Technology for Three-dimensional Wind Field Retrieval Using the Shipborne Weather Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Typhoons and other disaster weather have long development cycles and are extremely destructive. Three-dimensional (3D) wind field retrieval is crucial to understanding the internal kinematics and dynamics of severe weather and predicting its evolution and tracking. The stratospheric airship is large in size, can fly at high altitudes, and has a long time in the air. It is very suitable for complete observations of weather systems with long development cycles. However, the flying speed of airships is slow, and the traditional fixed elevation angle symmetrical coplanar technology is no longer applicable. Therefore, it is very necessary to conduct the 3D wind field retrieval research under airship platforms. The paper proposes a multi-angle asymmetric coplanar analysis technology (MA-ASCAT) model suitable for shipborne weather radar, and compares the performance with the traditional method. It initially verifies the feasibility of the method and provides a theoretical basis for further research.

articleTitle: Lightweight Siamese Tracking based on Cross-correlation Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: When performing object tracking tasks, precisely tracking the desired target is the optimization goal of the tracking algorithm. Generally, deep learning models with larger model sizes and higher computational costs tend to have stronger computational capabilities. However, uncontrolled increases in model size and computational cost can make the algorithm difficult to use in practice. Therefore, to find a suitable balance between increasing computational cost and improving computational performance, this paper introduces a lightweight object tracking method that introduces a CNN attention mechanism. Based on SiamRPN++, this algorithm employs a more concise corner prediction head and uses depthwise separable convolution to replace general convolution, significantly reducing the computational cost of ResNet-50. Moreover, symmetric point-wise expansion (PE) and point-wise linear projection (PLP) are utilized to maximize computational performance while minimizing computational cost. Additionally, the Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) network is employed to introduce an attention mechanism to each convolutional module. These strategies effectively make the algorithm lightweight and improve its computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Specific Emitter Identification Based on Fuzzy Oversampling Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Specific emitter identification is a key technology for spectrum management and electromagnetic environment awareness. Data privacy protection makes it challenging to obtain labeled data of specific emitter, and the few-shot problem causes the overfitting and decreased recognition performance in deep learning methods which depend on large datasets. This paper proposes a method based on Fuzzy Oversampling Data Augmentation (FODA), which generates synthetic samples in random directions and assigns multi-class fuzzy labels to achieve diversified sample augmentation. And the intra-class compactness of samples is enhanced by reducing the variations between semantic features and corresponding class centroids in the high-dimensional feature space, leading to optimized classification performance. Few-shot experimental scenarios are constructed with a 10-class Wi-Fi public dataset. The experimental results indicate that the identification accuracy of FODA has achieved optimal average accuracy compared to the comparative models across different shot data, and been improved on average by 24.61% compared to the baseline in the ablation experiments.

articleTitle: TVTADMM-Net: an ADMM network based on total variation polarization texture denoising
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) system can obtain richer scattering characteristics of ground objects. However, the inherent speckle noise in SAR images severely degrades their quality, and traditional denoising methods are difficult to apply to denoise polarimetric SAR images in complex scenarios, especially the texture details. Therefore, an ADMM network based on total variation (TV) polarization texture denoising is proposed in this paper. It preserves the backscatter coefficient properties of the feature target by "smoothing" the texture details. That is, the TV regularization term is added to the denoising process to construct a polarised texture sparse denoising model. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through experiments with multi-band airborne and spaceborne polarimetric SAR data

articleTitle: Analysis on Anti-Interference Performance of Random Stepped-Frequency Waveform for Automotive Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the widespread application of automotive radar, the likelihood of inter-radar interference has significantly increased, especially in complex urban environments. Utilizing advanced waveforms is crucial for radar anti-interference. This paper investigates the anti-interference capabilities of automotive radar using the Random Stepped-Frequency (RSF) waveform. Initially, we analyze automotive radar interference under traditional Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW). Subsequently, we explore the anti-interference principle of the RSF waveform by deriving its signal model. Finally, numerous experiments are conducted to demonstrate the superior anti-interference performance of the RSF waveform. The results indicated that the RSF waveform markedly reduces radar signal collision probability in both time and frequency domains, thereby reducing the interference probability of radar.

articleTitle: Frequency Diversity Array Backscatter for Efficient IoT Multi-Device Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of enabling multiple internet of things devices (IoTDs) to share the same communication channel efficiently with low power consumption. We consider a novel monostatic backscatter communication system, where the base station (BS) uses a frequency diversity array to generate a specific remote beam that activates the devices. By activating reflective devices with a shaped beam and using a maximum likelihood receiver at the BS, we can decode signals to achieve multiple access. Then, we derive a closed-form expression for the aliasing probability of reflected signals, and obtain the numerical solution of the system outage probability through simulation. Numerical simulations verify the feasibility and advantages of the scheme, showing that our scheme enhances IoTD communication efficiency and reduces deployment costs.

articleTitle: Efficient SAR Automatic Target Recognition Based on Self-distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Many current SAR-ATR methods utilizing deep learning mainly emphasize improving model generalization. Consequently, this approach results in a substantial expansion of the model’s parameter set. This study introduces a new neural network architecture that combines low parameter count with high generalization, incorporating a self-distillation technique during the training process. Initially, we employ a substantial quantity of DWConv to diminish the count of trainable parameters and merge features with distinct receptive fields to enhance model efficacy. During the training phase, the model backbone’s generalization is enhanced through the implementation of a self-distillation technique, which is not incorporated in the inference process. Experimental evaluations conducted under the OFA protocol reveal that the proposed method achieves outstanding performance and generalization.

articleTitle: First Analysis of PIESAT-01 Interferometric Cartwheel for Ocean Current Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The World's First Multi-Baseline Distributed InSAR Satellite System ‘PIESAT-01’, which has the ability of Along-track interferometric (ATI), and can simultaneously form multiple effective orbital baselines to obtain the ocean current. This article presents the results of ocean current processing based on PIESAT-01 IW data for the first time, and introduces the data processing flow and the used processing method.

articleTitle: SC-DVNet: A Dual-Branch Recognition Network for Synthetic Aperture Radar Images Based on Scattering Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Ship classification using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images is a crucial component in marine monitoring. With the rise of deep neural networks (DNN), the abstract feature maps obtained by CNN-based methods have significantly improved classification performance. However, most current DNN-based methods are predominantly inherited from optical imagery, designed only for SAR intensity images, which may present challenges for further improving recognition performance. Therefore, this paper proposes using the point Scattering Center (SC) model for scattering feature extraction combined with graph convolutional networks for ship classification tasks. Comprehensive ablation experiments were carried out to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach. Finally, experimental results on OpenSARShip1.0 dataset verify that the performance of the suggested approach notably outperforms DNN-driven techniques.

articleTitle: A source separation approach for the joint representation of OBA and SBA under reverberation conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Spatial audio is implemented in three formats, i.e., Channel-Based Audio (CBA), Object-Based Audio (OBA), and Scene-Based audio (SBA). The joint representation of multiple audio formats can combine their advantages to satisfy the technical requirements of complex audio scenes. Specifically, the joint representation of object-based audio and scene-based audio plays a crucial role in spatial audio. However, the recorded SBA signal contains the associated components of OBA, which results in mutual interference during sound field reconstruction. Therefore, separating the target SBA component from the original SBA signal becomes the key to achieving the combination of the two audio formats.In fact, our previous work deals with outdoor applications, and a source separation approach for the recorded SBA signals in the joint representation of OBA and SBA under non-reverberation conditions was proposed. In this paper, a linear convolution model for the original SBA signal under reverberation conditions is firstly built up for the indoor applications. Then an NMF-based sound source separation algorithm is proposed, while a novel EM parameter initialization method is also proposed for the algorithm. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed separation algorithm is verified by groups of experiments.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Quantization Method for SAR Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to the limitations of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) beam width and irradiation direction, the radar echo energy varies across different regions in wide scenes, resulting in uneven luminance in SAR images, which affects subsequent SAR target detection and recognition. This paper proposes an adaptive quantization method for SAR images. Firstly, the luminance variation curves are statistically analyzed along the range and azimuth directions to obtain a luminance distribution map. Then, the inverse function of the luminance distribution map is calculated to get a luminance compensation map. Finally, the compensation map is multiplied with the SAR amplitude values to obtain the adaptive quantization results. This paper demonstrates on the real-data SAR-Vehicle dataset that the proposed adaptive quantization method can compensate for the uneven luminance caused by SAR beam drift. The method also improves the target detection and recognition performance of common target detection networks.

articleTitle: Multisource Data Integration of Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 for Above Ground Biomass Inversion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Remote sensing data provides several advantages for vegetation parameter inversion, including non-invasive measurement, high spatiotemporal resolution, and extensive coverage. However, as multisource remote sensing data continues to advance, challenges emerge in data fusion, particularly in ensuring consistency across various data sources and addressing physical differences among them. To address such challenges, this paper employs multisource re mote sensing data as inputs for Above Ground Biomass (AGB) inversion. As a scattering model, the Water Cloud Model (WCM) is widely adopted for vegetation parameter inversion due to its simplicity and ability to describe both vegetation and soil scattering mechanisms. In this study, Sentinel-1 data is utilized to extract backscatter coefficients and incidence angle information, while Sentinel-2 multispectral data is used to calculate soil moisture through the tasseled cap transformation. These variables are employed to calibrate the coefficients of the WCM, facilitating the bio mass inversion process. The approach effectively integrates multiple sources of remote sensing data, overcoming limitation of data saturation typically associated with single-source data, and achieving accurate biomass inversion across different polarization modes.

articleTitle: A PS Deformation Estimation and Error Compensation Algorithm Based on Temporal Coherence for GNSS-based InBSAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System-based Bistatic Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (GNSS-based InBSAR) uses on-orbit satellites as transmitters. Therefore, its cost is much lower than that of spaceborne InSAR system. Meanwhile, its repeat-pass time is shorter lead to faster monitoring frequency. However, the system characteristic of low SNR leads to low accuracy of deformation phase extraction. In this paper, A PS deformation estimation and error compensation algorithm based on temporal coherence is proposed. The interferometric phase model of PS in line of sight direction is established. The coherence coefficient is introduced to iteratively estimate the atmospheric phase, deformation rate and deformation acceleration. The IGSO raw data of Beidou navigation satellite are processed. the experimental results show that the average accuracy is 19.48 mm, where the optimal accuracy can reach 16.14 mm.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Direct Position Determination Using Multiple Asynchronous Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Existing direct position determination algorithms using multiple asynchronous sensors utilize the properties of the noise subspace and signal subspace to construct a multiple signal classification-like cost function. Based on this algorithm, this paper further leverages the characteristics of the signal subspace to develop a new cost function that produces sharper peaks at the target locations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm offers higher resolution performance in the presence of closed spaced target scenario.

articleTitle: Interactive Three-dimension Group Convolution Network with Non-local Fusion Attention for Hyperspectral Image Classifcation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Three-dimensional convolutional networks (3DC-NNs) have proven to be powerful tools for hyperspectral image (HSI) classification. However, most existing 3DCNN networks optimize global spectral bands, neglecting the distinct reflective characteristics exhibited in different spectral ranges. To address this limitation, we propose a novel Interactive 3D Group Convolution Network (IGCNet) that incorporates a cross-group interaction strategy. This model explores unique information within different spectral ranges and leverages the high relevance between adjacent groups to enhance the complementarity of information. Additionally, to overcome the constraints of local receptive fields, a non-local fusion attention mechanisms is designed to account for the global correlations of feature map and emphasize important spatial regions during the fusion of group convolutional features, thereby improving the spatial-spectral representation capability of features. Experimental results on two data sets demonstrate the superior performance of IGCNet.

articleTitle: PolSAR Image Classification based on Complex-value Linear Attention Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Advantages of active imaging and providing more diverse features with multiple polarizations have promoted the utilization of polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) in land cover classification. Despite the great success achieved by convolutional neural network (CNN) with attention mechanism before, there are still two major concerns. One is the real valued CNN would undoubtedly discounts the richer representations in complex-valued PolSAR and the other is the challenge of implementing attention in complex domain. In this paper, we design a complex linear attention mechanism which can be fully executed in the complex domain and then combine it with the complex-valued CNN, to extract abundant feature representations in the complex domain. Experiment on the public PolSAR dataset shows the prominent performance of the complex-valued CNN equipped with complex linear attention, which surpass the real-value CNN by 4.59%, 5.22%, 4.49% in terms of overall accuracy, average accuracy and mIoU.

articleTitle: Research On SAR-OPT Cross-modal Aircraft Target Detection Method Based On Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the field of remote sensing, the diversity of data modalities of different sensors limits the universality of target detection methods, and models suitable for specific modalities are difficult to generalize to new scenarios. In order to deal with the problem of missing samples caused by the occlusion of optical images by clouds or the difficulty of annotating SAR images, this paper proposes a cross-modal universal target detection method based on contrastive learning. This method utilizes the characteristics of optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images, and designs targeted contrastive learning agent tasks - performing random probability grayscale conversion on optical images and applying pseudo-color image generation to SAR images, so as to prompt the model to extract and identify similar features from the two modalities under the guidance of the loss function. In addition, by introducing spatial attention and channel attention mechanisms, the former is used to enhance the model’s attention to the global features of the image, and the latter is used to balance the RGB three-channel information of the optical image and the information of the single channel of the SAR image. Experimental results show that in few-shot and zero-shot scenarios, this method can effectively identify targets and show good generalization ability and robustness.

articleTitle: Intracloud Lightning Echo Simulation for the Airborne Weather Radar Based on Dielectric Breakdown Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Lightning is a long-distance discharge phenomenon that not only serves as a crucial atmospheric physical process but also frequently accompanies severe convective weather disasters such as short-duration heavy rainfall, hail, and thunderstorm winds. These pose a significant threat to the flight safety of civil aviation aircraft. Airborne weather radar, as equipment essential for ensuring the safety of aircraft operations, has significant advantages in detecting hazardous weather conditions. Lightning detection and warning based on airborne weather radar have become important research topics in the field of civil aviation, with lightning echo data serving as the foundation for developing detection algorithms. However, it is difficult to obtain the lightning echo data of airborne weather radar because of the instantaneous occurrence and complex change of lightning. To address this issue, this paper proposes a simulation method for airborne weather radar intracloud lightning echoes. The method first simulates the propagation path of the lightning channel using the dielectric breakdown model, then analyzes the backscattering cross-section of the lightning channel based on its plasma characteristics, and finally applies the weather radar equation to obtain the airborne weather radar lightning echoes.

articleTitle: Prototype-Guided Representation Distribution Optimization for Change Detection in High-Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Change detection is the process of automatically extracting change areas from bi-temporal remote sensing images. The key of deep learning-based change detection methods is to extract features that represent changes/non-changes. Most of the existing methods only enhance the representation ability of the changed regions through the model architecture design, but lack further constraints in the representation space. This paper introduces a prototype-guided representation distribution optimization method. By comparing pixel features with prototypes, confusing pixels can be determined, and these pixels are adaptively weighted during learning, so that similar representations are closer and different representations are farther apart. In addition, the representation distribution is also applied as transferred knowledge to knowledge distillation for lightweight CD model. Experimental results on two public datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A summary on antennas loaded with magnetic materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The ability to shrink the physical dimensions of an antenna without reducing antenna performance significantly has been of great interest among many miniaturized antenna design engineers. Over the decades, numerous antenna miniaturization technologies have been proposed, from antenna structural optimization, to lumped elements loading, and then to the use of high permittivity/permeability materials. In this article, we provide a review of various miniaturized antenna design techniques with an emphasis on magnetic materials loading. In particular, we will pay special attention to the following types of magnetic material loaded antennas: ferrite or yttrium garnet (YIG) loaded magnetic dipoles , ferrite or neodymium iron boron loaded solenoids . Finally, we propose an optimization scheme for ferromagnetic enhanced electric small antenna (ESA) loaded with YIG.

articleTitle: A Sidelobe Optimization Method using Spatial Code Based on Space-Time Coding Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Space-time coding array (STCA) can realize transmitting diversity and directivity through introducing a very tiny time delay between the adjacent transmitting channels, which could utilize the high degree of freedom of the radar transmitting end. However, STCA also bring problems, especially in sidelobe performance. Such as the resonance problem, which is caused by the frequency spectrum mismatch and will bring sidelobe performance distortion. In this article, a sidelobe optimization method that applies the spatial code is proposed, which can control the array pattern to solve the resonance problem. The simulation results can verify the feasibility of the proposed method. The resonance problem is eliminated and the sidelobe is reduced significantly on the basis of maintaining the spatial beam scanning capability of STCA.

articleTitle: Mainlobe Deceptive Jammer Suppression using Beampattern Synthesis in EPC-MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper presents a beampattern synthesis method aimed at suppressing mainlobe deceptive jamming signals in Element Pulse Coding-Multiple-Input–Multiple-Output (EPC-MIMO) radar. By applying phase coding in both the spatial and pulse dimensions, EPC-MIMO radar can suppress mainlobe deceptive jammers through data-independent beamforming. However, the performance degeneration occurs due to the existence of Direction of Arrive (DOA) mismatch. Therefore, an Iterative Weight Control (IWC) algorithm is devised by optimizing the weight vector to achieve ideal responses, where constant quadratic constraint and a dynamical power constraint are utilized to broaden the presumed null regions. At the analysis stage, the performance of IWC method in mitigating mainlobe deceptive jamming signals is compared with the state-of-the-arts beampattern synthesis techniques, highlighting the superiorities of the IWC approach.

articleTitle: Impact of Dataset Characteristics on the Accuracy of SAR Image Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The quality of a dataset significantly impacts the performance of algorithm models, yet a unified standard for SAR image dataset production remains absent. Currently, there is no consensus on the optimal image type, bit depth, and preprocessing methods to maximize algorithm effectiveness. This paper explores how these factors—image type, bit depth, and preprocessing techniques—affect target detection models by creating and training multiple SAR image datasets. The results reveal that 8-bit Tagged Image File Forma (TIFF) images, enhanced with linear stretching of the maximum and minimum values, achieve the best performance. These findings offer a valuable reference for establishing standards in the production of future SAR image datasets.

articleTitle: A Novel Three-Dimensional Subband Synthesis MIMO Array Radar Imaging Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In recent years, terrorist attacks have occurred frequently around the world, and public safety issues have received more and more attention. Compared with traditional security inspection methods, millimeter-wave three-dimensional imaging technology has been widely used in the field of security inspection due to its advantages of safety, non-contact and high-resolution imaging. However, its data acquisition efficiency is still one of the problems to be solved in this field. In this paper, a new three-dimensional subband synthetic MIMO array radar (3D-SS-MIMO-AR) imaging mode is proposed. It can realize simultaneous multi-channel signal transmission and multi-channel signal reception. Compared with the previous time division multiple input multiple output (TD-MIMO) imaging mode, it increases the simultaneous transmission channel, thus greatly improving the data acquisition efficiency. In this study, the array geometry model of 3D-SS-MIMO-AR imaging mode is established, the array transceiver mechanism is designed, the multi-subband transceiver timing relationship based on simultaneous multi-channel signal transmission is described, and the echo data processing of subband synthesis is analyzed. Finally, the effectiveness and correctness of the imaging mode are verified by point target simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Multipath Model and Ghost Suppression for Millimeter Wave Traffic Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Millimeter-wave traffic radar, known for its advantages of all-day, all-weather, and long-distance monitoring, plays a critical role in traffic safety. However, the presence of multipath ghosts has persistently degraded the performance of traffic radar systems. In this paper, we establish a radar echo signal model by analyzing the propagation paths of multipath signals. Key features, including the distance between multipath ghosts and road guardrails, as well as the continuity of detection point clouds, were systematically analyzed. Based on these identified features, we propose a neural network-based method for ghosting suppression. Empirical data analysis validates the accuracy of target detection and tracking by millimeter-wave traffic radar. The results demonstrate that the utilization of the proposed eight features effectively mitigates the presence of multipath ghosts, enabling precise positioning and accurate tracking of vehicles.

articleTitle: Low-Cost, High-Performance Algorithm and Hardware Architecture for SAO Mode Decision
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Sample adaptive offset (SAO) is applied for reducing sample distortion and attenuating ringing artifacts in both HEVC and VVC standards. The rate-distortion optimization process is used to select the best SAO parameter. It accounts for the majority of SAO complexity and determines the SAO filtering performance. Therefore, the rate-distortion cost calculation should be well handled to achieve both low cost and high coding performance. In this paper, we propose a simplified and optimized rate estimation algorithm based on the characteristics of SAO parameter syntax and entropy coding process. And we propose a hierarchical flow for rate-distortion cost calculation to further reduce the computational cost and storage cost for SAO mode decision hardware. The results show that the proposed algorithm achieves an average YUV loss of -0.10%, and the proposed SAO mode decision hardware architecture can be implemented by only 21.8k gates using TSMC 65nm process under 400 MHz.

articleTitle: Multichannel Sparse Recovery for Constant Modulus Signals via ℓ∞,1 Minimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Compressed sensing techniques have been extensively studied over recent decades, finding broad applications in signal processing. Convex optimization approaches for compressed sensing, such as l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,1</inf>-minimization, are employed for recovering sparse signals in multichannel scenarios. However, when joint sparse signals also exhibit the constant modulus (CM) property, l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,1</inf>-minimization fails to exploit this prior information. In this paper, we focus on utilizing l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞,1</inf>-minimization to recover sparse signals with the CM property. For this convex optimization method, a fast algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers is proposed. Extensive numerical simulations are carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞,1</inf>-minimization for CM signal recovery.

articleTitle: Swin Transformer-Based Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for ISAR Satellite Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Radar images contain rich information, encompassing motion, dimensionality, and electromagnetic characteristics. Unlike optical images, radar images are resilient to varying weather conditions and lighting, enabling continuous monitoring across diverse applications. However, substantial differences between radar and optical images, including their generation processes, definitions, and noise distributions, pose significant challenges for transfer learning, particularly in zero-shot inference when applying computer vision models to radar images, especially inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) images. In practical applications, access to abundant labeled optical images is common, while labeled ISAR images are often scarce, making it difficult to learn effective representations of ISAR objects in an unsupervised setting. This disparity underscores the need for robust domain adaptation techniques to bridge the gap between labeled optical data and unlabeled ISAR data, enabling accurate ISAR object classification without relying on extensive labeled ISAR datasets. This paper presents a novel approach that integrates state-of-the-art attention-based pre-trained vision models with metric learning to effectively leverage unlabeled ISAR images. By capturing shared features across domains, the proposed method achieves high classification performance on a satellite dataset, demonstrating results comparable to those obtained under supervised settings.

articleTitle: Improved 3D-Var Wind Retrieval Method for Rainy Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The traditional three-dimensional variational (3DVar) method for wind retrieval is mainly based on the measured radial velocity and continuity equation of the wind field, which is unsuitable for radar data under rainy conditions because of the difference between the velocity of raindrops and the background wind. To address that issue, this paper analyzes the relationship between wind-driven raindrops, background wind velocity, and radar data, and a new constraint equation for the improved 3D-Var method is developed based on the convective diffusion equation. To verify the feasibility of the new method, the trajectories of wind-driven raindrops and corresponding radar detection data are simulated with the aircraft wake vortex as the background wind. Results show that the improved 3D-Var method can directly retrieve the background wind velocity from radar data in rainy areas, and the retrieved wind field exhibits the basic characteristics of the aircraft wake vortex. For the whole simulation area, the root-mean-square errors of the retrieval results in horizontal and vertical directions are 1.25 m/s and 1.60 m/s, respectively.

articleTitle: A Moving Target Refocusing Method Based on Energy Accumulation Maximization for UAV Mounted Through Wall Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle mounted through-wall radar is an effective technology to detect targets behind obstacles. However, the azimuth velocity of moving target is unknown, leading to smeared radar image and affecting subsequent processing.
