Therefore, a refocus method based on maximizing energy accumulation is proposed. First, appropriate candidates of 2-D velocity are generated and then used for matched filters construction. Second, coarse imaging is performed using above filters and energy accumulation is employed. Third, the finely focused image is obtained by searching for the velocity based on energy accumulation maximization criterion. Both numerical simulation and field experiment validate the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Pulse Selection Method Based on Otsu for Frequency Agile Radar with Sparse Recovery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Frequency agile radar (FAR) can provide improved performance compared to the conventional pulse-Doppler radar due to the random-frequency pulses with sparsity in range-velocity domain. However, the sparse recovery performance of the target heavily depends on the accuracy of pulse selection in dense electric jamming environment. In order to deal with this problem, adaptive pulse selection method based on Otsu with sparse recovery is proposed for FAR. In the proposed method, the radar echo corrupted by jamming is firstly binarized by Otsu method. And then the pulses unaffected by jamming can be selected based on the number of range cells over the binary threshold. Afterwards the range and velocity parameter can be sparse recovery by the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) method. Simulated FAR data with jamming shows the proposed method can obtain accurate target estimation under the jamming environment.

articleTitle: A Ship Imaging Algorithm Based on Modified NCS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The echo characteristics of moving ship targets are complex and difficult to focus using traditional imaging algorithms. This article proposes an modified nonlinear chirp scaling algorithm (NCSA) algorithm, which first analyzes the echo model of a moving ship, then uses the RMA algorithm to implement Range Cell Migration Correction ( RCMC) , and finally uses the improved NCS algorithm to correct the azimuth space-variance. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has good focusing effect.

articleTitle: Accurate Vital Signs Detection Based on FMCW Radar in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Non-contact vital signs detection plays an important role in smart healthcare. However, most of the existing algorithms focus on stationary environments and the proposed algorithms are computationally intensive. To address the existing problems, this paper proposes the envelope fitting-adaptive fast ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EF-AFEEMD) algorithm. The time-varying DC offset is estimated by fitting the envelope of the signal. Afterwards, the demodulated signal is decomposed into multiple IMFs by adaptively determining multiple parameters of the decomposition. Finally, the appropriate IMFs corresponding to the vital signs signals are selected by calculating the correlation coefficient and local energy ratio (LER) of each IMF. Simulation has validated the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. Moreover, experimental results have shown that compared to EEMD and FEEMD, the proposed algorithm can ensure accuracy while greatly reducing computation, which is less than half of the computation time of other algorithms.

Author Keywords: adaptive fast ensemble empirical mode decomposition (AFEEMD)

articleTitle: Wide-Beam Synthetic Aperture Radar Down-Look Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) down-look imaging is widely used for sea surface observation. In recent years, the application of down-look imaging has gradually expanded to land areas. Wide beam can be used to obtain detailed topographic information. However, wide beam will cause the problem of azimuth spatial-variation. In this paper, a wide-beam SAR down-look imaging algorithm is proposed. The proposed algorithm can effectively solve the problem of range migration caused by aircraft motion and the problem of spatial-variant caused by wide beam. Experiments validates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: An Improved Deconvolution Algorithm for Time-Varying Phase Modulation Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Metasurfaces can modify radar echo characteristics by dynamically altering the phase of incident electromagnetic waves, thereby degrading radar signal processing performance. To understand modulation patterns and counteract novel electromagnetic interference, it is crucial to recover the time-varying phase modulation signals generated by metasurfaces. Therefore, this paper proposes an improved optimization-based deconvolution method. First, an optimization model is established by combining the least squares (LS) deconvolution principle with total variation constraints and imaginary part constraints. Then, the alternating minimization (AM), alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), and minimax (MM) frameworks are integrated to optimize the attenuation factor and modulation sequence. Finally, simulations validate the effectiveness of the improved method.

articleTitle: Phase-Only Null Broadening Adaptive Beamforming for Spherical Conformal Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The phase-only adaptive null broadening algorithm plays an important role in phased array radar and communications. At present, there are few studies on this method applied to conformal arrays. In this paper, a phase-only null broadening adaptive beamforming for circularly polarized spherical array is proposed. First, the interference-plus-noise covariance matrix (INCM) is reconstructed, and then the covariance matrix taper (CMT) algorithm is used to widen null. Finally, the non-convex quadratic optimization problem is transformed into a convex optimization problem using Semi-Definite Relaxation (SDR). Simulation results demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: TransCGAN-based Parameter Extraction Framework for SAR Image Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images have a wide range of applications due to their all-weather and all-day working conditions. However, SAR images with different scenarios and imaging conditions are insufficient or even rare, which is required in specific SAR image tasks. Fortunately, SAR image simulation technology can provide ample simulated images under these conditions at a low cost, addressing the scarcity of specific real SAR data. Accurate parameters are crucial for obtaining high-quality simulated images. However, it is time-consuming and labour-intensive to adjust parameters manually, and it often fails to achieve accurate simulation parameters. To tackle this problem, this paper proposes a TransCGAN-based SAR image simulation method that combines deep learning with traditional methods. By training TransCGAN, a conditional generative adversarial network (CGAN) integrated with Transformer architecture, a mapping between SAR images and simulation parameters is established. This enables the extraction of simulation parameters directly from the real SAR image, guided by the corresponding real SAR image. Ultimately, the parameters are subsequently converted into simulated SAR images via simulation software. Experimental results demonstrate that our TransCGAN-based method can effectively extract accurate simulation parameters from real SAR images, resulting in simulated images holding high similarity to real images.

articleTitle: A 3D Instantaneous Imaging Method for Maneuvering Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) imaging accurately depicts target posture and structure, providing rich feature information for space target identification. Well-focused Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) images serve as the foundation for 3D interferometric ISAR (InISAR) imaging. For maneuvering targets, it has been demonstrated that the Doppler frequency shift of their echoes varies over time. Additionally, keystone transformation cannot fully correct its Migration through resolution cells (MTRC) along the range dimension. Consequently, the range-Doppler algorithm fails to produce a clear two-dimensional (2D) image of maneuvering target. To enable 3D imaging based on defocused 2D images, a new method for 3D instantaneous imaging is proposed. First, a set of point clusters is obtained from defocused ISAR images. Then, the Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) algorithm is utilized for classification and denoising of the point clusters. The matching of point clusters between images is achieved through a scatterer association algorithm. Finally, the scatterers are inversely processed to obtain their high-resolution range profiles (HRRP), and the instantaneous 3D image of the target is acquired by 3D imaging method based on phase-derived technology.

articleTitle: Wearable Photonic-based Artificial Throat for Speech Detection and Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A wearable photonic-based artificial throat was proposed through the integration of optical fiber sensing and AI technologies. An optical fiber sensor, composed of polymer optical fibers (POFs) and elastomer optical fiber, serves as the core of the intelligent artificial throat. The optical fiber sensor is encapsulated within Dragon Skin 20 films, whose elastic modulus closely mimics that of human tissue, as a photonic-based artificial throat. This artificial throat exhibits a rapid response time, enabling it to detect minute vibrations such as airflow and muscle vibrations, which can then be converted into controlled sound. Finally, an AI algorithm was integrated with the proposed artificial throat, enabling the recognition of three monosyllabic words ("good," "age," and "book") with 100% accuracy. This successful combination of optical fiber sensing technology with AI demonstrates its applicability to the emerging field of voice control.

articleTitle: A Convolutional Neural Network Using Multi-Level Feature Projection for SAR Vehicle Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target recognition scenarios, traditional convolutional neural network (CNN) models often struggle with inadequate generalization performance. To address the challenging operating conditions in SAR vehicle target recognition, this paper proposes a new CNN model that employs multi-level feature projection. This model first uses a lightweight backbone network to extract multi-level feature maps. These feature maps are normalized to balance their weights across different levels and channels. Then, a new feature projection module is proposed to perceive and fuse multi-level features, which addresses high-dimensional characteristics and overfitting effects. Extensive experiments on the benchmark dataset validate the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Non-contact Detection of Sleep Apnea Event based on Respiratory Signal using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Sleep apnea is a common sleep disorder. In recent years, numerous studies have concentrated on developing automated diagnostic methods for sleep apnea based on machine learning and deep learning. However, most of these methods use the signals from PSG sensors, which usually obstruct the patients' breathing and cause discomfort. Radar-based contactless detection techniques overcome these limitations, but there are still some drawbacks. For example, most focus on sleep apnea classification and cannot localize events precisely. In this study, we propose a fine-grained, non-contact sleep apnea detection method based on respiratory signals. Our method combines convolutional neural networks and multi-head self-attention mechanisms. We evaluate the method on clinical datasets, and the results demonstrate that this method achieves an accuracy of 83.7% in 1-second-level sleep apnea segment detection. Additionally, the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) for the Apnea Index (AI) is 0.915, and the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) is 6.34. It has the potential to serve as an at-home monitoring method.

articleTitle: Semantic-compensated Meta-learning for Few-shot SAR Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High-value novel-class SAR targets exhibit distributional differences from base-class SAR targets, leading existing FSOD methods to suffer from model bias and poor generalization. To address this issue and more effectively detect few-shot targets, this paper introduces a semantic compensation method based on meta-learning (SCML). Specifically, we generate support compensation features enriched with query semantic information to mitigate distribution discrepancies and guide the model in adapting to new-class SAR targets under few-shot conditions, thereby significantly improving detection performance. On existing public datasets, our method demonstrates superior detection accuracy compared to other SOTA approaches.

articleTitle: Ionosphere Phase Decontamination for OTHR Based on Fourier Synchrosqueezed Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The ionosphere phase contamination of over-the- horizon radar (OTHR) leads to sea clutter and target Doppler broadening, which in turn degrades the target detection performance. To solve this problem, a method based on Fourier synchrosqueezed transform (FSST) is proposed. First, FSST is performed on the ionosphere contaminated data. Second, the time-frequency ridges are extracted and used to estimate the instantaneous frequency. Finally, the ionosphere phase disturbance error is estimated based on the instantaneous frequency, and the decontamination is realized through the phase compensation. The FSST has a higher frequency and time resolution than the other time-frequency (TF) analysis methods, and thus has a higher accuracy of the instantaneous frequency estimation. Simulation analysis shows that the FSST method has better ionosphere decontamination performance compared with existing methods.

articleTitle: Grating Lobe Suppression in MIMO Radar Networks using Kaiser-Kalmus Sum-Difference Beam Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: MIMO radar networks are composed of multiple separated MIMO sensors and each radar sensor can be viewed as a subarray. Although the MIMO radar networks can obtain a larger virtual aperture, excessive node or subarray spacing will lead to a wider grating lobe distribution. In order to solve the grating lobe problem, this paper proposes a Kaiser-Kalmus sum and difference beam cancellation method, which uses subarray beam to suppress array factor’s grating lobes. In the MIMO radar networks imaging scenario, the effectiveness of this algorithm was verified through simulation and experiments.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Optical-SAR Cooperative System Based on Mutual Information
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The current research on optical-SAR cooperative work mainly focuses on the fusion of optical and SAR images, while there are fewer studies on how the optical and SAR sensor can cooperate optimally for targets survey. In this paper, mutual information is employed as the evaluation metric of optical-SAR cooperative system. Firstly, the optical-SAR cooperative system is modeled according to imaging principles. Then the mutual information expression of the optical-SAR cooperative system is derived with the stochastic process theory. Finally, through simulation, the relationship between the mutual information of the cooperative system and the target detection probability is analyzed to verify the validity of the mutual information as the performance evaluation metric of the cooperative detection system.

articleTitle: Road Boundary Extraction from LiDAR Point Clouds Using Dynamic Programming Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that it is difficult and inaccurate to extract road boundaries from laser point clouds, a road boundary extraction method based on a dynamic programming algorithm is proposed. First, the point clouds are projected, and an obstacle grid map is obtained using the dual height difference algorithm to retain the ground features near the curb. Considering the distance from the boundary points to the driving trajectory, the dynamic programming algorithm is used to extract the road boundary. Starting from the driving trajectory, the algorithm searches for the white obstacle points in the grid maps on both sides, and the point with the minimum total cost is considered the boundary point. This study used the IQmulus & TerraMobilita datasets for experiments. The results showed that the accuracy and recall rates of the extraction results from both datasets were above 98.7%, and the F1 scores were both above 98.4%.

articleTitle: Research on Signal Coherent Synthesis for Distributed Coherent Aperture Radar under Differentiated Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the development of science and technology, the Distributed Coherent Aperture Radar (DCAR) system, which can realize the energy synthesis of electromagnetic wave signals in space, has gradually become a research hotspot to satisfy the increasing requirements for coordinated detection. However, most existing studies consider the consistent state of each radar in the DCAR system, which is not instructive for radar systems with varying array sizes or under non-parallel beam pointing. In response to this issue, this paper constructs a corresponding signal model based on DCAR detection. Then, simulates and prototype experiments verify the multi-radar coherent synthesis gain under various differentiated conditions. Finally, the improvements of coherent synthesized signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) under multiple synergistic conditions are given, and the feasibility and achievability of differentiated distributed synergistic enhancement of perception are preliminarily verified.

articleTitle: Deep Learning based Gesture Recognition with Millimeter-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Although millimeter-wave radar stands out in the field of industrial Internet of Things (IoT) due to its advantages such as low power consumption and wide coverage, in practice, when using millimeter-wave radar for gesture recognition, existing algorithms often result in recognition errors due to environmental interference. To address this challenge, the C2f-Star-SimAM (C2f-StarS) network is proposed to realize gesture recognition with 77 GHz frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar. In this process, one-dimensional Fourier transform (1D-FFT), moving target indication (MTI), and short-time Fourier transform (STFT) are adopted to generate Doppler-time maps (DTM). Experimental results verify the C2f-StarS network can improve accuracy and efficiency by effectively extracting gesture features in the presence of interference, achieving a high accuracy of 98.8% in gesture recognition.

articleTitle: Propeller-Modulation Clutter Suppression for Airborne Radar Based on 3D Sliding Window and Orthogonal Projection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: For non-side looking airborne radar (NSLAR), when the main lobe beam of the antenna passes through a turboprop engine, propeller-modulation clutter is generated. This expands the clutter Doppler spectrum and increases clutter’s non-stationarity, reducing Space Time Adaptive Processing (STAP) performance. To address this issue, a novel propeller-modulation clutter suppression method is proposed. Firstly, this method uses a blocking matrix and three-dimensional (3D) sliding window processing to generate more training samples. These samples are then used to estimate the clutter covariance matrix (CCM) of the sub-aperture data. Next, the echo data of the cell under test (CUT) is subjected to 3D sliding window processing to obtain sub-aperture data of echo. Finally, the non-stationary propeller-modulated clutter at near-range is suppressed using orthogonal projection (OP) of subaperture. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively suppresses propeller-modulation clutter.

articleTitle: A Target Positioning Method without External Information Assistance for Airborne CSAR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Radar is the abbreviation of radio detection and ranging, so radar is by its basic nature a ranging instrument. If radar range measurements from multi-views can be exactly performed and assembled, then the multi-views positioning method based on the range equations can localize a common target from a set of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images to its true coordinates. It is worth noting that the distribution of these SAR images has a great impact on the performance of the positioning method. Circular SAR (CSAR) is a special mode of SAR systems, it has attracted much attention for its ability to obtain scatters’ wide-angle backscatter information and realize high-resolution imaging. On the one hand, the wide-angle observation capability is an advantage in the multi-view positioning method. On the other hand, the curved trajectory of the platform fits the bill perfectly. However, the distribution of the selected sub-aperture images influences the positioning results greatly. Based on the proposed error transfer model, we analyze and conclude a principle of selecting sub-aperture images. The conclusions were verified by processing a set of real- measured CSAR data.

articleTitle: Range and Angle Estimation for Multi-Carrier FDA Radar with a Single Snapshot via ADMM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The multi-carrier frequency diverse array (FDA) radar enables accurate range and angle estimation with a single snapshot by employing the atomic norm minimization (ANM) method. However, solving the corresponding optimization problem with conventional CVX convex optimization toolbox is computationally demanding. To cope with this, in this paper, we develop and derive an implementation of the ANM method using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) for the multi-carrier FDA. This approach decomposes the optimization problem into multiple subproblems, iteratively updating the unknown parameters with closed-form solutions. Compared to the ANM-CVX algorithm, the proposed ANM-ADMM algorithm can significantly enhance computational efficiency while achieving similar estimation accuracy. The effectiveness is demonstrated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Research on comprehensive performance test method of automotive DAB terminals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: DAB, or Digital Audio Broadcasting, is a digital radio technology capable of transmitting high-quality audio signals to automotive systems. Since the beginning of 2024, it has become a mandatory test requirement for vehicles exported to European and Middle Eastern countries. China Automotive Engineering Research Institute (CAERI) has taken the lead in establishing the capability to evaluate DAB performance and functionality, becoming the only CNAS-authorized testing institution for DAB regulatory standards in China. In addition to using Audio Communication Tester SET (ACTS) to analyze the performance of component-level DAB DUTs (Devices Under Test), CAERI has also simulated the functionality of vehicle-level DAB DUTs in the laboratory using several ACTS with Radio Frequency Channel Emulator (RFCE). CAERI has developed a comprehensive performance testing methodology of automotive DAB terminals that covers both component and vehicle levels, and successfully completed multiple tasks for automotive enterprises.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Measurement of Tangential Wind Field Using a Digital Array Radar Based on Interferometry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The tracer particles of wind field are distributed soft targets, unlike hard targets such as aircraft and ships, how to obtain the tangential component of the wind field through monostatic Doppler radar is a challenging problem. Doppler weather radar can only detect the radial component of the wind field and retrieve wind vectors by combining the radial velocities of multiple points in space through various scanning methods. However, this is limited by assumptions of the background wind and cannot directly measure the tangential component. To solve the difficulty, we preliminarily propose an interferometric detection method (IDM) based on digital array radar to achieve direct measurement of tangential Doppler velocities and verify the feasibility of IDM based on simulation experiments of a typical wind field.

articleTitle: Modified CLEAN Algorithm Based on Two-Dimensional Matched Filter Outputs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The CLEAN algorithm is usually used to reconstruct images due to its low computational complexity. However, existing CLEAN algorithms cannot completely remove signal components of strong targets due to the low accuracy in estimating the target amplitudes, which results in weak targets being masked by the residual range-Doppler sidelobes generated by strong targets. In this paper, a modified CLEAN algorithm based on two-dimensional matched filter outputs (Modified MF-CLEAN) is proposed. Modified MF-CLEAN can improve the target amplitude estimation accuracy by performing multiple corrections to the amplitude estimation during the iterations. Simulation results show that Modified MF-CLEAN significantly outperforms the existing CLEAN algorithms in terms of the target amplitude estimation performance and success rate.

articleTitle: Pulse train coding design for MIMO radar against interrupted sampling repeater jamming with Doppler frequency shifts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Intercepting and repeatedly retransmitting radar signals, interrupted sampling repeater jamming (ISRJ) generates higher power false signals that can seriously affect radar operation. To combat this interference, a scheme for countering ISRJ with Doppler frequency shifts by designing a multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar with pulse train encoding and decoding is proposed. On the one hand, the scheme can suppress the pulse compression sidelobes of the target and ISRJ with Doppler frequency shifts. On the other hand, a detection matrix is designed to identify spurious peaks formed by interfering signals. Finally, the proposed scheme can accurately obtain target and jamming information in the environment while satisfying the constant mode (CM) constraints.

articleTitle: Underground Pipeline Precise Positioning Method Based on GPR Bscan Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) enables the positioning of underground pipelines without excavation. However, the accuracy and errors of existing methods are still insufficient due to the influence of strong clutter in actual environments. In this paper, an underground pipeline precise positioning method based on GPR Bscan images is proposed. First, the YOLOv8 neural network is employed for initially pipeline positioning. Next, by combining network post-processing with curve fitting, the pipeline depth is estimated with high accuracy, enabling precise pipeline positioning. Finally, in validation using measured data, the proposed method achieved a mean average precision (MAP) of 96.8% in the initially pipeline positioning step and a relative depth estimation error of 4.84% in the precise positioning step.

articleTitle: Multiview HRRPs Recognition Based on Dynamic Structure and Parameters Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High-Resolution Range Profile (HRRP) contains rich target features and is easy to obtain, making it important data in the field of radar aerial target identification. However, many current studies have only focused on single-view static networks, without making full use of the multi-view information of the target. Besides, the structure and parameters of the network are also fixed, which cannot learn the target features dynamically. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-view network (Dynamic Structure and Parameters Neural Network, DSPNN) that can dynamically adjust its own structure and parameters according to the input samples. Firstly, the network realizes the dynamic adjustment of network depth and convolutional kernel parameters through the skip gate mechanism and dynamic convolutional kernel. Next, the weights of the extracted features are reassigned through the spatial attention mechanism. Finally, the fusion of multi-view features is accomplished by the multi-input feature fusion module, which improves the feature adaptive extraction and fusion capability of the network. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method has superior aerial target multi-view HRRPs classification performance over other compared methods.

articleTitle: Ethical Review Key Points of Brain-Computer Interface Clinical Research
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) technology demonstrates enormous potential in clinical applications, resulting in its ethical risks requiring further verification. To ensure that the development and application of BCI technology benefit humans while avoiding harm to research participants, it is essential to have strict ethical reviews before the implementation of BCI clinical research. This paper proposes the key points of ethical review for BCI clinical research based on the four principles of biomedical ethics, and discusses the ethical risks of BCI technology from autonomy, non-maleficence, beneficence, and justice. This paper aims to support ethical review committees and investigators to have a better understanding and assessment of the risks and benefits of BCI clinical research, optimize research protocols, and protect the rights and safety of research participants.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Estimation Method for Group Target Number Based on Information Theoretic Criterion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The number of individuals within a group is crucial information for the correct association, robust tracking, and situation awareness. Traditional methods using the range profile’s peaks are not suitable when targets are densely distributed. The target number estimation algorithms based on monopulse systems have high computational complexity, while those based on array systems require additional sensor resources. To address these issues, this paper proposes a method based on multiple incoherent observations using one monopulse radar. By combining multiple incoherent observations from a single sensor with information theoretic criterion, this approach can estimate the number of targets even when the resolution of a single sensor is insufficient. The effectiveness of the algorithm is verified through simulations, and the algorithm's performance is analyzed.

articleTitle: Feature-Aided UKF-PHD Filter for Nonlinear Multi-target Tracking in Holographic Staring Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Traditional radar multi-target tracking relies on data association methods, which result in exponential computational complexity when clutter and target densities are high. The Gaussian mixture probability hypothesis density (GM-PHD) filter, built upon the random finite set framework, presents a more efficient approach for multi-target tracking without having to conduct explicit data association. However, this method is only applicable to Gaussian linear models, limiting its utility in practical scenarios. Moreover, radar environments often feature high clutter densities and low detection probabilities, making real-time and accurate target tracking challenging. To address these issues, this paper proposes extending the GM-PHD filter to nonlinear Gaussian models using the unscented transform and introduces a feature-aided unscented Kalman filter PHD (FAUKF-PHD) multi-target tracking algorithm. By leveraging the high-precision Doppler information contained in holographic staring radar echoes, the proposed algorithm adjusts the weights of Gaussian components, significantly reducing clutter weights to distinguish targets from clutter and pruning redundant components. The simulation outcomes evidently show that the FAUKF-PHD filter put forward in this study boosts the estimation accuracy and real-time performance under scenarios characterized by high clutter density and low detection probability.

articleTitle: A novel SAR image denoising method based on self-supervised network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Noise suppression is an important preprocessing step for sythetic aperture radar (SAR) image interpretation. In particular, noise affects the quality of SAR images, which in turn affects the subsequent down streaming processing, such as target identification, classificatio, etc. In this paper, a novel SAR image denoising method based on self-supervised framework is proposed, which utilizes the statistical distribution characteristics of noise and conducts denoising processing through the self-supervised network framework, and then achieves high-quality denoised radar image. Moreover, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through computer simulation experiments.

articleTitle: A Receive-Coherent Detector of Moving Target for Airborne Distributed Coherent Aperture Radar under Random Phase Errors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Airborne Distributed Coherent Aperture Radar (ADCAR) benefits from the signal coherent synthesis of multiple transmit-receive (TR) pairs echoes to improve signal gain and detection performance significantly. However, the independent partitioning of airborne distributed radars tends to introduce complex random phase errors that will severely reduce the target detection performance for the received coherent synthesis. In this paper, we first consider the receive-coherent model of ADCAR under random phase errors and introduce the Von-Mises distribution to model the random phase error. Then, a receive-coherent Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) detector (RCD-VEM-G) based on the expectation maximization (EM) algorithm is proposed according to the Von-Mises distribution model, which iteratively solves for the unknown parameters under the alternative hypotheses by the EM algorithm to achieve the GLRT for the target. Simulation results show that the proposed RCD-VEM-G detector ensures better detection performance under random phase errors for different shape parameter models and outperforms the conventional target detector, proving the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Transformer-in-Transformer Network with A Complex-Valued Mixup Module for SAR Automatic Target Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Convolutional neural network (CNN) has been demonstrated an effective approach for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) automatic target recognition (ATR) in recent years. However, CNNs usually extract characteristics through local receptive fields, resulting in the loss of global feature information of targets. Moreover, satisfactory target recognition performance using CNN generally depends on sufficient labeled sample images, which are difficult to obtain in SAR ATR conditions. To address these issues, we propose a Complex-Valued Mixup (CVM) module- aided Transformer-in-Transformer (TNT) network (CVM-TNT) for SAR ATR. The CVM module generates new samples through linear interpolation and utilizes both amplitude and phase information to extract richer electromagnetic scattering feature. The TNT network takes the advantages of global and local features to compensate the deficiency of traditional Transformer network that only extracts global features. Firstly, we divide the input images including amplitude and phase into several local patches as "visual sentences". Then, we use the outer conventional Transformer block to calculate global features and their global attentions of visual sentences. Subsequently, dividing the local patches into sub-patches as "visual words" and embedding an inner sub-Transformer block into the network excavates the local phase and amplitude features of visual words. Finally, both word-level and sentence-level features will be combined to boost the representation capability. Experiments implemented on the moving and stationary target acquisition and recognition (MSTAR) dataset have shown that the proposed CVM-TNT model outperforms the state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods in the case of small datasets.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of Rainfall on Polarized Radar ISAR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Polarized inverse synthetic aperture radar (PolISAR) is capable of all-weather, all-day and high-resolution imaging observation of targets, which is an important means of acquiring information about space targets, but the wave propagation effect under complex atmospheric environments may have a significant impact on the imaging results. This paper establishes the ISAR imaging model of fully polarized radar under complex rainfall conditions, analyzes the polarized electromagnetic wave amplitude attenuation and phase error caused by the propagation effect under rainfall environment. The theoretical derivation yields the effect of rainfall on PolISAR imaging. The experimental results verify the correctness of the ISAR imaging model under complex rainfall conditions.

articleTitle: Masking Radar Signals with Two Masks Overlapping in Frequency Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Electronic attack (EA) equipment can interfere radar systems by emitting interference signals with the assistant of the electronic support measurement (ESM) equipment. In this case, masking signalss can be designed to deceive ESM equipment and prevent EA equipment from emitting interference. This paper proposes an active anti-interference signal design method for Multiple-input Multiple-output (MIMO) radar. Designed masking signals cover a radar signal in the time domain, but the frequency band of the masking signals in the frequency domain does not completely overlap with the radar signal, making it difficult for an enemy ESM equipment to determine whether the obtained signal is a radar signal or interference masking signals. To reduce the cross correlation sidelobes between radar signals and masking signals, the masking signals are designed with upper and lower frequency bands with an identical center frequency, and then the spectrum of the masking signals can be efficient shifted to achieve the spectrum overlap, therefore, low cross correlation sidelobes can be ensured. Simulation results indicate that the propsoed algorithm can reduce the cross-correlation sidelobe level to the level of −100 dB, and it is also shown that the proposed algorithm is robust to the radar transmission delay.

articleTitle: Research on Radar Echo Extrapolation Method Integrating Terrain Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In recent years, severe convective weather has caused significant harm to lives and property, leading to flooding and geological disasters. Consequently, nowcasting and early warning of such events are crucial. Advances in artificial intelligence technologies have provided critical support for these efforts through radar echo extrapolation based on deep learning. However, most current deep learning methods primarily rely on historical radar reflectivity factors or vertically integrated liquid water content for extrapolation. Despite the significant influence of orographic effects on meteorological processes, the impact of terrain feature data on radar echo extrapolation remains underexplored. Therefore, this paper proposes a radar echo extrapolation model that integrates terrain feature data. By incorporating both radar and terrain feature data at the input stage, the model more effectively captures the spatiotemporal characteristics of meteorological processes, thereby enhancing its predictive capability. Additionally, a terrain-guided composite loss function is introduced to further constrain the model, leading to more accurate predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach can improves prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Improved Clutter Suppression Method for Bridge Vibration Measurement Based on GB-MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Ground based multi-input multi-output (GB-MIMO) radar has been gradually applied in the field of bridge vibration monitoring. During measurement, the interference of static clutter on the vibrating target signal in the same azimuth and range resolution severely affects the vibration measurement. The traditional method of removing static clutter is to estimate static clutter by fitting a circular curve to a complex signal point set, that is, fitting the vector of the circular curve center deviating from the origin of the polar coordinate system. Due to the clustered distribution of vibration points during non vibration time, the trajectory of complex sequence point sets will be distorted, resulting in poor clutter suppression effect. This article proposes an improved method for measuring the dynamic deflection of bridges by suppressing clutter. Firstly, obtain the vibration time period of the vibration candidate points through time-frequency analysis. Secondly, extract the complex sequence of each pixel during the vibration time period, and use the circular trace fitting method to estimate the stationary clutter. Then, based on outlier degree and outlier rate evaluation indicators, select vibration measurement pixels that can achieve effective clutter suppression. The effectiveness of this method was preliminarily verified by comparing the dynamic deflection curves of millimeter wave radar and laser vibrometer through model bridge experiments. In addition, the method was also validated through a high-speed railway bridge experiment.

articleTitle: Target Location in Distributed MIMO radar based on Coherent Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of target location is investigated in the distributed multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar based on coherent processing. At the modelling stage, the distributed MIMO radar is divided into three separated subarrays, where both transmit and receive functions are used in subarrays 1 and 3, while only receive function is adopted in subarray 2. Furthermore, a small frequency increment is introduced among different antenna elements in the subarray 1, in the meantime, a phase modulating operation is performed for various antenna elements in the subarray 3. In this respect, the target location performance can be improved significantly by means of the transmit modulation in subarrays 1 and 3. Under the circumstances, the model of target location is established, and a two-step estimation technology is shown, where a small location sector with respect to targets are firstly obtained, and the accurate location are further estimated. Specifically, in order to reduce the computational cost required by the multi-dimensional search procedures, an alternating procedure is developed by a sequence of 1-D searches obtained alternating between the optimization over each variable keeping the other fixed. Numerical results corroborate the effectiveness of the developed methods for the target location with distributed MIMO radar based on coherent processing.

articleTitle: Dual-Band HRRP Fusion Recognition via Wavelet Decomposition Embedded Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High-resolution range profile (HRRP) is a crucial technique for radar target recognition. Due to the coupling of azimuthal scattering information and aspect sensitivity, fine target recognition using HRRP remains challenging. One way to mitigate HRRP aspect sensitivity is through enhancing the dimensionality of radar information acquisition. Therefore, this paper proposes a Dual-Band HRRP Fusion Recognition Model via Wavelet Decomposition Embedded Autoencoder (DF-WD-AENet). The method we proposed mainly comprises two modules. Firstly, the autoencoder model based on wavelet decomposition (WD-AEM) achieves constraint on feature information, making it better suited for dual-band fusion. Next is the dual-band information fusion module (DFM), in which we achieved the interaction and fusion of feature information through convolutional block attention module (CBAM) and omni-dimensional dynamic convolution (ODConv), and used a fusion loss function to train the model. Experiment shows that the recognition rate of our method is 7.73% higher than that of single-band, proving the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Three-D Imaging of Urban Layover Scatterers Based on Learned LISTA Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper explores a Tomographic Synthetic Aperture Radar (TomoSAR) learning imaging model based on the Learned ISTA (LISTA) algorithm. It addresses the limitations of traditional sparse regularization methods encountered in TomoSAR, particularly their sensitivity to noise and high computational complexity. This study involves unfolding the Iterative Shrinkage Thresholding Algorithm (ISTA) into a neural network structure, allowing for the transformation of preset hyperparameters into learnable parameters, thereby enhancing model adaptability. This paper includes constructing a diverse training set and testing the model against various conditions, including different Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNRs) and scatterer spacings. The results demonstrate that the LISTA-based TomoSAR imaging algorithm achieves super-resolution performance and reduces computational complexity over traditional methods.

articleTitle: Research on the Simulation Method of Dual Polarization Phased Array Weather Radar Echo
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to efficiently simulate different weather processes in advance to provide higher performance and better algorithm scanning scheme for actual radar equipment, this paper constructs a dual polarization phased array weather radar echo simulation method. The WSR88D weather radar PPI volume scanning base data, including reflectivity, velocity, spectral width, differential reflectivity, differential phase and correlation coefficient, are bilinearly interpolated into CAPPI data as a three-dimensional weather field, analyzed for the different elevation angles of the WSR88D and the simulated radar in volume scanning mode (0.44°, 1.68°, 2.33°, and 3.1°) of the base data of WSR88D and simulated radar in volume scan mode, and the results show that the simulated base data is close to that of WSR88D.

Author Keywords: dual polarization phased array weather radar

articleTitle: Target location algorithm based on FMCW radar signal feature extraction and PCA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Non-contact vital sign measurement based on FMCW radar is a research hotspot. In order to solve the problem of inaccurate selection of range bin and jump phenomenon in target location, a target location algorithm based on signal feature extraction and PCA is proposed in this paper. Firstly, select the range of distance unit where the target may be located based on the signal features. Secondly, use PCA algorithm to extract the appropriate principal components from the vital signs sample matrix, and construct the sample center and confidence interval. Finally, the optimal phase signal in the range is selected according to the reference sample and the minimum distance criterion, and it corresponds to the range bin where the target is located. After the target position and the optimal phase signal are obtained by the algorithm, the breathing and heartbeat signals is seperated by VMD algorithm and reconstructed. The experimental results show that the algorithm can accurately extract the range bin of the resting target, and has a good tracking effect on the location of the displaced target, so as to ensure the accurate measurement of subsequent vital signs.

articleTitle: Analysis of SAR visibility and sensitivity based on Sentinel-1A images - a case study of Fengjie, the Three Gorges Region of China
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The Three Gorges Region is one of the regions with the most geological disasters in China. Fengjie county, located in the Chongqing section of the Three Gorges Region, is one of the most complicated areas of geological hazards in northeast of Chongqing. Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (InSAR) technology has been proven to be an effective method for surface deformation monitoring, such as the earthquake, landslide and land subsidence etc. Nevertheless, the application of InSAR technology in landslide monitoring is limited by observation blind areas. These blind areas are mainly caused by the large scale of slope in the study area and the direction of satellite. And, these blind areas are also caused by the land cover changes. In this paper, we obtained the observation capability of Sentinel-1A ascending data in Fengjie county, and projection of true surface deformation in the line of sight direction by calculating the relationship of synthetic aperture radar data and digital elevation model data. And we analyzed the relationship about visibility, sensitivity and InSAR monitoring points. It provides a priori assessment of SAR image selection for geological disaster monitoring in the Three Gorges Region, and a regional interpretation method of InSAR deformation values for mountainous areas with significant terrain fluctuation.

articleTitle: Cross-Polarization Isolation Requirement for Polarimetric Weather Radar Under ATSR Mode and STSR Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Polarimetric Doppler weather radar has become an irreplaceable tool for weather observation. Currently, polarimetric weather radar usually operates in the alternately transmitting and simultaneously receiving mode and the simultaneously transmitting and simultaneously receiving mode. In these two operating modes, the cross-polarization coupling of the radar system may affect the measurement accuracy of polarization parameters. This paper quantitatively analyzes the cross-polarization isolation level required in different operating modes and precipitation conditions to attain the accuracy of polarization parameter and spectral moment parameter measurement.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Distributed Radar Echo Simulation Software Design Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To address the design and functional analysis needs of radar echo simulation systems in complex environments, this paper proposes a design method for reconfigurable distributed radar echo simulation software based on the Component-Based Software Engineering (CBSE) approach. This method achieves flexible configuration and functional expansion of radar echo simulation software through component-based design and asynchronous task scheduling. It significantly enhances the adaptability and scalability of the system. The paper first conducts an in-depth analysis of existing radar echo simulation technologies, revealing their limitations. Based on this, it designs a radar echo simulation architecture that supports asynchronous scheduling of echo simulation tasks and context updates at different stages, allowing for flexible management of simulation tasks. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed method shows significant advantages in task scheduling efficiency, system scalability, and adaptability to heterogeneous environments. This research provides an innovative approach to the design and implementation of radar echo simulation systems and shows broad application prospects.

articleTitle: ERA-Net: End-to-End Recognition-Aware Sparse SAR Imaging Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High-resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging is crucial for effective target recognition. Current sparse aperture SAR imaging algorithm based on compressed sensing (CS) often lack constraints related to recognition performance, leading to the loss of key features beneficial for recognition. This results in lower recognition rates in the resulting images. This paper proposes a sparse SAR imaging method driven by target recognition tasks, and constructs an end-to-end recognition-aware sparse SAR imaging network (ERA-Net) from the perspective of SAR imaging interpretation integration. It not only effectively improves the accuracy of downstream recognition tasks, but also reconstructs higher quality SAR images that are conducive to recognition.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Geometric Feature Optimization for Object Detection in SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Object detection in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images is a de facto need in military and civilian fields. The detector frequently encounter difficulties in capturing object geometric information due to multi-scale objects and unobvious edge features. To tackle this issue, we focus on cross-scale geometric information perception ability of SAR image object detectors. First, we construct a YOLOv8-n network based SAR object detection framework. Secondly, we propose a cross-space learning method to tackle short-range and long-range dependence, which could alleviate the small object false alarm problem. We propose a novel box regression loss that utilizes the minimum point distance, integrating the center point offset and width-height variation of horizontal bounding boxes to facilitate accelerated convergence. Comprehensive experiments conducted on the SSDD, MSTAR, and SAR-AIRcraft-1.0 datasets highlight the effectiveness and advantages of our approach. The mean average precision (mAP) on these datasets reaches 97.6%, 99.22%, and 81.23%, respectively, surpassing existing detection methods.

articleTitle: Multi-angle Image Fusion in Ground-based Radar Lunar Imaging Based on Image Kurtosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The fusion of multi-angle lunar images can provide more comprehensive lunar topography information than original images, and ground-based (GB) radar has the ability to acquire multi-angle lunar images. In GB radar multi-angle lunar image fusion, proper radar trajectories should be selected, and image fusion algorithm should be used. In this paper, the multi-angle lunar image fusion technique for GB synthetic aperture radar (SAR) based on image kurtosis is proposed. To begin with, the echo signal model considering space-variant backscattering coefficient is established to reflect lunar topography feature. After that, a multi-angle radar trajectory selection method based on K-means algorithm is proposed to acquire multi-angle lunar images. Thereafter a multi-angle lunar image fusion algorithm based on image kurtosis and gradient descent is proposed to acquire the fused image. Finally, computer simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing Visual Grounding through Diffusion Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Remote Sensing Visual Grounding (RSVG) focuses on identifying location of targets in RS images mentioned by text descriptions. Existing method typically rely on multi-layer transformer framework, which uses visual encoder, text encoder and fusion decoder to align visual and text features. However, the absence of continuous and progressive text guidance can lead to inconsistencies between visual and textual features, thereby limiting grounding ability. Thus, in this paper, we present a novel remote sensing visual grounding framework by diffusion model, RSD-VG, which use U-Net to progressively refine queried object boxes by denoising using consistent language guidance. We validate the efficiency of RSD-VG on DIOR-RSVG dataset and compare it with previous methods and achieve promising results.

articleTitle: Radar Deception Jamming Identification Based on Multi-dimensional Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the advancement of electronic technology, Digital Radio Frequency Memory (DRFM) jammers are capable of generating highly realistic active deception jamming signals that closely mimic radar transmission signals, severely disrupting our radar systems’ ability to track real targets. To address this issue, this paper analyzes the differences in scattering point angle characteristics and polarization characteristics between target echoes and deception jamming. We propose a radar deception jamming identification method based on multi-dimensional feature extraction. This method calculates and analyzes features from multiple sets of measured radar data, obtaining jamming clustering thresholds for each feature. Based on these thresholds, we can distinguish between the jamming and the target The method maintains excellent recognition performance even under low jamming-to-noise ratios (JNR). Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: SR-PFGM++ Based Consistency Model for Speech Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Diffusion models and the extended Poisson flow generative model (PFGM++) have been applied to speech enhancement. They are sampled via stochastic differential equation (SDE) or ordinary differential equation (ODE), but usually require a large number of sampling steps. Hence, we introduce the consistency models, which allow for high-quality one-step generation with non-adversarial training. Specifically, based on our previous work, SR-PFGM++ (PFGM++ combined with stochastic regeneration) is distilled to train consistency model, resulting in the proposed Consistency Model for speech enhancement. Test results on the VoiceBank-DEMAND dataset show that the proposed model significantly reduces the inference time relative to SR-PFGM++ while maintaining comparable performance. Besides, mismatch test results on the TIMIT+NOISE92 dataset demonstrate the generalization ability of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Angular Super-resolution Imaging of Airborne Radar by Detect-reconstruct Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Angular resolution of airborne radar is usually poor because of its limited aperture size. The adjacent formation targets are difficult to be distinguished. To distinguish the adjacent targets by airborne radar, in this paper, a detect-reconstruct approach is proposed. First, the L1 norm is adopted to sparsely restrict the aerial targets. Second, because the targets are sparsely dispersed in the range dimension, a range pre-detection step is proposed to reduce the echo dimension, and the analyzed target range bins are reduced. Finally, a detect-reconstruct approach is proposed in the azimuthal super-resolution procedure to avoid the artificial targets. In simulation experiments, the angular resolution and efficiency of the proposed approach are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Real-Time Detection of Moving Target Using Through-Wall Radar Based on GPU
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Through-Wall radar plays an important role in detecting moving targets behind walls in counter-terrorism and urban-sensing. While there has been a lot of research on moving target detection algorithm design, most of them suffer from high complexity in implementation for real-time detection, and thus limiting the practical applications. This paper proposes a real-time detection technology of moving target by through-wall radar based on GPU. This method includes multi-stream asynchronous parallel technology of the Displaced Phase Center Antenna based on GPU for clutter suppression module, block-thread parallel technology of the Back-Projection based on GPU for imaging module, and inter-block parallel and intra-block reduction technology of 2D Constant False Alarm Rate based on GPU for detection module. Based on CPU-GPU dual devices in through-wall radar system, this method can output the detection result per second, which meets the needs of real-time detection of moving targets in practical applications.

articleTitle: Automatic identification algorithm for insulation board bonding status based on improved YOLOv7
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: At present, for the detection of the bonding status of the building exterior wall insulation layer mainly relies on manual interpretation of radar images, which is not only time-consuming and prone to errors; at the same time, the background of the ground-penetrating radar image is relatively complex, so how to accurately determine whether it is the normal bonding state or the top debonding state or the subgrade debonding state between the insulation board and the bonding agent or between the wall and the bonding agent is still a difficult problem. For the detection of the three different states of normal bonding, top debonding and subgrade debonding, the YOLOv7 algorithm is used to achieve automatic identification; on this basis, in order to improve the phenomenon of multi-inspection and misdetection, the BiFormer attention mechanism is introduced after the ELAN module of YOLOv7, and the improvement of the YOLOv7’s mAP@0.5:0.95 can reach 0.7788, and the phenomenon of multi-detection and misdetection is greatly reduced, which verifies the feasibility and accuracy of the improved model, and significantly improves the accuracy and efficiency of the model for the identification of defects in the bonding status of the insulation board.

articleTitle: Open-Set Specific Emitter Identification Based on Activation Reshaping and Important Neurons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Aiming at the challenge that existing research on open-set specific emitter identification (SEI) has low identification performance due to high similarity between known classes and unknown classes, this paper proposes an approach based on activation reshaping and important neurons. This method utilizes convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract latent features from the signals of emitter individuals. Specifically, activation reshaping and pruning based on Shapley value are applied in the penultimate layer of the CNN to enhance differentiation between known and unknown emitter individuals. The open-set score derived from model logits and the Energy score function is leveraged in proposed method to effectively discriminate unknown emitter individuals from known emitter individuals, thereby transforming open-set recognition into closed-set recognition. A balanced trade-off between accuracy for known and unknown classes is achieved by the proposed method. Experimental results demonstrate that under various degrees of openness, the proposed method achieves more accurate open-set SEI classification results.

articleTitle: Indoor Moving Target Detection Method Based On Azimuthal Accumulation For UAV Mounted Dual Channels Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Through-the-Wall radar transmits an ultra-wideband (UWB) signal capable of penetrating the walls, which can be used to detect targets behind obstacles. Combined with unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), the detection of moving targets inside buildings can be realized with high flexibility. However, in the through-the-wall scenario, the target motion leads to poor imaging results and deterioration of detection. So that, a moving target detection method based on azimuthal energy accumulation is proposed in this paper. In detail, firstly, the displaced phase center antennas (DPCA) method is used to suppress the stationary clutters. Then, the keystone transform and azimuthal accumulation are employed. Finally, the detection results are derived by using 1D-CFAR. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by experiments.

articleTitle: Imputation of Doppler Cardiograms Using a Fine-Tuned Time-series Foundation Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The robust and continuous measurement of Doppler Cardiograms (DCG) using radar faces challenges due to missing data segments. These missing segments can arise from various factors, such as hardware limitations, data transmission issues, and the removal of artifact-contaminated segments. The variability and non-linearity of DCGs, present significant challenges for traditional methods in imputing missing values. In this paper, we introduce DCG-Moment, a fine-tuned Time-series Foundation Model (TSFM) for DCG imputation. Experimental results demonstrate that the DCG-Moment model consistently outperforms traditional interpolation methods and other deep learning models under various conditions of data loss, achieving lower Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and higher Pearson correlation coefficient (CORR). Moreover, it shows significant improvements in Inter-beat Interval (IBI) estimation tasks. This study highlights the potential of applying large-scale pre-trained models to radar signal processing, with the learned representations offering further potential for completing additional DCG analysis tasks.

articleTitle: Lightweight NPU Method Based on Hyper-Threading Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning, the processing power of Neural Processing Unit(NPU) continues to improve. However, this leads to an increasing scale of logical resources for NPU, making it challenging to deploy NPU on Field-Programmable Gate Array(FPGA). To address this issue and enable the deployment of high-computational-power NPU on FPGA, this paper proposes a lightweight NPU method based on hyper-threading technology, considering the characteristics of NPU hardware architecture. This method effectively reduces the logical resources usage of the NPU while ensuring only a minimal decrease in computational power, thus enabling successful FPGA deployment. The overall experiment is based on the Virtex UltraScale+ HBM VCU128 FPGA platform. After testing, it was found that the NPU, previously undeployable, could be successfully deployed after lightweight processing. The resource usage ratio of LUTs decreased by about 10%, and the computational power only decreased by 4%. In other words, by using this method, the scale of logical resource usage of the NPU was effectively reduced while ensuring a minimal decrease in computational power, improving the deployment situation of the NPU on FPGA. This approach has certain reference value and significance for the lightweight design of NPU.

articleTitle: Evaluating the influence of ETAD product for PSI estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (InSAR) technology is widely used for ground deformation monitoring, including infrastructure safety, subsidence, landslides, and earthquakes, due to its all-weather,wide range, and high-precision characteristics. InSAR technology obtains high-resolution and large-scale surface deformation information by comparing the phase differences between two SAR images obtained at different times, and combining sensor parameters and geometric relationships. However, this technology encounters various errors during the processing, including phase decoherence, atmospheric delay phase, phase unwrapping errors, and accuracy issues with digital elevation models (DEM). The Extended Timing Annotation Dataset (ETAD) for Sentinel-1 allows for the correction of range and azimuth timing to account for geophysical effects and inaccuracies in data focusing. In this study, we evaluate the influence of ETAD correction on PSI estimation, specifically on interferogram quality, velocities, and geolocation accuracy. We integrated multiple correction layers in the ETAD data, including tropospheric delay, ionospheric delay, solid earth tidal displacement, bipartite azimuth shift, distance shift caused by Doppler effect, and azimuth shift caused by frequency modulation mismatch. By applying ETAD data to phase correction of Sentinel-1 data, the experimental results showed that the average phase standard deviation of the original interferogram decreased from 1.8747 rad to 1.6917 rad, a reduction of 10.12%. The RMSE of deformation time series improved from 9.8814 mm to 5.8717 mm post-correction, confirming better alignment with GNSS data.The geographic positioning of PS points showed a notable shift towards building locations, enhancing overall positioning accuracy in the PSI process.This indicates that ETAD data has a significant effect on improving the accuracy of Sentinel-1 data processing.

articleTitle: Joint Allocation Of Multi-aircraft Radar Transmit And Maneuvering Resource For Multi-target Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multi-aircraft radar detection often uses preset transmit patterns and flight paths, and detection performance can be dramatically degraded by mismatched irradiation to transmit resource and blind area avoidance of enemy targets. Aiming at this problem, this paper proposed a joint transmit and maneuvering resource allocation method (JTMRA) for multi-aircraft radar tracking multi-target, to achieve high precision detection and tracking of enemy targets. First, we designed a multi-target tracking performance evaluation mechanism based on the Bayesian Cramér-Rao Lower Bound (BCRLB); Secondly, we established a joint optimal allocation model of multi-aircraft radar transmit and maneuvering resource, and analyzed the correlation between the optimized variables and the tracking performance; Finally, the simulation results showed that the method proposed in this paper obtained highly accurate target tracking results with limited resource.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of 3D Reconstruction of Spaceborne Curved SAR Based on FrFT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Curved Spaceborne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) 3D imaging has the advantage of high timeliness and is a hot topic in the field of SAR 3D imaging research. However, current studies do not sufficiently analyze the factors affecting curved SAR 3D reconstruction. Therefore, this paper first derives an analytical model for target reconstruction accuracy based on the discrete fractional Fourier transform (FrFT) and verifies the theoretical correctness through simulations. Secondly, simulations demonstrate the impact of FrFT search step size on reconstruction performance, and finally, the correctness of the theoretical model is proved by vertical surface target simulation.

articleTitle: Communication Modulation Classification based on multi modality feature deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC) is a crucial step before signal analysis in non-cooperative scenarios and an important component of cognitive radio technology. Recently, AMC methods based on Deep Learning (DL) have received increasing attention due to their powerful feature extraction capabilities. However, most existing DL-based methods only consider a single feature as input, without leveraging different attributes of the signal, which limits classification performance. To achieve better classification performance, we propose a cross-domain multimodal scheme for AMC. This scheme sends features from different modalities into a single DL model and controls their effects by multiplying weights. The proposed method divides different modal domains into three groups, including raw data, time domain, and frequency domain. Eight modal features are selected, and an analysis of different modal features is conducted. Finally, we investigate the complementarity between different modal features through extensive simulation experiments, which helps guide how to select feature modal transformations based on the modulation set, thereby effectively extracting knowledge from the received signal.

articleTitle: On the Value of Terrain Classification Using SAR Altimeter Delay Doppler Image
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) altimeter can provide highly accurate terrain data. In complex environments such as mountainous regions, terrain classification can improve data accuracy and reliability. However, classical methods rely on altimetry sequences, which may result in inaccuracies in environments with interference or when there are deviations in the prior Digital Elevation Model (DEM). This paper proposes a terrain classification method using SAR altimeter Delay Doppler Image (DDI). First, we introduce the SAR altimeter echo model, which can be used to generate DDIs. Then, typical terrain factors are selected for initial classification, and a Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-based model is constructed to select the main features, which are then used to choose samples. Finally, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model is trained to achieve classification of DDIs. This process enables precise terrain classification. Experiments using simulation data verify that the proposed method can effectively classify DDIs. This approach has the potential for improving terrain assessment in various applications.

articleTitle: Ziv-Zakai Bound for Wideband Single-Source Direction-of-Arrival Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The Ziv-Zakai bound (ZZB) for wideband Direction- of-Arrival (DOA) estimation of a single source within the subband model is examined. The study involves deriving the regularity condition and determining the minimum error probability, ultimately leading to a closed-form expression of the ZZB. This expression is dependent on several factors: the prior DOA distribution, the number of snapshots, signal wavelength, the quantity of involved subbands, and the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). In scenarios with high SNR or a large number of snapshots, the estimation error decreases, causing the ZZB to approach the well- known Cramér-Rao bound (CRB). Conversely, in the a priori performance region, where the number of snapshots or SNR is low, the estimation error tends to be distributed across the entire prior parameter space, with its boundary approaching the prior covariance. The ZZB theoretically analyzes and derives a tighter bound, providing a more effective reference for the analysis of estimation errors.Simulation results indicate that the ZZB effectively predicts performance across all regions of interest.

articleTitle: UAV Model Recognition Based on Multi-Station Collaborative Multi-Angle Attentional Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Traditional UAV detection and recognition systems rely primarily on a single radar, which can only detect local information from one side of the UAV. The measurement data has limited feature dimensions, and the target characteristics can change with the UAV's orientation, impacting recognition accuracy. This study performs research on UAV model recognition using multi-angle information fusion. It presents a UAV model recognition approach based on multi-station collaborative multi-angle attention feature fusion.
