An innovative multi-dimensional parallel residual convolutional attention neural network architecture is developed to extract critical multi-view properties of the target. In addition, a channel attention method is used for multidimensional feature fusion, allowing UAV recognition via multi-station collaboration. A comparison of single- and multi-station radar recognition was carried out. The results demonstrated that multi-station recognition improved accuracy significantly when compared to single-station recognition, demonstrating the efficacy of multi-station collaborative UAV model recognition.

articleTitle: Physics-aware TomoSAR Reconstruction with Deep-and-Shallow Hybrid Regularizations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Tomographic Synthetic Aperture Radar (TomoSAR) can produce three-dimensional images. Currently, imaging methods based on deep learning achieve high accuracy and efficiency but typically rely on supervised learning, which requires paired data. However, obtaining true scene values and highly reliable simulation data is challenging. To address this issue, this paper aims to achieve TomoSAR reconstruction using physics-aware unsupervised learning with deep-and-shallow hybrid regularizations. The proposed method generally employs the first-order gradient descent optimization algorithm for reconstruction. Here, the embedded proximal mapping steps are fused with both shallow and deep regularizations through the techniques of deep image prior and the plug-and-play denoiser, respectively. The deep regularizations are used in an unsupervised learning manner, with parameters gradually refined to optimal values during reconstruction without supervised learning. The proposed method is validated through both simulation and measured data imaging experiments. Results confirm that it is robust to noise interference while retrieving more scatterers in the scene, providing an alternative way to harness the strengths of deep learning while maintaining a physics-aware process.

articleTitle: Low-Power B5G Communication Technology Based on Digital Beamforming and DOA Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This study explores advancements in Beyond 5G (B5G) communication systems, focusing on improving signal quality, system efficiency, and energy management. We assess the impact of Digital Beamforming (DBF), Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation, and Deep Learning (DL) algorithms across three configurations: without advanced technology, with DBF and DOA, and with DBF, DOA, and DL integration. Numerical simulations confirm that incorporating DL significantly enhances signal integrity and energy efficiency, particularly in long-range scenarios. The proposed DL model achieves competitive performance metrics, with MSE, MAE, and RMSE values all below 0.1, indicating its effectiveness in optimizing spectral and energy efficiency. These findings highlight the potential of DL in real-time beamforming and underscore its role in the future development of B5G networks.

articleTitle: Parametric Concomitant Search Based on IMM-ACT Maneuvering Target Tracking Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The existing Interacting Multiple Model (IMM) algorithm encounters issues such as model switching lag and increased filtering errors when tracking maneuvering targets, particularly in scenarios involving frequent target turns. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an Adaptive Coordinated Turn-Interacting Multiple Model (IMM-ACT) maneuvering target tracking algorithm based on parameter-concomitant search. The algorithm employs a parameter-concomitant randomized search to generate multiple parallel ACT sub-model filters, which adaptively estimate the current target’s turning parameters to form the main model filter in real-time. By effectively covering changes in the target’s motion patterns, the proposed algorithm captures rapid transitions in target motion. Simulation results demonstrate that the IMM-ACT algorithm identifies changes in target motion patterns more quickly and accurately than existing algorithms, thereby significantly improving the accuracy of target tracking.

articleTitle: UAV Spectrum Sensing against SSDF Attacks under Transmission Errors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) spectrum sensing is susceptible to Spectrum Sensing Data Falsification (SSDF) attacks, which pose a threat to its data security. However, most existing SSDF defense strategies overlook transmission errors between secondary users (SUs) and fusion center (FC). Hence, this study introduces a reputation-based defense method against SSDF attacks for UAV spectrum sensing, accounting for potential transmission errors between UAVs and FC. Based on the probability of each UAV reporting correct sensing results, we assign a reputation value to each UAV and exclude those with a value lower than or equal to the threshold from participating in collaborative spectrum sensing. To enhance precision, we calculate the individual detection probability for each UAV. By evaluating performance under the same sensing environment and considering transmission errors, we compared our method with an error-free SSDF defense approach that ignores these errors. Simulation results confirm that calculating the individual detection probability yields more precise results, and our proposed method is more effective in distinguishing legitimate users.

articleTitle: Human Action Recognition Using Dual-Stream Neural Networks with FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper presents a approach to human action recognition utilizing FMCW radar. We propose a method that extracts range-time and velocity-time features from radar echoes and processes them using a dual-stream neural network for action classification. The improved Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) detection algorithm, combined with a Shape Profile Constraint - Feature Map (SPC-FM) generation method, significantly enhances feature extraction by removing noise. Experimental results demonstrate an average classification accuracy of 96.4% across six common actions, showcasing the method’s robustness for applications in various domains, including medical monitoring and autonomous vehicle systems.

articleTitle: A Least-Squares-Based Algorithm for Estimating ATI SAR Interferometric Phase Errors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: ATI SAR systems have immense potential for high-resolution, wide-swath measurements of sea surface currents. However, due to the sensitivity of ATI interferometric phase to phase errors, the retrieval of sea surface currents using ATI technology often relies on ground scene calibration. To address this issue, we first review the principles of ATI SAR sea surface current measurement and analyze the sources and characteristics of phase errors. Based on this analysis, we propose a least-squares-based method for estimating and compensating ATI SAR phase errors. This method ensures robust estimation and correction of phase errors by accounting for their distinct distribution characteristics. Finally, we validate the proposed method using data from the PIESAT-1 satellite constellation, demonstrating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research and Design of a Lower Limb Rehabilitation Exoskeleton Robot Driven by Cables
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the development of science and technology and economic society, research on postoperative rehabilitation of lower limb fractures continues to deepen, and postoperative rehabilitation products are emerging one after another. However, traditional postoperative rehabilitation products for lower limb fractures have problems such as single function, low control precision, and bulky structure. At the same time, research on exoskeleton robots in the field of postoperative rehabilitation for fractures is not in-depth. Based on existing exoskeleton robots and driving methods, this paper designs a lower limb fracture postoperative rehabilitation exoskeleton robot that can provide axial mechanical stimulation and assistive torque. The design adopts the driving method of cable driving, and through the unique design of the coupled movable pulley group, it realizes the combination of two working modes, making the exoskeleton capable of providing axial mechanical stimulation and knee joint assistive torque. Finally, the axial load characteristics and torque characteristics of the exoskeleton device were verified by 3D printing prototype, meeting the requirements of perfect working mode and precise control system.

articleTitle: A Parameter-Optimized Random Forest Method for CSI based Passive Indoor Occupancy Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper examines the question of the passive indoor occupancy detection based on channel state information (CSI) data. At the outset, we propose an antenna averaging and dividing (AAD) method for boosting the quality of CSI data obtained from commercial Wi-Fi devices. Then, utilizing the preprocessed data as the input, the prediction classification is carried out using a Random Forest (RF) model, employing the Bitterling Fish Optimization (BFO) method to optimize the RF parameters. Furthermore, a window-based statistical method is proposed to further enhance the prediction accuracy. Finally, we construct a CSI acquisition platform that utilizes a desktop computer equipped with an Intel 5300 NIC and a TP-LINK router; experimental results assess the dependability of the proposed algorithm using the dataset of Track 1 of Huawei Cloud’s First Wi-Fi Perception Contest.

articleTitle: Off-Grid DOA Estimation for Block Orthogonal Matching Pursuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation problem with multiple incident signals and multiple snapshots, an off-grid Block Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OG-BOMP) algorithm is proposed to address the performance instability of the Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) algorithm. Under multiple snapshots conditions, the vectors of signal sources to be estimated from different snapshots exhibit joint sparsity. By converting the multiple measurement vectors (MMV) model into a block single measurement vector (SMV) model, this joint sparsity can be fully exploited. After further considering off-grid errors, more accurate off-grid parameters are obtained, leading to more precise estimation results. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves estimation accuracy compared to traditional OMP and BOMP algorithms under multiple snapshots and exhibits strong multi-target resolution capability.

articleTitle: Monitoring Deformation of Elevated Transport Infrastructure Using InSAR and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Time Series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (TS-InSAR) technique has been widely applied in earth observation field. However, there are still challenges in the fine monitoring and interpretation of long-distance, wide-span urban elevated transport infrastructures. In this study, we present a case study on the Shanghai maglev, where we mosaicked InSAR time series by jointly estimating orbital errors across two frames of TerraSAR-X images. This approach enabled us to obtain extensive, long-term InSAR observations along the track. Additionally, we used deep learning methods to cluster the observed deformation patterns. The cluster results were then interpreted with structural knowledge and environmental factors, demonstrating that deep clustering on TS-InSAR analyses can enhance monitoring efficiency and automation. This data-driven post-processing approach offers a new solution to using TS-InSAR analyses in urban infrastructure monitoring.

articleTitle: A Reconstructed Shape Model of Asteroid (367789) 2011 AG5
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Asteroid (367789) 2011 AG5 is one of the most elongated near-Earth objects identified, with a length-to-width ratio of approximately 3.625, classifying it as a "Potentially Hazardous Asteroid." Using the latest 2023 Goldstone radar delay-Doppler observations, we developed a rough shape model of 2011 AG5. This model reveals an elongated, bar-like structure that can be approximated as two touching ellipsoids, one of which exhibits a large, wide indentation. A comparison between the reconstructed shape model and the Goldstone radar images shows a close match in contour features and a strong correlation in the asteroid's rotational orientation as observed in the radar time-sequenced images.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv8n for Concealed Object Detection in Human Body Millimeter Wave Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper, which builds upon the fundamental YOLOv8n architecture, adds the CAFM module to the neck network with the goal of improving detection accuracy and increasing sensitivity of the model to objects in millimeter wave images. This addresses the issue of insufficient detection in millimeter wave images that arises from the difficulty of extracting features of concealed objects. Subsequently, Inner-CIoU is employed as the loss function for bounding box regression, which aims to speed up the convergence of the model. According to experiments, the enhanced YOLOv8n model considerably raises mAP when compared to the baseline model.

articleTitle: Image Editing based on Diffusion Model for Remote Sensing Image Change Captioning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Remote Sensing Image Change Captioning (RSICC) is a task that utilizes natural language to describe changes in remote sensing images of the same area captured at different times. However, the significant temporal intervals between multi-temporal images, the infrequency of observable changes, and the limitations on observation locations make it difficult to acquire and annotate a large and diverse dataset for analyzing change in multi-temporal images. The scarcity of labeled data hinders the training of RSICC models, leading to poor generalization. Compared to annotated registered bi-temporal image, single-temporal data is easier to obtain. Therefore, to tackle the issue of poor generalization of RSICC models under limited annotated sample conditions, a text-guided image pairs generation (TGIPG) method is proposed to create synthetic RSICC datasets from single-temporal data and randomly sampled text instructions via a diffusion-based controllable image editing model. This approach generates more valid pairs of multi-temporal samples to address the constraints of limited change information. Specifically, this method utilizes language instructions to introduce change information into the diffusion process, gradually transforming the pre-phase image into the post-phase image. Our experiments on the LEVIR-CC dataset show that synthetic data can significantly enhance the performance of any RSICC model, with a restricted number of training samples, by employing this plug-and-play TGIPG method.

articleTitle: Pseudo-Centroid Representation Learning for Cross-domain Few-shot Classification from Remote Sensing Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Cross-domain few-shot classification is gaining significant attention due to its potential to address challenges in remote sensing applications, such as large domain gaps and limited labeled data. Recent approaches have explored leveraging unlabeled target domain data for semi-supervised learning, in addition to source labeled data, to improve cross-domain training. However, these techniques often struggle with getting discriminative representation for distinguishing categories in novel target domains, particularly when facing new categories and limited training examples. To overcome these issues, we propose a novel cross-domain pseudo-centroid representation (CDPCR) framework, designed to generate more discriminative and adaptable class representations for improved cross-domain learning. The framework consists of a semi-supervised cross-domain structure that integrates both source labeled data and a portion of target unlabeled data to establish the relationship between domains. A consistency regularization branch is introduced to stabilize model outputs by aligning predictions on the target unlabeled data under input perturbations. Additionally, a pseudo-centroid contrastive representation learning module is incorporated to enhance intra-category feature consistency while improving the separability of inter-category representations, aiding the model in adapting to classification tasks across diverse domains. The effectiveness of the proposed CDPCR framework is validated through comprehensive experiments conducted across 8 cross-domain scenarios using remote sensing scene classification datasets.

articleTitle: Estimation of Insect Morphological Parameters Based on Single-Frequency Echo Intensity-Independent Estimators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Estimating the morphological parameters of insects, such as mass and length, is crucial for accurate species identification. Traditional entomological radars employ absolute radar cross-section (RCS) estimators to determine these parameters. However, when radars lack angle measurement capabilities, these absolute RCS estimators can underestimate the parameters if insects are not in the beam center. To address this challenge, a method using two single-frequency echo intensity-independent estimators (EIIE) was proposed, but it could only estimate the mass of insects below 200 mg with limited accuracy. This study explores the feasibility of using additional single-frequency EIIEs to estimate the morphological parameters of insects up to 1000 mg. An analysis was performed to examine the relationship between four EIIEs at X-band (9.4 GHz) and the mass and length of 159 insects in an anechoic chamber. The results revealed significant correlations between these EIIEs and the insects' morphological parameters. Subsequently, morphological parameter estimation was achieved by establishing the mappings from four EIIEs to mass and length using random forest algorithm. The findings indicate that this method is effective for insects up to 1000 mg, with mean relative errors of 14.38% for mass and 9.96% for length.

articleTitle: Fundus Image Generation Based on Generative Adversarial Networks with Dual Discriminators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Generative adversarial networks for fundus image generation can address the scarcity of fundus images, reduce preparation costs, and protect patient privacy. Existing methods for generating adversarial networks often have drawbacks, such as unrealistic local details, unclear resolution, and reliance on conditional inputs like blood vessel annotations. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a generative adversarial network with dual discriminators that generate fundus images from random noise. This network consists of a generator and two distinct discriminators that consider both the global features and local details of fundus images. Extensive experiments validate the proposed method. The inception score, Fréchet Inception Distance, and Kernel Inception Distance achieved by our method are 1.882, 80.52, and 0.0681, respectively. These results indicate that our method can generate fundus images with diverse, realistic, and clear local details, as well as high overall quality.

articleTitle: Preliminary Result of Multi-plane Interferometry Topography Measurement with UAV InSAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) is a highly effective tool for mapping topography and detecting subtle ground deformations. Topographic information is essential in both imaging and interferometric processing, especially for UAV InSAR. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach called multi-plane interferometry, which leverages double-pass interferometry data to extract additional topographic information, thereby facilitating subsequent imaging and interferometric processing. When applied to unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) InSAR, the proposed method shows promising performance on actual datasets, highlighting its effectiveness and potential for broader applications.

articleTitle: Phase unwrapping in DOA estimation via on the least squares of the nearest projection point
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The phase interferometer offers a number of advantages, including a simple structure, high direction-finding performance and low computational complexity. As a result, it has become a popular technique for Passive Direction Finding. However, the phase interferometer is significantly affected by phase measurement error, which can easily lead to phase ambiguity when the minimum element spacing exceeds half a wavelength. For this, we propose an enhanced least squares nearest projection point (LS-NPP) phase unwrapping algorithm. By fitting multiple snapshots of phase-difference points using the least squares method, and then utilizing the wrapped phase-difference pattern (WPDP) to identify the nearest phase projection point to the fitted phase point, the ambiguity number is obtained, thereby achieving phase unwrapping. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm exhibits a higher probability of correct phase unwrapping under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions.

articleTitle: Long-distance detection method of the high-speed target under distance ambiguity based on DP-RFT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In recent years, high-speed aircraft technology has made huge development and been applied to various fields, which is a significant challenge for radar warning systems. High-speed targets move quickly, requiring the early long-distance detection. Additionally, the "plasma sheath" effect provides these aircraft with an ability of stealth, resulting that the radar cross-section (RCS) is only 0.02m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 0.5m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Aiming at the need of early detection for long-distance targets, this paper uses a narrowband stepped-frequency pulse system with high pulse repetition frequency (PRF) to enhance radar detection ability. To solve the problem of step frequency synthesis distortion caused by the high speed of the target, a parameter estimation method of moving target based on DP-RFT is proposed. Then, aiming at the range ambiguity problem at high PRF, a range ambiguity suppression method based on the frequency switching is proposed. This method can realize long-distance detection of the high-speed target without range ambiguity.

articleTitle: Fast Moving Target Focusing with FDMA Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper deal with the challenge of focusing on fast-moving targets in a frequency division multiple access (FD-MA) radar system. At the modeling stage, the linear frequency modulation (LFM) waveform is transmitted by introducing a frequency increment (at least equal to the bandwidth) across the transmit array elements. The received signals are subsequently processed by a filter bank to separate the transmitted waveforms, which in turn provides additional degrees of freedom in the range domain. Particularly, a compensation procedure is designed to eliminate the incoherence between echos between different transmit element due to frequency diversity. To this end, as the outputs of different matched filters become coherent in the spatial domain, the keystone transform (KT) operation is employed to correct the range walk caused by the fast movement of the target, making it possible to focus the target in the space-time-range domain. Furthermore, the angle of the target is estimated and further utilized for beamforming, enhancing the range resolution. Numerical results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in focusing the fast moving target with a FDMA radar.

articleTitle: A High-precision Range Estimation Method for FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper presents a signal processing algorithm for FMCW radar. An improved CZT distance estimation method based on spectrum interpolation factor of Rife algorithm is proposed. By using the result of the Rife algorithm to determine the spectrum refinement range of CZT, the range of spectrum refinement is further reduced and higher precision of target range estimation can be achieved. The simulation results show that the proposed method has good anti-noise performance, and the average ranging accuracy is nearly doubled compared with the original CZT estimation method.

articleTitle: Correction of Sampling Time Jitter for Stepped-Frequency Radar by Minimizing Entropy of Range Profile
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: There is a sampling time jitter in the stepped frequency radar system, which leads to phase discontinuities during the synthesis of a wideband spectrum, resulting in grating lobes of range profile. This paper derives the gradient of entropy with respect to the phase error coefficient by minimizing the entropy of the range profiles, and iteratively solves for the distribution of phase error in each sub-band. Subsequently, a linear regression method is used to more accurately estimate the error in each sub-band, and then to correct it. Finally, simulation results demonstrated the algorithm’s effectiveness by comparing the entropy of images before and after correction.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Hyperspectral Image Blind Super-Resolution via a Kernel Prior Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Hyperspectral images typically suffer from low resolution due to inherent hardware constraints, complicating downstream tasks like detection, classification, and recognition. In our study, we introduce a kernel prior network (KPNet) designed to address the the hyperspectral image (HSI) blind super-resolution (BSR) challenge in an unsupervised fashion. Double-DIP, comprising two deep image priors (DIP), enables the simultaneous reconstruction of high-dimensional spectral data and kernel estimates via an untrained encoder-decoder network configuration in the parameter space. The KPNet creates a reversible connection between complex blur kernel distributions and simple hidden variable distributions. In addition, the proposed DIP can also estimate reliable blur kernels, which can be integrated into existing blind super-resolution techniques. Comprehensive experiments conducted on standard datasets demonstrate that our proposed approach markedly surpasses current techniques in performance.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Optimization of Missile-borne Synthetic Aperture Radar Target Echo Simulation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper proposes a system architecture of missile-borne SAR echo simulation based on GPU+FPGA for the problem of SAR trajectory not being accurately predicted. The real-time and distance accuracy involved in the system are demonstrated, the method of large-capacity data signal processing based on GPU and a refined delay modulation based on FPGA is proposed, and relevant simulation experiments are performed to verify the effectiveness and rationality.

articleTitle: Improved Boreal Forest Height Estimation by Fusion of TanDEM-X InSAR and ICESat-2 Data Based on Sub-aperture Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: TanDEM-X twin-satellite interferometric system is widely used to estimate forest height. However, TanDEM-X acquires single-polarization data in standard mode, which makes it difficult to provide sufficient observation information to support the Random Volume over Ground (RVoG) model invertible. To overcome these problems, this paper proposes a boreal forest height estimation framework based on sub-aperture decomposition, which extracts the surface phase through time-frequency analysis and realizes the wall-to-wall extinction coefficient acquisition driven by Ice, Cloud, and land Elevation Satellite-2 (ICESat-2) canopy height. Specifically, we explored three strategies: 1) TanDEM-X coherence alone; 2) TanDEM-X complex coherence + surface phase; 3) TanDEM-X complex coherence + surface phase + ICESat-2 canopy height. We then tested and validated the results in a Spanish boreal forest test area. The validation results with airborne LiDAR forest height showed that the TanDEM-X forest height inversion performance can be effectively improved by providing the surface phase through sub-aperture decomposition. The third strategy achieved the best consistency by further providing the extinction coefficient of the RVoG model, which improved the forest height estimation accuracy from 4.39 m (Strategy 1) to 2.42 m at 30 [m] spatial resolution.

articleTitle: 2D Resolution Coherent Enhancement of Distributed Spaceborne SAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Distributed spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can discern the intricate details of target structures and precisely characterize them. It uniquely excels in fields like ultra-high-resolution imaging, multi-view coherent fusion, moving target detection, and target recognition. This paper investigates the coherent enhancement of the two-dimensional resolution of SAR in both azimuth and range under distributed spaceborne platforms. In the multi-sub-band distribution pattern of overlapping frequency spectra along the range direction, the joint channel error from overlapping frequency bands is employed to estimate and compensate for inter-sub-band errors, and the bandwidth is synthesized to enhance range resolution coherently. Subsequently, for multi-aperture distribution patterns with azimuthal gaps, a method based on compressive sensing is proposed for sparse recovery of the gap data. This approach effectively elevates azimuth resolution and suppresses spurious targets in the azimuth direction.

articleTitle: Correction Method for Digital Beamforming in the Range-Doppler Domain for Tandem Bistatic SAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper investigates a correction method for digital beamforming (DBF) based on tandem bistatic Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR). Due to its unique geometric configuration and electromagnetic characteristics, the tandem bistatic SAR system offers significant advantages in enhancing resolution and target recognition capabilities. However, traditional DBF techniques encounter performance limitations when processing elevation-direction signals in tandem bistatic SAR systems. To address this issue, the paper first analyzes the imaging principles and characteristics of the tandem bistatic SAR system, and then establishes a linear approximation model for the relationship between point target azimuth angles and transmitter-receiver distances, providing a theoretical foundation for DBF correction. A range-Doppler domain DBF processing method is introduced to enhance elevation-direction signal processing performance. Simulation experiments confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: UAV Localization in Non-Line-of-Sight Building Aera Using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In modern urban scenarios, UAVs have become essential platforms for reconnaissance and surveillance due to their high mobility. However, building obstructions can cause UAVs to enter non-line-of-sight (NLOS) areas behind building corners, potentially endangering urban safety. The existing localization algorithms cannot accurately localize the target position, especially in the absence of building layout information. To address this issue, this paper proposes a ghost-matching localization method based on genetic algorithm, incorporating multipath propagation mechanisms such as diffraction and reflection of electromagnetic waves within buildings. The ghost positions of the target are first obtained using conventional Back Projection (BP) imaging. Subsequently, an objective function incorporating the unknown street width is established based on the geometric relationship between the target position and the ghost positions. This objective function is then optimized using genetic algorithm to estimate both the target location and street width. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately locate the target position without prior building layout information, validating the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: A Squint Imaging Algorithm for the Multireceiver SAS with High Mapping Rate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In squint multireceiver synthetic aperture sonar (SAS), the platform moves continuously along the azimuth direction during the interpulse and intrapulse. The intrapulse motion results in Doppler scale effect (DSE) of the echo signal, and the squint angle will exacerbate this effect. Considering the intrapulse motion of the sonar platform, we derived the time-varying time delay and range history, and established a Doppler scale signal model for squint multireceiver SAS. Utilizing the shear theorem of two-dimensional Fourier transformation, the two-dimensional spectrum of the echo signal was derived. Finally, we proposed an algorithm to correct the DSE in the squint multireceiver SAS, and its effectiveness was tested by the simulation experiment.

articleTitle: Aerial target positioning method based on distributed node hybrid measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In actual detection scenarios, receiving stations are a very valuable sensing resource. Given the number of receiving stations, it is desired to achieve the highest possible positioning accuracy. To this end, we conducted research on a three-node hybrid target localization method using a combination of multiple measurement methods. Firstly, by using the spatial geometric relationship between the distributed node network configuration and the target, the measurement models of the target receiving cone angle DOA, time difference of arrival TDOA, and frequency difference of arrival FDOA were established. Secondly, the LS problem about the reference distance and target X-coordinate estimation is established by using DOA measurement and TDOA measurement, and then FDOA measurement is used to assist in improving the accuracy of parameter estimation; Finally, TDOA measurement is used to construct a pseudo-linear equation group to estimate the Y and Z coordinates of the target, and the WLS method is used to locate the target. This method effectively utilizes mixed measurement information and reduces the number of required DOA measurements. Target positioning can be completed with only three receiving stations, which reduces system costs and has broad application prospects.

articleTitle: Frequency Agile Waveform Design and Coherent Processing for High-speed Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Frequency agile waveform has excellent interception and interference immunity for radar. However, the agile frequency introduces jitter initial phase and agile Doppler, which results in a non-coherent echo signal, making it difficult for the target to obtain a high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain. In addition, the range cell migration (RCM) correction is also a problem in frequency agile radar for high-speed target detection. In this article, a frequency agile waveform with the same frequency set in each group and a novel processing method is proposed for high-speed target detection. The first pulse with same carrier frequency in each group can be used to estimate the coarse velocity via the keystone (KT) algorithm. Thus, the RCM correction in a coherent processing interval (CPI) can be realized with the estimated velocity. Then, the agile initial phases can be mutually canceled by the same-frequency signals. Finally, the coherent accumulation after cancellation can be realized by the non-uniform discrete Fourier transform (NDFT). Simulation experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed waveform and processing method for high-speed target detection.

articleTitle: Scintillation Parameter Measurement via Amplitude Stripes in SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The scintillation stripes have been frequently captured in numerous acquisitions of the Advanced Land Observing Satellite (ALOS) Phased Array-type L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (PALSAR). Even though the amplitude stripes can impede the SAR imaging and interferometric applications, the amplitude stripes can be beneficial for EPB sounding. In this study, a methodology that extracting the amplitude stripe pattern via normalized sub-band processsing and orientational filtering (NSB-OF) to measure the ionospheric scintillation parameters is proposed. First, a sub-band analysis is performed to suppress the ground scatter and sharpen the amplitude stripes. Second, the amplitude stripe is extracted in the NSB image through a band-rejection OF. Finally, the scintillation parameters, including scintillation strength C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>L and spectrum index p are estimated. Another scintillation index S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> is then indirectly derived by the estimated C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>L and p. The proposed methodology is applied to a group of PALSAR images with amplitude stripes and validated with the indirectly and directly measured S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>. The results demonstrate that the NSB process has a high efficiency for the extraction of stripe pattern and measurements of scintillation parameters.

articleTitle: SEGLCT: An Efficient Time Frequency Analyse Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To solve the problems of cross term interference, low resolution, and unsatisfactory noise suppression ability in existing time-frequency analyses(TFA) methods, this paper proposes an effective TFA method — Synchro-extracting transform generalized linear Chirplet transform(SEGLCT). Firstly, this method performs Synchro-extracting transform (SET) on the input signal to obtain a Synchro-extracting operator (SEO); Secondly, the generalized linear Chirplet transform (GLCT) is used to perform TFA on the input signal and obtain coarse TFA results. Then, a SEO is used to construct a filtering matrix and perform filtering cancellation on the coarse TFA results. Finally, the optimized TFA results can be obtained. This method fully integrates the advantages of SET and GLCT, and has high time-frequency clustering and noise stability. The experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-DSP Joint SAR Real-Time Imaging System Based on PFA Sub-Aperture Imaging Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The Synthetic Aperture Radar(SAR) real-time imaging system designed with multi-DSP architecture has been widely used in both airborne and satellite platforms. In the context of real-time imaging systems, Polar Format Algorithm(PFA) fall short of meeting the system’s real-time demands. This paper proposes a multi DSP architecture SAR imaging system based on sub-aperture PFA to meet the real-time imaging requirements. The system utilizes multiple sub-aperture echo data to design a "2+1" DSP C6678 hardware architecture, and implements the sub aperture PFA algorithm in parallel on the hardware to improve imaging efficiency. Furthermore, we performed phase gradient autofocus processing on the imaging results and achieved high-resolution images. The experimental results show that compared with traditional PFA, the proposed sub aperture PFA algorithm and hardware architecture reduce imaging time by 54%.

articleTitle: An Improved Method for Designing MTD Filter Coefficients Based on Second-Order Cone Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To improve the convergence performance of filter coefficient solving processes, align the filter frequency response curve more closely with the desired frequency response curve, and enhance the robustness of the filter coefficient solving method, this paper proposes an improved MTD filter coefficient solving method based on second-order cone programming. This method can achieve a filter frequency response that closely aligns with the desired frequency response. The effectiveness of the method is verified through simulation experiments and actual measured data.

articleTitle: MDFNet: Multimodal Feature Decomposition and Fusion Network for Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The semantic segmentation of multimodal remote sensing (RS) images, utilizing optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data, has raised attention in recent studies. Advanced studies adaptively modeled and fused modality-share and modality-specific information beneficial for segmentation and achieved competitive performance. However, in challenging scenarios such as low image contrast or blurred textures in optical images and speckle noises or foreshortening in SAR images, modality-specific information may lost. This study proposed a multimodal feature decomposition and fusion network (MDFNet) designed for multimodal RS image semantic segmentation using optical and SAR images. By decomposing multimodal features into modality-share and modality-difference features and applying gradient descent on modality-difference features, modality-specific information beneficial for segmentation can be retained. Specifically, we designed a MDF decoder with MDF blocks. MDF block maps multimodal features into the same feature space and calculates the difference of multimodal features to obtain modality-share and modality-difference features respectively, then fuses these features. MDF decoder optimizes modality-difference features by gradient descent using adaptive modeling, thereby retaining modality-specific information that is beneficial for segmentation. Comprehensive experiments conducted on the DFC20 dataset demonstrated that the proposed MDFNet surpasses representative methods.

Author Keywords: multimodal remote sensing image semantic segmentation

articleTitle: A New Multi-modal Dataset and Two-stage DNN Approach for Acute Ischemic Stroke Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multi-modal data play an essential role in medical diagnostics, in particular for the detection of acute ischemic stroke (AIS). However, existing methods for AIS detection focus on single-modality learning, neglecting the advantages of integrating multiple modalities as well as lacking multi-modal database. In this paper, we introduce a novel multi-modal dataset consisting of 80 cases with 5 medical modalities and propose a two-stage deep neural network (DNN) framework designed for AIS detection. The proposed framework includes two subnet: A lesion localization subnet for the preliminary identification of potential lesion regions, and a stroke segmentation subnet for the precise delineation of stroke areas. Additionally, we incorporate a Transformer-based multi-modal fusion module that effectively learns cross-attention between different modalities. The proposed method is evaluated on our newly established multi-modal dataset, and experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves the state-of-the-art performance for AIS detection.

articleTitle: Blood Glucose Control Based on Hybrid Neural Network and Optimized PID Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Type-1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is a challenging disorder that requires keeping blood glucose (BG) levels in the euglycemic range for healthy living. To achieve this, we proposed a BG regulation method that integrates a composite neural network glucose prediction model with an optimized proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control algorithm. Firstly, the hybrid neural network model utilizes convolutional neural networks (CNN) and Transformer architecture which enables accurate predictions of future BG trends. Secondly, the PID control algorithm is developed using a particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm with standard PID control to set optimum parameters. For validation, in silico experiments have been conducted on ten virtual patients for a 36-hour scenario of the UVA/Padova metabolic simulator. The results revealed an enhancement in BG management. The obtained BG concentration (BGC) values were found in the euglycemic range for 91.5% of the time. Moreover, the BGC values were above 180 mg/dl for 3.8% of the time, the high BG index (HBGI) was found at 1.2 and the blood glucose risk index (BGRI) was also found at 2.5.

articleTitle: An Improved Range-Doppler Algorithm In High Squint Spaceborne SAR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The main challenge faced by spaceborne SAR imaging in high squint case is the severe range-azimuth coupling caused by variation of azimuth frequency with slant range, which makes it difficult for original side-looking SAR imaging algorithms to be directly applied to high squint SAR imaging. To address this issue, this paper introduces a spaceborne high squint SAR imaging technique utilizing Range-Doppler algorithm. The relationship of the Doppler centroid with range is calculated accurately to effectively solve the problems of the asymmetric range compression sidelobes and poor edge target focusing in high squint SAR imaging, by improving the secondary range compression technique. Through simulation experiments, it was confirmed that the presented method can considerably enhance spaceborne high squint SAR imaging quality.

articleTitle: SW-Former: Refined Transformer Models for Multi-Temporal PolSAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multi-temporal PolSAR data contains dynamic change information of surface targets over time. The increase in multi-temporal features adds pressure to represent temporal-polarimetric relationships. Therefore, some researchers prefer using Transformer model to handle these complex relationships. However, the native Transformer typically treats all Polarimetric features at a single time step as a token, and part of its structure is not suitable for multi-temporal PolSAR data tasks. To address this, we introduce an improved Transformer model called the Sliding Window Temporal-Polarimetric Transformer (SW-Former). In this model, sequences with the same polarimetric features in all time steps are treated as a token. Sliding window embedding is used to divide each token into equal-length patches. This extends the data volume and captures the inter-temporal semantic information that is not available in the native structure. Additionally, the native self-attention is replaced with a Temporal-Polarimetric Attention, which focuses on effective information from both the temporal and polarimetric dimensions. To prove the effectiveness of the proposed method, two datasets are considered in the experiments. Compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) methodologies, the classification performance in terms of overall accuracy (OA) can be improved by about 1.59% and 1.41% respectively, which proves the superiority of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Contactless Material Identification Based on Millimeter-wave Radar and Residual Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Material identification of objects has significant applications in industrial automation and smart homes. However, existing material recognition systems often suffer from low accuracy, high cost, or inconvenience. In this paper, we propose a contactless material identification method based on millimeter-wave radar and residual network. The method firstly utilizes a speaker to excite the micro-vibrations of the target object, and captures the radar echo data of the target through the millimeter-wave radar. By analyzing the phase variations in the reflected signals, we capture the micro-vibration characteristics of the object. After feature extraction, we construct a residual network model, which can enable high-precision material recognition. We evaluate our system through experiments on different objects of four common materials. The experimental results show that our method achieves a high recognition accuracy of 99.3%. Compared with traditional material recognition techniques, our approach has significant advantages in terms of non-destructive detection, low cost and low power consumption. Moreover, the method maintains accurate recognition even when the surface of the target is covered by plastic film or paint.

articleTitle: Deformer-FPN: FPN network based on deformable convolution and lightweight upsampling operator for ship detection in SAR image
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper proposes a Deformer-FPN target detection network based on the minimum model size yolov5-v7 (yolov5s) for detecting ships of different scales in SAR images. Due to the varied size of the ship and the different resolution of the image, ships exist in a multi-scale space in the SAR image. To address this issue, we enhance the feature extraction of the target in complex backgrounds and improve the adaptability to ship size. Firstly, we incorporate the latest deformable convolutional DCNv3 into the input part of the existing Feature Pyramid Network (FPN, a neural network architecture). This integration enhances feature extraction in complex backgrounds and improves adaptability to ship size. Additionally, we introduce an additional small-size feature reinforcement branch to further strengthen the extraction of small-size targets. Secondly, we introduce a lightweight general-purpose upsampling operator (CARAFE) to capture global spatial semantic information of ship features, addressing the limitation of nearest neighbor upsampling that only considers adjacent pixels. Experimental results on the SAR ship detection open source dataset (SSD) demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The Yolov5s+Deformer-FPN detection algorithm achieves an average accuracy of 91.89% and a recall rate of 92.47%. The experimental code reference is as follows: https://github.com/Maple1024/Deformer-FPN.git

articleTitle: ISAR-Diff: A High-Resolution ISAR Imaging Method Based on Conditional Diffusion Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and incomplete echoes, the performance of inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging tends to degrade rapidly. To address this issue, this paper proposes a high-resolution ISAR imaging method based on a conditional diffusion model, dubbed as ISAR-Diff. Specifically, an ISAR imaging diffusion model is trained. Then, the complex-valued ISAR image is then inferred using the diffusion model with a guidance function, conditional on complex-valued echoes. In particular, an ISAR imaging guidance function is designed to make ISAR-Diff applicable to different scenarios and to improve the reconstruction accuracy. Experimental results based on Monte Carlo simulation and measured data demonstrate the superiority of ISAR-Diff in low SNR and incomplete echo scenarios.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler Shift Compensation for Ballistic Targets Based on Residual Network ResNet50
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: During the mid-flight of a ballistic target, there are two types of motions: high-speed translational motion and micro-motion. Since the translational motion causes the Doppler curve to be shifted and tilted, the translational component needs to be compensated. In this paper, a new micro-Doppler shift compensation method for ballistic targets based on Residual Network ResNet50 is proposed. The micro-Doppler compensation is converted into a regression analysis of radial motion parameters, and the regression analysis is carried out using ResNet50. According to the results of simulation experiments, the algorithm can realize the compensation of translational components.

articleTitle: A Ship Target Calibration Method Based on GRFT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Calibration is a key technology in ISAR (Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar) processing. Traditional calibration techniques are typically aimed at uniformly oscillating targets. However, for sea surface moving targets, their oscillation exhibits significant sinusoidal characteristics, reducing the performance of traditional algorithms. To address this issue, this paper proposes a GRFT-based (Generalized Radon-Fourier Transform) calibration method for sea surface ships. Based on the construction of the ship's echo model, the relationship between the motion parameters and the calibration-required angular parameters is established. The PSO-GRFT-CLEAN (Particle Swarm Optimization, PSO) algorithm is then used to estimate the motion parameters of the two sub-apertures, completing the calibration of the ISAR image. Simulations on ship models demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Slow-moving Target Detection Method with FDA-MIMO Radar Based on Doppler-spreading Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: It is difficult to distinguish the Doppler frequency between clutter and slow-moving targets when airborne radar is looking down, which makes it difficult to perform detection. To solve this problem, an frequency diverse array multiple-input multiple-output (FDA-MIMO) radar slow-moving target detection method Doppler-spreading (DS) effect is proposed in this paper. FDA-MIMO radar clutter and ground moving target signal models are established. Using DS effect, clutter and slow-moving targets are separated in the Doppler domain, and then clutter suppression and target detection are effective. Simulation results confirm the efficacy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of Bistatic Radar for Target Location Based on Conditional Entropy Lower Bound
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: As a new kind of detection technology, bistatic radar has attracted more and more attention. The target location accuracy depends on the topology configuration of bistatic radar. To improve the target location accuracy, it is necessary to optimize the configuration of the bistatic radar system. In this paper, a method for optimal configuration of bistatic radar system based on the conditional entropy lower bound (LB) of bistatic radar is proposed. Firstly, the conditional entropy and its LB of the target position estimate in given bistatic radar system’s polar observations are deduced theoretically. Then, the optimal topology configuration of bistatic radar is obtained by minimizing the conditional entropy LB. Finally, the effectiveness of this method is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Improved CLEAN-AP for Dual-Polarization Alternating Transmission Weather Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Weather radar has become an indispensable tool for modern meteorological services around the world. The quality of radar data is related to the performance of various meteorological applications such as disastrous weather detection, precipitation estimation, and weather forecast. However, the existence of ground clutter will affect the quality of radar data. Ground clutter usually exists in low-elevation and / or close-range radar observations, which seriously affects the measurement of meteorological parameters such as power, speed, spectrum width and polarization parameters. Removing the influence of ground clutter can measure weather phenomena more accurately, so as to improve the performance of radar in meteorological applications. This paper introduces an adaptive filter based on autocorrelation spectral density, which can suppress the adverse effects of ground clutter without reducing the quality of meteorological data. The clutter environment analysis adaptive processing (CLEAN-AP) filter can adjust its suppression characteristics in real time to match the dynamic atmospheric environment and meet the suppression requirements of near space airshipborne typhoon radar. In the alternating polarization (AHV) mode, CLEAN-AP is affected by the coupling of phidp under the velocity estimation, and an improved scheme for AHV weather radar is proposed.

articleTitle: Hybrid RIS-Enabled Individual Channel Estimation for MIMO Systems Using Efficient Decoupled Atomic Norm Minimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication systems, the reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) has been recognized as one of the key technologies to enhance system performance. This paper introduces a hybrid RIS architecture integrated with dynamically controllable active elements, which reduces the cost of RIS deployment. Based on this architecture and the sparsity characteristic of millimeter-wave channels, we propose an atomic norm minimization (ANM)-based method for individual channel estimation. This method maximizes the decoupling of high-dimensional coupled parameters, further reducing the computational complexity of estimating for individual channels while ensuring estimation performance. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed method not only achieves higher estimation performance but also exhibits a significant advantage in computational time compared to orthogonal matching pursuit.

articleTitle: Modified Probabilistic 2 Satisfiability Reverse Analysis via Ensemble Attribute selection Operator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The validity of logic mining depends on the validity of logic rules and the logic mining model. Standard system logic mining technology has obtained a series of optimization methods. The most effective optimization methods include embedding permutation operators and optimal attribute selection, but they fail to map unbalanced data sets well. Therefore, In order to improve the efficiency of the reverse analysis model of the existing system logic mining and to fit the unbalanced data, this paper introduces a PRO2SAT logic mining model based on traditional reverse analysis. It uses the generalization attribute of different positive literal proportions of PRO2SAT and the Ensemble Attribute Selection (EAS) strategy to help extract the best logic from the data set in the correct search space. The experimental results show that the proposed PRO2SATRA logic mining scheme has significant improvement in accuracy and competitiveness compared with the standard 2SAT reverse analysis method.

articleTitle: Polarization Clutter Suppression for Maxmizing Signal-to-Clutter Ratio under Linear Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The detection of ultra-low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) poses significant challenges, primarily due to their low flight altitude, making them highly susceptible to severe interference from complex ground clutter. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-channel fusion polarization clutter suppression method based on fully polarimetric radar, effectively mitigating complex ground clutter. The proposed algorithm first performs a weighted fusion of the four polarization channel information from the fully polarimetric radar. Subsequently, Under the linear constraints, based on the optimization criterion of maximizing the signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR), a genetic algorithm is utilized to approximate the optimal solution of the objective function, thereby effectively suppressing complex clutter. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is analyzed and verified using field-measured radar data. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm improves the signal-to-clutter ratio by an average of 22.92 dB compared to single-polarization channels, providing a valuable reference for the polarization suppression of complex ground clutter and enhancing the accuracy of low-altitude UAV polarization detection.

articleTitle: Labeled Random Finite Sets-Based Group Target Tracking with Multi-Detection Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In radar tracking applications for low-altitude group targets (such as bird flocks or drone swarms), the traditional point target measurement model is often unsuitable due to the complex micro-Doppler signatures and multipath effects. Algorithms based on labeled random finite sets (RFS) challenges with multi-detection problems. This paper presents a new method for tracking low-altitude group targets using labeled RFS in radar systems. To mitigate the disturbance from multi-detection, we propose modified assignment cost matrices in the update process, which reduces the number of false associations, and thus achieves quality enhancement of trajectory estimations. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Collaborative Detection Planning Algorithm in Airborne Radar Network Based on Mission Utility
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a collaborative detection planning algorithm in airborne radar network based on mission utility. The basis of the proposed algorithm is to adaptively optimizes the assignment results of mission-radar node selection parameters, in order to maximize the global utility of airborne radar network in collaborative detection mission allocation, while satisfying the constraints of the given limitations of the maximum available time resources, echo signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and system performance. Furthermore, we derive the global utility function of airborne radar network within a mission quality framework, and ulteriorly employ it as the criterion function to evaluate the multi-mission integrated execution efficiency. By incorporating the interior point method, we develop a three-step solution methodology to address the aforementioned optimization problem efficiently. Numerical simulations validate the superiority and reliability of our proposed algorithm in terms of mission utility, outperforming existing approaches.

articleTitle: Fusion and Comparative Study of Fuzzy k-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting for Indoor Positioning Systems via WLAN/WiFi Fingerprinting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel indoor positioning system based on WLAN/WiFi fingerprinting leveraging a multi-model fusion approach. We combine the strengths of Fuzzy k-Nearest Neighbors (FKNN), Random Forest (RF), and Gradient Boosting (GB) algorithms to achieve superior positioning accuracy. Each model is meticulously implemented and optimized using the publicly available UJIIndoorLoc dataset, a comprehensive benchmark for indoor localization. Our experimental results demonstrate that the fusion of these models significantly outperforms individual approaches, achieving substantial improvements in indoor positioning accuracy.

articleTitle: A Simulation-Based Post-Processing for Layover Unmixing Using 2d Range-Elevation Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: SAR is an active microwave imaging system, known for its unique ability to provide high-resolution images under various weather conditions. Geometric distortion is a significant factor affecting the application of SAR, particularly in complex terrains or densely built-up areas. TomoSAR utilizes multi-baseline acquisitions to eliminate layover and achieve accurate three-dimensional reconstruction of the scene. However, the performance of TomoSAR heavily depends on the number of acquisitions, which can be a limiting factor. In this paper, we proposes a new way for layover unmixing with limited single-pass SAR acquisitions. The method involves simulating typical layover scenarios to generate a range-elevation spectrum, followed by layover mitigation processing. Specifically, point targets overlapped in a single pixel are separated by applying linear fitting to the data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can separate layover targets and reconstruct their 3D point clouds in various layover scenarios. This method providing a new solution for improving the quality of 3D reconstruction in complex scenarios.

articleTitle: Distributed radar incoherent fusion method for independent non-identically distributed fluctuating targets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the research of distributed radar incoherent fusion, most of them consider independent identically distributed target RCS models, furthermore the signal-to-noise ratios of each node of the radar may differ greatly under non-ideal conditions, which reduces the detection performance of the incoherent detector. Therefore, this paper investigates the node selection of independently non-identically distributed lognormal fluctuating targets for incoherent detector under distributed radar. Specifically, this paper approximates the lognormal sum by using a new lognormal probability density function (pdf) and gives an approximate expression for the detection probability. Finally, some conclusions are drawn from numerical simulation experiments on node selection.

articleTitle: Multi-Terrain Radar HRRP Target Detection Using Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: As radar resolution improves, high-resolution radars have significantly enhanced target detection performance through the generation of high-resolution range profiles (HRRPs). However, when the range resolution is much smaller than the target, the target’s energy is dispersed across multiple range cells, leading to poor detection performance with traditional energy-based detection algorithms. Furthermore, existing detection algorithms are highly sensitive to clutter characteristics and exhibit poor adaptability to varying scenarios. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) HRRP detection algorithm based on contrastive learning for multiple terrains. The algorithm improves the contrastive learning loss function to achieve well-clustered representations of clutter samples during training. Test samples are evaluated by calculating the Mahalanobis distance between them and the training samples, and compared against detection thresholds to accomplish target detection. Testing results show that the proposed algorithm achieves superior detection performance across multiple terrains. Furthermore, to reach a 90% detection probability, the proposed method requires a signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) reduction of 1 to 4 dB compared to the competing methods.

articleTitle: Range-Doppler processing for passive radar based on joint tracking and dynamic compressed sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Passive radar (PR) systems use accessible sources of illumination for tasks such as detection and tracking. Improving the performance of range-Doppler (RD) processing is essential to subsequent detection of PR systems. Traditional RD processing methods such as cross-ambiguity function (CAF) and compressed sensing (CS) have limited performance when dealing with weak targets. In this paper, we propose a RD processing method in PR based on joint tracking and dynamic compressed sensing (DCS), which can more accurately reconstruct RD maps by utilizing inter-frame motion information of the target. The cubature Kalman filter (CKF) is employed to predict the target motion state of each RD map in the proposed method. Then a dynamic extended orthogonal matching pursuit (DEOMP) is presented to generate more accurate RD maps by utilizing the prediction information to determine the support set. Numerical simulations are conducted to validate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Different PolSAR Input Schemes and Its Influence for Costal WetLand Area Classification: A Comparison
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To explore the impact of data input schemes for deep learning on the final classification results, this paper studies different combinations of polarization feature input schemes using the polarization decomposition method.The classification results obtained through convolutional neural networks indicate that some current polarization input schemes fail to effectively utilize polarization information. The proposed schemes in this paper are superior to these schemes. Under limited resources, information from the polarization coherence matrix can be utilized. When the performance of the machine configuration is sufficiently good, using polarization features from the polarization decomposition scheme yields the best classification results.

articleTitle: Assessment of Damage Degree in High-Rise Building Structures Based on Continuous Wavelet Transform and Improved ResNet18
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Vibration-based Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) has garnered significant attention due to its ability to monitor health state in real-time. Current applications of SHM mainly focus on the occurrence of damage but are unable to assess the severity of the structural damage. Achieving damage severity assessment through multi-channel signal processing has become a key focus of current research. To address this issue, we propose an improved TriAxial-ResNet18 architecture, which is capable of processing acceleration signals in the three directions simultaneously, thereby enabling comprehensive damage assessment. In this study, finite element modelling (FEM) is utilized to emulate various damage states in the investigated high-rise building, generating signals under different health states. Time-frequency feature imaging based on continuous wavelet transform (CWT) is employed to visualize the vibration signals, converting the raw signals into two-dimensional images for training and validating the deep learning model. Experimental results indicate that the TriAxial-ResNet18 model achieves high classification accuracy in distinguishing various damage levels across different monitoring points. By integrating simulation technology with deep learning methods, this research provides an economical and efficient solution for SHM in high-rise buildings.

articleTitle: Research on Health State Identification Method of Main Circulation Pump Based on CEEMDAN-TIMF-HT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The main circulation pump (MCP) is core equipment of reactor, which controls the circulation flow of reactor coolant. Aiming at the problem that the health status of nuclear power MCP is difficult to identify, a method of health status identification of MCP based on adaptive noise complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition, target intrinsic mode functions and Hilbert transform (CEEMDAN-TIMF-HT) is proposed. CEEMDAN is used to decompose the monitoring signal of MCP under various states to acquire multiple Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs), and the TIMF component is selected according to TIMF selection variable. Then, the spectrum analysis of all IMF components (IMFCs) is performed to further determine whether the TIMF component selection is correct. Finally, the HT is carried out on the TIMF components, and the Hilbert spectrum of each TIMF component is obtained. The objective is to analyse the vibration signal characteristics of the MCP in both its healthy and faulty states. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is an effective means of identifying the fault state characteristics of the MCP, thereby enhancing the reliability of MCP operation.

articleTitle: HRRP Target Recognition Based on Modified Gradient Boosting Decision Tree
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Focused on radar automatic target recognition in open set environment, Extreme Value Theory (EVT) is introduced to modify Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (GBDT). We mark the method as Open Set Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (OSGBDT) in the paper. OSGBDT is structured with two steps. First, EVT is utilized to model the distances distribution among samples across features. Positive samples with closely spaced intervals are grouped into the same leaf node during decision tree splitting. Next, EVT is used to model the outputs of prediction models for each class. The probability that a test sample belongs to an unknown class is estimated. Experimental results based on High Resolution Range Profiles (HRRP) database demonstrate that OSGBDT outperforms state-of-the-art open set recognition methods.

articleTitle: Location Distributed Modeling for Improving Scale Adaptability of SAR Incremental Target Detectors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the continuous increase in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data, it becomes a real challenge to efficiently update existing SAR target detection models. The incremental target detection method is a solution that can update the model using only new data while preventing old knowledge from being forgotten. However, existing incremental target detection methods lack consideration of the characteristics of SAR targets, which does not lead to desirable results in SAR target detection. There may be significant scale differences between targets of different SAR classes, and if cross-scale targets participate in the incremental learning process, the localization ability of the detector will be greatly reduced. For this reason, Location Distributed Modeling (LDM) is proposed in this paper to improve the scale adaptability of SAR incremental target detectors. The method first transforms the traditional bounding box into a rectangular distribution by 2-D Gaussian modeling and further forms a new incremental localization loss by measuring the difference between the distributions. LDM can weaken the sensitivity of the incremental target detector to the scale of the target and improve attention to the center offset and the overall distribution. We set up several data incremental scenarios with the multi-class SAR target detection dataset MSAR in this paper, and the experimental results show that our method significantly improves the scale adaptability of SAR incremental target detectors.

articleTitle: A System Design Method for Adaptive Selection of Imaging Modes in Spaceborne SAR Echo Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, a new parameter design method for spaceborne SAR echo simulation is discussed. Existing system parameter design methods often rely on experience to roughly determine the imaging mode first, and then calculate the system parameters for individual imaging mode, with high complexity and uncertainty. For the four modes mainly used in spaceborne SAR imaging, namely strip, spotlight, sliding spotlight and TOPS, this paper proposes a method that can adaptively select imaging mode according to the requirements of azimuth scene swath width and azimuth resolution, and analyze the trend of the imaging modes with the changes of the two indicators.
