The echo simulation and imaging verification of the design results obtained with multiple sets of indicators meet the requirements of the initial input, proving the effectiveness of the method described in this paper.

articleTitle: Change Feature Refinement and Cross-Scale Interaction Network for High-Resolution Remote Sensing Image Change Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Change detection represents a fundamental research area within remote sensing technology. Nevertheless, in practical applications, the spatial arrangement of terrestrial features is frequently highly complex. The changing objects vary significantly in size and exhibit irregular, complex shapes. Many mainstream methods are hindered by the intricate spatial scales of these changed objects, culminating in suboptimal detection performance. To overcome these obstacles, we propose a change feature refinement and cross-scale interaction network (FRCI-Net) for effective change detection. To capture more robust change features, FRCI-Net first employs a feature interaction module (FIM) and a differential feature refinement module (DFRM) to accurately capture change regions while enhancing the boundary details of the change features. To further enhance the recognition ability for multi-scale change targets, FRCI-Net leverages a cross-scale interaction module (CIM) to enable attention-driven integration and consolidation of change features across divers scales, thereby improving the network’s scale awareness of various change targets. Experiments conducted on two benchmark datasets validate that the proposed method surpasses six advanced methods.

articleTitle: A Multi-Parameter Landslide Early Warning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Landslides present significant risks to human safety and infrastructure, necessitating advanced early warning systems. This paper proposes a multi-parameter landslide early warning method that integrates multiple parameters, including coherence, velocity, and acceleration, with a dynamic time decay model. The proposed method emphasizes the importance of considering the time-dependent nature of landslide precursors and enhances the accuracy of warnings by dynamically adjusting the weight of these parameters over time. The feasibility of this landslide warning method has been verified in actual landslide cases.

articleTitle: STIFormer: Spatial-Temporal Interactive Transformer for Dual-Phase Remote Sensing Images Semantic Change Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The Semantic Change Detection (SCD) in remote sensing images requires accurate extraction of change regions while distinguishing between different types of changes. The temporal span between the two phases is often considerable, resulting in a diverse range of change types across a wide imaging field, with some changes being more apparent than others. Additionally, the scale of change regions can vary from local to global, posing significant challenges for SCD in dual-phase remote sensing images. To address these issues, we propose a semantic change detection method leveraging spatio-temporal dependencies. Firstly, we individually process the dual-phase remote sensing images using an encoder structure with shared weights to extract semantic-level features. These features are then subjected to convolutional operations to generate representations of change regions, enhancing the capability to extract less obvious changes. Subsequently, a transformer structure representing the semantic changes in the dual-phase images is introduced. This structure effectively utilizes the spatio-temporal characteristics of the images to obtain global and change features, addressing the issue of insufficient feature representation for large-scale change regions. Finally, we introduce a semantic learning scheme that utilizes spatio-temporal constraints consistent with the SCD task to guide the learning of semantic changes. The proposed network is evaluated on datasets obtained from high-resolution and resource series satellites, achieving an IOU of 94.49% and an accuracy of 99.04%. These results convincingly demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Airborne Radar Operating State Recognition Based on Multi-Parameter Fusion RCS-Conv Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Airborne radar operating state directly reflects the combat intention of the target platform, playing a crucial role in electronic warfare. However, the challenge of parameter overlap among different operating states poses a new obstacle to radar state recognition. To enhance the capability of recognizing radar operating states with overlapping parameters, a multi-parameter fusion residual coordinate shrinkage ConvNet (RCS-Conv) is proposed in this paper. First, the temporal regularities of electromagnetic data and the correlation features among parameters are analyzed. Subsequently, discriminative features conducive to radar state recognition are identified. Moreover, a stream-level deep recognition framework incorporating a coordinate attention (CA) mechanism is meticulously designed. This recognition method not only captures inter-channel dependencies and positional information but also extracts discriminative timing and parameter correlation features. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate recognition of airborne radar states in complex electromagnetic environments.

articleTitle: A Novel Feature Extraction and Land Cover Classification Method Based on Tensor Algebra for Multi-band SAR Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multi-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can provide more reliable results than the single-band case through feature level fusion for land cover classification. The existing feature level fusion approaches of multi-band SAR simply stack the features of each pixel in different bands, which are limited in capturing inherent correlation among different bands, leading to suboptimal classification performance. In order to classify land cover more accurately, a novel classification method based on tensor algebra for multi-band SAR is proposed in this paper. First, each pixel is represented as a fourth-order tensor constructed by combining multi-features of different bands in the neighborhood window. Then, a novel tensor discriminant locality preserving projection (TDLPP) is proposed for feature extraction from tensors, integrating local manifold structure and global label information. Finally, the lower-dimensional features extracted by the TDLPP are classified using the classic classifier, such as K-Nearest Neighborhood (KNN) classifier. The experimental results on the real multi-band SAR dataset confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Monitoring deformation of Genhe-Labudalin Highway using Sentinel-1 InSAR analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The Genhe-Labudalin Highway (GenLa Highway) serves as a critical infrastructure link between Genhe City and Labudalin Town in Inner Mongolia, traversing extensive areas of continuous and island permafrost. The stability of this highway is compromised by hazards related to freeze-thaw cycles. Therefore, monitoring its stability is of paramount importance. Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) technology has proven invaluable in detecting slow-moving deformations over large areas, making it a vital tool for infrastructure stability monitoring. This study employs 114 Sentinel-1 images, acquired between May 2016 and April 2020, to perform time-series InSAR analysis of the Genla Highway. The analysis reveals linear displacement trends and seasonal displacement along the GenLa Highway and its surrounding areas. The time-series data indicate seasonal deformations, with a maximum displacement of ~20 mm. Significant uneven deformations are observed along the roadbed and adjacent areas, posing further threats to the highway’s stability. Additionally, human activities influence the seasonal freeze-thaw cycles of the permafrost, potentially exacerbating the instability of infrastructure in these regions.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Through-Wall Radar Imaging Based on Few Shot and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Through-wall radar and its imaging play an important role in the detection of enclosed space. However, the resolution of the existing through-wall radar imaging method is not high enough to serve the practical application. The deep learning methods alleviate the problem but they suffer from the insufficient labeled data. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a high-resolution imaging method of through-wall radar based on few shot and transfer learning. Firstly, a cGAN network is trained on the source data and is used to initialize the parameters of the target cGAN as the pre-trained network. Secondly, the target cGAN is fine-tuned on target domain to obtain the transferred cGAN. Finally, during the online phase, the low-resolution radar image in target domain is input into the transferred generator to get the high-resolution optical image. Simulation results show that, when there is limited amount of target data, the quality of generated images can be improved in fewer iterations by using the knowledge of the pre-trained source network.

articleTitle: An ISAR Image Reconstruction Method via Signal Support Reweighted l1 Minimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The sparse aperture caused by data loss or unintentional interference is the actual problem in radar imaging process. Therefore, a compressed sensing (CS) based ISAR image reconstruction method with signal support aided is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the signal support is constructed from FFT-based imaging results. Then the signal support is introduced as a prior information into the reweighted function during the CS reconstruction. The simulation results show that, when the azimuth effective aperture ratio is as low as 30 % and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) equals to -10 dB, the proposed method can obtain clear imaging results like that of complete aperture data. Besides, compared with the traditional CS reconstruction method, the number of false points in the reconstruction results by proposed method is greatly reduced.

articleTitle: An Azimuth Ambiguity Suppression Method without Resolution Degradation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Azimuth ambiguity is caused by the combination of antenna sidelobe and finite azimuth sampling, which seriously influences the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image quality and application. Current suppression methods have been designed at the cost of resolution loss mostly. Therefore, an ambiguity suppression method without resolution degradation is proposed, and the core is employing ambiguity refocusing and threshold segmentation. Firstly, an accurate analytical model of azimuth ambiguity is established to provide theoretical basis for ambiguity refocusing. Secondly, by taking advantage of the entropy difference before and after refocusing, ambiguity area detection is accomplished. Finally, the ambiguity energy in obtained detection area is eliminated by threshold segmentation and amplitude suppression. The presented approach is verified by both simulation results and Chinese LJ2-01 satellite.

articleTitle: Tensor-based Parameter Estimation of FDA-MIMO Radar with Mutual Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In practice, the performance of Frequency Diverse Array Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (FDA-MIMO) radar is affected by mutual coupling. In this paper, a tensor-based approach for parameter estimation in the FDA-MIMO radar system with mutual coupling is proposed to address the issue. Firstly, the tensor-based model is established. Then, the Parallel Factor (PARAFAC) decomposition is used to obtain the steering matrix. The decoupling operation is performed using the Toeplitz matrix, and the phase properties of the steering matrix are used to estimate angle and range information. Simulations have validated the superiority and efficacy of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: High-Resolution ISAR imaging based on deep unfolded Bayesian network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Under complex observation conditions, high-resolution ISAR images can be attained by the compressive sensing technique. However, the conventional methods require numerous iteration steps and time-consuming parameters tuning. To address this issue, we propose an ISAR imaging method using a deep unfolded Bayesian network. Firstly, the signal model and probabilistic model are constructed. After that, the iterative algorithm is derived. On this basis, the deep unfolded network is proposed to achieve accurate reconstruction. The experimental results indicate that well-focused imaging can be obtained by the proposed method in low SNR and incomplete data conditions.

articleTitle: Learning Low Rank Approximation IAA for Forward-Looking Scanning Radar Super-Resolution Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In forward-looking scanning radar imaging, spectral estimation method can improve the azimuth resolution. However, when dealing with large-scale echo data, the computational complexity is significantly elevated due to the inversion of high-dimensional matrices. To solve these problems, this paper proposes a low rank approximate iterative adaptive angular (IAA) super-resolution imaging method based on deep networks. By combining the advantages of data driven and model driven, this method avoids the problems of manual parameter selection and slow iteration update in traditional algorithm. At the same time, due to the learning and fitting ability of deep networks, the proposed method can maintain good angular super-resolution performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the algorithm exhibits reduced computational complexity and improved resolution compared to conventional methods.

articleTitle: A Transformer Self-Attention Guided Graph Convolutional Network for Drone Swarm Trajectory Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel trajectory prediction algorithm for infrared drone swarms, addressing the challenges posed by flexible motion patterns and complex intraswarm interactions. The proposed method leverages a Transformer-based self-attention mechanism within a graph attention convolutional network framework. In the encoding phase, a graph convolutional neural network (GCN) is employed to enhance the representation of temporal features. Subsequently, an attention-guided graph neural network is utilized to effectively capture and encode interaction features among drones within the swarm. The Transformer attention mechanism is then integrated into the decoder to refine the prediction process. This encoder-decoder architecture is specifically designed to extract and map the temporal and spatial interaction features of individual drones, providing accurate trajectory predictions that consider the unique dynamics of drone swarms. Experimental results on an infrared drone swarm trajectory prediction dataset, as well as the publicly available pedestrian trajectory prediction datasets ETH/UCY, demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior performance in terms of ADE and FDE metrics.

articleTitle: Anti-Smeared Spectrum Jamming Technology of Time-Frequency Filtering Combined with LSD
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Smeared spectrum (SMSP) jamming generates interference signals that are highly coupled with the radar transmit waveform in the time-frequency domain by changing the FM slope and the number of retransmissions of the intercepted radar waveforms. This paper proposes a time-frequency filtering combined with line segment detector (LSD) anti-SMSP jamming method based on multi-parameter coded waveform. In this method, part of the interference is filteredrFT out in the fractional-order Fourier transform (FrFT) domain, and then the time-frequency points identified as SMSP jamming are discarded by short-time Fourier transform (STFT) in the time-frequency domain, and the target signal is reconstructed using compressive sensing. Finally the LSD detection method based on the SMSP jamming inter-pulse disorder characteristics under the multi-parameter coded waveform is used to further filter out the remaining jamming energy. The simulation results validate the correctness of the theoretical analysis of the proposed method, and compared with the traditional FrFT combined with STFT method, the output jamming to signal ratio of the proposed method is reduced by 10 dB, and the output integral sidelobe ratio is also reduced.

articleTitle: A spaceborne TOPSAR imaging acceleration scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the TOPSAR working mode, due to the limitation of system design, the pulse repetition frequency of the system is less than the overall bandwidth, which leads to the phenomenon of spectral aliasing and time-domain aliasing. There are a large number of operations such as matrix point multiplication, matrix and complex number multiplication in the three-step imaging algorithm process. At the same time, there are a large number of fast Fourier transforms, and there is a significant difference in the velocity in the azimuth and range directions. In view of this, this paper proposes a scheme to accelerate the algorithm by using graphics processor and matrix transpose, and experiments are carried out to verify the effectiveness and efficiency of the imaging algorithm

articleTitle: The Imbalanced Recognition of Space Micro-Motion Targets Based on GRB Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Limited by the quantity of space micro-motion targets launches and observation conditions, datasets for recognizing space micro-motion target usually is class imbalanced. Under such circumstances, the recognition performance of the available methods degrades rapidly, and in some cases, even complete failure. To tackle this issue, this paper proposes a gradient-guided class re-balancing loss (GRB Loss) for the imbalanced datasets of space micro-motion targets recognition. Particularly, in the proposed GRB Loss, we design an adaptive weighting function, which use the accumulated positive and negative gradient ratio of each classification node as input, to assign the weights to the positive and negative gradient, so as to improve the imbalance of the positive and negative gradient ratio in each classification node. Experimental results show that the proposed method enhances recognition performance on imbalanced datasets and remains robust across varying imbalance ratios.

articleTitle: Efficient On-board Remote Sensing Scene Classification Using FPGA With Ternary Weight
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Remote Sensing Scene Classification (RSSC) is essential for applications such as environmental monitoring and catastrophe management, which often have stringent time constraints requiring real-time processing. On-board processing significantly enhances real-time performance but is challenged by limited computational resources and strict power requirements. To address these challenges, this study proposes an FPGA-based accelerator designed for Ternary Weight Networks (TWNs), which use ternary values {+1, 0, -1} for weights. By adopting TWNs, the multiplication operations in convolution are eliminated, resulting in a significant reduction in computing and power needs. Experimental results show that TWNs significantly reduce network parameters while retaining classification accuracy comparable to Full-precision Weight Networks (FPWNs). The FPGA-based accelerator achieves an energy-efficiency ratio of 434.11 GOP/W, outperforming most existing CNN accelerators, hence meeting the requirements for on-board RSSC.

articleTitle: Maritime Target Detection of PCL System Based on non-cooperative Pulse Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Accurate situational awareness of maritime targets in 24/7 is crucial for safeguarding national maritime rights and ensuring maritime safety. The basic principle of PCL system for targets detection was provided. In order to analyze the detection performance of PCL systems based on pulse radar signal, experimental research on maritime targets detection was conducted. The experimental observation scenario was selected in the urban area of Yantai and its related area. The measurement of direct path pulse signal parameters, analysis of antenna scanning characteristics and data pre-processing, PD processing, CA-CFAR detection and display correction were completed based on field measurement data.

articleTitle: A Gradient-based Method with Denoising for Target Shadow Profile Retrieval in Forward Scatter Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The existing nonlinear least-squares method for target shadow profile retrieval in forward scatter radar only considers noiseless samples of the forward scatter shadow ratio. Inspired by optical diffraction tomography, in this paper we propose to use a gradient-based method with denoising to tackle scenarios involving noisy samples. Simulation results demonstrate its superiority over the conventional least-squares method. More specifically, an essential prerequisite for the least-squares method, i.e., the number of samples being greater than or equal to the number of pixels, is no longer required by the proposed method. Moreover, the proposed method retrieves the target image with a higher peak signal-to-noise ratio than that using the least-squares method.

articleTitle: Research on Passive Polarization Calibration Methods for Insect Radars in Non-Ideal Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Most current insect radars use a fully polarimetric system that measures polarization information to determine biological parameters such as the insect’s head orientation, body length, and weight. Amplitude and phase inconsistencies between the polarization channels in radar systems, along with cross-polarization interference from dual-polarized antennas, can introduce polarization errors. These errors distort the radar's polarization data, leading to significant inaccuracies in the derived insect parameters. Additionally, insect radars are often deployed in complex outdoor environments where fluctuating factors such as temperature and humidity cause time-varying polarization errors, making it challenging to calibrate these errors accurately. Polarization calibration techniques are designed to estimate and correct these system errors, forming the foundation for obtaining accurate polarization information from radar. This paper aims to analyze the performance of existing polarization calibration methods under conditions of time-varying polarization errors. First, the sources of polarization errors, the concept of polarization calibration, and its classifications are introduced. Next, the system error model for polarimetric scattering matrix (PSM) measurements is analyzed, and several typical passive polarization calibration methods are presented. Then, a qualitative analysis of the time-varying effects of system polarization errors is conducted using measured data, and a comparative analysis of the performance of typical passive polarization calibration methods under these conditions is provided through simulation experiments. Finally, the applicability of existing polarization calibration methods to current insect radars is discussed.

articleTitle: Gridless Wideband DOA Estimation Method Based on Comprehensive Subband Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the development of radar technology, direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation of wideband signals has attracted tremendous attention. This paper introduces a novel subband data fusion method for wideband signal DOA estimation, which can be applied in scenarios such as integrated sensing and communication systems. The proposed method decomposes the received signals into narrowband signals and a two-sided correlation transform (TCT) is utilized to focus the array output at all subband frequencies to the reference center frequency. Then the subband data fusion process is executed, in which the different subband frequencies result in varying angular resolutions, and each subband has distinct signal power. A novel weighting scheme that integrates angular resolution and signal power is proposed to address this problem, which is not proposed by other methods. Atomic norm minimization (ANM) is then utilized to calculate DOAs. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the compared methods in both precision and resolution, especially with large relative bandwidth.

articleTitle: Bearing-only Localization Based on an Array Network with Distributed ADMM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The two-dimensional target localization problem for a network of distributed sensor sub-arrays (with a sub-array at each receiver) is investigated in the compressive sensing framework based on group sparsity, and the well-known alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) method is applied to derive a distributed implementation algorithm. It does not require transmission of the impinging signals from each sub-array to a central processor, while the whole optimisation process is realised in a distributed way. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm under certain conditions performs better than the existing group sparsity based localization method in terms of localization accuracy, speed and computational complexity.

articleTitle: Point Cloud Based In-vehicle Occupancy Detection Method by Using 77GHz mmWave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In recent years, with the introduction and development of vehicle-to-everything (V2X) and child presence detection (CPD), there’s an increasing demand for in-vehicle perception systems. Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar has become one of the mainstream sensors in this field for high accuracy, small size, and low power consumption. In this paper, we develop a real-time in-vehicle occupancy detection method based on 77GHz mmWave radar. Firstly, a pre-processing framework based on dual-path detection is used to obtain more point clouds from weak targets. Then density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) is applied to classify the occupants’ point clouds. Finally, we propose a novel probabilistic population-assisted occupancy detection algorithm based on the long and short-term feedback results, which can suppress missed detection and false alarms well. Our algorithm has been successfully deployed onto the radar board and achieves an average accuracy rate of 99.10% under various complex scene experiments.

articleTitle: Band selection method based on target to background separation for anomaly detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Hyperspectral anomaly detection is to detect abnormal pixels that are different from background pixels when the target spectral characteristics are unknown. Significantly, using full-band hyperspectral data for anomaly detection will produce the so-called Hughes phenomenon and high computational cost. Besides, the redundancy of full-band data will drown out the abnormal target characteristics and reduce the detection performance. Therefore, it is particularly important to select the band in advance. However, the band selection methods currently used for anomaly detection lack relevance to the task, resulting in a large number of selected bands and failing to effectively improve the performance of anomaly detection. To address theses problems, this article proposes a band selection method for anomaly detection based on the separation of target to background. Specifically, we take the RX algorithm as the core, design an indicator function to measure the separation of target to background based on the Mahalanobis distance. Besides, we use a forward update search algorithm to quickly approximate the optimal band combination. The former is associated with anomaly detection tasks and compatible with multiple types of abnormal targets, while the latter fully explores possible band combinations and avoids the huge overhead of the exhaustive method. We have conducted extensive tests on different scene data sets and different anomaly detection algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in subsequent anomaly detection compared to its competitors, even with fewer selected bands.

articleTitle: A tracking filter algorithm for migratory birds based on group situation constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Aerial animal migration is closely related to human life, and radar is one of the most effective means of observing it. However, scanning radar has a low data rate, a short integration time, and lacks prior knowledge of target speed, while migratory animals exhibit high mobility. These factors make traditional tracking filter algorithms ineffective at predicting their movement. To address this issue, this paper proposes a tracking filter algorithm based on group dynamics constraints, leveraging the characteristic behavior of migratory animals flying in groups. First, the dynamic state of the group is calculated using the group as the research unit. Then, tracking filtering is performed under the constraint of group dynamics. Simulation and field data have verified the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: RS-AFRFT: A Coherent Integration Method for High-Speed Extended Target Detection in Agile Frequency Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the domain of high-speed target processing using Agile Frequency Radar (AFR), a coherent accumulation algorithm based on the Agile Frequency Radon-Fourier Transform (AFRFT) has been developed. However, when the synthesized bandwidth is large and there is a lack of prior target information, the real-time performance of this algorithm can significantly degrade. Additionally, multiple scattering centers under wide-band conditions can hinder the detection of extended targets. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Reorder and Segmentation AFRFT (RS-AFRFT) algorithm. This algorithm first sorts all pulses according to their frequencies, then segments the rearranged pulses to widen the search steps. Finally, it completes the inter-pulse accumulation by combining intra-segment AFRFT processing with inter-segment fusion processing. Theoretical analysis and simulations based on real electromagnetic data confirm the superior performance of the proposed algorithm. Compared to the traditional AFRFT algorithm, the RS-AFRFT method not only effectively reduces computational complexity but also improves target detection performance by integrating multiple scattering centers of extended targets.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Elvation Estimation Method for Meter-wave Radar in A Composite Terrain Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper focuses on elevation estimation problem in a composite terrain scenario. Due to the array reflection echoes from different terrains, the existing elevation estimation methods are not applicable. An adaptive maximum likelihood method is proposed. Firstly, two paralell echo models are constructed for the upper and lower sub-arrays with same size, and the approximate position of the terrain boundary is estimated by the correlation coefficiency comparison. Then, the accurate position of the terrain boundary is computed via transition point detection of the amplitude difference between channel data and designed model. Finally, a composite model is constructed to estimate the target’s elevation. Simulation verified the effectiveness of the designed adaptive super-resolution elevation estimation method.

articleTitle: An Efficient Compression Method for Collaborative 3D Mapping in Confined Space with Limited Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: LiDAR is a key sensor for 3D mapping, and as the measurement accuracy of the sensor continues to improve, the order of magnitude and the memory required to acquire 3D point cloud data are getting larger and larger. However, due to the limited computational resources of unmanned platforms for collaborative 3D mapping in confined space, the large memory occupancy of the point cloud data will bring challenges to the subsequent transmission, storage and collaboration. In order to save storage space and improve transmission and processing efficiency, this paper expresses the 3D point cloud based on the voxel octree structure. We use cropping to remove the irrelevant point cloud information first, and further optimize the compression algorithm of the voxel octree by detecting the point cloud resolution and then setting the voxel filter in partitions. Experimental results verify the proposed method compress the point cloud as much as possible while reducing the loss of key information.

articleTitle: Sum-Difference Analysis Based Design for Third-Order Sparse Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Recently, third-order cumulants (TOCs) as a non-conventional odd-order statistics, has been introduced to direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation with the third-order nested array (TONA), which significantly increases the number of uniform degrees-of-freedom (uDOFs) and can even be comparable to the fourth-order cumulant approach. In this paper, through analysis of the second-order sum-difference co-array, a third-order sparse linear array (SLA) design scheme suitable for TOCs is proposed, which can extend the commonly used second-order SLAs to the third-order. By selecting an appropriate generator array, the derived third-order SLA has far more uDOFs than the existing TONA, greatly improving its DOA estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Rapid Detection of Periglacial Talus Deformation on the Tibetan Plateau Using LT-1 A/B SAR Satellite Constellation Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Periglacial Talus, a type of landform characterized by the accumulation of rock debris at the base of alpine rock walls, are numerous worldwide and extensively distributed in the periglacial environments of the Tibetan Plateau. Climate warming significantly impacts rockwall–talus systems through frost action, permafrost changes, and deglaciation dynamics, affecting mountain hazards and hydrology of permafrost environment. The new lunched SAR satellite constellation Lutan-1 A/B (LT-1 A/B) present a novel opportunity to assess the deformation of periglacial talus. In this study, we firstly employ high-resolution GF-2 optical images to identify periglacial talus landforms in the high-risk geological hazard zone of the northeastern Himalayas. We then use LT-1 A/B SAR data with a refined stacking approach to rapidly detect and analyze deformations in these talus formations. We identified a total of 148 periglacial talus landforms. By utilizing LT-1 SAR data, we successfully detected deformations in these talus formations. The results reveal that the line-of-sight (LOS) deformation velocity of talus in the study area is lower than other periglacial landform such as rock glacier, some of the talus showing noticeable movement within their outlines. The results of this study demonstrate the capability of Stacking InSAR technology to rapidly identify deformation anomalies in areas prone to landslide hazards, and highlight the value of LT-1 SAR satellites in examining the dynamics of periglacial talus geomorphology.

articleTitle: An Unambiguous Angle and Range Estimation Method using MR-FDA-MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Frequency diversity array (FDA) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar systems have drawn widespread focus due to their capacity for providing angular and range information simultaneously. Unfortunately, the estimation accuracy is constrained by the amount of physical sensors. This paper proposes a method for unambiguous angle and range estimation using a combination of the minimum redundancy array (MRA) and FDA-MIMO radar. The MRA is applied to extend array degrees of freedom by differential processing. Following the implementation of range compensation, a two-dimensional spatially smoothed algorithm is employed to address the rank deficit issue in the equivalent array. Finally, the target’s angle, ambiguous zone and range offset are identified through a MUSIC algorithm. The efficacy for the designed methodology is corroborated by the simulated experimental outcomes.

articleTitle: Spectrogram-Driven Heart Sound Classification using YOLOv8 for Mobile Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach using the classification of abnormal or normal phonocardiogram (PCG) recordings by transforming them to spectrograms and applying YOLOv8 model for real-time classification. Unlike traditional models that work directly with raw audio or time-series data, our approach adopts the use of spectrograms to exploit the strengths of deep learning-based classifiers resulting in better accuracy. The model was trained on the PhysioNet/CinC 2016 dataset with a remarkable accuracy of 94.5%, F1-score of 0.95, recall of 0.97, precision of 0.95, and MCC of 0.83. Compared to traditional models such as LSTM or ResNet-18, YOLOv8 had a clear advantage in handling class imbalance within the dataset given. Although the LSTM models give promising results, they have larger computational overheads, which makes them unsuitable for real-time applications. Future work will investigate the optimization of YOLOv8 for deployment on microcontroller-based systems to improve efficiency within mobile health applications by minimizing inference time and resource usage. From our results, we believe that this method holds great promise to be implemented towards improving portable health diagnostics as a more accurate and efficient means of cardiovascular monitoring.

articleTitle: Research on SAR Image and Optical Image Fusion Classification Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to better integrate and classify multi-source image features, we constructed a multi-source remote sensing data feature extraction and fusion classification framework U-DSDNet based on a combination of dual channel convolutional neural networks and self attention. Build two independent channel networks to extract feature information. Introducing self attention mechanism to fuse multi-source image feature information, improving classification accuracy and stability. Meanwhile, we use Sentinel series satellite data to demonstrate the classification accuracy of U-DSDNet. Through comparative analysis with UNet, DeeplabV3+, and PSPNet, the experimental results show that in the SEN-OPT-SAR dataset, the overall accuracy of the U-DSDNet model is 3.8%, 0.2%, and 1.6% higher than the three models, respectively, verifying the superiority and effectiveness of the U-DSDNet model in land classification tasks.

articleTitle: Performance Limit of Phase Gradient Autofocus Class Method for Synthetic Aperture Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Motion errors are a primary obstacle to achieving ideal imaging in airborne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR). Due to the precision limitations of motion measurement equipment, autofocus techniques are often necessary. However, there exists an upper limit to the estimable range in practical autofocus, and no suitable model has yet been proposed to explain this phenomenon. Additionally, the complexity of mathematical derivations has hindered comprehensive analysis of defocus effects caused by different types of errors. This paper uses Phase Gradient Autofocus (PGA) as a case study to describe a geometric perspective for understanding the essence of SAR defocus. Based on this model, we can not only intuitively analyze the defocus effects induced by arbitrary errors but also theoretically derive the performance limits of PGA-like algorithms. Finally, the proposed theory is validated through simulations.

articleTitle: RFI Localization Scheme for Dual-Channel SAR System based on Alternating Constraints Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Radio frequency interference (RFI) source localization is essential for providing valuable priori information for RFI mitigation. For synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system, existing RFI localization methods face the challenge of severe localization ambiguity. To deal with this deficiency, this paper studies the mapping relationship between the interferometric phase properties of RFI and the location. It establishes a localization framework with alternating constraints to achieve an unambiguous range and azimuth localization. Finally, the localization accuracy is validated in real dual-channel echo data combined with simulated RFI. Compared to existing localization methods, the proposed approach could achieve azimuth accuracy at the meter level and range accuracy at the kilometer level without ambiguities.

articleTitle: Deceptive Jamming Mitigation Based on Proximal Policy Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the increasing reliance on radar technology in modern warfare, the operational capability of radar in countermeasure environments has become increasingly important. For waveform agile radars, randomly choosing transmit waveforms from a large set of orthogonal waveforms is not the optimal approach to mitigate the interference signal. Aiming at deception jamming mitigation, an anti-interference decision-making method based on proximal policy optimization (PPO) is proposed for waveform agile radars. By applying reinforcement learning algorithm, the radar can learn the strategy of the jammer through interaction with the environment and take the best action to obtain high return. This method effectively suppresses deception jamming while ensuring good detection performance of the radar. Numerical simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An edge enhancement-based fusion method of infrared and visible images in low light
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The combination of infrared and visible images can result in the generation of a single image with a high degree of detail and important targets in a variety of scenes, which is beneficial for human recognition. However, in low-light environments, low-intensity visible images tend to blur valuable information, which is often overlooked. This results in the loss of important information. While existing methods address the issue of low illumination and highlight the illumination, a considerable amount of structural information is lost when adjusting illumination, resulting in the omission of texture details. To solve aforementioned problems, we proposes a method for edge enhancement in low-illumination scenes. This approach aims to minimise the loss of edge information while simultaneously enhancing the illumination, thereby producing fusion images with enhanced texture detail. The initial step involves the design of an illumination enhancement module, which is employed to segregate the compromised illumination present from the scene information. Given the fact that image edge information has the capacity for effective structural modeling, a low-light visible image edge extraction network is designed to model structural information, which can accurately highlight important structural information and insert it in fused images. The results produced by this method have better visual perception and minimize structural loss. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the method outperforms SOTA methods in term of visual quality and quantitative metrics.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing Monitoring of Pasture Growth Using the Coherence Characteristics of InSAR Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Grassland resources play a crucial role as significant assets on Earth, exerting vital functions in carbon cycling, soil conservation, water resource management, and climate regulation. However, in recent years, excessive human exploitation and various pest infestations have led to the gradual desertification of existing grasslands. Therefore, it is imperative to conduct real-time monitoring and effective management of these resources. This study employs synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images to monitor and analyze the pasture status in the steppe region. In contrast to conventional monitoring methods, this approach offers a wide monitoring range and an extended observation period. Additionally, it leverages the advantages of SAR data, such as its independence from weather conditions compared to optical imagery. By calculating the coherence index using SAR data and combining it with optical imagery, we analyze the growth conditions of pasture in the study area. The research demonstrates a strong correlation between the variations in coherence index regions and the growth trend of pasture. For the issue of weather interference in optical imagery acquisition, the coherence index derived from SAR imagery can fully substitute for optical imagery in steppe analysis.

articleTitle: A Low-Altitude Small Target Radar Recognition Algorithm Based on Micro-Doppler Features and Vision Transformer Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In low-altitude airspace surveillance scenarios, accurately distinguishing between birds and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is of vital importance. However, the high similarity in flight altitude and speed between birds and UAVs makes it extremely difficult to distinguish between these two types of targets. To enhance radar recognition performance for both UAVs and birds, this paper proposes a low-altitude target recognition algorithm that combines micro-Doppler features with a Vision Transformer network (ViT) under a staring radar system. Verified with real-measured data, the recognition accuracy for three types of UAVs and birds reaches 94%.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Waveform Design for Countering Noncooperative Utilization in Bistatic Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Noncooperative parties (NCPs) can directly capture and use the electromagnetic signals from our bistatic radar to achieve covert detection with low power and forwarding deception. Existing methods increase the difficulty for NCPs to extract, classify, and process signals by transmitting complex modulated waveforms, but still cannot prevent waveforms from being utilized. This paper proposes a multidimensional waveform for countering noncooperative utilization in bistatic radar. First, fully use the degrees of freedom of the area array emitter to synthesize the desired signal in a specific azimuth-elevation direction through waveform modulation in the element, time and coding domains. Then, the alternating projection algorithm is used to solve for the waveform to counter noncooperative utilization, under constraints on signal-to-noise ratio loss and constant modulus. This makes NCPs unable to receive the radar signal or receive pre-designed deceptive signal. Simulations validate that the designed waveform can reduce the efficiency of NCPs while maintaining the performance of cooperative parties.

articleTitle: A Novel Compensation Method to Calibrate Dispersion Effect for Spaceborne Synthetic Aperture Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The ionospheric dispersion effect introduces additional phase errors to the chirp signal, leading to undesirable deterioration in range compression, including range shift and main lobe broadening. The contrast optimization autofocus (COA), as a representative of parametric-based methods calibrating the dispersion effect, updates the chirp rate empirically and manually. Moreover, it only compensates for quadratic phase errors while failing to address linear and higher-order phase errors. To this end, this paper proposes a novel compensation method. Compared to the COA, two specific step sizes are derived to quantitatively restrict the range shift and quadratic phase errors for accurately updating the chirp rate. Subsequently, the total electron content (TEC) inferred by chirp rate errors is applied to construct the conjugate compensation term associated with range-frequency achieving full-order phase error calibration. The simulated experiment demonstrates the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Convolutional Modulation Jamming on Azimuth Multi-Channel SAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the development of SAR imaging technology, high-resolution wide-swath (HRWS) imaging technology has matured. To obtain HRWS images, a multichannel SAR (MC-SAR) system is used to solve the conflicting requirements of high resolution and low pulse repetition frequency (PRF). In this paper, we first derive deceptive and noise jamming echo models based on the convolutional modulation jamming principle and the multichannel signal model, respectively. The effect of jamming on multichannel imaging is analysed by comparison with the mathematical normal echo model. Finally, the analysed results are verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Earth-Based Radar Asteroid 2D Imaging Technology Based on Rotation Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic aperture technology is a very important astrometric method. As humanity continues to explore the universe, the issue of low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) presents significant challenges for earth-based astronomical radar imaging. This is especially true when observing asteroids, as their rapid and unknown rotation speeds lead to traditional sub-aperture integration methods not only failing to improve SNR but even further deteriorating image quality. In view of this, this paper proposes a full coherent imaging method based on the search for the rotation period of asteroids. First, a set of sub-aperture image sequences can be obtained using the delay-Doppler algorithm. Second, scene grids are divided at the target, assuming an unknown rotation period as a pending parameter. Then, this paper derives the RD positioning model formula under rotating scenes, resamples different sub-apertures, and precisely compensates the phase. Next, the different sub-aperture images are coherently integrated and the image entropy is calculated. Finally, the above steps are iteratively repeated until the optimal rotation parameters and imaging results are obtained. Computer simulations verify the effectiveness of the algorithm proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: A Method of Anti Interrupted Sampling Multiple Shift Frequency Repeater Jamming for Dual-Frequency Radars
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multiple frequency shift jamming is an effective jamming pattern for dual-frequency continuous wave(DFCW) radars. When it was used into self-defense jamming, it can produce multiple false targets and affect the detection efficiency of radar. In this paper, an anti-jamming method is proposed to combat interrupted sampling multiple frequency shift repeater jamming(ISMFSRJ) for DFCW radars. Time-frequency(TF) analysis and Hough transform are used to identify the real target Doppler frequency in the TF plot. Theoretical analysis and simulation verification are carried out. The results of simulation prove that the proposed method can effectively combat ISMFSRJ when the jammer’s repeater signal time is shorter than the radar signal processing period.

articleTitle: IRJ-MARL: Intelligent Radar and Jammer Zero- sum Waveform Game based on Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In modern electronic warfare, jammer adopts a more intelligent jamming strategy than before. Recent radar anti-jamming methods focus on using reinforcement learning (RL) to combat the fixed expert strategies which ignore the intelligence of the jammer. To address that issue, a method using multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to design an intelligent radar and jammer zero-sum gaming scenario is proposed. Firstly, two sets of jamming and anti-jamming models are constructed, which incorporate changes in waveform duration and frequency. Secondly, a method which joint MARL and supervised learning (SL) is proposed to analyze the electronic environment and make decisions for radars and jammers. Finally, the simulation results confirm that the proposed method outperforms traditional RL algorithms in combat effectiveness, highlighting the impact of specifically tailored reward functions on the interplay between the radar and jammer.

articleTitle: Missing Modality Completion for Multi Frequency Radar HRRP Recognition Using GAN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High-resolution range profile (HRRP) is one of the commonly used methods in radar automatic target recognition (RATR). Recently, obtaining HRRP under different modalities, such as frequency and polarization, to improve the RATR performance has become an important development direction. However, in practical applications, sensor failures or interference may lead to modality loss during the model testing phase, resulting in decreased performance or even causing the model to fail to function properly. This paper primarily addresses the scenario of frequency modality loss and specifically proposes a modality completion and recognition network with generative adversarial network-embedded (MCRN-GAN) model. The model first generates and completes the missing modality features using the frequency feature transformation loop (FFTL) based on GAN. Subsequently, it fuses multi-modal features based on spatial and channel attention mechanisms to obtain a joint representation of dual-frequency features. Finally, a fully connected layer is used to complete the classification. Experiments on Ku and W frequency modality datasets demonstrates that the proposed method can effectively handle missing modality data after sufficient training without significant performance loss.

articleTitle: A Novel Method of Ground Target Positioning based on Heterologous Image Registration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a target high-precision positioning method based on heterogeneous image registration, including target longitude, latitude and altitude. The longitude and latitude are obtained by registering video SAR images with optical map, and the positioning information on the optical map is precisely known. Based on the registration of video SAR images and optical video images, the target height can be solved according to the projection direction difference of the height target on the two types of images, and the target altitude is calculated by adding the ground altitude. The video SAR and optical video images come from the integrated sensor, and the high frame rate imaging of video SAR can simultaneously satisfy the positioning of moving and stationary targets. Finally, the positioning results of this method is verified by measured data.

articleTitle: Mu-SAR High Resolution Imaging based on a sub-LFM Combination Waveform Design Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multistatic synthetic aperture radar (Mu-SAR) systems can achieve high-resolution imaging in a short time by coherently fusing multiple measurements. However, due to multiple transmitters and receivers, the echo data of a target based on the transmitting signals from different transmitters may be overlapped in one receiver. To achieve Mu-SAR high-resolution imaging, the transmitting signals of different transmitters should be designed. In this paper, a sub-LFM combination waveform design approach is proposed to achieve high resolution imaging for MuSAR. First, the echo model of MuSAR is analyzed. Second, the waveform design problem for MuSAR is transformed as a sub-LFM combination optimization problem. Finally, the waveform is optimized based on Multi-objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MPSO) algorithm. Simulations are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Relaxed Phase Optimization for 0-1 Combinational Problem in MHT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multiple Hypothesis Tracking (MHT) is a key algorithm in the field of target tracking, especially for dense multi-target tracking in strong clutter background. This paper proposes a new method based on phase optimization to solve the global hypothesis generation problem in MHT. By converting the combinatorial optimization problem into a phase optimization problem and solving it using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), we effectively solve the contradiction between computational complexity and optimization accuracy. Experimental results show that this method shows excellent performance in multiple complex scenarios.

articleTitle: Current Status and Prospects of the LuTan-1 Mission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: LuTan-1 have been launched for about one and a half years. It is now running in good situation. The in-orbit test last for one year and all the indices’ requirements are proven to be fully fulfilled. We started to collect the data over China at 22<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> June, 2023. Since now we have pushed more than 77,000 images. Most of the images are send to the satellite application centers of each province to monitor the geohazards and natural resources. Users mainly use the data for potential geohazards monitoring. Besides, the data are widely used for agriculture monitoring, coal mining deformation monitoring, flood monitoring, et al. In this paper, we overview the application status of LuTan-1. Meanwhile, the follow-on project of LuTan-1 is proposed to fulfill more application requirements.

articleTitle: A Pre-Processing Method for Ultra-High Resolution Space-Borne Sliding Spotlight SAR Data with BV-PRI and Stepped Frequency Chirps
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Sliding-spotlight SAR can realize high resolution. However, as the resolution becomes higher, problems of large echo signal range migration, and large bandwidth signal generating and receiving are introduced. Hence, block varying pulse repetition interval (BV-PRI) system is presented to overcome the large range migration problem, and stepped frequency chirp technology is used to achieve large bandwidth signal. In this paper, a pre-processing method for ultra-high resolution space-borne sliding spotlight SAR data with BV-PRI and stepped frequency chirps is introduced to reconstruct the two-dimensional (2-D) uniformly sampled signal from the raw data by using the steps of azimuth linear shift, range pre-processing and azimuth resampling. Simulation result is presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Target Tracking Algorithm Based on Feature Association
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To address the issue of degraded target tracking performance with Range Gate Pull Off (RGPO) jamming, we propose a target tracking algorithm based on radar multi-dimensional feature track association to counter RGPO jamming. Relying on the stepped-frequency radar system, we develop a target tracking algorithm that replaces kinematic features with multi-dimensional feature association of the target. After tracking filtering, the radar can adaptively select target features with jamming conditions through two rounds of track screening and two rounds of feature screening. The algorithm calculates feature similarity and discrimination , finally uses the Hungarian algorithm to determine the minimum cost matching result as the final association result. Simulation and measured data processing results show that this algorithm can mitigate the impact of jamming and significantly improve the radar’s target tracking success rate.

articleTitle: Few-shot unsupervised domain adaptation for SAR target recognition based on input alignment and class confusion loss
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the development of simulation technologies and deep learning, utilizing simulated images to train Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) target recognition model has become a research hotspot. However, SAR target recognition is hindered by the domain gap between simulated and real images, particularly under few-shot settings which mean only a limited number of unlabeled target domain samples are available for training. Regarding this issue, this paper proposed a new few-shot Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) method based on input alignment and class confusion loss (named IACC). Our method consists of two modules. The input alignment module (IAM) utilizes a special image-to-image translation model which can realize realistic image translation in few-shot settings, while the Class Confusion Module (CCM) employs a novel loss function to align the feature space and enhance classifier performance. Experimental results on the SAMPLE dataset demonstrate the superior performance of our method in both UDA and few-shot UDA scenarios compared with other existing methods. IACC offers a promising solution for SAR target recognition in challenging domain adaptation scenarios with limited data.

articleTitle: A Novel Sparse Frequency Radar Waveform Employing Multi-frequency Component Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Traditional radar systems typically use wideband signals but have limited anti-jamming capabilities. Sparse frequency waveforms offer a solution to narrowband interference issues. However, existing sparse frequency waveform design methods often handle the entire signal uniformly, resulting in fixed frequency notch positions and limited waveform flexibility. In this paper, we propose a new method for optimizing sparse frequency waveforms. While maintaining constant waveform pulse width and range resolution, we increase the degree of freedom by extending the length of phase coded signals. Pulse compression is applied to each frequency band component with the objective of minimizing sidelobes, using the minimax algorithm based on sequential quadratic programming (SQP) to obtain optimal phase coded waveforms. Simulation results demonstrate the method’s capability to flexibly design sparse frequency waveforms and reduce pulse compression sidelobe levels.

articleTitle: A Collaborative Federated Approach for Multi-Client SAR Target Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is widely used due to its capability for all-weather, all-day surveillance. However, the high costs and challenges of data acquisition often lead to a scarcity of data for individual satellites, impeding application expansion. Moreover, the sensitive nature of SAR data necessitates strict privacy requirements when exchanging information among clients. In this context, federated learning (FL) offers a promising solution that provides a distributed learning paradigm that leverages a single client’s data while preserving data privacy. Despite its potential, few studies have applied FL to multi-client SAR target recognition. This paper introduces a novel FL-based framework for collaborative multi-client SAR target recognition, enabling multiple satellites to collaboratively train a model without data sharing, thereby upholding data privacy. Experimental results demonstrate that it effectively preserves model accuracy while protecting privacy. Through iterative training, our framework’s performance converges towards that of centralized training, achieving a validation accuracy of 99.25%, which highlights its effectiveness and practical applicability.

articleTitle: Room Temperature Terahertz Magneto-optical Effect of Wafer-scale TbCaBi:Rare-earth Iron Garnet Single-crystal Film under Low Magnetic Field Intensity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A large-area single-crystal thick film of RIG was successfully created on a 3-inch GGG substrate using the liquid phase epitaxy technique. The RIG crystal had a thickness of approximately 390 micrometres. In the frequency range of 0.1 to 1.0 THz, the RIG material exhibited a notable refractive index of approximately 4.40, with a transmission rate of approximately 40% and an absorption rate varying between 6 and 50 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. Moreover, an investigation into the MO characteristics of the RIG material at THz frequencies was conducted utilising THz time-domain spectroscopy. The experimental results provided evidence of the presence and significance of the MO effect in the RIG crystal. To gain further insight, the THz Faraday rotation angle of RIG crystal was measured under the influence of an external magnetic field of 0.18 T using a THz-TDS system. It is noteworthy that the recorded Faraday rotation angle reached 17°, with the calculated Verdet constant for the RIG sample estimated to be approximately 140°/mm/T. These results highlight the distinctive characteristics of the large-area single-crystal thick film of RIG, which exhibits minimal losses, exceptional transmission capabilities, and robust MO effects within the THz spectral domain. Consequently, this material displays considerable potential for a diverse range of applications, including THz magnetic polarization.

articleTitle: AIEngiMentor: Scalable Deep Learning System for Hands-on Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this research, we proposed AIEngiMentor, a scalable system that assists students by automatically detecting and diagnosing errors in robotics and engineering assembly. It integrates deep learning models for multi-stage video segmentation and recognition, leveraging the Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) to handle both device- and component-level complexities. AIEngiMentor incorporates a Video-based Adaptive Integrity Algorithm (VAIA), which dynamically adjusts to step-by-step requirements from the Learning Management System (LMS). This architecture delivers real-time, precise feedback, even when processing low-quality or moving images with complex backgrounds. Unlike costly industry solutions, AIEngiMentor provides an affordable, practical alternative, ensuring the accuracy and safety of circuit and device connections by validating each step against LMS-defined criteria. Preliminary results show AIEngiMentor outperforms manual inspection in accuracy and enhances student learning by enabling focus on complex problem-solving tasks. The system's adaptability and precision also indicate potential for broader use in industrial automation and healthcare, where real-time error detection is critical.

articleTitle: ISAR Imaging Based on Probabilistic Pattern-Coupled Sparse Bayesian Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper we consider the inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging. To obtain high resolution target images, a novel probabilistic pattern-coupled sparse Bayesian learning (P-PCSBL) algorithm is proposed, which uses a probabilistic coupled prior model to represent the block sparse structural characteristics of ISAR images. The P-PCSBL algorithm is derived by variational Bayesian inference technique, where a decay factor is introduced to make the reconstructed signal sparser, thereby enabling the P-PCSBL to have the ability of suppressing noise. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the P-PCSBL has robust block sparse recovery performance and can obtain high quality ISAR images under low signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Radar Deception Jamming Recognition Based on GCN and Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: As the variety of radar jamming increases, there is a significant threat to radar systems. Anti-jamming techniques are crucial for addressing this major threat, with jamming recognition being the initial step. In this paper, we propose a multi-channel radar deception jamming recognition model based on graph convolution networks and transformer (GCN-T). Firstly, the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) is performed on the jamming signal to obtain the time-frequency distribution, which is modeled as an undirected graph. Secondly, GCN is used to acquire the spatial information in the data, transformer is used to capture the global features in the data. Finally, a fully connected layer is used to obtain the classification results. Extensive experiments on various jamming datasets and comparisons with existing methods are included to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed recognition model, and the recognition accuracy can reach 97.27 % to 99.14 %.

articleTitle: A Pursuit of Affective Computing System of EEG Multi-leads Time-Frequency Analysis and Multi-scale Entropy Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Precise electrophysiological feature fusion plays an important role in Brain-Computer Interaction technology. Geared to the critical demands of affective computing, this paper discusses the synergic effect among multiple encephalic regions and diverse emotions based on datasets of the human electroencephalogram (EEG). Based on the database of 14-leads EEG signals of 23 healthy subjects whose emotions are evoked by watching a video clip, we reconcile time-frequency analysis, power spectrum analysis, and multi-scale entropy analysis methods to collect multi-dimensional feature indexes from 5 EEG frequency bands for fusion comparison under 3 different emotion categories and 9 subcategories. Then we summarize the classification basis and carry out verification with statistical significance analysis. It is found that the sampling entropy of the stimuli state is gradually higher than that of the baseline state with the increase of frequency, and the indexes of the 3 kinds of emotion categories or 9 kinds of emotion subcategories are generally significantly different, which could provide an important basis for emotion recognition, and to untangling the time-frequency dynamics of EEG energy and entropy under varying emotions.

articleTitle: Style Adaptation and Deformable Convolution for Change Detection Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Remote sensing image change detection plays an important role in the fields of urban change detection, environmental protection and geologic hazard identification. Change targets are mostly irregular shapes, and it is a challenge to extract the change characteristics of remote sensing images using ordinary convolutional methods because the perceptual field of convolution is fixed. In this paper, a style adaptation and deformable convolution network(SDNet) is proposed and use a deformable convolutional network with residual links in SDNet. Global context and change characteristics details can be captured in a much shallower way. In addition, a special detection module is proposed for comparing multilevel features extracted from two branches, where the features of each branch are shared. In order to reduce the background and illumination of the diachronic images, a style adaptation technique is used to make the two images similar in style. The effectiveness of our proposed approach has been validated through experiments conducted on two public datasets.

articleTitle: Spatial Representation and Motion Attention Fusion Network for Few-shot Action Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Recently advancements in few-shot action recognition technology have been notable. However, certain challenges persist. One issue is that it is difficult to effectively model motion information, which results in subpar performance on datasets that emphasize motion itself. Another issue is the neglect of the integration of global background information and local detail information, leading to a lack of attention to appearance information in the models. To address these challenges, we propose Spatial Representation and Motion Attention (SRMA) fusion network. By constructing a dual-branch structure comprising Motion Attention Enrichment Module (MAEM) and Spatial Attention Enrichment Module (SAEM), the network simultaneously captures and models motion information while also focusing on the global and detailed information of the motion space. Furthermore, we integrate the cross-entropy loss from both branches as the loss function for the entire model. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms most other approaches across multiple datasets.

articleTitle: Efficient Underdetermined Wideband DOA Estimation Based on Single Uniform Linear Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: An efficient underdetermined wideband direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation method using a single uniform linear array (ULA) is proposed. The subband model is first obtained by applying frequency decomposition manner to the received signals. Then, apart from averaging subband DOA estimation results by employing narrowband sparse iterative covariance estimation (SPICE), a joint weighting wideband sparse iterative covariance estimation (JW-WSPICE) method is introduced by leveraging the information from multiple interesting subbands jointly. Compared to existing group-sparsity-based wideband DOA estimation methods, similar performance can be achieved while the selection of hyperparameter via a time-wasting search process is avoided.

articleTitle: A Nonlinear Clutter Map Detector for Rockfall Detection under Moving Debris and Dust Clutter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The rockfall detection requires the Doppler radar to detect falling rocks amidst strong and heterogeneous ground clutter. Clutter map detectors are employed to provide robust detection in such scenario. In addition to ground clutter, falling rock causes moving debris and dust clutter, whose intensity has abrupt changes and causes false alarms. This paper proposes a nonlinear clutter map detector to handle such clutter. Employing a nonlinear transform of the echo power, this detector generates a maximum and a minimum sequence which characterize the intensity of abrupt clutter and stable clutter, respectively. It provides stable performance in slow-changing ground clutter and abrupt moving debris and dust clutter. Field data shows that the proposed nonlinear iterative clutter map can reduce 76.2% of false alarms caused by debris dust clutter, without affecting the detection of falling rocks.

articleTitle: DRL-Based Service Function Chains Embedding Through Network Function Virtualization in STINs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Space-terrestrial integrated networks (STINs) are gaining increasing attention for their outstanding benefits in providing seamless connectivity, enhancing network resilience, increasing capacity, and expanding coverage.
