The combination of network function virtualization (NFV) and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is a promising candidate to boost the capability of STINs to deliver high-quality services. In this paper, a STIN architecture based on artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms and the process of embedding Service Function Chains (SFCs) into highly dynamic STINs are studied. Then, we propose an enhanced DRL-based SFCs embedding algorithm that initiates with a feature fusion phase of links, followed by aggregating the feature vectors of all nodes and their neighboring nodes to form context information. This context information is then used as part of the input state for the DRL-based SFCs embedding algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively reduce the latency of SFCs embedding when compared with other existing algorithms, thus showing the superiority of our proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Real-time Image Recognition System based on Ultra-Low-Latency Spiking Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Remote sensing technology plays an important role in many tasks such as natural disaster detection, weather and climate monitoring and military defense. Currently, remote sensing image processing predominantly relies on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Transformers, which require a huge amount of multiplication and addition operations, bringing pressure to the deployment of satellite platforms with strict power consumption and computing power constraints. Spiking neural network (SNN), where the signal is encoded as a spike train instead of analog values, significantly reduces energy consumption compared to traditional artificial neural network. This paper proposes an all-input parallel deployment approach that minimizes or eliminates interactions with off-chip memory, thereby accelerating inference speed and reducing power consumption. We deployed LeNet ultra-low latency SNN on the Xilinx VC709 Board. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed accelerator achieves a processing speed of 1240 frames per second, an accuracy rate of 98.14%, and a power consumption of only 0.745 Watts, making it well-suited for the low power and real-time requirements of remote sensing tasks.

articleTitle: An Image Deconvolution Method for Ground Penetrating Radar Based on Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) represents an established non-destructive detection technology. Enhancing resolution of low-frequency GPR data of a broad detection enables acquisition of high-quality GPR images, which is of great significance for interpreting and processing GPR data. Nevertheless, historical research methods have encountered challenges including decreased signal-to-noise ratio, instability in effects, computational complexity, etc. This paper introduces a generative adversarial network-based approach to enhance low-frequency GPR image resolution. The proposed technique effectively disentangles overlapping echoes and compresses hyperbolas to yield high-resolution images. In the field experiment, the proposed method is also successfully applied to the data of different frequency other than the training data, which proves the effectiveness and generalization of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Change Detection of Optical and SAR Based on Mixed Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Heterogeneous change detection can combine the advantages of multi-source images and capture change information more comprehensively. Firstly, the log-ratio operator and Hierarchical Fuzzy C-Means (HFCM) algorithm are used to suppress speckle noise and enhance the contrast between different regions to generate the initial change map. Then, the convolutional neural network is used as the main framework and the convolutional block attention module (CBAM) attention mechanism is combined to make the network focus on the key regions, improve the ability of model to recognize the changing regions, and obtain the final detection result. Experimental results on heterogeneous data sets of SAR and optical images demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve higher accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: Land Cover Classification for Polarimetric SAR Images Based on Global Membership Tensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The increasing resolution of PolSAR images makes it challenging to achieve satisfactory land cover classification performance with a single feature. Existing research considers combining multiple features to integrate polarimetric and multi-modal information from images, thereby better representing the diversity of land cover. Nevertheless, in the process of extracting multimodal information, the challenges of dimensionality disaster and dynamic range discrepancies persist, and how to effectively eliminate redundant information while preserving higher-order correlations among features remains a significant research challenge. This paper proposes a PolSAR land cover classification framework based on a global membership tensor, which avoids the dimensionality disaster and dynamic range difference issues by concatenating the pre-classified membership matrices, and utilizes Tucker decomposition to extract higher-order correlation information embedded in the tensor structure of the global membership tensor for final land cover classification. Experiments are carried out on the multi-frequency Hainan dataset acquired by the Aerospace Information Research Institute Chinese Academy of Sciences (AIRCAS). The experimental results indicate that the proposed classification framework based on global membership tensors successfully integrates polarimetric and texture features for effective land cover classification.

articleTitle: LOF Clustering-Based Adaptive CFAR Detection for Multi-Target ISAC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In multi-target integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) scenarios, conventional constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detectors often encounter performance degradation due to their reliance on fixed parameter settings, which lack adaptability to dynamic environments. By leveraging the local outlier factor (LOF) clustering algorithm, an adaptive detector named LOF-CFAR is proposed to deal with this challenge. Considering the sea clutter environment, LOF-CFAR identifies the interfering targets and sea spikes as undesirable outliers within the reference window, effectively mitigating the influence of target masking and improving the accuracy of clutter background estimation. Through simulation comparisons with conventional detectors that struggle to adapt to varying conditions, the proposed LOF-CFAR method demonstrates superior detection performance in multi-target scenarios, even without prior knowledge about the distribution and quantity of interfering targets.

articleTitle: Physics-informed neural network solution of the generalized (1+1) dimensional Sine-Gordon equation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: We employed a novel physics-informed neural networks (PINN) to tackle (1+1) dimensional Sine-Gordon equation (SGE). A test problem with known analytical solution is numerically solved to demonstrate the effectiveness of the PINN, and compared to standard explicit finite difference method (EFDM) and Chen-Charpentier et al.’s finite difference method (CCFDM). Although the three methods used show good agreement, our research shows that the EFDM results accord with the analytical solution the best. Given the consistent agreement between the numerical results obtained by all three methods and the analytical solution, all three methods are recommended as competitive options. The methods employed in this study can be a valuable asset for present and future model developers engaged in various nonlinear physical wave phenomena, such as solitons evolution or soliton interaction as well as optical pulses propagation in nonlinear media, including optical fibers.

articleTitle: Adaptive Interference Detection and Removal in SAR Images Based on the Order-2 Tracy-Widom Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel eigenvalue-based detector for adaptive detection of radio interference in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. The proposed method leverages the increased eigenvalues caused by interference in single-look-complex SAR image blocks, where the interference is expected to have a small set of eigenvalues, particularly with a dominating one. Specifically, the method segments the image into multiple blocks, computes the eigenvalues of each block’s covariance matrix, and compares the largest eigenvalue with a threshold to determine the presence of interference under the criteria of constant false alarm rate. The threshold is determined by the order-2 Tracy-Widom distribution of the largest eigenvalue for each image block under the assumption of image homogeneity. The proposed detector is integrated with our previously proposed block subspace filter for adaptive interference detection and removal. Experimental results on Sentinel-1 double-polarization and Gaofen-3 HV-polarization images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method on adaptive detection and suppression of interference artefacts in SAR images.

articleTitle: Real-Time Frequency Synchronization for High Maneuverability Platform Radar System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The pulsed alternate phase synchronization performs well in spaceborne bistatic radar system while relying on data post-processing. This prevents its application in missions equipped with low stability frequency sources.In this paper, a real-time frequency synchronization scheme for high maneuverability platform (HMP) radar system is proposed. The synchronization performance of this scheme is firstly predicted. It reveals that the estimates are biased by a dominant deviation related to the platform acceleration and pulse alternate interval. The other errors are detailed and the error compensation strategy is briefly provided. Additionally, a comparison is made between two frequency estimation methods and their corresponding applicable scenarios are explained, respectively. Finally, the computer simulation verifies the performance prediction.

articleTitle: SAR Image Stitching Method for M×N SAR Sub-images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to obtain SAR images with a wider field of view and higher resolution, it is often necessary to stitch image sequences taken from different perspectives within the same scene.This paper presents an image stitching method for M × N SAR sub-images. The method mainly consists of the following steps: sub-image registration, global optimization of sub-image offsets, antenna pattern inverse distortion processing, and seam blending of sub-images. This method can obtain SAR images with wider field of view and higher resolution.

articleTitle: Non-local Architecture Net Semantic Segmentation Network for Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Remote sensing images play a vital role in geographic information acquisition and resource management. However, challenges such as complex terrain variations, varying object scales, and diverse lighting and weather conditions often hinder the accuracy of edge segmentation and small-object detection in existing methods. Traditional approaches typically rely on stacking multiple convolutional layers to expand the receptive field, which not only increases computational costs but also results in incomplete edge segmentation and poor recognition of small objects.To address these limitations, this paper introduces a Non-Local U-net (NLUnet) model based on the U-net architecture. NLUnet builds upon U-net’s strengths in local feature extraction by integrating a non-local mechanism that captures long-range dependencies, thereby effectively expanding the receptive field. This approach enhances the capture of global contextual information and reduces computational costs, particularly excelling in complex scenes. NLUnet significantly improves the segmentation of small objects and the completeness of edge segmentation.Experimental results on the Aerial Imagery dataset demonstrate the superior performance of NLUnet, achieving an IoU of 93%, an OA of 92%, and an average F1 score of 91%. NLUnet outperforms other methods in small-object segmentation, underscoring its effectiveness in complex remote sensing scenarios.

articleTitle: A Parameterized Generalized Radon-Fourier Transform-Based Method for Asteroid Detection Using Ground-Based Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The Generalized Radon-Fourier Transform is a powerful algorithm designed to integrate echo energy within complex motion models. Traditionally, the approach has been to convert the echo energy integration challenge into a parameterized model matching problem, typically using polynomial models. However, when dealing with the intricate motion of asteroids, polynomial models can lead to issues related to high computational order and significant complexity. To address these challenges, this paper introduces an innovative method that employs orbital elements as a parameterized model, effectively lowering the matching order and simplifying computational demands. Simulation results demonstrate a marked improvement in integration outcomes when compared to traditional polynomial models.

articleTitle: Small Object Tracking in Satellite Videos with Gaussian Wasserstein Distance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Tracking small objects is a major challenge in satellite video object tracking. The traditional metric, i.e. intersection over union (IoU) of bounding boxes, is sensitive to target scale, while minor location deviation can cause a significant drop. Especially for tiny objects occupying very limited pixels, the boxes may not overlap or be fully inclusive and thus the IoU metric fails to provide a consistent measure. This paper proposes a new method named GWD-SiamFC++, which introduces a novel bounding box metric based on the Gaussian Wasserstein distance (GWD) to the classical SiamFC++ framework to address this issue. GWD is a continuous and consistent metric, offering a more precise representation of pixel weights within bounding boxes and accurately distinguishing between non-overlapping or fully inclusive boxes. Besides, it features scale invariance and is insensitive to object size, making it more suitable for small object tracking. Furthermore, nonlinear transformations are devised based on the GWD concept and yield the training normalized Gaussian Wasserstein distance (TrGWD) and testing normalized Gaussian Wasserstein distance (TeGWD), which are integrated into the classical SiamFC++ framework for the training and the testing phases, respectively. Experimental results on the SatSOT dataset reveal that the proposed method attains a success rate of 48.2% and a precision rate of 70.6%, and maintains satisfying computational efficiency.

articleTitle: A method for enhancing infrared small target images under complex sky backgrounds
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Infrared target detection is currently widely used in both military and civilian fields. Due to the lower resolution of infrared images compared to visible light images and the lack of texture information in small targets, the quality of infrared small target images is often poor and not suitable for direct detection. Therefore, enhancing low-quality infrared small target images is a necessary step before object detection can be performed. This article presents a method for enhancing infrared images of small targets. The process begins with applying guided filtering to the original image. The resulting detail layer is then used as a guided image for a second guided filtering of the base layer, producing a second detail layer. Additionally, a novel approach to local contrast enhancement is introduced, which applies contrast enhancement specifically to this secondary detail layer. Experimental results has been demonstrated that the enhancement method proposed in this paper significantly improves the visibility of the target area while reducing background interference, without losing information about small targets. Additionally, this method outperforms other common techniques in terms of enhancement effect, as shown in comparative experiments.

articleTitle: Fully PolSAR Urban Building Generation via Re-expanding Polarimetric Feature Guided DDPM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) can produce results of high quality within many fields, such as generating and editing images. Based on the recently proposed method PFG-DDPM, we achieve the urban building generation of fully polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) image in this paper. Briefly, the double-bounce scattering is selected as the guide feature to re-expand the PFG-DDPM model (i.e., proposing a new model rPFG-DDPM with the double-bounce scattering feature Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">db</inf> and PFG-DDPM). Besides, to demonstrate its effectiveness, one PolSAR urban building dataset obtained from ALOS PolSAR data is constructed as well. Experimental results indicate that the images generated by our method rPFG-DDPM are much closer to real images than the original DDPM method.

articleTitle: Design and Characteristic Analysis of P4-Costas Composite Modulation Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The low probability of intercept (LPI) radar waveforms can reduce the effectiveness of enemy electronic interference. Composite modulation signals combine two or more modulation techniques, improving the LPI capability of the signal as well as its resistance to various types of interference. By using frequency and phase composite modulation, the spectrum can be expanded, the power spectral density can be reduced, and the signal can be more difficult to intercept. Current modulation radar waveforms exhibit certain low probability of intercept characteristics, but further improvement and enhancement are needed. This paper designs a radar waveform based on the composite modulation of linear frequency modulation (LFM), P4 code, and Costas code to enhance the LPI performance of radar emissions. Simulation experiments verify that, compared to radar waveforms with LFM and Barker code composite modulation, this new radar waveform performs better in terms of LPI characteristics and also shows improved anti-jamming capability.

articleTitle: Clutter Suppression Method for Passive Bistatic Radar Based on Clutter Time Delay Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the rapid development of various electronic interference technologies in modern warfare, PBR has gradually become a research hotspot in the field of radar in recent years, due to their layout mode of separate transmitter and receiver, which enables covert detection, flexible deployment, and strong battlefield survivability. However, because of this layout pattern, PBR also faces a large amount of short-range multipath and ground clutter interference during operation, causing targets to be submerged in the clutter and difficult to identify. In response to the above issues, this paper improves the classical time-domain clutter suppression method ECA by using clutter time delay estimation method, solving the problem of traditional ECA suppressing targets mixed in while suppressing short-range clutter. Simulation and measured data verify the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: A Time-varying Modulation Interference Suppression Method Based on Mutual Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Time-varying modulation targets disrupt the correlation between the echo signal and the reference signal by modulating the phase of the radar’s transmitted signal, thereby reducing pulse compression gain and significantly degrading radar target detection performance. Essentially, time-varying modulation targets impose a multiplicative interference on the radar signal. However, most existing suppression interference techniques are designed to counter additive interference, such as intermittent sampling repeater jamming. In this paper, a time-varying modulation interference suppression method based on mutual cancellation is proposed. Specifically, considering the characteristics of multiplicative interference and radar systems, this method involves the joint design of dual baseline transmission waveforms that are orthogonal in the frequency domain with constrained spectra and exhibit excellent matched filtering performance when multiplied in the time domain. Based on this, we formulate a non-convex optimization problem with the root mean square error between the weighted preset spectrum and the spectrum to be optimized as the objective function, and the constant amplitude of the transmitted signal as a constraint, proposing an effective solution method for this problem. Finally, some numerical simulation results are presented to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Radar range Extended target detection using Prototypical Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In radar ground stationary or slow-moving target detection, the target detection algorithm based on High-Resolution Range Profile (HRRP) is an important technical approach. Traditional target detection algorithms based on HRRP are difficult to apply in target detection tasks under multiple terrains. To this end, this paper proposes a feature detection algorithm based on deep learning for target polarized HRRP. This paper studies an end-to-end target detection algorithm based on prototypical networks. This algorithm utilizes prototypical networks to extract deep features from input HRRP and constructs the feature distribution of clutter. Then, it calculates the distance between the features of the input test sample and the clutter feature center, and compares it with the threshold calculated based on the false alarm probability to complete the detection. Under the backgrounds of bare soil and highway, the algorithm improves by 22% compared to the traditional energy detection algorithm for two types of vehicle targets at a signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) of 0dB.

articleTitle: Domain-Adaptive Deep Transfer Learning for Cross-Modal Heterogeneous Image Matching under Label-Scarce Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Deep learning has made significant strides in cross-modal heterogeneous remote sensing image matching, yet it remains heavily dependent on annotated target scene data for training models. Under label-scarce constraints, domain discrepancies between actual test data and training data often result in a decline in the performance of trained models. To tackle this challenge, a domain adaptation method is put forth for consideration in the paper for cross-modal heterogeneous image matching. The method achieves the transformation between the images of the existing scene and the target scene through style transfer, and narrows the domain offset between the images of the target scene generated by the transformation of images of the existing scene and the original target scene through adversarial learning. It aligns the target domain with unlabeled information and the source domain with labeled information from both the image and feature perspectives, thereby solving the matching tasks inside the target domain through the application of knowledge from the source domain. Experiments were conducted using two different optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) cross-modal datasets, alternating as both target and source domains in training and testing. Results confirmed that compared to current traditional matching methods and deep learning matching methods, our method demonstrates feasibility and effectiveness in cross-dataset transfer, effectively reducing the dependency on annotated data for matching tasks in the target scene.

articleTitle: Ground Clutter Suppression Based on Lifting Wavelet Transform for Airship-borne Weather Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Ground clutter is one of the significant challenges faced by airship-borne weather radar in observing weak meteorological targets. Traditional ground clutter suppression methods will inevitably cause the loss of useful weather signals. In this paper, an adaptive threshold ground clutter suppression method based on lifting wavelet transform is proposed. In the wavelet domain, weather signals are often found in other high-frequency layers, whereas ground clutter signals are dispersed in the low-frequency layer by wavelet decomposition. By compressing the large value coefficients identified as clutter components with an adaptive threshold, ground clutter signals in radar echoes can be effectively removed while preserving weather signals to the maximum extent. The proposed method is validated through simulations, ground observation results with airship-borne weather radar and real data from the C-band weather radar.

articleTitle: A Radar Super Resolution Algorithm for Cluster UAV Targets Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The development of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and their innovative "swarm" concept have presented a formidable challenge to public security and battlefield confrontation. Therefore, there is an urgent necessity for UAV detection technology to attain precise estimation of UAVs, thereby enabling comprehensive surveillance and assessment of clustered UAVs. In response to the detection demands posed by UAV swarms, this paper introduces a super-resolution method tailored for UAVs radar detection. Distinguishing from conventional spatial domain super-resolution approaches, this research formulates a convolution model specifically deduced within the Range-Doppler domain for swarm targets. Then, a sparse regularization method is utilized to construct the objective function for super-resolution estimation. Finally, a multiplicative iterative algorithm is employed to estimate the clustered targets within individual Range-Doppler units. The simulation outcomes have verified the effectiveness of proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Optimal Bi-ISAR Imaging Arc Selection Method with Bistatic Angle Derivative Constraint
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Bistatic inverse synthetic aperture radar (Bi-ISAR) imaging has a broad application in space surveillance and missile defense. However, the imaging quality for bistatic ISAR is closely related to the choice of the imaging arc. Aiming at the need of high resolution imaging of aerial moving targets, an optimal Bi-ISAR imaging arc selection method with bistatic angle derivative constraint is proposed. Firstly, the Bi-ISAR imaging model of moving target is constructed, and the expression of bistatic slant range history related to the bistatic angle derivative is derived. Then, the boundary of the Bi-ISAR imaging performance is theoretically analyzed from the dimensions of range cell migration (RCM) and azimuth-quadratic phase (AQP), and the corresponding constraints are figured out. Finally, based on the minimum fusion criterion, the optimal Bi-ISAR imaging arc are selected. The processing results of both simulation data and measured data verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Whittle Index Policy for Dynamic Task Scheduling of Multi-Platform Multi-Sensor Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Task scheduling is key to multi-platform multi-sensor systems, which faces challenges of complex sensor combination and high computational complexity. To deal with these challenges, this research introduces the concept of a sensor resource pool to characterize available sensors, and formulate the optimization problem as a restless multi-armed bandit (RMAB) process, considering both task execution and the limitations of the sensor resource pool. To tackle the formulated RMAB problem, we apply Whittle relaxation. Accordingly, the Whittle index policy is introduced for the dynamic task scheduling of multi-platform multi-sensor systems. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed policy.

articleTitle: Cross-Domain Detection Transformer with Multi-view Adaptive Feature Alignment in Remote Sensing Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) techniques are crucial for remote sensing object detection, designed to address performance degradation caused by the domain gap between training and test data. These methods leverage unlabeled target domain data, thus alleviating the high costs associated with data annotation. Recent developments in Detection Transformers (DETR) have simplified the detection pipeline and attracted significant research interest. Building on this architecture, we introduce an unsupervised domain adaptation detector for remote sensing object detection. Specifically, we introduce a multi-view adaptive feature alignment module that initially captures domain-specific features in complex backgrounds by leveraging a cross-attention mechanism. Subsequently, we employ contrastive learning to enforce the aggregation of domain-specific features from various perspectives, thereby improving the accuracy of feature alignment. Moreover, we demonstrate that integrating the self-training framework into DETR-based detectors can significantly mitigate the domain gap by further utilizing unlabeled data in the target domain. We validated the effectiveness and generalizability of our method across two remote sensing cross-domain detection scenarios using four public datasets.

articleTitle: Rotated Detection of SAR Ship Target based on Angle Prediction of Continuous Boundary
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In deep learning-based rotated synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target detection, the boundary discontinuity of angle prediction is a key problem that affects the prediction accuracy. Since the convolutional neural network (CNN) is a continuous function, the output of the function is continuous, but the boundary of the angle prediction is discontinuous, so it is impossible to use continuous CNN to fit the discontinuous angle prediction. Based on this, this paper proposes to use phase-shifting coder (PSC) to encode the angle. The PSC itself can be predicted using continuous CNNs, so the PSC coding can alleviate the boundary discontinuity problem to a large extent. Thus, accurate and continuous angle prediction can be achieved by using CNNs. The experiment results on the HRSIC dataset also show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Study on Insect and Bird Echo Recognition Using Machine Learning-Based X-Band Dual-Polarization Weather Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Weather radars have shown great potential in the field of aerial ecological monitoring. Leveraging a network of weather radars allows for the analysis of insect and bird migration patterns on a continental scale, thus better protecting bird habitats and preventing pest outbreaks. However, as the radar beam propagates, the observed altitude increases with distance, resulting in a decrease in low-altitude monitoring coverage by the weather radar network. To address this issue, China's new generation weather radar network (CINRAD) has extensively deployed X-band dual-polarization radars. However, the application of operational X-band radars for ecological monitoring is unprecedented, and the impact of wavelength on the scattering characteristics of insects and birds is unknown. To solve this problem, this study collects X-band radar echo datasets of insects and birds through joint observations with S-band and X-band radars, and further develops a machine learning-based algorithm to identify insect and bird echoes. By training the model to converge, the final recognition accuracy reached 83.11%. The algorithm was applied to two typical cases, confirming its robustness.

articleTitle: Fusion of Ascending and Descending Lutan-1 for Building Extraction in decision level
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Recent years, SAR has been widely utilized in building extraction for it can provide rich spatial information and cannot be influenced by weather. However, most researchers only use one single orbit of SAR, which can be significantly affected by SAR shadow and layover. Using both ascending and descending SAR can effectively resolve this problem for they contain complementary information from opposite site. Meanwhile, the fusion method is important for the extraction. Therefore, in this manuscript, we proposed a novel method for applying both ascending and descending SAR in decision level. Lutan-1 is utilized for its high resolution and stability. We reached the precision as 92.87%, while that for only use ascending and descending SAR are 86.20% and 83.45% respectively. This result indicates that our proposed method can effectively extract buildings and shows the opportunities of Lutan-1 in more fields.

articleTitle: Covert Communication Parasitized in SAR Signal Based on Active Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is an active microwave remote sensing technology with the advantages of all-day and all-weather operation, enabling the acquisition of high-resolution and large-scale surface reflectance information. Active Frequency Selective Surface (AFSS) consists of wave-absorbing metamaterials controllable by an external excitation source and is widely used in communication and stealth fields. This paper explores a covert communication method parasitized in SAR signal based on AFSS and presents a preliminary analysis of its communication performance. This method offers a novel approach for submarine communication or other scenarios requiring low communication rates but high communication security.

articleTitle: Waveform Design for Full Polarization Accurate Jamming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Interrupted-sampling repeater jamming is the main deception jamming method at present. Since there is no polarization modulation, full polarization Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar can easily identify jamming from the polarization domain. In this paper, an accurate jamming method for full polarization MIMO radar is proposed. The radar angular signal is polarization modulated to approximate real target return and target polarization scattering matrix. The polarization accurate jamming signal is obtained by solving the approximate problem with constant modulus constraint based on Majorization-Minimization (MM) algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed method can generate polarization accurate jamming signals which are similar to real target return in waveform domain and polarization domain.

articleTitle: FDA-MIMO beampattern optimization with complex circle manifold
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper investigates the design of beampattern in an Frequency Diverse Array (FDA)-Multiple-Input MultipleOutput (MIMO) radar by jointly optimizing the transmit waveform and receive filter considering the environment of jammers at specific range-angle intervals. In this regard, the optimization problem is formulated by forcing the constant modulus constraint on the waveform. For solving the devised non-convex problem, an alternating optimization procedure is introduced, where the optimization problem is partitioned into two subproblems related to waveform and filter, respectively. Particularly, the former is solved by utilizing a projection, descent, and retraction (PDR) method leveraging the complex circle manifold, whereas the latter resorts to a quadratic programming model. Hence, a desired beampattern with deep nulls at specific range and angle intervals can be formed. Finally, numerical results illustrate the convergence performance of the developed algorithm and the effectiveness of the devised beampattern in suppressing jammers.

articleTitle: Research on Scattering Characteristics of Insect Swarms Based on Simulation Software
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Density inversion is a key metric for observing large-scale insect migration using radar. However, there are still many unknowns in the study of insect population scattering characteristics, such as whether there is multiple scattering among individuals and whether physical shielding between individuals affects their scattering behavior. We conducted modeling to investigate the effects of multiple scattering on insect migration patterns, as well as the impact of physical occlusion. We first calculated the average RCS (radar cross section) at different incidence angles by creating an individual insect model. Then, we established a model for uniform insect distribution to study the impact of insect spacing on multiple scattering. We found that when the ratio of insect spacing to wavelength reaches 2-2.5 times, the average relative error between the RCS of the uniform insect distribution model and the RCS of a single insect is less than 20%. Finally, we established two types of insect physical occlusion models. The simulation results indicate that the average scattering intensity of the shielding direction aligns with the simple sum of individual scattering intensities, suggesting that the influence of individual physical shielding on the scattering characteristics of the population is negligible.

articleTitle: An algebraic method for moving source localization using TDOA and FDOA measurements with receiver location errors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper proposes a solution for locating a moving source using time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) and frequency-difference-of-arrival (FDOA) measurements while considering random errors in receiver locations. The proposed solution accounts for these errors to reduce estimation error, and it is analytically shown to achieve Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) accuracy for far-field sources under mild approximations and small Gaussian noise. Numerical simulations validate and support the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Application of ARIMA and Annual Variations Models in InSAR for Permafrost Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Temperature fluctuations are expected to drive nonlinear patterns in annual permafrost variations. The InSAR technique effectively captures these changes by tracking surface deformation over time. However, atmospheric phase noise often requires spatiotemporal filtering, which reduces temporal resolution for nonlinear signals. Additionally, the influence of temperature on annual freeze-thaw cycles remains underrepresented in InSAR models. This study presents a method to improve InSAR time-series analysis in permafrost regions. Rather than relying on traditional filtering that limits temporal resolution based on convolution kernel size, we utilize the autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) model to isolate nonlinear deformation signals. Furthermore, we extract annual variation parameters from the InSAR time-series deformation data. Synthetic experiments under varying noise delays reveal accuracy gains between 27.8% and 55.3% in nonlinear deformation analysis. Applying Sentinel-1 datasets from 2017 to 2021 and ground data from northern Alaska, we achieve a time-series deformation accuracy improvement of over 22%.

articleTitle: Multi-person Respiration Detection Method Based on Complex Independent Vector Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Frequency modulated continuous wave(FMCW) radar is widely used for non-contact vital signs detection due to its high accuracy and performance. Blind source separation (BSS) algorithms have become essential for multi-person respiration detection due to their low hardware dependence and robustness. However, traditional blind source separation algorithms only handle signals from a single range bin. Due to spectrum leakage, respiratory signals may appear in multiple range bins. Mutual interference between the respiratory signals of multiple people can lead to the failure of range bin selection. This paper proposes a complex independent vector analysis (IVA) algorithm based on FMCW radar for multi-person respiration detection. The method avoids the range bin selection problem by considering multiple range bins as multiple datasets for joint solutions. Meanwhile, the method overcomes the alignment ambiguity problem in traditional independent component analysis(ICA). The experimental results show that this multi-person respiration detection method based on FMCW radar is feasible.

articleTitle: Crag monitoring based on GNSS InBSAR: first image
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System based bistatic Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (GNSS-based InBSAR) is an effective means for deformation monitoring. But researches focused on dangerous rock scenario are rare. In this paper, GNSS-based InBSAR system is firstly used to observe typical dangerous rock masses in Chongqing. The results show that the system is suitable for dangerous rock mass.

articleTitle: Model Switching Detection-Aided Adaptive Transition Probability Matrix IMM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In conventional interactive multiple model (IMM) algorithm, the fixed transition probability matrix results in slow model switching and low tracking accuracy. Existing adaptive transition probability IMM algorithms still suffer from large errors during model switching. This paper proposes a model switching detection-aided adaptive transition probability matrix IMM algorithm. To deal with model switch time delay, a transition probability correction function is established, capable of dynamically and rapidly adjusting the transition probabilities. And a model switching detection method is proposed to improve tracking accuracy during model switching. By the numerical simulation, the method's efficacy is substantiated and confirmed.

articleTitle: A Recalibration Method for Historical SAR Data Through Inter-Satellite Alignment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Recalibration of historical Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data facilitates the adjustment of data that have not undergone radiometric calibration or have suboptimal calibration accuracy, ensuring consistency among diverse historical images. This consistency is crucial for long-term sequential remote sensing quantitative applications. Traditional calibration methods based on artificial calibrators require the presence of such calibrators in historical data, a condition often unfulfilled, rendering the recalibration process impractical. In contrast, cross-calibration methods based on natural scenes only necessitate contemporaneous and co-located calibrated satellite data to recalibrate historical datasets. However, existing cross-calibration methods for historical data recalibration typically utilize data from a single SAR sensor. This approach inadequately corrects system errors within the SAR sensor, resulting in low calibration accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a radiometric recalibration method for historical SAR data based on inter-satellite data alignment. Initially, suitable data from different SAR satellite sensors operating in the same frequency band are selected. Subsequently, a resampling method is employed to construct cross-calibration data pairs with consistent resolution. Finally, the recalibration coefficients are fitted using a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) to mitigate the impact of anomalous interference values. Experiment results on Sentinel-1A and GF-3A data demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared to traditional fitting methods, the proposed method reduced calibration errors in saline-alkali and bare land areas by 0.82 dB and 0.77 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Efficient Position Determination Using Low-Rank Matrix Completion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In increasingly complex electromagnetic environments, distributed systems are crucial for passive target localization. These systems, consisting of spatially dispersed sensing nodes, collaboratively enhance the localization of target signals. Particularly in blind localization tasks within low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) settings, distributed passive localization offers improved positioning performance. Traditional passive localization methods typically follow a two-step process: initially extracting parameters, such as the direction of arrivals (DOA), from raw data, followed by localizing the target. This approach often requires a high SNR. In contrast, Direct Position Determination (DPD) methods directly leverage all the received raw data, thus overcoming the constraints of the two-step process. However, DPD methods involve a time-consuming grid search within the area of interest. To address this challenge, we propose a radiation source localization method that utilizes random sampling. This method capitalizes on the low-rank properties of the grid search matrix used in DPD methods. By integrating random sampling with low-rank matrix completion algorithms, our approach efficiently localizes the radiation source. Simulation results demonstrate that this random sampling-based method significantly reduces computational demands while preserving high localization accuracy.

articleTitle: Open-Set Remote Sensing Object Detection Using Edge Information Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Typically, remote sensing object detection is limited to a closed-set detection environment. A problem is that when detecting the new untrained but valuable objects, they are incorrectly classified as known classes or background. In this paper, a method is proposed for open-set detection of remote sensing objects, which assigns robust pseudo-labels to unknown classes and trains the network to recognize new classes. The main idea is to combine the feature information of remote sensing objects and select regions in the image that are likely to contain unknown classes to form pseudo-labels. Through supervised learning, the network can distinguish and detect both known and unknown classes. Remote sensing objects are observed from an Earth observation perspective, with rich edge information. Pseudo-labels for unknown classes are obtained using image convolution features and object edge information. Experimental results show that this method outperforms existing methods in open-set target detection for remote sensing images.

articleTitle: An improved adaptive CFAR detector for non-homogeneous environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The conventional variability index constant false alarm rate (VI-CFAR) algorithm experiences significant degradation in detection performance when interference targets are located on both sides of the reference window. To mitigate this challenge, this paper proposes an enhanced VITM-CFAR algorithm which integrates the trimmed mean CFAR (TM-CFAR) method, evaluating the clutter environment of the cell under test (CUT) and adaptive deleting the front and rear reference half-windows. The method further categorizes the clutter edge environment into high and low-power areas. Depending on the partial deletion of reference units, the smallest-of CFAR (SO-CFAR) method is employed in multi-target environment and low-power region of the clutter edge, while the greatest-of CFAR (GO-CFAR) method is utilized in high-power zones. Monte Carlo simulation experiments are conducted to assess the effectiveness of the VITM-CFAR method. The results indicate that the proposed method has low CFAR loss under homogeneous environment, and is more robust under non-homogeneous environment, showcasing superior performanc against multi-target interference and clutter edge protection.

articleTitle: Photonic-assisted Wideband and Low Noise MMW Generation Based on Gain-Switched Optical Frequency Comb
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: We propose a photonic-assisted MMW generator based on externally injected gain-switched optical frequency comb. It is capable of operating from 10 to 100 GHz. The phase noise remains consistent across the whole range below -100 dBc/Hz@10kHz.

articleTitle: Suppression of Multi-Range-False-Target Jamming for Radar Network Based on Same-Origin Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to the limited perspective of single-station radar, its anti-jamming capability is limited when countering multi-range-false-target deception jamming. To solve this, an anti-jamming method based on radar network is proposed. This method first creates a target localization model based on transmitter and receiver stations. It then performs nearest-neighbor association and same-origin measurement detection on the localization results from each station and finally fuses measurement results to achieve accurate target localization. Simulation results demonstrate that this method effectively suppresses jamming and achieves precise target localization.

articleTitle: Real-time Implementation of Phased Array Radar Tracking Algorithm Based on Embedded GPU
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The embedded Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) module, which includes both Central Processing Unit (CPU) and GPU processors, can be easily integrated into radar systems, offering high performance and flexibility. Phased array radar tracking algorithm involves numerous modules with poor parallelism between them, leading to significant data blocking issues during sequential execution. Traditional implementations using CPUs or DSPs are time-consuming and inefficient. To address this problem, this paper proposes a real-time implementation solution based on embedded GPU. The solution decouples logic-intensive and computation-intensive tasks in the algorithm and maps them separately to the CPU and GPU within the embedded GPU module. Then three-level hybrid parallel processing method is adopted, which is based on grid-stride-based intra-kernel thread parallelism, CUDA stream asynchronous parallelism and CPU thread parallelism in order to realize real-time processing of radar echo data. Verification experiment using real measured data indicates that the proposed real-time implementation solution achieves significant acceleration with no loss of accuracy on the Jetson AGX Xavier embedded GPU platform, markedly improving tracking efficiency.

articleTitle: Ground-based Radar Tomography for the Moon Based on ADMM-Net
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Ground-based radar offers the advantage of all-weather, all-day operation and has become a significant facility for acquiring high-resolution 3-D images of the Moon. However, traditional tomographic imaging is limited by the observation conditions, particularly in the height dimension. While capable of super-resolution imaging, the existing compressive sensing algorithms struggle with optimizing hyperparameters during the iteration. To address this issue, a ground-based radar tomography super-resolution imaging method for the Moon based on a self-supervised compressive sensing network is proposed. This method redefines the tomographic imaging process as an optimization problem utilizing the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Subsequently, it extends the ADMM iteration process into a multi-layer neural network with trainable hyperparameters, referred to as ADMM-Net. The validity and robustness of the proposed method are verified through simulation experiments of lunar scenes.

articleTitle: YOLOv8-WRTNet: Instance Segmentation for Aerial Images under Weak and Repetitive Texture Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of insufficient accuracy of image detection and segmentation of traditional YOLOv8 methods in weak texture environments, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv8 method, YOLOv8-WRTNet, to enhance the accuracy and robustness of target detection segmentation. The algorithm firstly enhances the diversity and stability of feature expression by introducing an improved version of C2f module, which utilises feature separation, convolution processing and residual joining. Secondly, the BiFormer module is adopted to strengthen the model’s ability to capture and process multi-level features through dual-path feature fusion and multi-scale attention mechanism, which particularly enhances the target recognition ability in complex repetitive texture environments. Subsequently, combined with the FocalNext module, the model’s target detection and segmentation ability in complex backgrounds is enhanced through the integration of inflated depth convolution and jump connection, which effectively fuses fine-grained local information with coarse-grained global information. Finally, a custom Wise IoU loss function is designed and introduced to further improve the detection robustness of the model in complex scenes by dynamically adjusting the matching accuracy of the model to the target boundary. The experimental results show that the improved YOLOv8 method improves both accuracy and performance in the detection and segmentation tasks dealing with weak texture environments and complex backgrounds.

articleTitle: Monitoring The Cropping Pattern Of Paddy Fields In Hilly Mountainous Areas Using Time-Series Remote Sensing Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, a time-series surface reflectance dataset was constructed based on the time-series Sentinel-2 satellite data with topographic radiation and atmospheric corrections. A Shallow Water Index (SWI) was constructed based on the spectral characteristics of aquatic crop samples. Third, an algorithm for monitoring the cropping pattern of paddy fields was established by combining the time-series SWI and Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI). The algorithm was applied to monitor the cropping patterns of paddy fields in the Yongchuan District, Chongqing, China. Finally, samples from the field investigations were used to validate the results. The validation results showed that out of the 150 aquatic crop sample points, the monitoring algorithm recognized 143 points as aquatic crops with an accuracy of approximately 95.3%.

articleTitle: EM-based Batch Algorithm for Trajectory Estimation of Multiple Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This study investigates the trajectory clustering problem in the presence of multiple moving targets which are approximated by straight motion over the observation interval and monitored by a radar sensor network. The assumption is that the nodes in the network lack the knowledge of the measurements’ association with each target, causing challenging estimation and classification tasks. To solve this problem, a novel unsupervised classifier based on expectation-maximization algorithm is devised by exploiting the latent variable model combined with cyclic estimation methods to obtain closed-form updates for the unknown parameters and build up a maximum a posteriori rule allowing for target measurement clustering. Finally, we analyze the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm through simulation experiments in a scenario with trajectory intersections.

articleTitle: Passive Synthetic Aperture Localization of Moving Radiation Source Based on High-order Polynomial Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: For the passive localization problem of moving radiation source, this paper proposes a synthetic aperture passive localization method based on high-order slant range model. This method establishes the coupling relationships between the position and velocity parameters of the airborne observation station and the radiation source according to the high-order instantaneous slant range model. Then, the received signal data is rearranged in two dimensions using the synthetic aperture related technique and various modulation terms in the azimuth of the signal data are accurately estimated. The position and velocity information of the radiation source are inverted based on the obtained modulation terms. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Improved Two-step Imaging Method for Sliding Spotlight SAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Sliding spotlight SAR often suffers from Doppler ambiguity due to its wide Doppler bandwidth. The commonly processing method currently is the two-step algorithm, which uses deramp preprocessing to remove Doppler ambiguity and then uses commonly SAR imaging algorithms for imaging. However, under certain conditions, deramp processing can cause ambiguity in the azimuth time domain. The conditions for Doppler ambiguity and time-domain ambiguity are proposed, and the improved two-step imaging method for sliding spotlight SAR is proposed to achieve sliding SAR imaging without azimuth time domain and frequency domain ambiguity.

articleTitle: Fast Processing Techniques for Ground-Based Differential Interferometric Radar Based on Embedded GPU
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: For ground-based differential interferometric radar systems, aiming at the problems of low operation-speed performance, a rapid processing technology was studied based on embedded GPU. To achieve effective processing of high-speed data streams, an architecture design based on message queues is adopted in this paper, enabling parallel data transmission and processing. Message queue, as an efficient middleware technology, not only ensure reliable data transmission but also enable decoupling of data reception and processing through an asynchronous communication mechanism. This significantly enhances the system's throughput and response speed. To further optimize performance, condition variables are introduced to control the concurrency strategy in the message queue. When there is data to be processed in the message queue, the condition variable wakes up waiting threads to start processing messages; when there is no data to be processed, it suspends the threads. This mechanism ensures the maximization of system resource utilization. Parallel reduction techniques based on shared memory are adopted to achieve rapid selection of persistent scatterer. Shared memory reduces data access times, and the use of parallel reduction techniques is particularly effective when handling large-scale datasets. The results show that for 200 images with dimensions of 634 by 100 pixels, the method presented in this paper improves the processing speed by 16% compared to traditional methods, effectively enhancing the processing efficiency of ground-based differential interferometric radar systems.

articleTitle: Prospective Evaluation of Wearable ECG Monitoring for Heart Failure Assessment: Signal Processing and HRV Analysis in NYHA Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The swift progress in wearable device technology has permitted electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring to be conducted beyond the confines of traditional hospital settings, offering heart failure (HF) patients the benefit of affordable and prolonged home monitoring. This study addresses the challenges inherent in wearable ECG monitoring, including lower accuracy and increased susceptibility to motion artifacts and environmental noise, by employing a series of signal processing strategies to enhance ECG signal quality. We prospectively collected ECG signals from a cohort of hospitalized HF patients at West China Hospital using wearable devices, preprocessed the data to extract high-quality RR intervals, and developed a model using a random forest classifier combined with recursive feature elimination (RFE). The model manifested robust predictive accuracy, achieving an average AUC of 0.85 for both Micro- and Macro-Average ROC across New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional classifications. This research indicates the potential of wearable ECG monitoring in condition assessment and disease management for HF patients, pointing towards promising avenues for the future of personalized medicine and remote health monitoring strategies.

articleTitle: A Coherent Integration Method for High-speed Targets under low SNR Conditions in Distributed Coherent Aperture Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To realize the coherent integration for high-speed targets under the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) condition, an integration method based on Generalized Radon-Fourier Transform (GRFT) is proposed in this paper. Firstly, an accurate echo model for high-speed targets in distributed coherent aperture radar (DCAR) is established, which considers intra-Doppler modulation caused by high-speed motion. Secondly, a coherent integration method performed by GRFT is analyzed, where the compensation terms for high-speed targets are constructed. By GRFT, the target energy distributed in multi-frames can be integrated, which improves SNR to obtain coherent parameters (CPs) estimation under low SNR conditions. Finally, simulation examples are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: DoF Analysis for Extended Coprime Arrays in Near-field Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a sparse array enabled near-field communication system and characterize its spatial multiplexing gain. To this end, a closed-form effective degree of freedom (EDoF) is first obtained for the sparse uniform linear array (S-ULA) and then extended to the extended coprime array (ECA). Based on the closed-form EDoF, we show that the EDoF only depends on the main-lobe of a defined effective beam pattern based on a sampling function. Specifically, given the same number of antennas and array sparsity, a narrower main-lobe generally leads to a larger EDoF. Based on this, we further show that the EDoF for the ECA is larger than that of the S-ULA and dense ULA (D-ULA), due to narrower main-lobe of the effective beam pattern. Furthermore, we characterize the channel capacity of the ECA systems based on the obtained EDoF analysis. Finally, numerical results validate the accuracy of the obtained EDoF and channel capacity.

articleTitle: A Novel Off-Grid Model and Fast Iterative Method for DOA Estimation With Arbitrary Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High accuracy and low computational complexity are always contradictory for any grid-based DOA estimators. To overcome such difficulty, we establish a novel off-gird model based on approximated linear representation of continuous steering vector space, and propose an estimator based on grid location and adaptive step-size iteration (GLASI). The model is available for arbitrary array geometry as well as real-world arrays with imperfection, and allows optimal estimation through effective but compact approximation. Either MUSIC-type or sparse-based algorithm can be applied for coarse grid location, which enables GLASI to work regardless of source coherence and the number of snapshots. Simulation results verify GLASI enjoys remarkable performance superiority over its on-grid counterparts, with low grid density and thereby high computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Multi-view Bistatic SAR Automatic Recognition Study based on Ground Small Target SAR Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: MiniSAR systems possess unique advantages in ground target detection compared to traditional spaceborne and airborne SAR systems, mainly in terms of lower cost, real-time performance, and portability. Although numerous studies have focused on target recognition based on SAR systems with unmanned aerial vehicle, most are limited to monostatic SAR systems. Bistatic SAR systems offer stronger stealth capabilities compared to monostatic systems, as they can receive electromagnetic reflections from any angle. However, due to the lower intensity of received electromagnetic signals in bistatic systems, targets in SAR images tend to experience deformation and attenuation. In this study, based on independently developed monostatic and bistatic SAR systems, we study the integration of multi-view and large-scale deep learning models to aiming to address the issue of hard to recognized small targets. Additionally, the paper validates our proposed method on the publicly available MSTAR dataset and the self-developed FAST-Vehicle dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed multi-view target recognition method effectively identifies SAR bistatic deformed targets.

articleTitle: A Spectral Clustering Sorting Method For Radar Signals Based On SOM Anchor Extraction And Graph Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: As a key technology of reconnaissance system, radar signal sorting (RSS) aims to separate the pulse sequence emitted by different radar from received pulse stream. However, with the emergence of multi-function radars (MFRs), the complex distribution of pulses presents challenges for radar signal sorting in the battlefield electromagnetic environments. A spectral clustering sorting method for radar signal (WFG-SC) is proposed to tackle the problem mentioned above. Our method utilizes Self-Organizing Map (SOM) and K-nearest neighbors (KNN) to construct an adaptive topological graph of the pulse stream. Then, the spectral clustering algorithm is employed for radar signal sorting. Simulation results on MFR pulse dataset show that our method improves the performance of spectral clustering and outperforms some existing sorting methods.

articleTitle: An Efficient and Precise Parallel Implementation Scheme for 3D Stolt Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High-resolution radar imaging systems necessitate higher-order Taylor expansions of the range equation to achieve high-resolution imaging results, requiring enhanced processing and imaging efficiency from both the system and the algorithm. This paper proposes an efficient and precise three-dimensional Stolt interpolation parallel implementation scheme, which avoids lengthy and complex calculations. The nested interpolation scheme is implemented using GPU dynamic parallelism. To balance parallelism and complexity, the nested interpolation scheme is further optimized through multi-stream processing, reducing the demands on system performance and hardware resources while improving interpolation efficiency and maintaining high interpolation accuracy. This approach was validated through practical experiments using the GB-SAR imaging system, effectively demonstrating its practicality and reliability.

articleTitle: 2D Direction of Arrival Estimation in Distributed Non-Coherent Array Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Distributed non-coherent array radar effectively expands radar aperture while reducing radar hardware costs. The existing direction of arrival (DOA) estimation methods in distributed array radar mainly use the phase of the signals from each subarray. However, the non-coherent condition makes the phase relationship between each subarray chaotic which makes the existing methods no longer effective. In this paper, a method is proposed for 2D-DOA estimation in distributed non-coherent array radar. In this method, the signals of each subarray will be jointly processed to avoid the influence of the non-coherent condition. In experiment and simulation, we used distributed non-coherent array radar to estimate the 2D-DOA of multiple targets, and compared the result of our method with centralized array radar. The result shows that our method can separate the targets, while centralized array radar cannot, indicating that our method can achieve 2D-DOA estimation under the non-coherent condition and has higher angular resolution compared to the centralized array radar. Our method can be widely applied to autonomous vehicles and observational astronomy. It can effectively expand the radar aperture with the same number of antennas and reduce the hardware costs by eliminating the hardware devices which are used to meet the coherent condition.

articleTitle: Joint Route and Resource Optimization for Multiple Targets Tracking in Decentralized Airborne Networked Radars
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this article, a strategy of joint route and resource control (JRRC) strategy is present for decentralized airborne networked radar (ANR) in multi-target tracking (MTT) application. The Bayesian Fisher information matrix (BFIM) regarding adaptable working parameters of decentralized ANR, which contains the heading angle and power resource of airborne radars, is derived and adopted to measure the tracking accuracy. Considering the quality of service (QoS) scheme, which consumes the minimization of network resource and meets the desired MTT performance requirement at the same time, the JRRC strategy is then constructed to be a mathematical optimization model. In order to address the formulated problem with multiple optimization variables, a two-stage solution method incorporating the particle swarm optimization and the distributed algorithm based on the average consensus dual decomposition is developed. Numerical simulations show the validity of the JRRC strategy.

articleTitle: Employing FPGA to Implement NN Search in 3D-LiDAR: A Focus on Cache Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: 3-D Light Detection and Ranging (3-D LiDAR) sensors are essential for autonomous vehicle functions such as localization, sensing, and mapping. However, their significant computational processing requirement remains a compelling drawback. Although high-end GPUs and CPUs could resolve the abovementioned issues, their prohibitive costs and substantial power requirements hinder the commercial adoption of 3-D LiDAR in vehicles. This paper presents a novel Nearest Neighbour (NN) searching method based on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) for 3-D LiDAR, designed for exceptional efficiency and accuracy. The method aims to offer a real-time LiDAR data processing solution, which delivers superior results on both GPU and CPU platforms. The proposed method consists of three parts: LiDAR data pre-processing, hardware-accelerate NN search, and efficient caching architecture for point cloud Data. The LiDAR processing methods successfully were implemented on the proposed FPGA platform. Experiment results show that our custom test board can accelerate NN searching beyond the capabilities of CPUs. Finally, the system we’re proposing offers real-time functionality with a power consumption of just 2.8W. It upholds precision levels that can be compared favorably to software equivalents and even the latest LiDAR data processing techniques.

articleTitle: Feature Attention Complex-Valued-Based CNN for Ship Target Recognition of SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The details regarding targets within Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery are typically conveyed and maintained in complex-valued form. Namely, the information regarding both the amplitude and phase is essential. In the process of recognizing targets with SAR, the network only utilizes the amplitude image as input, while the phase information is neglected, resulting in poor recognition performance. This paper proposes a Feature Attention Complex-Valued-Based convolutional neural Network (FACV-Net) for SAR ship recognition to overcome these issues, which effectively utilizes phase information to improve target recognition. Firstly, to meet the requirements of network training in complex domains, a series of complex-valued operation blocks have been constructed. Moreover, a new complex-valued Attention Module (CAM) is introduced to ensure that the network focuses on the amplitude and phase characteristics of the target separately. Additionally, to address the mismatch problem between the amplitude and phase data, two distinct methods for complex-valued max-pooling are utilized. Ultimately, the performance of the proposed FACV-Net is assessed using the OpenSARship dataset, and the results indicate that this novel approach surpasses conventional networks in terms of recognition accuracy. When the CAM is added, the performance of the network sees a further enhancement of around 3% in accuracy. These findings confirm the proposed method’s effectiveness and advantage over others.

articleTitle: Spatial-Spectral Transformer for Local and Global Hyperspectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Deep learning techniques have become increasingly prevalent in hyperspectral image (HSI) classification. However, convolutional neural network (CNN)-based approaches often struggle with inefficient utilization of spectral sequence data and inadequate processing of fine-grained spectral details. In contrast, transformer models are inherently designed to capture sequence dependencies across spectral bands. Yet, most existing approaches tend to focus on either local or global feature extraction separately, which limits their ability to fully exploit the spectral information. To overcome these limitations, we propose the Local and Global Fusion Spectral Transformer (LGFST), an innovative architecture that combines Swin Transformer blocks, standard Transformer blocks, and a novel Local-Global Fusion (LGF) module. This architecture is designed to simultaneously capture both local and global features, thereby improving the extraction of detailed spectral information. The Swin Transformer block, integrated with patch merging and hierarchical attention mechanisms, expands the receptive field and enhances local feature representation through both intra- and cross-window interactions. Meanwhile, the Transformer block performs self-attention across all tokens to extract global features. The fusion of local and global features from these two blocks effectively improves the texture and discriminative power of spectral data, leading to enhanced classification performance, especially in scenarios with dense class distributions. Finally, the LGF module facilitates interaction between local and global feature sets, ensuring a seamless integration of information from both blocks. Extensive experiments on three benchmark HSI datasets demonstrate that LGFST outperforms conventional transformer models and sets new benchmarks in performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Human Activity Micro-Doppler Corner Feature Representation Method Based on Dual-Threshold Harris Extractor for Through-the-Wall Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Micro-Doppler corner signature is a subset of Doppler feature, which arises from the relative motion of human limb nodes. However, conventional micro-Doppler signature extraction methods have low precision on radar images with strong clutter and low resolution restrictions, which is difficult to meet the demand of through-the-wall (TWR) detection.
