To address these issues, this paper proposes a micro-Doppler corner representation method based on image segmentation and dual-threshold Harris corner extraction. Specifically, clutter suppression is first achieved using mean filter and Butterworth filter, resulting in distinctive TWR range and Doppler profiles. Then, the micro-Doppler corner feature image is evenly divided into segments. Furthermore, a corner extractor with two thresholds is performed on each segment. The smaller threshold is employed for detecting a larger number of corners, while the larger threshold enhances the detection of precise corners. Finally, pseudo corners are removed by SUSAN method. Experiments are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel Algorithm for Identifying Radar Clutter Caused by Wind Farm Interference
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Wind turbine radar echoes can significantly interfere with meteorological target detection, affecting weather predictions and disaster warnings. This paper proposes a Wind Turbine Clutter Recognition (WTC-RF) algorithm using Random Forest classification. With training and optimization, the algorithm achieves over 90% accuracy in recognizing wind turbine clutter. Testing on various secondary radar data confirms its ability to effectively detect and identify wind farm clutter.

articleTitle: An ISAC-ISAR Imaging and Tracking Method for Moving Target Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a significant feature in the 6G communication network owing to its monitoring capability around the base station. Meanwhile, inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging technology can obtain two-dimensional image of moving targets with fixed antenna. Inspired by this, an ISAC-ISAR imaging and tracking method is proposed for blind moving target sensing in this paper. First, the ISAC-ISAR echo signal model and imaging mechanism of blind moving target are established with orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) communication signal. Then, the fast imaging algorithm with wavenumber domain processed and tracking based on Kalman filter and Hungarian method for ISAC-ISAR blind moving target sensing are proposed, respective. Lastly, the ISAC real experiments are designed and processed based on universal software radio peripheral to demonstrate the performance and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Wavelet Feature Based SAR Ship Detection Algorithm in Sparse Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This study proposes a novel method for ship target detection in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images. Traditional ship detection methods rely heavily on manually designed features, which are less robust. In contrast, deep learning-based detection methods, which can autonomously learn parameters and extract features, have achieved promising results in SAR ship detection. However, SAR ship target detection faces challenges such as complex backgrounds, noise interference, and scale variation. These issues are particularly pronounced in near-shore scenes where background interference and dense ship arrangements lead to occlusion. Furthermore, unlike optical RGB images that have three independent channels, SAR images have a single-channel problem, making it difficult for Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to extract features from limited channel information. Additionally, most mainstream object detection methods use dense anchor boxes either directly or indirectly, which introduces a large amount of background regions with no ships in sparse SAR images. To address these issues, we first apply specific data augmentation techniques to handle background interference and occlusion in SAR ship targets. Next, we use wavelet transform techniques to enrich the channel information of SAR images. Finally, we adopt a sparse framework to cater to the sparse nature of SAR ship targets. Experiments conducted on the SSDD and HRSID SAR ship datasets demonstrate that our method has significant advantages compared to other advanced detection algorithms.

articleTitle: Airborne SAR Moving Target Velocity Estimation Using Fast Radon Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In response to the issue of velocity estimation for ground moving targets in Synthetic aperture radar (SAR), this paper proposes a fast Radon transform-based method for estimating the velocity of moving targets. First, a geometric and mathematical model for the multi-angle observation of moving targets by airborne SAR is established, followed by range compression and range curvature correction. On this basis, the Radon transform is utilized to estimate the slope of the range walk trajectory observed from multiple angles (≥2), achieving the estimation of the target's azimuth and range velocities. Due to the poor timeliness of traditional Radon transform in slope estimation, this paper designs a fast Radon transform algorithm. Based on the geometric information of the mismatch results of the Radon transform, it reduces the two-dimensional search to a one-dimensional search, significantly improving the efficiency of velocity estimation. Through multi-angle airborne SAR simulation experiments, the effectiveness and efficiency of the moving target velocity estimation algorithm for airborne SAR studied in this paper are verified.

articleTitle: Acceleration method for target HRRP generation based on DDPM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The target high resolution range profile (HRRP) is the sum of the vector projected on the radar line of sight of the target scatters, which can reflect the radial structure characteristics of the target and is one of the important means of radar target recognition. Existing HRRP-based target recognition methods adopt the idea of machine learning classification, which usually require sufficient training samples to obtain satisfactory recognition performance. To solve the dilemma of insufficient radar HRRP data caused by factors such as non-cooperative target and complexity of data acquisition process, this paper uses denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPM) to generate HRRP data. Furthermore, to solve the problem that the DDPM generation speed is too slow to meet the actual needs, this paper designs a fast DDPM HRRP (FDH) data generation method based on progressive knowledge distillation. Finally, the experimental results show that the generation speed is increased by about 25 times compared with the initial model under the premise of losing 7.6% similarity.

articleTitle: UAVs TOPS SAR Real-time Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Targeting UAVs TOPS SAR real-time imaging system, the overall system architecture, imaging algorithm and software architecture design scheme are given. Several engineering implementation problem such as Doppler center frequency correction, image distortion correction and image stitching are specifically designed. UAVs TOPS SAR is preliminarily verified by actual flight data. The rationality of SAR real-time imaging system design and effectiveness of real-time imaging algorithm are discussed.

articleTitle: Efficient Time-frequency Domain Filter Design Against SAR Interference
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) could be easily interfered with by a number of active jamming signals from enemy active jammers during its operating cycle, which seriously affects its battlefield information acquisition capability. In order to effectively combat multiple types of interference, this paper proposed an efficient time-frequency domain filtering method, which extracts the jamming-free pulses from received echo, and constructs an adaptive time-frequency domain filter by using its max time-frequency domain energy peaks, which could accurately extract and suppress interference. Simulation results demonstrate the significant suppression effect of the proposed method on the typical types of interference measured.

articleTitle: A Method of SAR Target Data Augmentation Based on Component-Level Perturbation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Large-scale, diverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image data plays a crucial role in Automatic Target Recognition (ATR). Directly acquiring SAR image data faces significant challenges in practical operation and acquisition costs, while methods such as electromagnetic simulation and image processing for obtaining image data also have insurmountable difficulties. Therefore, intelligent augmentation methods based on Variational Autoencoder (VAE) and Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) have been widely applied in the field of SAR image data augmentation. However, these methods are based on pixel-level augmentation, which not only deviates from the scattering mechanism of SAR targets but also tends to lose the structure and semantic information of the targets. To address this issue, we propose a component-based SAR image data augmentation method. We extract features from real SAR images, decouple the component information of the targets and perturb it, and finally obtain augmented data through attention mechanisms and reconstruction networks. This method not only reduces the adverse effects caused by background interference and occlusion on the targets but also helps to enhance the discriminability between different categories of targets, increasing the recognition rate of the targets on the dataset introduced in this paper by 2.56%.

articleTitle: An Information Geometry Detector for Space-time Adaptive Detection Based on KL Divergence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Slowly moving and weak target detection is a serious challenge for airborne radars, especially in heterogeneous clutter environment. For the reason that the height of airborne radar is high, the airborne radar usually faces a much more heterogeneous clutter environment and requires better anti-clutter ability for the detector. To address this problem, a novel KL-divergence-based matrix information geometry detector for space-time adaptive detection is proposed . The proposed method first transform the target detection problem into matrix manifold space, and then estimate the clutter covariance matrix with the manifold distribution characteristic of reference samples. By processing the radar echo in the nonlinear manifold space, the proposed method achieves better clutter suppression ability and target detection ability. The experimental results based on the Sea-detecting Data-sharing programe data validate the superior performance of the proposed algorithem.

articleTitle: Target Localization with Distributed FDA-MIMO and EPC-MIMO Radars Using CD-MUSIC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper investigates the issue of target localization using a distributed radar system, consisting of Frequency Diverse Array Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (FDA-MIMO) and Element-Pulse Coding MIMO (EPC-MIMO) radars in the environment of Gaussian white noise. The angle and range information are firstly obtained at each local radar station resorting to the Coordinate Descent Multiple Signal Classification (CD-MUSIC), which alternates between the two parameters while keeping the other fixed. Then, multiple sets of the local statistic are fused at fusion center, where an Iterative Least Squares (ILS) target localization method is performed to determine the target’s position. Numerical results are given to verify the localization performance with the devised approach in terms of Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), with comparison to the distributed radar system of all phased arrays.

articleTitle: Deformation monitoring of the skyscrapers by TomoSAR method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Land subsidence not only endangers the safety of houses, roads, infrastructure and underground pipelines but also causes cascading disasters. The total monitoring of urban surface stability is extremely important for monitoring the health of bridges, subways, buildings, etc. Compared with traditional spot measurement, Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) has the advantages of all-weather operation, wide coverage, low cost, high temporal and spatial resolution and high precision. In this paper, the tomographic SAR (TomoSAR) is adopted to solve the layover problem, especially for the skyscrapers in the densely distributed area. In the densely distributed Kowloon MTR station case, the elevation, linear deformation rate and thermal dilation of the skyscrapers are successfully estimated by 4D TomoSAR. The results provide support for health monitoring of buildings and the surrounding areas, facilitating early detection of potential risks.

articleTitle: A CS Algorithm for Multireceiver SAS with Angular Motion Error Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Motion is both the answer and the question, which is the perfect interpretation of synthetic aperture imaging. In multireceiver synthetic aperture sonar (SAS), the angular motion error of SAS platform leads to different sway and heave errors for each receiver, resulting in squint, which will have a significant impact on image quality. Considering the angular motion of the multireceiver SAS, we establish an echo signal model and propose a CS algorithm with angular motion error compensation under narrow-beam condition. The imaging results of the measured data demonstrate that our proposed algorithm can significantly improve the imaging effect.

articleTitle: Dual-Level Contrast Enhancement Method for Infrared Small Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the field of target detection, infrared small target detection(ISTD) is a critical area of research, playing a vital role in reconnaissance, guidance, and early warning systems. Existing spatial Filtering algorithms perform well in clean backgrounds; however, as these filters require manual design based on prior knowledge, they are prone to interference from complex scenes (e.g., clouds, buildings), leading to target omission. Small targets typically exhibit blurry features and weak energy, making direct detection susceptible to interference from high-intensity areas, which may result in missed detections. To tackle these challenges, this paper presents a two-tier contrast improvement method (DLCE). First, a gradient filter group is used to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the target, and then, built upon the concept of local contrast measurement (LCM), a novel intensity calculation method is developed. The new contrast window design effectively enhances the target’s SNR. Compared with existing algorithms, like MPCM (Multi-Scale Patch-based Contrast Measurement) on publicly available datasets, the proposed method more effectively enhances the target’s radiative intensity while suppressing background noise. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is confirmed by the simulation results.

articleTitle: FISTA-LPW: Super-Resolution Imaging of Low- Frequency Radar Based on Sparse Regularization with Learnable Partition Weights
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for bandwidth extrapolation (BWE) imaging of low-frequency radar based on sparse regularization with learnable partition weights (LPWs). The proposed method enhances the quality of super-resolution image reconstruction with limited observation bandwidth through weighting strategies and supervised learning. First, we assign distinct LPWs to scattering centers based on their frequency dependence factors (FDFs), allowing for different regularization strengths that improve BWE accuracy. We then propose FISTA-LPW, an unrolling algorithm designed to optimize these LPWs via supervised learning, utilizing full band spectrums as training labels to minimize extrapolation error in a data-driven manner. Our analysis demonstrates that sparse regularization with LPWs effectively addresses degraded extrapolation accuracy in scenarios with limited observation bandwidth. Experimental results from both simulated and real radar data show that our method outperforms existing BWE techniques in terms of super-resolution image quality, achieving a radar image reconstruction accuracy of 90% while using only 75% of the full bandwidth on real radar data.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Multispectral Demosaicking Method Using Neville Filters and Directional Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Snapshot multispectral imaging systems typically capture multispectral images in a single shot by covering the sensor with a multispectral filter array (MSFA). A demosaicking algorithm is generally required for such systems to reconstruct the full-resolution multispectral images. A two-stage demosaicking method is proposed in this paper. In the first stage, the image is progressively interpolated by Neville filters. In the second stage, the directional interpolation with a novel weighting function is performed to enhance the quality of the pre-interpolated image. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance in both subjective and objective assessments.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Surface Defect Segmentation with a new Battery Surface Gray Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Batteries are essential products for providing power to industrial equipment and devices. Factories producing batteries need to conduct defect segmentation on thousands of batteries, which is costly and inefficient when done manually. Early methods for defect identification, relying on features like pixel intensity, color distribution, or texture, often suffer from low accuracy and poor generalization, challenging adaptation to new data distributions. Industrial defect segmentation has gradually shifted towards using deep learning methods, which effectively address issues like generalization. However, a critical challenge remains: the lack of datasets. Existing datasets for battery defects are insufficient to support deep learning-based segmentation methods. In this paper, we proposed a new Battery Surface Gray Dataset (BSG Dataset), specifically designed for battery manufacturers to address defect segmentation tasks. Our dataset, collected from multiple production lines using specialized AOI cameras, encompasses diverse factors like illumination and temperature, leading to variations such as irregular placement and uneven lighting. It comprises 3546 high-definition battery images, each meticulously annotated with accurate labels for two defect classes: scratch and dent. Finally, we evaluated and compared the segmentation performance of 7 advanced defect segmentation models on the BSG Dataset.

articleTitle: A Heart Rate Extraction Method Using Millimeter Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the development and commercialization of radar technology, real-time monitoring of human heart rate in a resting state using Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar is of great significance for assessing human health. This paper addresses the issue of interference in heartbeat signals caused by environmental noise, respiration signals, and their harmonics in radar signals. A heart rate extraction method based on the combined processing of Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) and Empirical Wavelet Transform (EWT) is proposed. The method involves using SSA on the preprocessed signal to obtain the main components and eliminate noise peaks near the heartbeat, followed by using EWT to decompose the signal into several components. The heartbeat signal is reconstructed by selecting components within a specific frequency range and correlating them with vital sign characteristics. Experimental findings reveal that the method achieves an average relative error of 2.76% for heart rate estimation over a 5-second window.

articleTitle: Cycle Slip Detection and Repair Method for Dual-Frequency Ionosphere-Free Combination and MW Combination Assisted by INS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A method for cycle slip detection and repair is proposed in this study to address the issue of integer cycle ambiguity fluctuations caused by multiple factors in satellite navigation systems. By integrating the high-precision short-term position information from an INS (Inertial Navigation System) with precise ephemeris data, the method establishes differenced ionosphere-free combination observables and MW combination observables between satellites and epochs. By leveraging the advantages of both observables, this approach effectively mitigates the effects of ionospheric delay, tropospheric delay, and hardware errors, enabling accurate detection and repair of cycle slip. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves precise detection and repair of large cycle slip, small cycle slip, equal dual-frequency cycle slip, and special ratio cycle slip, significantly enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of cycle slip detection. This highlights the potential and promising applications of INS-assisted satellite navigation systems in complex environments.

articleTitle: A Slant-range Estimation Method Based on Waveforms of Near-nadir Altimeter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Spaceborne radar altimeter is one of the most important instruments for measuring the ocean dynamic environment. The new generation of altimeter that works in near-nadir interferometry mode retrieves the sea surface height from the interferometric phase instead of the power waveform, which the nadir-looking altimeter uses for sea surface height re-tracking. However, the precise slant-range information also exists in the near-nadir-looking waveforms, which has been ignored so far. This paper proposes a precise slant-range estimation method based on near-nadir power waveforms. Since an analytical waveform model can hardly be established due to the asymmetrical measurement geometry, a large number of near-nadir looking power waveforms are simulated based on a semi-physical model, and a series of empirical analytical models of different looking angles are established based on waveform fitting. Statistical results show that the precision of the proposed method is better than 8cm for the typical near-nadir looking angle range below 4°.

articleTitle: Deforming Group Target Tracking Using GIW-PHD Filter with an Adaptive Group Birth Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Tracking group targets during dynamic events such as separation and combination presents significant challenges, particularly in maintaining tracking accuracy and ensuring timely detection of new targets. To address this, we propose a method based on the GIW-PHD filter. The method first detects group target deformation through changes in group volume, then adjusts the birth intensity and measurement clustering weights based on the deformation information to enhance the robustness during splitting and merging. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, showing improved tracking accuracy and successful detection of new targets born from group deformation.

articleTitle: Predicting Vertical Profiles of Aerial Insect Population from Entomological Radar Utilizing the GRU Encoder-Decoder Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Monitoring and predicting aerial insect population (AP) are crucial for effective pest control strategies. Although traditional entomological radars have contributed to monitoring insect migration, their low resolution limits detailed observations, making accurate predictions of AP challenging. The new generation of high-resolution phased array radars, with their superior range resolution and rapid data update rates, can precisely monitor and quantify AP, capturing the dynamic changes in populations as they respond to meteorological factors over time and space. These dynamics necessitate more accurate predictions of AP. In this study, we introduce deep learning techniques for predicting AP by proposing a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)-based encoder-decoder model designed for shortterm predictions of AP vertical profiles. Our approach integrates historical AP data and meteorological factors, where the encoder captures past states, and the decoder combines this information with the current meteorological conditions to predict AP. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively predicts vertical profiles of AP.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional asteroid reconstruction algorithm based on Multilayer Perceptron
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The three-dimensional reconstruction of asteroids is one of the most popular fields within asteroid research. In this paper, a simple Multilayer Perceptron neural network is proposed, which relies on ISAR radar to reconstruct the three-dimensional point cloud model of the asteroid. Compared with the traditional algorithm, it does not need to manually adjust a lot of parameters to complete the reconstruction of different asteroids, and the network structure is simple and lightweight, requiring very little training data. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm.

articleTitle: Target Estimation with Angle-Only Observations of Distributed Passive Radar Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Passive radars that rely on angle-only measurements cannot obtain the distance between radars and targets. To obtain position estimates of targets, passive radars can be connected to a central processor through communication links. Therefore, fusion algorithms are required to combine observations from distributed passive radars. For the scenario where all radars and targets are moving, most existed fusion algorithms use filtering methods to estimate the velocity and position of moving targets. In fact, most filtering algorithms have some limitations which will limit the algorithm’s effectiveness to a large extent. In this paper, two fusion algorithms are proposed for the central processor. The first algorithm, known as the gross least squares (GLS), employs all observations from passive radars to implement moving target estimation, and thus needs significant computation at the central processor. The second algorithm, termed as the recursive least squares (RLS), iteratively optimizes the velocity and position of moving target. Exploiting the continuity of target motion, current target position and velocity estimates are used as initial values in the next moment. With good initial values, the number of iterations decreases and thus the computational cost is reduced at the central processor. Numerical results show that both algorithms benefit from more observations. The GLS algorithm provides more accurate position and velocity estimates of the target but requires substantial computation cost. The RLS algorithm may suffer a slight performance loss but offers a lower computation cost. The results demonstrate the trade-off between accuracy and computational cost, providing useful insights for practical applications.

articleTitle: Maritime Target Detection Method Based on SDP-YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to the influence of sea clutter, detecting maritime targets, especially small ones, is extremely challenging. With the continuous development of image recognition technology, techniques that convert one-dimensional maritime radar echo data into two-dimensional images and use neural networks for target recognition have been proposed. This paper applies this technology by converting radar echo data containing targets and pure sea clutter into two-dimensional images using the Symmetric Data Path (SDP) method. The YOLOv8 algorithm is then employed for classification to determine the presence of targets. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using a dataset shared by the Naval Aviation University.

articleTitle: Air target detection coverage performance analysis and station deployment optimization of FSR based on GNSS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The global navigation satellite system (GNSS) provides wide coverage, all-weather service, which can be used as the radiation source. And the receiving node is simple. By deploying the receiving array on the ground, airspace monitoring can be realized. It is a potential remote warning method. Aiming at the station deployment optimization of forward scatter radar (FSR) network based on GNSS, firstly, the detection coverage performance of the single baseline system for three typical targets is analyzed including plane, missile, and helicopter. The results show that the detection area can be approximately circular. Then a receiving array deployment optimization method is proposed to use the minimum cost to cover the rectangular detection area. The particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is used. Finally, the effectiveness of the method is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: A Micro-Doppler Analysis Method With Joint Parameter Estimation and Signal Separation Based on MIMO Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In traditional human micro-Doppler signal applications, people usually move towards or away from the radar. There may be more situations in reality. This paper explores a new type of human micro-Doppler signal application and proposes a corresponding processing algorithm. In the new application, multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar is used to replace traditional real aperture radar to reduce costs. At the same time, MIMO radar observes human motion on the side of the human body to obtain micro-Doppler curves. Compared to traditional applications, the new application can better serve security checks and human screening. Based on the wavenumber domain transformation, L-statistic, and the image contrast maximization, this paper proposes an algorithm for Joint Parameter Estimation and Signal Separation (JPESS) to analysis the micro-Doppler curves with translational phase under the side view. In this paper, the L-statistic algorithm is used to separate signals into rigid body parts and micro motion parts. By maximizing the image contrast, JPESS can utilize the separated signal of rigid body parts for optimal estimation of the speed and acceleration. After using estimated parameters to compensate for the micro-Doppler curve and searching for parameters by minimizing the total energy of the time-frequency map, the parameters of each micro motion part can be obtained sequentially. Simulations have verified that the algorithm can obtain human motion parameters and separate micro motion parts’ signals with high accuracy and strong robustness.

articleTitle: Rotorcraft Micro-motion Feature Extraction Based on Multi-carrier Waveform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multi-carrier radar has been widely studied in the fields of imaging, detection and anti-jamming. However, the properties, compensation methods and feature extraction of multi-carrier waveform under micro-motion model are rarely discussed. This paper presents a micro-motion compensation and feature extraction method for multi-carrier waveform. Particularly, we theoretically analyze the effectiveness of the proposed method in the case of stepped frequency (SF) and randomized stepped frequency (RSF) waveform. Through building the physical model of the helicopter rotor and high-precision electromagnetic simulations, it is shown that the proposed method can approximate coherently fuse echoes of different carrier frequencies and thus can accurately estimate the target micro-motion parameters.

articleTitle: Radar Information Transformer: A Sparse Single Frame-Based Classification Network for mmWave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: 3D object detection is critical for autonomous driving systems, particularly in adverse weather conditions where 4D radar offering both spatial and velocity data outperforms traditional sensors. Despite its advantages, 4D radar struggles with noise and ambiguity in measurement. Existing detection methods fail to identify target objects due to their reliance exploring Local Features within sparse point clouds. To address these challenges, we propose the Radar Information Transformer Network (RITnet), which employs a feature-wise attention mechanism to capture the overarching characteristics of point clouds from 4D radar data, rather than relying on PointNet. We train our network on a proprietary radar classification dataset and the TJ4DRadSet dataset. Experimental results indicate that the overall classification accuracy reaches 97.5%, and exhibits good performance in terms of F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> scores and Hamming-loss compared to popular deep learning frameworks.

articleTitle: HRTD: A high-precision rotating target detector for SAR scenes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the past, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target detection research has mainly focused on the representation of bounding boxes. However, the distant contextual prior knowledge in SAR images has not been fully utilized, leading to challenges in detecting small targets and densely arranged targets with multi-scale characteristics. Therefore, this paper proposes a high-precision rotating target detector (HRTD) for SAR scenarios to address the aforementioned issues. More precisely, we introduce a multi-scale rotation-equivariant network (MRNet) and align rotation-invariant regions of interest to enhance target orientation prediction capability. The multi-scale dynamic global attention (MDGA) in MRNet can dynamically adjust the contextual multi-scale spatial receptive field in real-time, facilitating the comprehensive extraction of distant contextual features. This method achieves significantly better detection performance on the SSDD+ and SRSDD-v1.0 datasets compared to other algorithms.

articleTitle: A waveform optimization method for sparse frequency agile radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The sparse frequency agile (SFA) radar is able to achieve the same range resolution as the frequency agile (FA) radar with fewer frequencies. Sparse reconstruction methods are used to estimate target parameters for SFA radars to avoid high sidelobe problem caused by traditional matched filtering methods. The outcome of sparse reconstruction is determined by the sensing dictionary matrix, which is related to the selection of waveform frequency sequence. Therefore, this paper proposes a waveform optimization design method for SFA radars. Firstly, we determine the sensing dictionary matrix's maximum correlation coefficient (MCC) as our optimization objective. Then, an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm is employed to solve the above problem. It contains mutation steps and simulated annealing operations which can help particles escape from local optimal solutions. Finally, the simulation results prove that the proposed method can obtain the optimal SFA waveform with lower MCC, thus improving the accuracy of sparse reconstruction.

articleTitle: A Distributed Radar Multi-Jamming Recognition Method Based on Transformer Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the advancement of deception jamming and multi-radar cooperative anti-jamming technologies, multi-radar systems designed to counter multiple jammers have become a research hotspot, with jamming recognition being a critical step. In recent years, deep learning has been successfully applied to radar jamming recognition, where the jamming signal is transformed into a time-frequency map and subsequently treated as an image recognition problem. However, the performance of jamming recognition algorithms deteriorates significantly when multiple jamming signals overlap in the time-frequency domain. To address this issue, this paper proposes a distributed radar multi-jamming recognition method based on a Transformer network. This method employs adaptive beamforming to separate jamming echoes in the spatial domain, and then converts the jamming echoes from each radar node into time-frequency spectrograms using the short-time Fourier transform. These spectrograms are then input into the Transformer network to detect the type of jamming and estimate jamming parameters based on their relative positions in the time-frequency spectrograms. Finally, the multi-node processing results are fused to output the jamming type and the corresponding fused jamming parameters. Simulation experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Modulation Classification of Satellite Communication Signals by Contrastive Learning of Dual Time-Frequency Representations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Modulation classification occupies a crucial part in spectrum management of satellite communication signals. Nowadays, deep learning brings great potential for its performance improvement. This paper suggests an automatic modulation classification approach by contrastive learning of dual time-frequency representations. First, signals are converted into two kinds of time-frequency representations by Short-Time Fourier Transform and Smoothed Pseudo Wigner-Ville Distribution. Second, a feature extraction module with coordinate attention is employed to capture dual time-frequency representation features. The features are projected to the contrastive learning space by two projection heads for contrastive learning which can improve the model. Finally, the extracted features are transmitted to a fusion classifier for classification. The model is trained on a public dataset and compared with the current advanced modulation classification models. Experimental results indicate that the proposed approach has significant performance advantages and application feasibility in the modulation classification of satellite communication signals.

articleTitle: Research on Polarization Theory Based on Target Polarization Projection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Aiming at the information processing in classical polarization theory, such as polarization decomposition, optimal polarization, polarization filtering, polarization detection, and polarization classification, et al, they are of great significance which supported a large number of polarization applications. Although the theory is relatively rich, there are also some deficiencies, i.e., overlapping theories and inconsistent concepts, which have inconvenient effects on the systematic research of polarization theory. In this regard, this paper proposes the concept and mathematical model of "target polarization projection", in order to form two polarization basic theories with target polarization decomposition. It can achieve a series of polarization information processing such as polarization filtering, polarization detection, and polarization classification, thus providing a clear polarization theory framework and laying a theoretical foundation for the application of polarimetric SAR.

articleTitle: Active and Passive Radar Cooperative Target Tracking Method Assisted by Doppler Information
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Incorporating Doppler information into a hybrid active-passive radar system can effectively enhance target tracking performance. However, in practical tracking scenarios, using a low pulse repetition frequency can lead to Doppler ambiguity. Ambiguous Doppler measurements not only fail to improve target tracking accuracy but also significantly degrade overall tracking performance. To utilize accurate target Doppler information, this paper proposes a tracking method with Doppler ambiguity resolution based on a Gaussian mixture probability hypothesis density (GM-PHD) filter for penetration target tracking in a hybrid active-passive radar system. This method achieves joint processing of multi-target tracking and Doppler ambiguity resolution. the method utilizes radar’s position measurements for filtering to obtain an estimated value of the target’s radial velocity. It then calculates potential target radial velocity values based on ambiguous Doppler measurements and selects the radial velocity value with the maximum likelihood as the Doppler measurement without ambiguity. After Doppler measurements are unambiguous, the target states are updated again. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the GM-PHD filter with Doppler ambiguity resolution can ensure radar system tracking performance.

articleTitle: Preliminary Exploration of 3D Imaging Capability of the MSJosSAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Tomographic Synthetic Aperture Radar (TomoSAR) is a multidimensional information processing technique capable of distinguishing scattering objects in the vertical dimension and obtaining three-dimensional information from diverse environments such as urban areas and forests. This paper proposes a process for three-dimensional back projection(3DBP) tomographic reconstruction, leveraging the scalability of the two-dimensional time-domain projection algorithm in elevation. By integrating real data from a new type of airborne SAR system named Multidimensional Space Joint-observation SAR (MSJosSAR), preliminary results of three-dimensional reconstruction of buildings are presented and subjected to comparative analysis. The experiments demonstrate that under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions, 3DBP can effectively restore building structures, showing superior reconstruction performance compared to the OMP algorithm. This paper validates the feasibility of the proposed method and provides initial verification of the three-dimensional imaging capability of MSJosSAR system.

articleTitle: Application of tissue chip in the production of positive controls
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The purpose of this document is to introduce the application of manual tissue microarrays in the production of immunohistochemistry (IHC) positive tissue controls for ALK, P16, HER2, and EBER in paraffin sections in the Department of Pathology. Then, this article describes the techniques and applications for the production and sectioning of positive control tissue microarrays of paraffin tissue. Manual tissue microarrays include the following advantages over traditional positive control tissue production methods and fully automated tissue microarrays: ease of use, portability, speed, standardization, and low cost.

articleTitle: MDRK-RNN: A Multimodal Data and Runoff Knowledge-Driven RNN for Riverine Flood Extent Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Effective flood warning methods can significantly reduce the loss of life and property caused by extreme flood events. In this paper, we propose a new multimodal data and runoff knowledge-driven recurrent neural network (MDRK- RNN) for flood extent forecasting missions in large-scale riverine flood events, induced by concentrated heavy rainfall. Specifically, the multimodal data, i.e., historical flood extent mapping results from different satellites and digital elevation model of the target area, and runoff knowledge, i.e., estimated accumulated flood flow in the target area, are simultaneously fused to generate a combined conditional data, which is important for increasing the accuracy of the proposed MDRK- RNN model. Experimental results using measured data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed MDRK-RNN in forecasting flood extents.

articleTitle: Study on Array Antenna Radar OFDM-MIMO Three-dimensional Imaging Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To further improve data acquisition with array antenna radar three-dimensional imaging, a Array Antenna Radar Three-Dimensional Imaging based on OFDM-MIMO is proposed, called Array Antenna Radar Three-Dimensional Imaging based on OFDM-MIMO (AAR-3DIM-OFDM-MIMO). Firstly, this paper presents the principles for AAR-3DIM-OFDM-MIMO, then the geometry and echo model are established. Different transmitting array elements emit mutually orthogonal narrowband LFMCW signals, which are simultaneously received by different receiving array elements. Secondly, a new signal is synthesized from multiple narrowband signals with different carrier frequencies. A three-dimensional imaging processing method is used to reconstruct the image of the target scene. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method is subsequently validated with simulations.

articleTitle: Adaptive Radar Detection in Compound-Gaussian Environments with Missing Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper addresses adaptive radar detection in scenarios with incomplete observations due to measurement errors, sensor failures, or outliers, where the target is embedded in compound Gaussian clutter with unknown covariance matrix. The detection problem is formulated as a binary hypothesis test, with a set of selection matrices introduced to represent the observations at each snapshot. At the stage of detector design, a two-step design strategy is employed: first, the Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) is derived assuming known covariance structure; then, the actual covariance matrix in the GLRT is replaced with its maximum likelihood estimate, which is calculated based on the non-missing components of the secondary data using an expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm developed in this paper. Numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness of these detectors in compound Gaussian clutter environments, showing superior performance compared to the existing detector designed for scenarios with Gaussian interference and missing data, as well as the classical linear imputation method.

articleTitle: Development and Validation of a Portable Microwave Imaging System for Stroke Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper proposes a system architecture for a portable microwave stroke detector operating within the 0.5-2 GHz frequency band. The system is divided into two components: the front-end detection equipment and the back-end control equipment. The detector utilizes a frequency domain confocal imaging algorithm to define the imaging area and accurately estimate brain signals by compensating for signal loss at the point of incidence. Experimental validation was performed on healthy volunteers, solution-filled models, and human specimens. The results demonstrate that the system can accurately locate hemorrhages and achieve rapid stroke detection without false positives.

articleTitle: A Through-the-Wall Radar Azimuth Sidelobe Suppression Based on Multibit Coherence Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to the utilization of a sparse MIMO array, through-the-wall radar image often suffers from high azimuth sidelobe, which makes detection in sheltered space difficult. To overcome this challenge, a through-the-wall radar azimuth sidelobe suppression method based on multibit coherence factor is proposed. The imaging phases across different channels are quantized according to the specified quantization bits. Furthermore, the quantized phases are used to generate the weight. Finally, the original radar image is weighted to suppress the azimuth sidelobe. Through numerical simulations and field experiment, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified, and the influence of quantization bits on the proposed method is analyzed.

articleTitle: Jitter error detection and compensation method based on H-infinity filter fusion for remote sensing satellite image
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Satellite jitter is a common phenomenon in high-resolution satellite applications, leading to image blurring, geometric distortion, difficulties in image stitching, and reduced spatial resolution. Therefore, accurately detecting satellite jitter and compensating for it in images is crucial. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for multispectral satellite jitter detection and compensation, which integrates the results of two different detection methods to enhance detection accuracy and effectively compensate for the images. First, dense matching is performed between the bands of the multispectral imagery to obtain the relative registration error between two bands; Then, dense control point matching is conducted between the single-band image and the corresponding Ortho-Images. Next, a method based on the H-infinity filtering model is proposed to fuse the results of the two detection methods and compensate for the original image. Comparative experimental analysis shows that the compensation results after fusion exhibit significant improvements compared to those obtained using a single detection method.

articleTitle: Time and Phase Synchronization Methods For Distributed Coherent Aperture Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Distributed aperture radar can enhance target detection performance and sensitivity through coherent operation without requiring larger radar apertures and higher transmission power. However, achieving coherent operation for distributed aperture radar is a significant challenge. In this work, we research the methods for time and phase synchronization of distributed coherent aperture radar. Firstly, we present a method of transmit coherence which establishing a likelihood function based on conditional probability and estimating the time synchronization error of each array radar by optimizing the likelihood function using analytical and iterative methods. Next, the method of receive coherence is introduced, the minimum value of the information entropy function is solved to obtain the phase synchronization error estimation of the received signal. After completing time and phase error compensation, signal coherent superposition at the target is achieved. Simulation results show that the method achieves signal coherent superposition and theoretical gain.

articleTitle: Open Set HRRP Recognition Using Adaptive Learning with Enclosed Decision Boundaries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High resolution range profiles (HRRP), which contain fine geometric structure information of targets, plays animportant role in the field of Radar automatic target recognition (RATR). In the actual application of RATR, radar may often capture targets that are non-cooperative, making it difficult to establish a comprehensive database, and traditional recognition algorithms are prone to misjudgment when facing unknown targets. Therefore, Open set recognition (OSR) is proposed to simultaneously recognize in-database and out-of-database targets. Considering the pose sensitivity of HRRP, minor changes in the target’s pose can cause significant changes in the HRRP images, leading to a potentially dispersed distribution of samples from the same category in the feature space, which makes it difficult for traditional fixed decision boundaries in OSR to adapt. To address this, this paper proposes an HRRP open set recognition method capable of adaptively learning closed decision boundaries. Based on Hierarchical dirichlet processes (HDP), the method achieves adaptive clustering of subclasses under different categories according to the data distribution characteristics of each category, determining multiple small decision boundaries within each category, and allowing the decision boundaries to dynamically adjust according to the sample features. Finally, experiments with real HRRP data have verified the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Deep MVDR: A High Resolution DoA Estimation Method against Array Gain-Phase Error
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Direction of Arrival (DoA) estimation is a critical issue in array signal processing, and several classical methods such as Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR) and Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC), have been proposed to solve this problem and have achieved remarkable results. However, these DoA estimation methods suffer performance degradation under model mismatches such as gain-phase errors. Deep learning (DL) methods have strong capability to learn the mapping from received data to true angles directly, achieving notable performance in model mismatches scenarios, but their performance tends to degrade in different SNRs or snapshots scenarios. To address these issues, a high-resolution DoA estimation method named Deep MVDR is proposed in this paper, which consists of covariance-enhanced autoencoder, DoA estimator and super resolution modules. These modules can utilize the feature extraction capabilities of neural networks to improve performance and refine spatial spectrum. Simulation results demonstrate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method across various target numbers, SNRs and snapshots with gain-phase errors, and show that Deep MVDR outperforms other existing methods in terms of spatial resolution.

articleTitle: Transductive Multi-Prototype Network for HRRP Recognition with Missing Aspects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The High-Resolution Range Profile (HRRP) plays a pivotal role in radar automatic target recognition. However, due to its aspect sensitivity, the absence of aspects within the training data can lead to a decline in recognition accuracy. To mitigate this issue, we introduce a novel Transductive Multi-Prototype Network (TMP-Net), leveraging the intrinsic similarity within test data to propagate labels along a manifold, thereby achieving classification. TMP-Net addresses the aspect sensitivity by utilizing multiple prototypes per class. Additionally, a loss function term is proposed to ensure the existence of the manifold. Experiments on the MSATR dataset demonstrate that TMP-Net outperforms existing methods by 10.22% in recognition accuracy even with only 10% of aspects represented in the training set. Furthermore, analysis reveals the advantages of employing multiple prototypes.

articleTitle: Sparse View HRRP Recognition Based on Dual-Task of Generation and Recognition Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In recent years, high-resolution range profiles (HRRPs) have played a significant role in radar target recognition. The pose sensitivity of HRRPs results in unsatisfactory target recognition capabilities under sparse viewing angles. However, for non-cooperative targets, obtaining full-view HRRPs is often challenging, leading to suboptimal performance in HRRP-based target recognition. To address the issue of target recognition under sparse viewing angles, we propose an end-to-end model DGR for sparse view recognition that integrates combined generation and recognition tasks. The DGR model extracts deep features of HRRPs through an attention mechanism and utilizes these features for both target recognition and the generation of adjacent-view HRRPs, with both tasks mutually reinforcing each other for improved performance in recognition and data generation. Furthermore, by employing domain adaptation methods, the model learns the variability of target HRRPs in the source domain and applies this knowledge to the target domain, enhancing its generalization ability. Experimental results demonstrate that the DGR model achieves optimal recognition and generation capabilities simultaneously.

articleTitle: Subsurface Structure Detection Based On Space-borne Multistatic VHF-Band SAR Tomography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to the severe attenuation, current remote sensing satellites cannot provide the required depth and resolution for subsurface detection. Spaceborne multistatic SAR tomography technology has the potential to fulfill detective requirements for high spatial resolution and large depth with high frequency (HF) band or very high frequency (VHF) band. In this paper, a novel model for desert subsurface target detection is constructed, where multiple images of the same scene are generated using echo data from each radar receiver from various altitudes. Then the images are aligned using image registration and deramping operations. The separation of overlapping targets is achieved through focusing operations on the vertical dimension. Finally, the 3D reconstruction results of different spectral estimation algorithms are obtained and the factors affecting the resolution are analyzed.

articleTitle: Distributed Aperture Coherent Synthesis Method based on Two-stage Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To solve the problem that it is difficult to accurately estimate the coherent parameters of distributed aperture radar under the condition of low signal-to-noise ratio, a distributed coherent synthesis method based on two-stage compensation is proposed in this paper. This method utilizes prior information such as system layout, beam pointing, and inertial navigation station location to perform coarse alignment of echoes at the first stage in time, and then uses cross-correlation method to estimate coherent parameters of delay and phase within a small range, and perform precise compensation of time and phase at the second stage, so as to realize the coherent synthesis of multiple radar echoes. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively realize distributed coherent synthesis processing under low signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: A Passive Jamming Identification Method based on HRRP and SSM-Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Jamming identification is an important part of the field of radar technology in the modern battlefield and is a prerequisite for the implementation of radar anti-jamming measures. Passive jamming creates multiple false targets by scattering radar transmitter signals to induce and deceive radar. Aiming at the problems of existing passive jamming recognition methods relying on manual feature extraction and insufficient utilization of timing features, a passive jamming recognition method based on SSM-Transformer is proposed. The method first characterises the timing-dependent information of HRRP sequences through the SSM module, and then extracts the deep timing-associated features by using the multi-head attention mechanism in the Transformer encoder. The experimental results show that the proposed method has a recognition accuracy of up to 98% when the JNR is not lower than 21dB, which has higher recognition accuracy and better generalisation performance compared with the existing methods.

articleTitle: Multi-frame Temporal Modeling for Multi-object Tracking in Satellite Video
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the advancement of remote sensing technology, video satellites have played an increasingly important role in both military and civilian domains, and they are widely used in areas such as military guidance, intelligent transportation, and disaster response. Multi-object tracking (MOT) in satellite video is a crucial research topic in these fields and has made certain progress. However, due to the difficulty of tracking objects in complex scene and low resolution, current MOT methods face issues of low accuracy in satellite video. In this work, we propose a joint-detection-and-tracking method called multi-frame temporal MOT (MFT-MOT). Firstly, a heatmap guided multi-frame temporal modeling method is introduced to extract features with temporal semantic information while suppressing background noise. Then, we utilize a weights-shared encoder-decoder network to facilitate interaction of temporal and spatial information and capture inter-frame object motion tracks at low resolution. Experiments on SAT-MTB dataset shows the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: A Polymer-Based Unclad Optical Fiber Sensor for Wearable Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This study utilized polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) plastic tubing to fabricate three different-diameter unclad PDMS flexible optical fiber for wearable sensing applications. This novel method for producing unclad PDMS flexible optical fibers is simple to operate and cost effective. The fabricated unclad PDMS optical fibers of three different diameters were tested for changes in transmittance, tensile force, with strain. The unclad PDMS flexible optical fiber developed in this study offer potential applications in wearable devices and provide new insights into the design of optical fiber sensors.

articleTitle: Optimization of Intermittent Sampling and Repeating Jamming Waveform Based on DPSO
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Intermittent sampling and repeating jamming is an effective jamming method against linear frequency modulation pulse radar, but it suffers from issues such as strong regularity in the distribution of false targets and lag of primary false targets. Based on the research on intermittent sampling and repeating jamming, this paper proposes an optimization method for intermittent sampling and repeating jamming using a discrete particle swarm optimization algorithm. By varying the number of retransmissions within each sampling period, the statistical characteristics of the jamming signal's pulse compression output are altered. Then, the discrete particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to determine the optimal number of retransmissions, thereby achieving a near-suppression effect. Simulation experiments verify the excellent jamming performance of the proposed algorithm. Compared with traditional swarm intelligence algorithms such as the ant colony algorithm, the jamming waveform generated by the proposed algorithm exhibits less regularity, stronger jamming suppression, and significantly improved jamming performance.

articleTitle: Range-angle Imaging Based on the Prior of Target Scattering Characteristics in Distributed Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: We consider the problem of target range-angle imaging using distributed arrays. High resolution imaging requires a large array aperture. However, due to the limited number of array elements, the subarrays are usually sparsely located, which results in severe under-sampling and ambiguity problem, degrading the imaging performance. To this end, we propose a range-angle imaging method based on the prior of target scattering characteristic to resolve the ambiguity. The main idea is to use the information increment of priors to reduce the dependence on the measurements. Particularly, we first statistically extract the prior distribution of target scattering intensity by data analysis on the target images. Then we use these priors to design weighting parameters and achieve the ambiguity-free images by solving a weighted sparse recovery problem. Finally, numerical simulation results verify the feasibility of the proposed method.

Author Keywords: the prior of target scattering characteristics

articleTitle: Sensing Assisted Full-Duplex Unmanned Aerial Vehicle for Maximum Coverage of Users
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle mounted base stations (UAV-BSs) combine mobility and deployability, providing reliable communication coverage for users. This paper investigates a sensing assisted UAV equipped with full-duplex hardware platforms. We study layout optimization algorithms for UAV base stations in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) scenarios. Our algorithm maximizes the number of users with different quality of service (QoS) requirements. Additionally, the transmission slots of the integrated signals is analyzed. Furthermore, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed solution can obtain significant throughput gains and coverage over the conventional designs.

articleTitle: An Ionospheric Pollution Correction Method Based on Parametric Time-Frequency Analysis of PCT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The ionosphere serves as the primary propagation medium for High-Frequency Sky-Surface Wave Radar (HFSSWR). However, its non-stationary and time-varying characteristics cause severe broadening of the first-order sea clutter spectrum in the combined sky-emitting and ground-receiving mode, hindering the detection of slow ship targets. To address this issue, this paper presents an ionospheric contamination correction method for HFSSWR based on the Polynomial Chirplet Transform (PCT) algorithm. Unlike the traditional Chirplet Transform (CT), which uses a sinusoidal kernel, this method employs a polynomial kernel for time-frequency analysis of the broadened echo spectrum. It extracts the phase contamination function by estimating the instantaneous frequency, thereby correcting the ionospheric phase path perturbation in the echo spectrum. This approach effectively suppresses sea clutter broadening caused by ionospheric perturbations. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that, compared to conventional ionospheric decontamination methods, this method achieves superior suppression of broadened sea clutter spectra caused by both small- and large-amplitude ionospheric phase perturbations, improving the signal-to-noise ratio. This method effectively mitigates sea clutter broadening in HFSSWR.

articleTitle: A Terrain Data-Assisted Tracking Method for Rolling Rock
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The rolling rock's trajectory is variable and complex, which could easily cause false associations, and affect tracking accuracy. To address this issue, a rolling rock tracking method based on terrain data assistance is proposed. Firstly, three-dimensional (3D) terrain data is utilized to predict the rolling rock's motion direction and project it onto a two-dimensional(2D) radar coordinate system. Then, based on the deviation between the associated measurements and the predicted direction, false association are rejected, and the state and covariance matrix are corrected using the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF). Finally, the correction of rolling rock trajectory is achieved, enhancing tracking performance. Experimental data is used to validate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Faster Few-Shot Object-Detection: Two-Stage Fine Tuning Integrated with External Memories
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Traditional object detection requires a large amount of annotated data to ensure model accuracy and generalization, but in practical scenarios, labeled samples are often limited. Few-shot Object Detection (FSOD) addresses this issue by enabling models to quickly learn and infer with minimal labeled data, which is crucial for real-time applications. Although various FSOD approaches, including feature representation, meta-learning, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and self-supervised learning, have been proposed, challenges like overfitting and poor generalization persist. This paper introduces a two-stage fine-tuning model incorporating an External Memory Module. Through the use of two small, learnable, shared memory units that extract visual word representations from limited images, the model enhances generalization and reduces computational complexity. The external attention mechanism, optimized through back-propagation, improves the model’s effectiveness and efficiency.

articleTitle: Fast Calibration of Beam Directions Based on RNN for Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The accuracy of beam directions is a key characteristic of phased array antennas, which requires precise calibration. Current calibration methods require sequential measurements of beam directions at all angles within the field of view by rotating the turntable mechanically, which is very time-consuming. This paper proposes a fast calibration method of beam directions based on Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) for phased arrays. The RNN is used to learn the characteristics of beam direction errors at measured angles and predict of those errors at other angles. Experiments show that, to meet the same calibration accuracy, the proposed method only measures beam directions at 1/10 of the angles that are measured in the current method. Hence, the proposed method can significantly enhance the efficiency of beam direction calibration.

articleTitle: High precision time and frequency difference of arrival estimation in complex electromagnetic environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Conventional time and frequency difference of arrival estimation methods often deteriorate severely in complex electromagnetic environments, particularly in the presence of co-channel interference. To address this challenge, a high precision time and frequency difference of arrival estimation method is proposed based on spectral filtering and cyclic correlation. In the proposed method, the received signals are first converted into the frequency domain, where the spectral filtering method is applied to remove the interferences from other channels. Sequentially, the cyclic frequency values of the processed signals are calculated using the strip spectral correlation algorithm (SSCA) to differentiate the signal of interest (SOI) from co-channel interferences. The alpha-cross ambiguity function (α-CAF) is then constructed based on the cyclic frequency of SOI. Finally, a two-step approach including a coarse search for the peak of α-CAF followed by a fine search, is utilized to quickly obtain the time and frequency difference of arrival for SOI. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated by numerical simulations.

Author Keywords: time and frequency difference of arrival estimation

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Based Denoising Approach for Synthetic Aperture Sonar Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Sonar (SAS) is one of the techniques used for underwater imaging, and in this paper, we use the range Doppler algorithm for SAS imaging and consider the position errors of sonar platforms in practical scenarios. These errors can seriously degrade the imaging result; however, correcting them and performing compensation with high-precision equipment could be very costly. In this paper, a deep learning approach is proposed using artificial neural networks for image denoising, specifically targeting noise induced by motion uncertainties. As demonstrated by computer simulations, it can recover the images with better quality without employing complex algorithms and hardware compensation.

articleTitle: Tensor-Based Chaotic Convolutional Neural Network for Remote Sensing Data Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the advancement of deep learning techniques, the classification of remote sensing data using artificial neural networks has emerged as a prominent research area. Despite this progress, the emulation of brain structures by traditional artificial neural networks remains at a relatively low level. Therefore, there is an urgent need to explore novel methods that can more effectively simulate human brain functions and enhance algorithmic performance. At the same time, artificial neural networks in image processing require the transformation of raw data into vector form. However, this conversion disrupts the inherent relationships between adjacent positional data in the raw data, resulting in the loss of crucial spatial structural information. To address these issues, we propose a tensor-based chaotic convolutional neural network model for the classification of remote sensing data. Firstly, we constructed a 3D discrete chaotic system, utilizing both Logistic mapping and Tent mapping, to achieve a more uniform iterative distribution and a broader full mapping range. This system was then integrated with convolutional neural networks to devise a novel chaotic convolutional neural network algorithm. By introducing chaotic mechanisms, this algorithm addresses the drawback of neural networks being prone to local minima. Secondly, we established a tensor model for remote sensing data. In contrast to existing methods that convert raw data into vector form, our approach represents raw data in tensor form, thereby preserving the spatial structural information among the three channels of the raw data. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm was validated using the NWPU-RESISC45 remote sensing dataset

articleTitle: A Novel Framework for Pothole Area Estimation Based on Object Detection and Monocular Metric Depth Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Currently, autonomous driving technology is rapidly developing. Accurate detection and area estimation of potholes are crucial for enhancing the safety of roads. Previous studies typically relied on physical models based on camera angles or LI-DAR data for pothole area estimation, which often suffered from significant errors and limited range capabilities. To address these issues, a novel framework for pothole detection and area estimation is proposed. Initially, potholes are detected using the high-precision yet lightweight object detection network YOLOv5n-p6; subsequently, the metric depth of pothole keypoints is estimated via the monocular metric depth estimation model ZoeDepth; finally, a pinhole camera model is utilized to compute the area of potholes. Experimental results demonstrate that established pothole detection model maintains high accuracy while achieving model lightweightness, and the proposed area estimation model provides predictions that closely match the actual pothole areas. This research offers a new methodology for pothole detection and area estimation, potentially improving road safety in autonomous driving.

articleTitle: Dangerous Rock Masses Monitoring based on the GNSS-based InBSAR System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The global navigation satellite system (GNSS)-based interferometric bistatic synthetic aperture radar (InBSAR) system employs the GNSS satellites as transmitters. The receiver is stationed on the ground to detect the scene’s echo. It can be utilized to evaluate typical dangerous rock masses. The signal model of the GNSS-based InBSAR system and the bistatic SAR imaging algorithm are introduced in this paper. Besides, the configuration of one-dimensional fields of the GNSS-based InBSAR system is described. Finally, the experiment is carried out in Wushan County, Chongqing, southwest of China. The experimental findings validate the proposed algorithm for the GNSS-based InBSAR system. A preliminary deformation monitoring result of dangerous rock areas using GNSS based InBSAR with BeiDou satellites is obtained in this research.

articleTitle: Mosaicking Large-Scale InSAR Deformation Velocity Over Sparse GNSS Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: SAR interferometry is commonly employed to map large-scale surface deformation. In applications spanning thousands of kilometers spatially, mosaicking multiple deformation velocity fields into a seamless entity is a critical process. This article analyzes the limitations of the existing mosaicking model, in particular the ill-conditioned problem posed by polynomial models over sparse Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) constraints.
