To resolve this issue and further extend InSAR measurement to regional and global scales, we propose a more robust solution within the framework of block adjustment, which effectively imposes constraints on the entire system even in the presence of limited GNSS data. Comprehensive testing on Sentinel-1 datasets over the North China Plain validates the efficiency of our approach in deriving a spatially continuous deformation field. Compared to traditional methods, our approach delivers a ~50% improvement in inner frame alignment. These advancements enable us to capture more accurate and continuous deformation features over wide areas, providing valuable insights for advancing large-scale deformation mapping within geodetic studies.

articleTitle: Software radio-based hybrid radar data acquisition and real-time transmission system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid radar data acquisition and real-time transmission system based on software radio is proposed to solve the problems of poor flexibility and versatility of traditional single-functionality radar systems in multifunctional applications as well as poor real-time performance of the system transmission data. The system includes a host computer and a software radio platform. The host computer mainly completes the setting of control parameters and the control of the whole system, this paper utilizes the HJX-ADRV9009-X2 software radio platform to realize the radar data acquisition and real-time transmission under the three working modes of active detection, passive reconnaissance and active detection + passive reconnaissance. After testing, the system data transmission rate can reach 9.3Gbps. the system is more versatile and real-time, and can realize the function of multi-purpose in practical use.

articleTitle: A Refined Bilateral Filter For InSAR Phase Denoising
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) is a powerful tool for terrain mapping, which can obtain the digital elevation model(DEM) by two or more SAR images. Phase filtering technology can improve the accuracy of interferometric phase, which determines the quality of the DEM. However, the traditional phase filtering methods struggle to balance noise suppression and terrain detail preservation. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a refined bilateral filter for InSAR phase. The main contributions are summarized into two aspects. Firstly, the bilateral filtering method is extended from real domain to complex domain. It consists of spatial and value kernels, which can balance noise suppression and detail preservation. Secondly, a refined bilateral filter based on nested processing is proposed. It embeds the spatial kernel in the filtering of value kernel, which can achieve high-accuracy phase estimation. Compared to the traditional filtering methods, the proposed method can simultaneously maintain the details and suppress phase noise. Computer simulations and real airborne InSAR data validated the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Modified Frequency Scaling Algorithm for Highly Squinted FMCW-SAR Mounted on Maneuvering Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This article proposes a new method for FMCW- SAR installed on highly squinted maneuvering platforms. A modified range walk correction method was proposed to solved the additive component of the range azimuth coupling. Then, in order to correct the space variation in azimuth time domain of the frequency scaling component, an improved fourth-order frequency scaling function and remaining video phase correction function is proposed. Finally, the azimuth frequency-domain nonlinear chirp scaling function is used to correct the azimuth space variation of Doppler parameters and complete azimuth focusing. Finally, we validated the effectiveness of the proposed MFSA through simulation of SAR point targets with highly squint angle.

articleTitle: Soil Moisture Retrieval over Agricultural Fields Using Dual-Polarimetric SAR Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The model-based polarimetric decomposition technique can utilize information of different channels to describe the complex interaction processes between soil and canopy, elegantly achieving the decoupling of scattering signals from the surface and vegetation. However, the dependence on fully polarimetric SAR data limits the application of this method. In this study, an advanced soil moisture retrieval method coupling model-based decomposition and surface scattering model is proposed for dual-pol SAR data. The generalized volume scattering model based on fully polarimetric decomposition theory is reconstructed as a projection on Stokes vector to facilitate the simple removal of volume scattering contribution. Soil moisture is subsequently estimated iteratively based on a cost function using an Oh semi-empirical model considering surface roughness. The measurements obtained from the ground campaign in Manitoba, Canada and L-band UAVSAR images collected during the campaign are used for validation. The proposed method achieves accurate soil moisture estimation based on reasonable separation of surface and vegetation scattering signals. The root mean square error (RMSE) of soil moisture inversion for the VV-VH mode reached 0.052 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with a correlation coefficient of 0.82, while the RMSE for the HH-HV mode was 0.073 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with a correlation coefficient of 0.68.

articleTitle: Advanced Scale-aware Attention for Enhanced Tiny Object Detection in Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Recent advancements in remote sensing object detection have progressed, but distinguishing objects from complex backgrounds remains difficult, especially for tiny objects. To address this, we introduce the Advanced Scale-Aware Attention (ASA) module, which retains key channel information while minimizing computational cost. This module reorganizes channels into the batch dimension and splits them into multiple sub-features. The ASA module contains three branches: the first encodes weights based on scale and channel relationships. The second and third branches use different convolution kernel sizes to capture features across various receptive fields. These branches collaborate to enhance pixel-level relationships, improving foreground-background contrast. On the AI-TOD dataset, our method improved AP50 by 8.6% over state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: A New Approach for Interferometric Phase Reconstruction over Decorrelated Regions with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), a powerful geodetic technique, can accurately provide ground deformation measurements with high spatial resolution and wide coverage. However, InSAR suffers from decorrelation due to heavy vegetation or large ground movements, especially when exploring areas with geohazard events. Ignoring or masking these incoherent areas can stabilize InSAR phase unwrapping but at the cost of losing valuable spatial information, such as the deformation near the epicenter of an earthquake. To retrieve information over the masked areas, a generative interferometric phase reconstruction (IPR) technique has been developed to handle various fringe patterns and dynamically changing decorrelated regions. In this paper, we proposed a new generative adversarial network (GAN) called PhaseNet, designed for IPR under different fringe rates and masked patterns. The model was trained using a simulated InSAR dataset under a pixel-space loss function. The structural similarity index (SSIM) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) were used as reconstruction metrics to evaluate model performance. The model achieved an SSIM of 0.98 for the original simulated interferogram despite 15% of the pixels being masked. The largest disparity between the clear and reconstructed phases in the synthetic validation dataset remained within the range of ±1 radian in phase or sub-centimeter in deformation.

articleTitle: A Fast MART Method with Voxel Filtering for GEO SAR-Based Computerized Ionospheric Tomography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Ionospheric monitoring is crucial for space environment assessment and the success of space mission. Traditional computerized ionospheric tomography (CIT) based on Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) are constrained ground receivers, while CIT based on geosynchronous synthetic aperture radar (GEO SAR) offers an ionospheric tomography solution that does not rely on ground receivers. This approach leverages the abundant Permanent Scatterer (PS) points in the SAR image for electron density reconstruction, providing strong adaptability to various environments. However, due to the large number of PS points in the large coverage area of GEO SAR and the abundance of total electron density (TEC) data, the conventional multiplicative algebraic reconstruction technique (MART) is inefficient in processing iteration. To this end, this paper proposes a fast MART method based on Voxel Filtering, and verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method through a tomographic experiment. The results show that the proposed method ensures reliable tomographic results, effectively improves the iteration speed, and significantly improves the computational efficiency, which provides strong support for GEO SAR-based CIT with huge TEC data.

articleTitle: Insect Species Identification Based on Electromagnetic Scattering Parameters Measured by Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an AdaBoost model for insect species identification based on electromagnetic scattering parameters. Utilizing 14 electromagnetic scattering parameters of insects measured by fully polarimetric radar, an average identification rate of 90.74% is achieved for 9 migratory insect species. Compared with the method that first estimates body size parameters from electromagnetic parameters and then identifies insect species based on those body size parameters, our proposed method directly identifies insect species using electromagnetic parameters and improves the identification rate by 15.55%. This improvement demonstrates the potential for more accurate and efficient automated monitoring systems for migratory pests.

articleTitle: A Novel Off-Grid Deep Learning framework for DOA Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel off-grid deep learning-based Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation algorithm is proposed, specifically designed for accurately determining the direction of reflected signals. Accurate DOA estimation is crucial in a wide range of applications including radar, sonar, communications, and healthcare. Despite the prevalence of advanced deep learning algorithms for DOA estimation, nearly all suffer from errors of grid. Consequently, a neural network framework with a corresponding loss function was developed to eliminate off-grid errors. The proposed model does not require pre-determining the number of targets, unlike traditional off-grid algorithms, and it delivers more precise DOA estimations. Viewing DOA as a regression issue, this model utilizes the signal’s covariance matrix as input. After processing through a neural network module to obtain pseudo-spectrum, another neural network module refines these into coordinate error values, ultimately yielding precise DOA estimations. The simulation results demonstrate significant advantages.

articleTitle: Grating Lobe Suppression Based on FCN for Through-the-Wall 3D SAR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In through-the-wall 3D synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging, under-sampling in the height direction is usually unavoidable, resulting in severe grating lobe effects. Traditional grating lobe suppression algorithms have poor performance, and existing neural network research is limited to 2D SAR images, which cannot achieve high-quality grating lobe suppression for 3D SAR. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a grating lobe suppression algorithm for through-the-wall 3D SAR based on fully convolutional networks (FCN). Simulation results demonstrate that, compared to traditional grating lobe suppression algorithms, the proposed network significantly suppresses grating lobe effects in 3D SAR, achieving optimal imaging quality. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is demonstrated with measured data.

articleTitle: Information supplement based on Tip-adapter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The Contrast Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) model learns to associate image and text content by pre-training on a large number of image and text pairs. The CLIP model can understand the relationship between image content and text description, thereby achieving functions such as image recognition, classification, and retrieval in various tasks. And due to its zero sample learning ability, it can perform effective task inference even without a large amount of labeled data. The proposal of CLIP model has brought new research ideas and application possibilities to the field of multimodal learning, and has shown excellent performance in the zero-shot domain. When we want to apply CLIP to the field of few-shot remote sensing image classification, the main challenge is how to fine-tune the knowledge stored in the clip so that the entire model can better adapt to downstream tasks and how to solve the problem of overfitting in training models under the situation of few shot samples. The commonly used CLIP-based fine-tuning methods have poor performance under few-shot conditions. In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised learning based cached model method, which classifies the test set for the first time based on a small amount of labeled data in the training set as the cached model. The high confidence pseudo labeled data in the test set is used as a supplement to jointly classify the remaining low confidence test samples. The experiment shows that our proposed innovative method has significantly improved accuracy compared to previous methods on two benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Change Detection in Heterogeneous Remote Sensing Images Based on Copula-Supervised Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Change detection (CD) in heterogeneous remote sensing images has been extensively applied in response to emergencies. There have been substantial improvements during the past decades in addressing heterogeneous CD challenges, driven by the rapid advancements in deep neural networks (DNNs). However, most DNN-based heterogeneous CD methods often exhibit black-box behavior, limiting their interpretability and controllability in many practical CD applications. To overcome these issues, we propose a neural copula change detection (NCCD) framework, an approach for the heterogeneous CD problem that leverages an interpretable neural network supervised by copula theory. In NCCD, copula’s mathematical characteristics are incorporated as loss functions to supervise a neural network in modeling dependence between bi-temporal heterogeneous remote sensing images. The trained neural network works as a copula function to estimate the degrees of dependence that serve as the indicator for identifying changes. Experimental results on two real heterogeneous CD datasets substantiate the effectiveness of our NCCD.

articleTitle: Analysis of Antenna Pointing Error for Ground-Based Radar Lunar Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The accurate mapping of the lunar surface is crucial for future missions, yet ground-based (GB) radar system faces challenges due to antenna pointing error. This paper investigates the pointing error in GB radar antennas used for lunar surface imaging. To begin with, the systematic errors in GB radar system are analyzed, and empirical error models for both elevation and azimuth angles are established. Based on these error models, an antenna pointing error model is developed, an echo signal amplitude loss model is then formulated for analysis. Simulations demonstrate the time-varying of this error and its impact on image quality. The impact on the imaging quality is minor, yet specific directions exhibit more pronounced degradation, particularly in the Y-axis, with more noticeable degradation in Peak-Side-Lobe Ratio (PSLR) and Integrated-Side-Lobe Ratio (ISLR).

articleTitle: Visualizing Deep Neural Networks with Double-Sliding Window
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Deep neural networks are widely used in target recognition, image classification, speech signal processing. However, it is quite difficult to understand how deep neural networks complete the tasks from different fields. This paper proposes a method to analyze the principle of deep neural networks for target recognition by applying double-sliding window and dropping features to the model input image samples. First, the input image is divided into several blocks. Then, part of features in each block are removed in turn to observe the effect of the classification results. Finally, the average of the effect from each feature in the input sample on the classification results is calculated. Experimental results prove that the effects of features from the input image on the decisions of classification results are performed well by the method proposed. It can help realize the visualization analysis of target recognition with deep neural networks

articleTitle: A Passive ISAR Modulation Method Based on Time-Modulated Corner Reflectors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The time-modulated corner reflector (TMCR) is an improvement of the traditional corner reflector based on time-modulated metasurfaces, which can manipulate the characteristics of electromagnetic waves in real-time. In this paper, a novel passive ISAR modulation method based on the asynchronous control of TMCRs is proposed, which can directly destroy the ISAR imaging mechanism. Through the joint inter-pulse and intra-pulse periodic modulation, multiple corner reflectors are alternately switched between strong and weak reflection states asynchronously, which can interfere with the alignment process of range profiles and further causing errors in initial phase compensation. The intra-pulse modulation model is constructed firstly. On this basis, the design criterion for inter-pulse modulation mode is described in detail. Finally, experiments are conducted based on the measured data of the UAV, which verifies that the proposed method can effectively interfere with the ISAR imaging.

articleTitle: A CFAR Detector Based on Elastic Net for HFSWR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In practical scenarios, target detection for high-frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR) is challenging because it is performed in a complex multi-target detection background. This paper proposes a constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detector based on the elastic net to address the issue of target detection in multi-target backgrounds for HFSWR. The objective function of the proposed CFAR detector not only considers the goodness of fit of the clutter model to the clutter but also incorporates a regularization term. Specifically, the Weibull distribution is used to fit the HFSWR clutter. Additionally, due to the sparsity of the targets, an elastic net-based regularization term is incorporated, which is flexible, stable, and effectively captures sparsity. By minimizing the objective function, estimates of the target echo in each cell can be obtained. Cells containing targets are then excluded based on these estimates, while the remaining cells are used as reference cells to estimate the background distribution parameters. The proposed CFAR detector performs well in both simulations and experiments on real data, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection for IoT Time Series Signals with GANs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) enables interconnection of heterogeneous devices through wireless and mobile communication technologies, with sensing devices continuously generating a large amount of time series signals. Extracting valuable information from this data has become increasingly challenging. In this context, anomaly detection techniques have emerged to identify events of interest. This paper proposes UatGAN, an unsupervised anomaly detection method for IoT time series signals utilizing generative adversarial networks (GANs). The method combines autoencoders (AEs) and GANs, using the encoderdecoder structure of AE to learn compressed representations of input data, and enhances sensitivity to anomalous inputs through adversarial training of GANs. Considering time correlation, the dynamic time warping (DTW) algorithm is introduced to calculate reconstruction errors, and a new anomaly diagnosis strategy is proposed. Experiments conducted on public datasets demonstrate that our method detects anomalies more accurately than baseline methods.

articleTitle: SAR-Optical Images Matching Based on Variant U-Net Combined With FFT Correlation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The primary challenge in matching SAR with optical images lies in the significant heterogeneity that stems from their different imaging mechanisms. To address this issue, we developed the variant U-Net that transforms these heterogeneous images into a unified feature space for matching. Initially, A Siamese network with shared weights extracts feature maps, which are abstract representations of key patterns and features, from both SAR and optical images, transforming the disparate images into a unified representation space. Subsequently, through an FFT layer, the feature maps undergo normalized cross-correlation (NCC) to generate a similarity heatmap. The peak of the heatmap indicates the optimal matching position. Finally, the heatmap is fed into a softmax classifier to finalize the best match, thus converting the matching process into a classification task. In addition, we incorporate cross-entropy loss and mean-squared error loss to aid the model’s training process, improving the accuracy and stability of the classification. Results obtained from benchmark datasets clearly show that our method outperforms other advanced methods in terms of matching precision and accuracy.

articleTitle: A Nonlocal Estimation Method of Optimal Coherence for PolInSAR Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The traditional coherence optimization algorithm has been successfully applied to polarimetric interferometric synthetic aperture radar (PolInSAR) data, but often suffers from spatial discontinuity. This paper introduces an innovative approach for optimizing the scattering mechanism vector(SMV) through nonlocal estimations. The proposed method constructs a pixel-level optimization model by leveraging patch-based nonlocal similarity, effectively enhancing the accuracy of SMV estimation while preserving high resolution. Both simulated and observed ESAR data are employed to evaluate the performance of various methods. Experimental results confirm the advantages of the proposed approach in detail preservation and phase recovery.

articleTitle: Subspace Projection Algorithm based on Code Agile Waveform for Folded Clutter Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The Internal Clutter Motion (ICM) results in an expansion of the clutter Doppler spectrum. With conventional waveforms, the presence of range ambiguity causes short-range strong clutter with ICM to be folded into the long-range interval. The folded clutter, along with Doppler expansion, submerges low-speed small targets, significantly affecting the target detection performance of ground-based early warning radar. Agile waveforms improve the distinguishability of echoes from different range intervals by varying the waveform parameters between pulses, enhancing the degree of signal processing. Therefore, this paper proposes a subspace projection algorithm based on code agile waveform to suppress the folded clutter with ICM. First, the clutter subspace is constructed using the echo model of the code agile waveform and the distribution characteristics of clutter in the range-Doppler domain. Next, subspace projection is applied to each range interval, with iterative processing between intervals to achieve folded clutter suppression. Finally, the joint mismatch filtering and Pulse Doppler (PD) processing is performed to realize coherent accumulation in each range interval. The simulations and processing results of real measured data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in suppressing folded clutter and improving the detection performance of small targets at long-ranges and low-speeds.

articleTitle: UAV-SAR Panoramic 3D Imaging for Urban Area: A Multi-angle Tomography Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Tomographic synthetic aperture radar (TomoSAR) three-dimensional (3D) imaging technology solves the layover problem in SAR imaging, and has broad application prospects in urban areas by virtue of the flexibility of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platform. However, the occlusion of urban buildings causes serious shadow problems, resulting in the loss of 3D structures of urban areas. At the same time, the nonlinear signal processing algorithms in TomoSAR further aggravate the loss of scattering information. Aiming at the above problems, a multi-angle TomoSAR 3D imaging method is proposed in this paper to realize panoramic 3D imaging in urban areas. The proposed method combines the advantages of TomoSAR imaging and back projection (BP) algorithm. Firstly, the 3D structures of urban areas can be accurately reconstructed by TomoSAR imaging, becasue of its advantage of achieving super-resolution. Then, geometric positioning is used to achieve the accurate fusion of multi-angle 3D structures. Finally, BP algorithm is used to obtain the lossless scattering information because of its advantage of high fidelity, so as to realize panoramic 3D imaging. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by multi-angle TomoSAR simulations based on UAV SAR parameters.

articleTitle: A space-based radar nonlinear tracking method for air targets based on VB-PHD filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Space-based radar has better coverage and is not limited by the curvature of the earth. Aircraft target tracking is particularly important in space-based radar system. However, the long observation distance and strong nonlinear observation increases the challenge of target tracking. Therefore, we proposed a space-based radar nonlinear tracking method for air targets based on variational Bayesian probability hypothesis density (VB-PHD) filter. The relationship between state and observation is established. Then, the VB method is adopted to deal with uncertainty of measurement noise variances. Besides, the cubature filter is introduced to deal with the strongly nonlinear models, and the recursion process is completed by using the third-order spherical radial volume rule. Finally, simulation scenarios with different measurement noise parameters were constructed, and the tracking result comparisons show that it effectively solves nonlinear problems, and tracking precision can be significantly improved.

articleTitle: Decision-Making and Parameter Optimization of Anti-Jamming Measures based on HPPO
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the current dynamic jamming scenarios where radar faces diverse types and varying parameters of interference, it often requires simultaneous decision-making on a limited number of anti-jamming measures and their corresponding continuous parameters. To address this mixed action space optimization problem, this paper proposes a method for anti-jamming measure decision-making and parameter optimization based on the Hybrid Proximal Policy Optimization (HPPO) algorithm. Building on the PPO algorithm, the single output layer of the actor network is modified into two independent parallel output layers, each independently calculating the importance sampling values for measures and parameters, followed by policy updates using a shared advantage function. Simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Towards Realistic TomoSAR Reconstruction Through Light Reconstruction and Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Tomographic synthetic aperture radar (tomoSAR) is an effective tool for large-area urban 3D mapping. TomoSAR reconstruction is fundamental to the quality of the mapping product. Recently, deep learning (DL) techniques have shown promising reconstruction precision compared to traditional methods. However, current work processes the data in a fiber-by-fiber manner to assemble the final 3D scene tensor, which may deteriorate the correlations existing within these fibers due to the spatial structure in the scene. In this work, we propose a new reconstruction neural network that features light reconstruction and enhanced computational processing. We use 2D slices as the basic processing unit. First, the rough reconstruction result is obtained through a light reconstruction that regularizes only the sparsity feature. Then, to enhance the spatial structure, we process the rough result with an enhancement stage through a deep neural network module. To harness correlations within the 3D scene tensor, we adopt an inter-slice and intra-slice strategy. The spatial structure within slices is explored first through a U-Net structure, while the structure between slices is further explored through a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) based module. Both simulated and measured data are used to evaluate the reconstruction neural network. Results reveal a high gain of spatial features, such as more complete building surfaces, compared to current methods.

articleTitle: Deformation Monitoring of Xijiang Railway Bridge with Ground-based Radar Interferometry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Ground-based interferometric radar (GBIR) is an innovative tool for monitoring bridges deformation. Bridges are usually located over rivers and valleys, and the severe water vapor make it challengeable to extract accurate deformation from atmospheric delay error. Moreover, GBIR can only capture the one-dimensional linear deformation, but hard to retrieve the multi-dimensional deformation. In this study, the Xijiang Railway Bridge is taken as an example to conduct deformation monitoring experiments. The independent component analysis (ICA) is used to remove atmospheric effects errors. The error average optimization rate of ICA is 83.96%, shows excellent performance in GBIR bridge error removal. We also use a data fusion framework based on GBIR and inertial vision-based measurement (IVM) to obtain multi-dimensional dynamic deformation of the bridge with crossing train. The maximum of deformations along the vertical and lateral directions are 211.3 mm and 123.4 mm.

articleTitle: An Autofocus Algorithm for TOPS Mode BP SAR Image Based on Spectrum Compression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the high squint TOPS mode SAR imaging by using the BP imaging algorithm in the rectangular coordinate system of the ground plane, the wide swath SAR image without distortion in the ground plane can be obtained in a short time. However, how to quickly complete the motion error compensation of the BP image is still a difficulty in practical application. This paper proposes an improved spectrum compression method, which can quickly realize the follow-up operations such as autofocus of the BP image of the ground plane in the high squint TOPS mode of the mobile platform. Firstly, considering that the traditional BP spectrum compression method is only applicable to the spotlight imaging mode, combined with the virtual rotation center theory of high-squint TOPS SAR and the wavenumber spectrum analysis, an improved exact spectrum compression function is derived, which can obtain the unambiguous ground plane TOPS mode BP image spectrum through full-aperture compression. On this basis, the phase gradient autofocus (PGA) can be used to quickly complete the full aperture motion error estimation and compensation. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by simulation data processing.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Deceptive Jamming on Azimuth Scanning Multi-mode SAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Detective jamming is one of the main methods of SAR active jamming. After intercepting SAR signals, jammers generate deceptive point targets or scene targets by methods of 2-D convolution modulation to forward echo. The existing jamming system research is usually limited to strip SAR, but deceptive jamming has different characteristics in multi-mode SAR. Based on the azimuth scanning multi-mode SAR signal model and the jamming signal model, this paper describes the special time-frequency relation leading to different effects, and verifies the analysis results through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: 3D Near-field Fast Imaging Method for MMW MIMO Array Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper proposes a three dimensional (3D) fast imaging algorithm for multiple inputs and multiple outputs (MIMO) array radar based on 3D wavenumber support domain approximation. Firstly, the MIMO array radar system and echo signal model are introduced and extended into the wavenumber support domain form. Then, the Born approximation theory of 3D wavenumber support domain of reference point for MIMO array is established to fast imaging. Based on that, the 3D fast imaging results with reference points of different sub-scenes are splicing and fusing to reconstruct the fine imaging result to eliminate the distortion and defocus caused by the approximation phase error. Finally, a real imaging experiments are conducted with a millimeter-wave MIMO array near field imaging system to demonstrate the performance and feasibility of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Analysis of polarimetric weather radar data quality in the region of large normalized spectrum width
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The data quality of polarimetric weather radar is affected by the spectrum width (SW), especially for the alternate transmission and alternate reception (ATAR) mode weather radars, where the interval between co-polarization signals is twice the pulse repetition time (PRT). Therefore, with the increase of the SW, the correlation of the signals decreases rapidly, leading to the degradation of the data quality. Moreover, for weather radars using the dual pulse repetition frequency (PRF) technique, different PRFs of adjacent radials have different impacts on the performance of radar data, resulting in differences in the estimates for adjacent radials. In this paper, we analyze the bias and standard deviation (SD) of radar data for different normalized SWs and PRF ratios using generated weather-like time-series I/Q data by signal simulation. The results show that when the normalized SW (NSW) is larger than a specific value, the values of bias and SD of radar data (except SNR) increase. For the weather radar using DPRF, the estimated SW from a ratio of lag-0 to lag-2 autocorrelations (SW02 estimator) and the correlation coefficient (CC) are most likely to show stripes. When the NSW is less than 0.3, the striated data can be avoided. Finally, the measured Ku-band weather radar data is used for verification, when the SW is greater than 2.5 m/s (i.e., NSW>0.32), the estimated SWs using the SW02 estimator and CCs have obvious stripes, which is consistent with the theoretical analysis results.

articleTitle: Cascaded Calibration Method for High Resolution Automotive Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Beamforming technology plays a crucial role in autonomous driving systems, enhancing the target resolution and positioning accuracy of array radars. However, array radars often suffer from various errors due to weather and environmental conditions, which significantly affect the performance of digital beamforming algorithms. To solve this issue, a cascaded calibration algorithm without the accurate calibration sources and rotation information, capable of effectively estimating gain-phase error, is proposed. This algorithm ensures that the calibrated array beam closely aligns with the desired direction, addressing the calibration residual issues in existing algorithms. Finally, simulation experiments indicate that the method can effectively and stably calibrate arrays with gain-phase error even under conditions of low SNR, small snapshots, and limited array elements.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-based Approach to 3D Reconstruction of Asteroids Using Ground-based Radar Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The principal method employed for the three-dimensional(3D) reconstruction of asteroids is the optimisation method based on spherical harmonic functions. Nevertheless, this approach is inherently time-consuming and prone to local optima, which can lead to the emergence of distortions in the resulting 3D shapes. In order to address these issues, this paper puts forward a deep learning-based method for the reconstruction of asteroids in three dimensions. The dataset employed for the deep learning method comprises multi-angle range-Doppler images of asteroids consisting of a range of shapes. In order to demonstrate the robustness of this method, this paper presents the reconstruction of 3D models of asteroids with several different shapes. This paper provides a comparison of the reconstruction accuracy. The above analysis demonstrates that the proposed method is effective in reconstructing 3D models of asteroids. This paper improves the limitations of conventional methods.

articleTitle: An Unsupervised Domain Adversarial Wavelet Learning Method for registration of Optical and SAR Heterogeneous Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Optical images and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) remote sensing images are highly complementary information for Earth observation and applications. Accurate registration of these two data types is essential for subsequent collaboration processing and analysis. However, traditional methods struggle to achieve effective registration due to nonlinear radiometric disparities and geometric distortions. Meanwhile, supervised deep learning approaches require costly manual annotations. To address these issues, this paper proposes an unsupervised registration method based on domain adversarial wavelet learning. We innovatively design an inter-domain adversarial mutual transfer (IAT) module to alleviate cross-modal differences while preserving structural features. Additionally, wavelet transform is employed at different scales for feature matching, to mitigate radiometric disparities and enhance feature recognizability. By incorporating an attention mechanism, the network structure is optimized through spatial alignment and image similarity. The proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative and qualitative aspects of benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: SAR Deceptive Jamming Using Space-Time Coding Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper aims to implement Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) deceptive jamming by utilizing a Space-time coding array (STCA) to secure the target from imminent threats, which is of significance in the modern warfare. At the modelling stage, a SAR deceptive jamming scheme is developed by introducing a time offset across array elements to shift the transmitted signal, which is termed as the STCA. In this context, the extra degrees-of-freedom (DOFs) is obtained, and multiple false targets can be generated in the range domain. Notably, the number and position of false targets can be flexibly and accurately specified through the design of array element number and time offset. Moreover, the azimuth micromotion modulation is employed by encoding the slow time pulses and transmit elements, which is capable of changing the azimuth position of each false target. Finally, the range-Doppler (RD) algorithm is applied to perform SAR high-resolution imaging. Numerical simulation results illuminate the effectiveness and feasibility of developed scheme for SAR jamming in terms of different system parameters.

articleTitle: Interpretable SAR Target Recognition Based on White Box Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) as an all-weather, all-time imaging radar has extensive application value in both military and civilian fields. Although the application of deep learning technology has significantly improved the accuracy of SAR image target recognition, the lack of transparency and interpretability in traditional neural networks greatly limits the application of deep learning models in the SAR field. To address the "black box" issue of traditional neural network models and further enhance the application of deep learning models in the SAR field, this paper introduces the recent interpretable white-box neural networks into SAR target recognition task and discusses the potentials in terms of the performance, robustness and interpretability. The applied white-box neural networks are designed mathematically derivable and implemented with neural network structures. The decision-making process of the model can be analyzed in detail to gain a deeper understanding of its internal mechanisms. Extensive experiments are conducted on the MSTAR dataset. The results show that the white-box neural networks not only achieved high accuracy but also demonstrated strong interpretability and robustness with noisy labels. This research provides new insights into the development of SAR target recognition technology and lays the foundation for the design and implementation of future interpretable and intelligent radar systems.

articleTitle: Sparse Array Optimization for Beampattern Synthesis with Low-Bit Phase Quantization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthesis of beampattern with low-bit phase quantization is a worthwhile research problem in extensive applications. In this paper, we focus on minimizing the number of elements under the low-bit phase quantization constraint. After establishing a quantization-based beampattern synthesis model, a mixed-norm optimization problem is raised for sparse array construction. By solving the problem via reweighted ℓ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> norm approximation, optimal configuration of the sparse array is obtained. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method with low-bit phase quantization.

articleTitle: Scanning Radar Angular Superresolution for Low SNR Applications by Modified Combination Regularization Norms Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Regularization algorithms with combination regularization terms have an advantage at improving the angular resolution of the forward-looking scanning radar. Especially, the combination of L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> regularization constraint and total variation (TV) regularization constraint can simultaneously improve the angular resolution and achieve clear outline reconstruction performance. However, the ill-posed feature of convolution matrix leads to serious noise amplification phenomenon in the superresolution imaging procedure. In this paper, an modified combination regularization norms (M-CRN) approach is proposed to improve the angular resolution of forward-looking scanning radar when the echo signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is low. First, based on the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> regularization norm and TV regularization norm, the forward-looking scanning radar superresolution problem is modeled as a combination regularization norms problem. Second, the iterative re-weighted least square (IRLS) method is applied to obtain the optimized solution of the objective function. Finally, in the iterative procedure, the convolution matrix is repaired through the truncated singular value decomposition (TSVD) strategy, which can mitigate the ill-posed feature of convolution matrix, resulting in the combination regularization terms approach can be used in the low SNR applications. Simulations are carried out to demonstrate the proposed M-CRN approach.

articleTitle: A Parallel Mechanism for Fast Digital SIC in Full-Duplex ISAC systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A novel parallel mechanism for rapid digital-domain self-interference cancellation (SIC) in full-duplex (FD) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems is proposed. The processing delay is minimized by employing a parallel cancellation architecture and substituting filtered sampling symbols with known modulation symbols, thus enabling effective and timely SIC for radar sensing. The proposed parallel SIC technique is presented through comprehensive system modeling, algorithm definition, feasibility assessment, numerical simulations, and experimental validations. The analysis shows that the proposed algorithm, with its high convergence speed, can effectively eliminate self-interference under severe conditions of self-interference and high-frequency variations, thereby enhancing the SIC capabilities of the full-duplex ISAC platform and contributing to the improvement of sensing performance.

articleTitle: An Efficient Multi-Antenna Wideband Digital Channelization Structure for FPGA Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Digital channelization plays an important role in passive sensing. In this paper, a novel efficient multi-antenna digital channelization structure for FPGA implementation is proposed. From the perspective of time division multiplexing, pipelines are designed to process the whole data from all antennas in turn without delay. In this proposed structure, the polyphase filter module and the parallel FFT module are divided into a small block by time division recalling for complexity reduction. This pipeline-based structure ensures the data are processed sequentially within limited number of FPGA clocks, and significantly reduces the number of complex multiplications, which facilitates the implementation in resource-limited FPGA.

articleTitle: A Vital Signs Intelligent Detection Framework of FMCW MIMO Radar Based on 3-D Beamforming and Muli-site Fusion of Heartbeat Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper presents a framework for frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar non-contact vital sign monitoring to achieve accurate heart rate (HR) in low SNR environments. The framework consists of two main parts. The first part includes a 3-D cardiac beamformer based on heartbeat signal quality, which is a beamformer composed of the distance dimension, azimuth and zenith angles. Proposed a new beamformer method and combined with the heart signal quality evaluation model to focus the radar array beam on the human heart to improve the signal quality. The second part proposed the multipart signal fusion (MSF) method, which fuses the reflection intensity of different parts of the trunk to improve the signal-to-noise ratio, thereby improving the performance of BR and HR. Finally, the HR and BR signals are separated by filter.

articleTitle: Tidal Deformation of Asteroids Measurement With Earth-based Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The observation of tidal deformation of asteroids is of significant value to the field of astronomy, as it offers an indirect means of discerning the internal structure and material distribution of these celestial bodies. The measurement of tidal deformation of asteroids has been in its infancy due to the limitations of optical observation accuracy and radar imaging resolution. In this paper, we employ differential interferometric synthetic aperture radar (D-InSAR) to model the tidal deformation of asteroids process and analyze the temporal and spatial baselines. We then introduce the asteroid ISAR imaging and D-InSAR methods. Subsequently, the tidal deformation of asteroids is modelled using numerical simulation software and simulation experiments are conducted. The line of sight to deformation was obtained for the radar images both before and after the deformation, using a D-InSAR process. The deformation error is on the order of sub-mm-level, and the simulation proves the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: DEM estimation algorithm based on offset correction for GNSS-based InBSAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: DEM with low accuracy will bring offsets to the target position in the imaging results. For GNSS-based InBSAR, the system has the characteristics of low bandwidth and poor resolution, and the offset phenomenon will be aggravated. Therefore, DEM estimation algorithm based on offset correction is proposed. The algorithm introduces the least squares to obtain the local DEM. Then, the offset estimation variance and the resolution cell size are used to determine the imaging range. Finally, the optimal global DEM is obtained based on the offset. The algorithm reduces the offset effect caused by low-precision DEM, and the measured data confirm the effectiveness of the algorithm

articleTitle: Preliminary Results of UAV-Borne High-Squint SAR Sub-Aperture Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Unmanned-aerial-vehicle (UAV) borne high-squint synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can flexibly provide two-dimensional (2-D) radar images of the oblique forward areas in advance. In 2024, a high-squint SAR data acquisition experiment using a high-band radar system mounted on a multi-rotor UAV was carried out successfully. The experiment is demonstrated in this paper, including SAR system introduction, experiment design, data processing and imaging results. Finally, a high-squint SAR sub-aperture image is obtained by using the method introduced in this paper.

articleTitle: Waveform Design to Mitigate Mutual Interference between Automotive MIMO Radars
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Millimeter-wave radar has been extensively employed in intelligent transportation systems to enhance the traffic safety. However, mutual interference between different automotive radars can distort the reflected echoes. To mitigate this issue, a novel multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) orthogonal waveform design method is introduced in this paper. Precisely, a new optimization model on the basis of the p-norm metric is first constructed, which converges to the peak sidelobe level (PSL) minimization of correlation functions as p approaches infinity. Furthermore, derivations are performed so as to leverage the fast Fourier transform (FFT) and inverse FFT (IFFT) operations during following optimization to reduce running time. Finally, the gradient descent (GD) technique is utilized to find out the optimum orthogonal waveforms promising desired correlation properties. Massive numerical experiments verify the high computational efficiency and superior correlation properties of the proposed method in comparison with the state-of-the-art ones.

articleTitle: Comparison of Pansharpening Algorithms: Developing a Data-Driven Evaluation Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Convolutional neural network (CNN)-based methods are increasingly crucial in image processing and computer vision. In remote sensing image pansharpening, CNNs have shown excellent fusion performance, attracting significant research interest. However, challenges remain, such as the lack of detailed pansharpening dataset simulations, standardized training-testing datasets, and simple, unified coding frameworks. Additionally, there is insufficient evaluation of recent deep learning pansharpening methods and evaluation of algorithms from the perspective of different subsequent applications, limiting comprehensive evaluation. This study constructs a comprehensive evaluation system for datasets, fusion algorithms, and evaluation methods. By statistically analyzing results, improve the accuracy and richness of algorithm evaluations, enabling more effective and objective method comparisons. Used WorldView-2 satellite imagery for visual assessments, supervised and unsupervised quantitative evaluations on 100 images, and land cover classification accuracy experiments. Traditional methods like BDSD and PRACS showed strong fusion results and land cover classification accuracy, deep learning methods generally outperformed traditional ones. This research provides detailed images and data resources for pansharpening, offering valuable references for future studies in this field.

articleTitle: Quantitative Suppression Method For FMCW SAR Leakage Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The traditional continuous wave radar system increases the distance between the transmitting and receiving antennas and improves the isolation between them, which is not suitable for small platforms such as satellite and airborne. This article proposes a quantitative suppression method for FMCW SAR leakage signal. By utilizing the stability of the leakage signal and implementing sampling quantization to filter out weak echo signals, a FMCW SAR signal extraction system is designed based on this method.

articleTitle: A Novel Three-Stage PolSAR Ship Detection Framework based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PolSAR) image ship detection is one of the crucial applications of PolSAR systems and holds significant research value. However, current deep learning-based polarimetric SAR image ship detection methods face challenges such as difficult post-processing and slow detection speed. To solve the above problems, we propose a novel Three-Stage Polarimetric SAR Ship Detection Framework based on deep learning. The main concept is to use a sliding window to extract image slice samples, then employ the Ship Coarse Location Module (SCLM) to identify slice samples containing ships. Next, the Polarization Feature Enhancement Module (PFEM) enhances the features of these slice samples to reduce the feature distance of pixels of the same category and increase the feature distance of pixels of different categories. Afterward, the enhanced slice samples are fed into the KAN Vision Transformer Detection Module (KVITDM) for patch-level detection. Finally, decision fusion is applied to combine the detection results generated from different initial sliding window positions. Experimental results show that the proposed method has good performance in different scenes and outperforms traditional and existing deep learning-based polarimetric SAR ship detection methods.

articleTitle: A Robust Parameter Estimation Method of Space Targets Based on the Information Fusion of Wideband and Narrowband Radar Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Structural and micro-motion parameter estimation of space targets is crucial for target recognition. Because of the shortcomings of the same type radar in parameter estimation, a method is proposed for estimating the parameters of space targets based on a hybrid-scheme radar network. By effectively fusing the characteristics of radars, the method achieves robust and precise estimation. Firstly, the micro-Doppler and micro-range curves of the scattering centers are obtained through feature extraction algorithms with high precision and robustness. Then, using a combination of a wideband and a narrowband radar as the basis, the parameters are preliminarily estimated. This method can also achieve effective estimation when the line-of-sight of radars are similar, demonstrating good adaptability. Finally, the parameter information estimated from all combinations is fused to further enhance the estimation accuracy. Simulation results show that when the signal-to-noise ratio is greater than 0 dB, the estimation accuracy of the proposed method is superior to simply taking the mean of the parameter groups, demonstrating good robustness and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Robust Adaptive OS-CFAR Detector for Maneuvering Group Target Based on Formation Prior Knowledge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Detecting the individuals such like the bird flocks or a UAV swarm is a great challenge for radar systems. The lack of prior knowledge about the characteristics of dynamic group targets leads to the performance degradation of conventional detectors. In this study, we present a robust adaptive OS-CFAR detector for maneuvering group targets, leveraging prior knowledge of their formation. The group target’s state is updated and predicted using the random matrix approach. The projection length of the group target in the radar beam direction is computed using the predicted information during the group target tracking process. Using the projection length, the number of reference units occupied by the group target within the reference window is determined, and this prior knowledge is applied to update the detection parameters of the OS-CFAR detector. The simulation result shows that the algorithm can update the detection parameters timely and avoid target missed detection.

articleTitle: SAR Aircraft Detection based on Scattering Enhancement and Location Attention network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to the interference caused by the complex background and the discreteness of aircraft scattering, the task of detecting aircraft in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images remains a challenging one. To address these problems, a novel method named scattering enhancement and location attention network (SELANet) is here proposed to detect aircraft via combining traditional image processing and deep learning together. At first, a scattering information enhancement module (SIEM) is proposed to highlight the scattering points of aircraft targets. Moreover, to more effectively focus on the location of aircraft targets, a spatial location attention module (SLAM) is further designed. Experiments are performed on the SADD dataset and the results indicate that SELANet is more apt for aircraft detection. On average, the Precision, Recall, and F1-score values are respectively 3.6%, 2.9%, and 3.2% higher than the baseline of standard YOLOv8s algorithm.

articleTitle: A CTU-Level Rate Control Algorithm for Screen Content Based on GLCM Characteristic Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the rapid development of interactive services such as cloud gaming and cloud desktop, the efficient compression of screen content has become increasingly important. These services offload application storage and computation to the cloud, reducing reliance on local hardware and emphasizing the need for high-quality video transmission over networks. This paper addresses the challenges in screen content coding (SCC) by proposing a novel rate control algorithm tailored for screen content, which is distinct from traditional video due to its unique characteristics like sharp text edges and repetitive graphic patterns. Our approach leverages the Grey Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) feature extraction to perform texture complexity analysis at the Coding Tree Unit (CTU) level, optimizing bit allocation based on the texture's angular second moment (ASM). We introduce a method to estimate the similarity of adjacent blocks and dynamically adjust bit allocation to account for this. The proposed method ensures low latency and stable bitrate, crucial for cloud gaming and desktop applications. Extensive experiments on the HM-16.10+SCM-7.0 and HCM-16.20+SCM-8.8 demonstrate that our approach significantly improves bitrate accuracy and compression efficiency while achieving superior subjective video quality. The algorithm's performance is benchmarked against state-of-the-art methods, showcasing its effectiveness in various screen content scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhanced GP-PNF Detector for PolSAR Image Pixel-level Detection using Target Characteristics Modeling and Superpixel Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) target detection method based on geometric perturbation filter and superpixel segmentation is proposed to address the issues of high computational complexity and insufficient utilization of polarimetric information in existing pixel-based and superpixel-based target detection methods. In the detection stage, the PolSAR image is first decomposed into polarimetric components, and the polarization characteristics of the target are modeled. Then, a set of geometrical perturbation-polarimetric notch filter groups (GP-PNF) is constructed to enhance the contrast between the target and clutter and achieve coarse localization of the interested targets in complex scenes. The detection results of GP-PNF are further subjected to superpixel segmentation, and a superpixel-level polarimetric dissimilarity metric (SCDM) is defined to distinguish further the polarization characteristic differences between targets and clutter in local regions, reducing false alarm rates. Comparative experiments were conducted using real measured polarimetric data of ground background with various classical detection algorithms. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively detect targets in complex backgrounds of PolSAR images without requiring background modeling.

articleTitle: Tomographic imaging method of GB-ArcSAR with arc-shaped interferometric baseline
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: When observing building scenarios, there exists the layover problem. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) tomography can use multiple two-dimensional (2D) SAR images acquired from different heights to inverse the range-azimuth-height 3D information of the targets. Ground-based arc-scanning synthetic aperture radar (GB-ArcSAR) can obtain a series of SAR images at different heights by performing azimuthal scanning on horizontal planes with different pitch angles, which makes it has tomography capabilities. However, the baseline of GB-ArcSAR is arc-shaped, which makes the existing tomographic imaging methods suitable for linear tomographic baselines cannot be directly applied to GB-ArcSAR. This paper proposes a tomographic imaging method of GB-ArcSAR with arc-shaped interferometric baseline. Through Taylor expansion of the distance between the target and the sampling position, a mapping relationship between the target pitch angle and interferometric phase was established. Based on the mapping relationship, the measurement matrix was constructed. Validation of the proposed method is achieved through simulations and measured data.

articleTitle: A Novel Quantification Method of Cardiopulmonary Coupling Based on Cross-Frequency Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Dynamic heart rate is a reflection of the functionality of the autonomic nervous system (ANS) and is closely related to vital signs. Combining it with respiratory signals for the analysis of cardiopulmonary coupling (CPC) can provide a more precise depiction of physiological states. However, traditional CPC algorithms emphasize the correlation within the identical frequency band of respiration and heart rate variability (HRV), which may not effectively reveal the intrinsic relationship between them. A novel method of quantifying CPC bidirectionally and across multiple frequency bands is proposed in this study by employing the Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) and phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) techniques, applying it to analyze respiratory signals and Electrocardiograms (ECG) from groups of different ages to assess the performance of their autonomic nervous system. We observed a superiority of CPC value in healthy infants, indicating a decline in the function of ANS as one ages.

articleTitle: Self-Ensemble Semi Supervised Learning Based SAR and Multispectral Local Climate Zone Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Local climate zones are essential for understanding urban climates and their effect on environmental processes. Here we demonstrate self-ensemble learning based approach to classify local climate zone. The big So2Sat LCZ42 benchmark dataset has been used in this paper. The dataset contains SAR and multispectral data from sentinel 1 and sentinel-2 satellites. SAR has the capability to penetrate though cloud cover and provide surface structure and texture information, whereas multispectral data provides spectral information to distinguish waterbodies, vegetation and built-up areas. Semi supervised learning using Student-Teacher network and Student-Student has been implemented in this paper to increase the accuracy achieved by baseline neural network. Student-Teacher network (ST-Net) use exponential moving average, and that’s why the teacher network is tightly coupled with student network. we use Student-Student network (SS-Net) by replacing teacher with an independent student. The SS-Net is not tightly coupled and hence performs better than baseline (Resnet) and ST-Net.

articleTitle: Parametric Sparse Representation Based Technique For 2-D SAR Autofocusing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Aiming at the azimuth defocusing problem of SAR image caused by the unstable velocity of the platform, an autofocusing method based on parametric orthogonal matching pursuit (P-OMP) algorithm is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the SAR echo data is processed by range dimension pulse compression and migration correction. Then the range-cell of the strong scattering point is selected according to the energy distribution. Based on P-OMP algorithm, the optimal focusing factor is estimated from the selected range-cell data. With the estimated focusing factor, a well-focused image can be obtained. Experimental results shown the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Impact of seasonal change on deformation measurement performance of GNSS-based InBSAR in vegetated area: preliminary results
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System-based bistatic Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (GNSS-based InBSAR) stands as an efficient approach to realize mm-level deformation measurements. To elucidate the impact of seasonal variations on the performance of GNSS-based InBSAR deformation measurements in vegetated areas, a statistical and analytical assessment of long-term observation data from Beidou Navigation Satellite (BDS) is conducted in this paper. The results demonstrate that there is an obvious improvement in deformation measurements accuracy during 2024.01.01-2024.03.02. This finding is consistent with the arrival of winter and the decreasing trend of surface vegetation density. The impact of seasonal change on deformation measurement performance of GNSS-based InBSAR in vegetated area is validated.

articleTitle: Fine-Grained Recognition Framework For Ship Targets In SAR Images Based On Component Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Applying deep learning network models in SAR image processing has significantly improved speed of target recognition performance. Nevertheless, due to the SAR imaging principle distinct from optical images, these models struggle to distinguish strong scattering characteristics from clutter, resulting in a high false alarm rate in applications of target recognition. To ensure correctness practically, the expert analysis for discern various structures is strongly necessary for fine-grained recognition after possessing through integrating intelligent models, with extra time and manpower cost. This study introduces a fine-grained recognition framework for ship targets in SAR images based on component architecture. A ship targets dataset from Gaofen-3 SAR images, with three classified ship types is designed to train the model, including meticulous analysis and labeling for target categorization, axis orientation, and key component localization. Features of different dimensions extracted via pre-trained ResNet-50 to construct a weight dossier, and a multi-task joint detection mode are embedded into the framework to integrate the experts’ ship recognition method built on component architecture into the intelligent network model. This yields an accuracy rate surpassing 89% for ship identification, eclipsing conventional intelligence models by a significant margin. The framework successfully bolsters the ability of target awareness affiliated with SAR ocean monitoring.

articleTitle: Improved multiple hypothesis tracking using incomplete measurements for group targets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Tracking targets within a group has received much attention in the radar field recently years. Group targets are usually closely spaced with similar velocity, making it hard to distinguish multiple targets. For precise target tracking, the tracking radar usually employs a narrow beam to achieve the high range-angular resolution. However, targets may enter and exit the narrow beam frequently during the observation, bringing difficulty for stable tracking. Moreover, it is also hard to distinguish different targets when their tracks intersect on the range-doppler plane. These kinds of incomplete measurements increase the difficulty of group targets' association and tracking. Therefore, this paper proposes an improved multiple hypothesis tracking method using incomplete measurements. The adaptive detection probability model and track intersecting probability are combined in the multiple hypothesis tracking framework to reduce false associations and improve tracking performance. Finally, simulation and experiment results verified the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Two-Dimensional Imaging Method Of Vortex Electromagnetic Waves Using FDA Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, a two-dimensional imaging method of vortex electromagnetic waves based on frequency diverse array (FDA), which generates time-varying orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes, is analyzed. Based on the FDA-OAM model, the different mode vortex electromagnetic wave beam can be obtained at the target point by setting different array parameters and sampling times. In this paper, a time-varying OAM beam based on a circular FDA array is designed, which enhances the flexibility of the vortex electromagnetic wave mode and shows the unique advantage of FDA in OAM beam formation. In addition, the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm is introduced in this paper to realize the 2D imaging of single target and multiple target point distance and azimuthal direction, which eliminates the angular aliasing phenomenon during fast Fourier transform (FFT) imaging under Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) structure. The simulation results verify that the proposed FDA-OAM can realize the high-resolution imaging of target distance and azimuthal direction.

articleTitle: An Efficient Transposition Method for Spaceborne SAR Data Based on HBM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The onboard real-time processing of Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is of great significance for the rapid acquisition of surface information. As a key step of SAR imaging processing, the efficiency of data transposition directly affects the imaging quality and processing speed. In order to solve the problem of traditional double data rate synchronous dynamic random-access memory (DDR SDRAM) limiting the transposition speed, this paper proposes a SAR data transposition method based on high bandwidth memory (HBM). The method makes full use of the high bandwidth and multichannel characteristics of HBM, and significantly improves the transposition speed by optimising the data read/write process, providing a new solution for real-time imaging processing of satellite-borne SAR.

articleTitle: Design of a Sanskrit Devanagari Script Recognition and Sanskrit to Chinese Translation System Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This study endeavors to enhance the accuracy of Sanskrit Devanagari script recognition through advanced deep learning techniques and to achieve accurate conversion from Sanskrit to Chinese using machine translation technology, in support of the digitization of ancient literature and the preservation of cultural heritage. A combination of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) is used for text recognition, along with a neural machine translation system based on the Transformer model for translating Sanskrit to Chinese. Experimental results show that the OCR system employed in this study achieves an accuracy rate of 89%, a recall rate of 77%, and an F1 score of 0.826 in recognizing Sanskrit text. The machine translation system effectively converts Sanskrit into semantically accurate Chinese text, with translation quality quantified by BLEU and METEOR evaluation metrics, reaching scores of 41% and 30% respectively. In summary, the findings of this paper not only optimize the text processing workflow for Sanskrit but also provide a similar framework and practical experience for text recognition and translation of other similar languages, contributing to the further advancement of cultural exchange and linguistic research.

articleTitle: Refined Time-Frequency Feature Matching for Interrupted Sampling Repeater Jamming Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Interrupted sampling repeater jamming (ISRJ), a common form of coherent jamming, can create numerous false targets surrounding the real target after pulse compression, significantly affecting the target detection ability of radar. To solve this problem, a refined time-frequency (TF) feature matching method based on the intra-pulse frequency agile (IPFA) waveform for ISRJ suppression is proposed. Firstly, the TF template is constructed based on the transmitted waveform TF distribution. The feature information is extracted by shifting the TF template and matching the result of the binarization of the echo TF distribution. Then, the target echo is located according to the feature information extracted from the TF template under different shift times. Next, the time-domain signal is extracted by the inverse TF transformation of the echo TF distribution, which is matched to the template of the target location. The undisturbed signal is extracted to construct the range-dimension filter. Finally, the extracted time domain signal is filtered for jamming suppression and target protection.
