Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method performs better ISRJ suppression than conventional methods. Meanwhile, the proposed method effectively mitigates the compound jamming composed of different ISRJs, demonstrating strong resistance to jamming.

articleTitle: Stroke Extraction Method for Calligraphy Characters Based on Enhanced Pix2pix Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Extracting strokes from calligraphy characters is a key challenge in preserving traditional Chinese calligraphy digitally. In this paper, we propose a new method of stroke extraction using the Pix2pix network, which includes advanced attention mechanisms and a multi-scale discriminator. We add contextual transformer block and multi-head self-attention modules to the generator to better capture detailed strokes, focusing on edges and intersecting areas. Additionally, a multi-scale discriminator evaluates features at different resolutions, improving precision by distinguishing real images from generated ones. This method effectively solves the challenges of stroke extraction in calligraphy characters. The experimental results clearly demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Integrated Sensing and Communication Based Deformation Monitoring in Practical 5G Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is attracting significant attention and is the key to meeting future mobile communication requirements. The feasibility of ISAC has been verified in use cases such as multi-target detection, environmental reconstruction, and personnel breathing. To expand the use cases, this paper explores the capbility of deformation monitoring based on ISAC. First, derive a deformation model and introduce the hardware prototype. We use 5G commercial base stations deployed widely to transmit configured monitoring signals. The experiments are conducted in typical outdoor environments with large objects around. A corner reflector moves by a specific distance that simulates the target deformation. Second, determine the positions of the target and reference point in the ranging-angle (RA) map and calculate the phase change of the target in real time. Third, estimate the deformation size based on the phase change of the target echo signal. The experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper can achieve millimeter-level deformation monitoring accuracy, which can be compared to the performance of traditional methods.

articleTitle: Multi-frequency jitter detection and analysis based on parallax imaging for remote sensing satellite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: As the resolution of satellite payloads continues to enhance, the vibrations of the platform increasingly undermine the geometric accuracy of high-resolution satellite imagery. This degradation significantly impacts the precision of CCD geometric splicing, the accuracy of positioning, and the overall clarity of the images. The existing research only focuses on the detection and modeling of single-frequency platform jitters, and there is insufficient research on cases involving multiple frequencies. Therefore, we propose a multi-frequency jitter detection method for remote sensing satellites based on parallax imaging and elaborate on the process of multi-frequency jitter detection in detail. Firstly, high-precision registration errors are identified through dense matching techniques. Subsequently, they are analyzed with Fourier transforms and corrected using sine functions. Finally, multi-frequency modeling is performed using the sine function model. The consistency of the modeling results between different CCD is presented, proving the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Scattering Centers Parameter Estimation Accuracy and Resolution Improvement Limit Derivation of Multiband Fusion Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multiband fusion (MBF) technology has the ability to achieve a high inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) range resolution without a hardware upgrade. In this technology, several sub-band echoes (SBE) corresponding to different bandwidth and different center frequenmcy are fused to produce wideband echoes (WBE). Therefore, the resolution of the SBE is improved. In state of art MBF methods, the SBE are assumed to obey a scattering model and the scattering center parameters (SCP) in the model are estimated to reconstruct the WBE. However, there is a lack of derivation of the accuracy of SCP and the limit of resolution improvement under the geometric theory of diffraction (GTD) model. The Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) is used to achieve the deravation in this paper.

articleTitle: Space-Time Adaptive Processing Algorithm for EPC-MIMO radar via 3D Atomic Norm Minimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The issue of suppressing range-ambiguous clutter is explored with Element-Pulse Coding (EPC)-Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar in this paper. In general, by incorporating a tunable coding coefficient in both slow-time pulses and transmitted elements, the range-ambiguous clutter can be distinguished from different range ambiguity regions in transmit spatial frequency dimension, and further suppressed through Space-Time Adaptive Processing (STAP)-based method. In specific, to tackle the problem of insufficient Independent Identical Distribution (IID) training samples, a STAP-based method utilizing Three-Dimensional Atomic Norm Minimization (3D-ANM) is proposed to reconstruct the clutter covariance matrix (CCM). Simulations are performed to confirm the efficacy of the proposed 3D-ANM algorithm.

articleTitle: Cross-Band Fusion for Multispectral Scene Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the daily acquisition of vast amounts of remote sensing images by satellites, effectively utilizing these images for Earth observation has become a significant research focus. Multispectral image scene classification plays a fundamental role in advancing the understanding of remote sensing imagery. Existing methods for multispectral image scene classification do not sufficiently explore the interrelationships between different bands, which limits the performance of models in this task. Unlike these, we propose a cross-band fusion method for multispectral scene classification. Specifically, we employ two appropriate visual backbones to extract band-level visual features from different bands, followed by a cross-band fusion module to fuse the features from various bands adaptively. This approach fully explores the complementary information between different bands, achieving enhanced accuracy in multispectral scene classification. Extensive experiments on a commonly used dataset BigEarthNet validate that our proposed cross-band fusion method outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods.

articleTitle: Wide-Area Spaceborne TOPSAR Interferometric Registration Processing Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to meet the high-precision registration requirements for TOPS mode with multiple Burst images, this paper conducts an investigation into the interferometric imaging methods for multi-Burst data and proposes an improved Enhanced Spectral Diversity (ESD) algorithm registration technique on the basis of Sentinel-1A satellite data. First, the single look complex (SLC) data are subjected to deramping processing, which transforms the azimuth signal into a baseband signal, facilitating next registration processing.The second step include both coarse and fine registration. Some residual systematic offsets still remain after the coarse registration, which need fine registration to compensate.The fine registration presented in this paper has been improved based on the traditional ESD algorithm, simplifying the overall process and enhancing the registration accuracy.Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of this processing method have been verified through experimental validation.

articleTitle: Retina and Choroid Segmentation Method Based on Multi-scale Feature Extraction and Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The change of layer thickness of retina and choroid is closely related to eye diseases. In clinical applications, optical coherence tomography (OCT) is utilized to visualize retina and choroid. Precise segmentation of the retina and choroid in fundus OCT images is essential for the early detection and diagnosis of ocular diseases. Effective feature extraction and feature fusion have not been fully explored in current studies, which results in poor segmentation results. This paper presents a novel end-to-end segmentation framework for simultaneous segmentation of the retina and choroid. To extract more effective features, a multi-scale channel feature extraction module is designed, which increases the network’s receptive field and allows for the acquisition of effective channel information. To fuse deep features with shallow features, a cross fusion module is proposed, capturing the relationship between high-level features and low-level features. Experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms others in segmentation performance.

articleTitle: Preliminary Exploration of Unknown Object Detection in Terahertz Radar Images through Incremental Recognition Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Hidden object detection in terahertz radar images is crucial for public security and anti-terrorism efforts. Detecting unknown objects in real-world scenarios remains a challenging issue. To address this, we propose a novel study using incremental recognition methods. This approach trains with only a few samples from new object classes without needing to retrain old classes, reducing training time and cost while preserving recognition of previously learned objects. Within our research, we employ the Faster R-CNN architecture as the fundamental object detection model, subjecting it to training on both the base and new classes. To enhance training for new classes, we employ a new-class aware RPN to automatically label new class objects and use a fine-tuning strategy. Our experiments on the Active Terahertz Imaging Dataset for incremental recognition yielded good results. Our proposed method achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 41.4% for recognizing all classes. Additionally, the recognition performance for new classes improved by 6.7% in Average Precision (AP) compared to simply incorporating new class training. This demonstrates the feasibility of incremental recognition for unknown object detection and validates the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Spatial Modeling and Multi-Scale Attention Aggregation for Semantic Segmentation of Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: As remote sensing technology advances and high-resolution sensors are deployed, the analysis of high-resolution remote sensing images encounters challenging issues, such as intra-class variability, and inter-class similarity, due to the unobvious appearance and complicated background. The high-resolution remote sensing images pose critical issues for precise semantic segmentation due to these fundamental issues. To this end, we propose an adaptive hierarchical aggregation network. Different from the previous approach of modeling semantic interdependencies solely within a single feature map in the channel dimension, we introduce multi-scale channel-wise feature aggregation to capture global contextual dependencies. Meanwhile, we design an adaptive detail-aware module to model long-range spatial dependencies, adaptively extracting effective details from different levels as compensation. Additionally, this module utilizes depth-wise separable convolution to selectively filter out irrelevant spatial details from lower-level feature maps. The outputs of the two modules are fused layer by layer to achieve refined feature representation, thereby generating precise pixel-level segmentation results. Our experiments are conducted on the Vaihingen dataset and the Potsdam dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm surpasses several existing state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: Distributed RF Frequency Transfer with Fixed Phase in Reciprocal Media
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To enhance the coherence and efficiency of distributed radars, we propose a method of distributed RF frequency transfer with fixed phase in reciprocal media. Based on the reciprocal media, each radar unit receives a forward frequency signal from the source and a reverse signal reflected back to eliminate delay and keep the frequency the same as the source, ensuring that the phase of the frequency standard across the radar units remains consistent. A mathematical model has been developed, and an error analysis addressing amplitude and phase imbalances has been conducted. To validate the accuracy of this method, the system was simulated using a 10-meter coaxial cable, demonstrating its robustness and effectiveness in practical scenarios.

articleTitle: Visual Instruction Tuning for Holistic and Regional Remote Sensing Imagery Comprehension
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Recently, the visual instruction multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have been extensively studied in the nature scenario. However, current remote sensing (RS) MLLMs mainly focus on image-level understanding and typically allow interaction only through text instructions, resulting in limited accuracy and efficiency. To address those limitations, a visual instruction model is proposed in this article to extend MLLM’s fine-grained perception ability by incorporating bounding boxes with language instruction, aiming at achieving region-level visual understanding. To achieve this goal, a visual instruction dataset featuring multi-modal box-based region-text pairs is constructed. Furthermore, the visual instructions and images are encoded by the different encoders and subsequently fed into a large language model (LLM) along with text instruction tokens for tuning. Finally, experimental results demonstrate the proposed model’s promising performance in region-level image comprehension.

articleTitle: Wideband MIMO Radar Waveform Design Method For Amplitude-Phase Joint Optimization Under Low PAR Constraint
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: We consider the design of wideband multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar waveforms to approximate the desired beampattern. Radar waveform design is usually challenged by the constants modulu constraint, however, with the improvement of hardware performance,low peak-to-average ratio(PAR) waveforms are acceptable in modern radar systems, for this reason, we allow the waveform mode value to fluctuate in a certain range and obtain the low PAR waveform by alternating phase and amplitude optimization of the waveforms. Comparison with the constant modulus waveform obtained by other methods at normalized energy shows that our designed waveforms have a better approximation of the desired beampattern.

articleTitle: A New Method for ISAR Imaging of Non-cooperative Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the imaging of non-cooperative targets in inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR), the migration through range cells (MTRC) and phase error caused by rotation will lead to image blur. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a harmonic wavelet imaging algorithm based on Keystone transform. The algorithm corrects MTRC through Keystone transform and realizes efficient processing of target signals through harmonic wavelet transform, thereby obtaining high-resolution ISAR images. Moreover, this approach circumvents the need for prior target information, streamlines the imaging process, and is well-suited for high-resolution imaging of non-cooperative targets. The method’s effectiveness is confirmed through scattering point simulation data. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach produces clear and well-focused ISAR images even when targets rotate at varying speeds. In comparison to traditional imaging methods, the image contrast achieved by this algorithm is enhanced by 1 to 2 times.

articleTitle: A Novel Suppression Method for Pulse-Doppler Radar with Coexistence of Clutter and Jamming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Pulse-Doppler radars are widely applied in moving targets detection where jamming and clutter are recurring and inevitable. Previous research has proposed various solutions for jamming and clutter suppression individually. However, the simultaneous existence of typical deception jamming and strong clutter significantly obstructs radar detection performance more than the presence of only one component. This paper proposes a novel suppression method to address the jamming and clutter coexistence problem. We first achieve jamming discrimination and in turn cancel clutter component through constructing clutter subspace. Afterwards, jamming suppression is accomplished by frequency parameters estimation of jamming segments and subspace projection considering the deception jamming time-frequency characteristics. The proposed method can distinctly suppress deception jamming and strong clutter, performing effective target detection after traditional pulse-Doppler processing. Simulations are conducted to verify the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Establishing Clear Regions in Multi-PRF Pulse Doppler Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A novel approach for establishing clear regions in multi-pulse repetition frequency (PRF) pulse Doppler radar is proposed. The clear regions are constructed using the sigmoid function, resulting in a continuously differentiable functional expression for the clear region area. This allows for optimization using gradient-based methods. Compared with Clear Area Evaluation Matrix (CAEM) and Blind Zone Map (BZM) method, the method proposed breaks the limitation of optimization method. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a larger clear region area compared with the CAEM and BZM method.

articleTitle: Doppler Measurement-Based Positioning and Tracking Methods with External Radiation Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper introduces a new approach for addressing the complex problem of Multi-target tracking in external radiation radar systems equipped with Multi-static Doppler measurements. Drawing from research on sensor arrays and mobile sensors, the method utilizes the Generalized Labelled Multi-Bernoulli (GLMB) filter to navigate the intricacies of Multi-target tracking across sensor arrays. The study validates the effectiveness of the GLMB and the computationally efficient Gibbs-GLMB filters in a setup involving three transmitters and one receiver. Experimental results, assessed with the Optimal Sub-Pattern Assignment (OSPA) metric, suggest that the Gibbs-GLMB filter accelerates computation while potentially compromising on measurement precision, which could lead to reduced accuracy in specific cases. The investigation also examines the influence of sensor geometry on tracking results, indicating that there is an association between tracking performance and sensor arrangement.

articleTitle: A modified Lie transform for rough sea surface modeling with breaking waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Sea surface modeling is a powerful tool for radar signal simulation and sea clutter analyses. Especially in some challenging scenarios, e.g., under high sea states, collection of radar sea clutter data is probably unavailable, while realistically modeling of sea surface and electromagnetic echo simulation thereafter enable comprehensive measurements and analyses. Under high sea states, the wind-induced breaking wave phenomenon becomes serious and occupies a large portion of radar backscattering power. However, the standard Lie transform, employed for the nonlinear sea surface generation process, does not take into account the influence of wind speed and direction and therefore cannot describe breaking wave under high sea states. In this paper, a modified Lie transform is proposed for breaking wave modeling under high sea states. The proposed method utilizes a second-order approximation of the Lie transform and incorporates the wind speed and direction factors for nonlinear superposition, allowing for precise descriptions of sea surface varying with sea states. Experiment results validate that the proposed method is consistent with the Cox-Munk testing model and outperforms the standard Lie transform.

articleTitle: Relative Atmospheric Wind Speed Measurement Based on Time-Delay D-InSAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Accurate wind speed measurement is of great significance for meteorological analysis, weather forecasting and climate change research. Spaceborne differential interferometric synthetic aperture radar (D-InSAR), with its all-day, all-weather, high-resolution observation capabilities, has shown potential for indirectly measuring wind speed by monitoring changes in atmospheric water vapor. This paper proposes a method for relative atmospheric wind speed measurement based on time-delay D-InSAR. The principle involves using a distributed satellites monostatic D-InSAR system to acquire atmospheric differential interferograms of the same region within a short time interval. By using image thresholding to identify the displacement of hotspots, we can infer the average relative wind speed from the movement of water vapor clusters. The results demonstrate that D-InSAR can accurately measure the average wind speed, which is a cumulative effect across various altitude layers. The measured wind speed has an average relative error of 0.07 and a root mean square error of 1.02 m/s when compared to the theoretical wind speed. This validates the feasibility of using D-InSAR for wind speed measurement. In the future, this technology could be further extended to 3-D wind speed measurement and enhance accuracy by improving the algorithm, which will offer a new approach for atmospheric wind speed monitoring.

articleTitle: An Automated Extrinsic Calibration Method of a multi-layer LiDAR and a Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This article introduces an innovative technique for automating the extrinsic calibration of LiDAR and camera setups, employing a specially crafted circular calibration target. The process consists of three key phases: initially, the central characteristic and the perpendicular plane of the calibration target are identified within both the point cloud data and the captured imagery. Subsequently, constraint equations are established from these matched features to compute a preliminary estimation of the transformation matrix linking the LiDAR and the camera. In the final phase, a symmetric and nonnegative latent factor model enhanced by triple decomposition is applied to refine the extrinsic calibration to a high degree of precision. Empirical evaluations indicate a 47.59% enhancement in the alignment accuracy of 3D points from the LiDAR coordinate system with those of the image pixel coordinates relative to conventional methods. Notably, this performance improvement persists even under noise conditions reaching up to 0.1 dB, with the maximum reprojection error constrained below 9.35 pixels, thereby underscoring the method's resilience to noise interference.

articleTitle: Fast Spatio-Temporal Signal Recovery Based on Differential Smoothness Regularization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Spatio-temporal signal recovery has been extensively studied, focusing on leveraging signal structures, such as low-rankness and high spatio-temporal smoothness, to recover complete signals. This paper introduces a fast algorithm for spatial-temporal signal recovery based on the differential smoothness regularization, utilizing the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Our proposed algorithm updates variables through associated closed-form solutions in each ADMM iteration and is guaranteed to converge to the global optimum of the optimization problem. Extensive numerical results are presented, demonstrating the superior performance of the proposed algorithm over state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: Joint Secure Transmit Beamforming Designs for Physical Layer Security in MIMO-ISAC System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This article concentrates on the physical layer security (PLS) towards an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, which communicates with legitimate communication users (CUs) and detects the single sensing target, which is considered to be eavesdropper because it might intercept the transmitting message from the base station to CUs. The joint transmitting beamforming for secure communication and sensing is designed to maximize the sum secrecy rate (SR) of system under the constraints of quality-of-service of CUs, the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of sensing and the power budget of the system. The optimal solution is obtained by the semidefinite relaxation and successive convex approximation algorithms. The availability of the beamforming design in ensuring the SR of the ISAC system is showed by Simulation results.

articleTitle: Research and application of pipeline safety monitoring based on fiber Bragg grating sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Monitoring and maintenance of equipment is very important in engineering applications. This paper proposes a pipeline safety monitoring system based on fiber Bragg grating sensors, which can effectively and directly monitor a series of important structural parameters during equipment operation. The system is installed into the actual application scenario for testing, the expansion of the pipeline, strain and the relevant support structure of the inclination, deformation and other data can be remote real-time monitoring, and thus determine the safety and stability of the equipment and the overall structure. The test results show that the corresponding data can be monitored in real time, and has a high degree of consistency with the actual situation, which provides a powerful help to the subsequent maintenance and analysis.

articleTitle: Dense False Target Jamming Suppression based on Time-domain Collaborative Waveform Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Dense false target jamming with a fixed delay for each pulse (DFTJ-FDEP) poses a significant threat to radar systems by overwhelming them with false targets that mimic the characteristics of real targets in the pulse compression domain, thereby impairing their detection and tracking capabilities. To address this challenge, a time-domain collaborative waveform design method is proposed in this paper. By designing a cover signal with the same transmission direction as the detection signal, and optimizing its emission timing and pulse width, the method increases the characteristic differences between false and real targets in the pulse compression domain. Additionally, by incorporating the Kittler joint information entropy-based dense false target jamming suppression algorithm, this method effectively suppresses DFTJ-FDEP. The effectiveness of this approach is validated through simulations.

articleTitle: Influence of Radar System Parameters on The Super-resolution Performance for Airborne Forward-looking Scanning Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Forward-looking scanning radar uses a servo antenna to scan the forward area and detect targets. However, due to the limitation of antenna aperture, it is difficult to obtain high-resolution images. Direct inverse convolution, a method to enhance image resolution, is ineffective due to the measurement matrix’s pathology. Various super-resolution methods of convolutional inversion have been proposed to solve the pathology problem and acquire high-resolution images. However, the analysis of radar system parameters affecting the super-resolution performance boundary of the algorithm is not presented. This paper analyzes the impact of radar system parameters on the super-resolution performance of forward-looking scanning radar and demonstrates the factors that affect the super-resolution performance. It provides a theoretical understanding of the performance boundaries for the super-resolution method. Additionally, simulation experiments demonstrate the super-resolution performance gain caused by changes in the radar system parameters.

articleTitle: An Evaluation Method Based on Image Texture and KL Divergence for SAR Image Quantization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Raw images obtained from Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging processing typically exhibit a broad dynamic range (14-16 bits). Subsequent processing requires these images to be compressed and quantized into 8-bit grayscale images, which can result in the loss of detailed information. Consequently, when selecting quantization algorithms, it is essential to employ quantitative evaluation criteria to assess their performance. However, traditional evaluation methods designed for optical images are not suitable for SAR images due to their inherent characteristics, such as poor texture information and a concentrated grayscale distribution.In this paper, we propose a method that leverages the local texture information of an "ideal image" to construct the "distance" between the quantized image and the "ideal image," based on the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence. We also present experimental results demonstrating the numerical values obtained through this quantitative measurement algorithm.

articleTitle: An Autofocus Method Based on Generative Adversarial Networks for Harmonic SAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Harmonic synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is a new type of radar that has the ability to resist interference from fundamental frequency clutter. Due to the environment and dynamics, the harmonic SAR platform is unable to maintain uniform linear motion, which causes motion errors in the echo signals. Motion errors greatly affect the quality of harmonic SAR images and cause the image to appear defocused. In order to address this issue, a two-dimensional error phase model of harmonic SAR based on non-uniform motion is first constructed. Second, an autofocus generative adversarial network (GAN) for the harmonic SAR is constructed by using the deep learning method. Subsequently, the network is trained and tested using harmonic SAR imaging results. Finally, the focus results of the proposed method and other autofocus methods are given, and the focusing results are evaluated by using image entropy. The focusing results demonstrates the feasibility of using deep learning to solve the problem of SAR autofocus.

articleTitle: Fourier-Based Equivariant Graph Neural Networks for Camera Pose Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Traditional graph neural networks often face challenges in accurately modeling nonlinear transformations, such as rotation and translation, commonly encountered in real-world applications like robot navigation and augmented reality. Our approach enhances pose estimation accuracy by implementing equivariant encoding of nodes and edges within the graph structure, ensuring robust feature representation under various geometric transformations. Additionally, we use an equivariant spatial attention mechanism to facilitate the interaction of node information within the graph, improving accuracy in complex scenarios. Experimental results show our method surpasses the existing state-of-the-art.

articleTitle: An Edge Filtering-Based Spatial-Spectral Joint Hyperspectral Target-Level Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Hyperspectral images have demonstrated exceptional performance in anomaly detection due to the strong distinctiveness of the spectral information they contain across different types of surfaces, drawing significant attention in applications such as civilian rescue operations and military search missions. However, commonly used hyperspectral anomaly detection techniques currently suffer from two major drawbacks: 1) existing anomaly detection algorithms overly focus on the spectral features of hyperspectral data while neglecting the spatial features contained within the image; 2) current detection algorithms typically operate at the pixel level, lacking relevant research aimed at achieving precise target set annotation. To address these two issues, this paper proposes an edge and keypoint detection-based hyperspectral image target set anomaly detection algorithm. First, a hyperspectral image edge enhancement operator based on the Scharr operator is designed to highlight target edge information by calculating the spectral similarity between pixels. Next, a spectral boundary-keypoint generation algorithm is proposed, which determines the coordinates of the target edge extrema by detecting edges in four directions. Finally, a target box generation algorithm is developed, combining boundary keypoints with anomaly detection results, and the results are optimized using Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) by traversing combinations of extreme points. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves the Intersection over Union (IoU) between the generated target boxes and the ground truth boxes while reducing the center offset, compared to state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Target Tracking with Radar Sensors in Highway Divergence and Convergence Sections
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: As the junction between highways and other urban roads, the divergence and convergence sections cause vehicles to perform frequent and complex acceleration, deceleration and lane changes. This poses a challenge for traffic radar to accurately estimate the position of vehicles. The classical algorithm based depends too much on the prior model and cannot accurately track complex vehicle movements. This paper proposes an improved method to achieve accurate tracking of vehicle targets in the divergence and convergence sections. Firstly, based on the unscented Kalman filter framework, we derive the filtering algorithm framework after introducing model errors. Secondly, we design a gated recurrent neural network to learn the implicit target motion state information in the dataset through the memory of the recurrent neural network, and converted it into model error through the gating structure. Then the model error is compensated in the state estimation. In the simulation, the position and velocity errors of the proposed algorithm are reduced by 16.83% and 17.45% compared with the baseline filter.

articleTitle: A High-Precision Interference Sources Location Method Based on Satellite-Based Multi-Feeder Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Signal interference seriously restricts the service capability of communication satellites. The accurate location of interference sources is the key step to solve the interference of communication systems. At present, the satellite mainly uses the multi-beam amplitude comparison to locate the target, the positioning accuracy is low, and the multi-target measurement depends on the pre-signal sorting. With the development of payload technology, multi-beam of satellite can be generated by multi-feeder antenna, and the coherence between feed signals can bring higher precision on DOA measurement. In this paper, a method of interference source location based on multi-feed antenna is proposed. Firstly, multi-beam data acquisition is realized by using beamforming network, and then the signal of each feed channel is estimated through integrated channel signal. Finally, the multi-target DOA estimation and location is realized by using MUSIC technology. The simulation results show that the proposed method can realize multi-target DOA estimation with higher accuracy than the conventional amplitude method.

articleTitle: Enhanced Performance of Channel Coded CE-OFDM-IM with Phase Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Constant envelope orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (CE-OFDM) greatly reduces the peak-to-average ratio (PAPR) by embedding information into the phases of carriers. However, during the process of wide application, CE-OFDM is faced with a significant obstacle in balancing the bit error rate (BER) performance and bandwidth. To address this challenge, we adopt the approach of combining index modulation (IM) with CE-OFDM to utilize the potential frequency diversity gains, while using low density parity check (LDPC) coding and employing soft desicion to further enhance the BER performance. Simulation results show that the CE-OFDM-IM system with channel coding and soft decision reduces the BER while improving spectral efficiency.

Author Keywords: Constant envelope orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (CE-OFDM)

articleTitle: Rapid Simulation Method of Radar Echo for PolSAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multi-polarization characteristics are crucial for PolSAR applications. This article proposes a rapid scattering model for the electromagnetic simulation of composite scenes under both co-polarization and cross-polarization. The model utilizes a scattering center model to represent target scattering, while background scattering is computed using the integral equation method. Under cross-polarization, the locations of scattering centers of the target are extracted based on numerical current, and the amplitudes are determined by Padé approximation. By validating against numerical methods, this model accurately simulates SAR images under multi-polarization conditions.

articleTitle: Predicting Avian Frequency Based on Weather Radar and Citizen Science
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Predicting aerial animal migration holds significant importance for the study and conservation of wildlife, particularly in guiding protective measures for various bird orders. Existing large-scale prediction models utilize weather radar data. However, weather radar cannot accurately distinguish the detected animals, and thus cannot target specific bird orders. This paper first analyses the correlation between weather radar data and citizen science (eBird) data, then proposes a deep learning model to predict eBird avian frequency based on weather radar data. The results indicate that in the Bohai Bay area across three provinces, the correlation between avian migration traffic estimated by weather radar and eBird frequency reached as high as 0.837, demonstrating the feasibility of using radar data to predict eBird frequency. In the prediction experiments, the proposed model achieved a correlation of 0.782 between the predicted results and the actual values, validating the effectiveness of our model. Future applications will focus on enhancing the performance of the prediction method and incorporating additional data sources, such as flight call record, to supplement the limitations of manual bird report.

articleTitle: Reconstruct Radar Echo Radial Velocity Data based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Improving the resolution of weather radar echoes enables forecasters to observe the occurrence, development and dissipation of severe weather in more detail, so as to improve the accurate early warning ability of severe weather, which is of great significance for reducing the impact of severe weather on people’s lives and work, as well as reducing its losses to the economy. Therefore, this paper proposes a new method, which is based on the Regularized Deep Residual Attention Network (R-DRAN), which reconstructs the radial velocity data of weather radar echoes with super-resolution without changing the hardware equipment, so as to assist in more accurate detection of weather processes. The results show that R-DRAN can not only capture more detailed information, but also effectively retain edge information, which significantly improves the reconstruction quality.

articleTitle: Learning DCT Subband using Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Deep learning-based infrared small target detection (IRSTD) methods typically exploit spatial domain cues to infer dim and weak infrared targets. However, relying solely on spatial domain information is sub-optimal due to the lack of structure and texture details of the target. Alternatively, we learn frequency priors to enhance targets in frequency domain, and propose a Frequency Domain Enhanced Network (FDENet). It contains a frequency domain discrete cosine transform enhancement (FDE) module with KAN-inspired DCT learning mechanism. Specifically, the FDE module uses multiple univariate nonlinear functions to combine continuous multivariate functions to directly map frequency-aware cues without spatial features. It then aligns the frequency-aware cues and with the spatial features to capture dimly weak targets. Generalization experiments and comparative studies on two real-world infrared single-frame image datasets fully demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Near-Field BP Imaging Algorithm Based on Antenna Pattern Gain Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Ultra-wideband MIMO radar can provide precise range and azimuth information of multiple targets and is widely applied in military, aviation, transportation, and other fields. However, the antenna radiates electromagnetic energy in a specific direction, and the coverage area in azimuth is limited. Compared with targets in the antenna’s main lobe, the large-angle targets outside the antenna’s main lobe scatter weaker radar echoes. Therefore, weak targets will be overshadowed by strong targets. This paper proposes a near-field BP algorithm based on antenna radiation patterns compensation. The antenna radiation pattern was measured in the anechoic chamber. Then, digital beamforming technology was utilized to construct a gain compensation matrix achieving radar data compensation from different directions. Experimental results showed that the proposed algorithm effectively enhanced the energy of large-angle targets in multi-target scenes.

articleTitle: Aerial Insect and Bird Identification Method based on Spectrum Estimation of Weather Radar IQ data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The global decline in aerial migratory animals, such as birds and insects, due to climate and environmental changes significantly impacts the aerial ecological environment and human survival. Although weather radar data products can provide valuable information about the large-scale movement of airborne organisms, they cannot reflect the activity of multiple biological scatterers within a resolved volume. The aim of this study is to extract more detailed biological information from the Level I IQ data of weather radar. We introduce the estimation method of IQ data spectral moment, and propose the recognition method of biological scatterers by RD spectrum and resolution unit Doppler spectrum. Reflection factor products generated from IQ data retain more discrete biological information than base data products. Birdwatching experiments in Changsha further demonstrate the ability of the Doppler spectrum to reveal the activity of a variety of biological scatterers within a resolution volume.

articleTitle: Spatial-Temporal Phase Unwrapping Method for GB-InSAR Based on Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Ground-based interferometric synthetic aperture radar (GB-InSAR) can effectively achieve high-accuracy measurement of surface deformation, which is widely used in the field of landslide monitoring and warning. The accuracy of phase unwrapping (PU) is one of the key factors affecting the accuracy of deformation measurement. This paper proposes a spatial-temporal PU method based on the Kalman filter to address the errors of PU caused by large interferometric phase gradients between deformation pixels and stable pixels. Firstly, for stable pixels, the minimum cost flow method is used for PU. Then, for the deformation pixels, the temporal domain Kalman filter is employed to estimate the unwrapped phase and obtain the estimation of ambiguity number in the spatial domain. Finally, optimizing the objective function of PU by minimizing the estimation error of ambiguity number improves the unwrapping accuracy for the deformation pixels. The results of simulation and measured data have shown that this method can effectively correct the phase unwrapping error caused by large interferometric phase gradients and improve the reliability of deformation inversion.

articleTitle: Continuous semantic change monitoring of land cover with Landsat time series
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Rapid urbanization has led to frequent land cover changes, making continuous monitoring essential for capturing land use dynamics and enabling quick responses. It is crucial to detect both the dates and types of these changes, which current change detection models struggle to achieve simultaneously. In this study, we propose a supervised approach called Temporal Semantic Recognition Change Detection (TSRCD), using a Transformer-based sliding detector to learn mappings from spectral data to land cover changes over time. During monitoring, the model utilizes previously detected land cover types and additional observations as dual prompts to iteratively predict the next time point’s land cover type. We validated our approach using all clear Landsat data from the Wuhan urban agglomeration between 2008 and 2022. Experiments show that increasing the peek window size improves change detection accuracy, stabilizing at around ten, with an approximate 8% improvement in F1 score compared to CCDC. TSRCD not only tracks the dates of land cover changes but also accurately identifies change types, achieving 92% accuracy. In summary, TSRCD provides a novel and comprehensive solution for monitoring land cover changes using long-term series remote sensing data.

articleTitle: A lightweight object detection network based on YOLOv5 for SAR image
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Remote sensing image target detection is one of the key technologies in the field of intelligent interpretation of remote sensing images, and it has significant application value in various areas, including military defense. When performing remote sensing image object detection on airborne and spaceborne platforms, the vast amount of remote sensing data processing and limited computational resources impose high real-time requirements on the object detection algorithms. This paper designs a lightweight object detection network model named YOLOv5-tiny, based on the existing deep learning network detection model YOLOv5s, and deploys it on the Jetson TX2 development board for training and testing. Experimental results show that the proposed YOLOv5-tiny model, when tested on the SAR-AIRcraft-1.0 with an input image size of 640x640, is 10 times smaller than YOLOv5s; it has a computational cost of 5.2 GFLOPs, which is 1/5 of YOLOv5s, and the processing time for a single image is reduced to half that of YOLOv5s, with only a 0.1% decrease in accuracy.

articleTitle: A Novel Method For Non-planar Target Imaging With DSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In case of circular or non-linear acquisition trajectory, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) focusing becomes increasingly sensitive to elevation. For non-planar target imaging, it not only appears fore-shortening along range but also blurred along azimuth. As the wider integration angle and higher elevation of objects, the defocus cannot be ignored. Generally, the polar format algorithm (PFA) is an efficient imaging algorithm for circular or non-linear SAR. However, in the process of PFA, the impact of focusing at an inexact altitude is not be considered. In this article, the conventional PFA is adapted to incorporate the known digital surface model (DSM) into the imaging process. Firstly, the maximum allowable elevation deviation (MAED) δz<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> is derived. Secondly, for non-planar target that higher than δz<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> , applying data extraction in range-Doppler domain and multiplying compensation function that constructed based on DSM data separately. The corresponding original echo data is then replaced with the processed data. The whole method only involves fast Fourier transform (FFT) and complex multiplication which makes it better operational efficiency. The experimental data results demonstrated the effectiveness and practicability of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Earth-Based Radar Height Dimension Imaging for Astronomical Object
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Observation for astronomical object, including the moon, asteroids, and terrestrial planets, is of significance in deep space observation. Earth-based radar is an important approach for astronomical object observation. Earth-based radar has the ability of two-dimensional (2-D) imaging for astronomical objects. However, earth-based radar height dimension imaging for astronomocal object has not been reported yet. In this manuscript, the analysis of earth-based radar height dimension imaging for astronomical object is discussed. The relative motion between earth-based radar and astronomical object is analyzed, and the sparse height sampling of radar is discussed. Thereafter the problem of sidelobe and grating lobe in height dimension imaging is discussed, and a data domain-image domain joint windowing method is proposed for sidelobe and grating lobe suppression. Computer simulation experiment and real data equivalent experiment with electromagnetic anechoic chamber are conducted to validate the analysis and the proposed method.

articleTitle: IAT-YOLO: A black pig detection model for use in low-light environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the large-scale intelligent pig farming industry, it is crucial to achieve real-time and accurate identification and positioning of each pig. However, the existing mainstream pig detection algorithms are mainly designed for white pigs, and the detection effect of black pigs is poor in low-light environments. In addition, when black pigs gather and adhesion and occlusion occur, the complexity of detection is further increased. Although strong light irradiation in the pigpen can improve the detection accuracy, it will have an adverse effect on the normal growth of pigs. To ensure accurate detection of black pigs in low-light environments without interfering with the normal growth of pigs, this research presents the IAT-YOLO model, derived from YOLOv7. It combines the brightness adaptive module IAT (Illumination-Adaptive-Transformer), the CA (Coordinate Attention mechanism) and the improved SPPCSPC-R module, which can effectively identify and locate the position and number of black pigs. Tests on the low-light black pig dataset reveal that the proposed model attains 96.8% accuracy, 83.8% recall, 91.8% mAP@0.5, and 54.5% mAP@0.5:0.95, which demonstrates higher accuracy and provides technical support for the intelligent detection of black pigs in such environments.

articleTitle: Adaptive Cyclic Wiener Filter for Repeater Jamming Suppression in Radar System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In complex interference environments, interference identification and suppression technology are key to ensuring the normal operation of radar and are an important direction for the development of future radar, with broad research prospects. This paper detailedly explores the effects of interrupted-sampling repeater jamming(ISRJ) on radar system operations. By capturing and retransmitting radar signals at specific times, this interference approach mimics real target signals, complicating the radar’s ability to distinguish between actual targets and interference. Initially, the paper developed models for radar echoes and interference signals and analyzed their cyclostationary characteristics. Based on these characteristics, a cyclic Wiener filter was designed to effectively counter the interference. Furthermore, this paper derived formulas for updating the coefficients of the adaptive cyclic Wiener filter, improving the efficiency of coefficient calculations. Simulation analyses of interrupted-sampling repeater jamming with different parameters confirmed the effectiveness of the cyclic Wiener filter in mitigating this type of interference.

articleTitle: Coherent Integration with Multi-pass Synthetic Aperture Radar Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can be used to acquire high-resolution images of huge areas and has been widely used in planetary exploration. However, in earth-based SAR imaging of the moon, the effect of additive noise is not ignorable and the restricted temporal window for single observation limits the potential for image denoising through integration methods. To address this issue, a method to achieve coherent integration with multi-pass SAR images for additive noise removal is proposed. The proposed method achieves envelope alignment through sub-pixel level image registration and phase alignment by compensating the flat earth phase and topographic phase, thus satisfying the requirement of coherent integration. The signal-to-noise (SNR) gain resulting from this method is given by a function of the correlation. The effectiveness of the method and the correctness of the function are verified by the simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Jitter analysis based on kernel density estimation and dual-dirac
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Accurate jitter analysis is critical for next-generation I/O designs. In this paper, a method to separate deterministic jitter (DJ) and random jitter (RJ) is proposed, which first obtains the Time Interval Error (TIE) histogram of the signal, then uses the Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) algorithm to smooth the histogram, and then defines a fitting parameter to perform a Dual-Dirac fit on the smoothed histogram to estimate DJ and RJ. Finally, the estimation results of the method are given, and the estimation errors of deterministic jitter and random jitter are 1.2% and 4.7%, respectively, which verifies the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Multiple Extended Target Tracking Algorithm with Adaptive Target Birth Intensity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A Multiple Extended Target Tracking (METT) algorithm using the Star-convex Random Hypersurface Model (SRHM) in cooperation with Adaptive Target Birth Intensity (ATBI) is proposed in this paper to solve the problem that it is difficult to obtain the prior of the extended target newborn intensity in complex environments. Firstly, the Cardinalized Probability Hypothesis Density (CPHD) filter is used to establish a Bayesian filter framework for multiple extended targets. Then the SRHM is used to model the measurement distribution of the extended target, and the CPHD filter flow is embedded by the Unscented Transform (UT). In addition, based on the ATBI algorithm, the intensity of the new target is reversely derived from the measurement data, and the filter no longer depends on the prior information of the new target. The numerical experiment results verified that the SRHM-CPHD filter based on ATBI algorithm has better performance than the traditional Gaussian Mixture (GM) model for METT in the unknown newborn target intensity scene, and is more sensitive to the phenomenon of target newborn.

articleTitle: A Water Body Extraction Network Based on Fusing SAR Images and DEM Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) plays a crucial role in flood monitoring and early warning systems through water body extraction techniques. However, unlike optical remote sensing images, SAR images are affected by unique imaging characteristics, including shadows, noise, and complex environments, which complicate interpretation. Most existing deep learning methods rely solely on single SAR images for model training, without incorporating additional information, leading to lower accuracy in water body interpretation, especially in challenging scenarios such as mountainous areas and densely vegetated regions. To address these challenges, we propose a water body extraction algorithm that fuses SAR images with Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data to improve the accuracy and robustness in complex environments. Four different fusion strategies are explored at both the image level and feature level, incorporating DEM and slope data into an existing encoder-decoder architecture. These enhancements effectively address the aforementioned issues. Experimental results demonstrate that the fusion approach significantly improves water body extraction precision and reduces false alarm rates compared to non-fusion methods. Through a comparative analysis of the different fusion strategies, the best approach was identified as image-level fusion using DEM data, achieving a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 0.95 on the GF-Floodnet dataset.

articleTitle: Joint Path Planning and Time Resource Optimization for Simultaneous Search and Localization Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To address the issues of low effective coverage rate during search operations, low precision in localization tasks, and single-task execution caused by predetermined flight paths in traditional UAV formations, this paper proposes an optimization method for path planning and time allocation that simultaneously achieves radar search functionality and multi-target joint localization tasks. Firstly, an effective surveillance rate is established based on the search requirements of the radar system, and the CRLB is used as the measurement accuracy indicator based on the target localization requirements. These two factors are then weighted to form the objective function to be optimized. Secondly, an optimization model is established based on kinematic constraints and time allocation constraints. Subsequently, the particle swarm algorithm is utilized to iteratively optimize the UAV’s path and time allocation frame by frame. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared to default path and time allocation, the proposed optimization scheme for path planning and time allocation offers superior overall performance in both search and measurement tasks.

articleTitle: High-Speed Weak Target Detection Method for Vortex Electromagnetic Wave Radar based on Bimodal Cyclic Baseline
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Vortex electromagnetic (EM) waves can provide more target information, which is orbital angular momentum (OAM), than traditional plane waves in the field of radar detection. By emitting multiple different modes of vortex EM waves to illuminate the same target, the azimuth information of the target can be obtained. The Linear Frequency Modulated (LFM) radar is often used in current OAM radar design. However, for the detection requirements of high-speed weak targets, long-term accumulation is necessary to capture the target. Due to the high-speed motion of the target, the movement of the target between different modes’ echo signal cannot be eliminated after accumulation, making it difficult to compensate and extract correct target azimuth information. Therefore, this paper proposes a vortex EM wave high-speed target detection technology based on bimodal cyclic baseline. By alternately emitting vortex EM waves with OAM mode difference of 1, the mode phase information is not blurred while achieving long-term accumulation, thereby achieving distance, velocity, and azimuth detection of high-speed weak targets. Simulation results compared with traditional phase comparison azimuth measurement method proved the superiority of our method. The work and results provide suggestions to the development of vortex EM wave high-speed weak target detection.

articleTitle: On-Chip High-Speed Programmable Silicon Photonic Fano Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: We propose and design a high-speed programmable silicon photonic Fano resonator chip, which shows a flexible tunability in terms of resonant wavelength, slope rate, extinction ratio and an ultrashort response time of 108 ns.

articleTitle: Calibration-Based 2-D DOA Estimation Exploiting 2qth-Order Cumulants for Polarimetric Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In practical engineering, there exist various types of array errors, causing significant degradation in direction finding performance. As a result, array calibration plays a crucial role in practical array signal processing. In this paper, a calibration-based two-dimensional (2-D) direction of arrival (DOA) estimation method based on 2qth-order cumulants is proposed, which can be applied to arbitrary polarimetric arrays with unknown array errors. All the errors are modeled into a non-parametric angle-dependent error matrix. The array output across 2-D potential angle grids are obtained by placing two calibration sources with arbitrary but different polarimetric parameters. Subsequently, an array calibration matrix is generated from the calibration process. The equivalence of the matrix pencils calculated by the calibration matrix and the non-ideal error-corrupted matrix is proven, forming a low-complexity calibrated polarization diversity 2q-MUSIC (CPD-2q-MUSIC) method without reconstructing the error matrix incorporating all array errors. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: XL-IRS Aided Near-Field Communications: A Two-Stage Hierarchical Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the forthcoming sixth generation (6G) communication, it is more likely that intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) will evolve into extremely large-scale IRS (XL-IRS) to enhance the quality of wireless communications. However, the far-field methods of IRS cannot be directly extended to XL-IRS in near-field communications. In this paper, we analyze the XL-IRS aided communication scenario, and propose a two-stage hierarchical beam training scheme for XL-IRS based on the quartering method and non-uniform distance sampling. Specifically, we design a two-dimensional hierarchical training scheme to determine the user’s direction in the direction domain. Then, we utilize the non-uniform distance sampling method to determine the user’s distance in the distance domain. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed two-stage beam training scheme can achieve the rate performance comparable to near-field 3D exhaustive search in the XL-IRS system, with lower training overhead.

articleTitle: Passive localization method for FH-OFDM signals based on passive synthetic aperture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Frequency hopping orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (FH-OFDM) signals are extensively utilized in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication system which hold significant value in the area of passive location. However, traditional passive localization methods could not achieve high localization accuracy for FH-OFDM signals when the signal noise ratio (SNR) is low. Therefore, this paper proposes a high-accuracy passive localization method based on passive synthetic aperture (PSA) for FH-OFDM signals. The method begins by using repeated sequences to eliminate residual frequency offsets (RFO) through the least squares (LS) solution, followed by using pilots to remove the baseband modulation information. Subsequently, the doppler phase information of FH-OFDM signals is utilized to construct a cost function pertaining to the target position. After eliminating the Doppler phase in the azimuth domain through grid search, we can get peaks in the range domain through transformation. Finally, the target position is ascertained through peaks accumulation across all FH-OFDM signals. Simulation results verify that the proposed method can achieve meter-level high-accuracy location for FH-OFDM signals when SNR is low.

articleTitle: Formation Configuration Design for Target Tracking in Multi-Unmanned Aircraft System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, a formation configuration design strategy for target tracking is proposed in a multi-unmanned aircraft system. The proposed strategy aims to enhance the system detection and tracking capabilities by optimizing the initial formation configuration and route planning of the unmanned aircraft, taking into account the constraints on the inter-aircraft distance, deployment zone and maneuverability limitations. The metric of the system detection capability is derived based on the detection area. The predictive Bayesian Cramér–Rao lower bound (BCRLB) is introduced to evaluate the target tracking accuracy. By combining the detection area and BCRLB, we develop a weight function to evaluate the system performance. On this basis, a two-phase optimization model is established for formation configuration and route planning. Then, interior point method is adopted to address this model. Numerical findings indicate that the suggested configuration design strategy performs better in detection and tracking by contrast with other conventional configurations.

articleTitle: Fine Tuning of Large Models for Hyperspectral and LiDAR Data Joint Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Pre-trained visual language models (VLMs) excel in various visual tasks due to the extensive knowledge they gain from large datasets of image-text pairs. The ability of VLMs to scale effectively is a major benefit, enabling their application across a diverse array of downstream tasks. This study focuses on leveraging VLMs to jointly classify hyperspectral image (HSI) and LiDAR data, facilitating the extraction of more generalized features from various remote sensing image sources. Firstly, this study employs a feature extractor to convert the low-dimensional patches of HSI and LiDAR data into high-dimensional latent feature representations, aligning with the VLMs' requirements for the dimensionality of visual input data. VLMs use continuous vectors for classification, generated by text template prompts with class names. However, prompt engineering often demands considerable specialized knowledge and time. To address this challenge, this paper introduces Prompt Tuning (PT) and Residual Tuning (RT) methods. PT enhances model performance by incorporating random prompts into the visual encoder, while RT introduces randomly initialized learnable text residuals (TRs) into text features, further improving the generality of VLMs. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method attains competitive classification accuracy on the Houston 2013 dataset, even with a limited quantity of labeled pixels.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Interference of System Errors in Compact Polarimetric SAR Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Compact Polarimetric (CP) SAR retains the observation bandwidth of Single Polarimetric SAR while capturing partial polarization information of the target, making it particularly suitable for large-scale remote sensing tasks. However, system errors have a huge impact on the signal transmission, propagation, and receiving of the CP SAR systems. Therefore, it is particularly important to evaluate the interference of system errors in CP SAR modes. In this study, experiments are conducted on both simulated and real measured polarimetric SAR signals, to understand the impact of various system errors on the scattering matrix and the extracted polarimetric features in CP SAR modes. The conclusions summarized in this study may benefit the design of future advanced polarimetric SAR systems.

articleTitle: High-precision pressure sensor based on Fiber Ring Resonator empowered by machine learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this study, the use of Fiber Ring Resonators (FRR) as highly sensitive pressure sensors is investigated. Enhanced system stability and sensitivity are achieved by employing the Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) frequency-locking technique. The shift in the resonance of the FRR due to external pressure variations is used to measure the applied pressure with high precision. Conventional pressure sensing methods rely on monitoring the PDH error signal generated by the lock-in amplifier. However, the output of the PDH system is not a directly readable value but rather a composite signal influenced by the PI controller and the characteristics of the system hardware. In this work, a machine learning-based data processing method is introduced and demonstrated in the FRR system to achieve high-precision pressure measurement. This paper presents the theoretical background, experimental setup, and results demonstrating the feasibility and advantages of this approach.

articleTitle: Closed-Loop Tracking OCOG-AGC Algorithm for Altitude Measurement Under Complex Terrain Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: By combining the offset center of gravity (OCOG) estimation with the front-end automatic gain control (AGC), a closed-loop tracking OCOG-AGC algorithm is proposed to address the problem of stable tracking of height finding radar in complex terrain environments. Fisrtly, the OCOG method is used to acquire the centroid of height finding waveform envelope inside the tracking gate to estimate the center position of echo front than traditional height measurement algorithms more accuratly. Moreover, the relationship between the height variation of the matched rectangle and the strength variation of the echo power is revealed for the system closed-loop tracking. As a result, the adaptability of the proposed OCOG-AGC algorithm is verified by processing the CryoSat-2 FBR satellite data in complex terrain conditions.

articleTitle: Data application test of LuTan-1 satellite based on the LandSAR software
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: LuTan-1 (LT-1) satellite constellation is used to conduct surface deformation monitoring. Following the launch of LT-1, we began to use the independently developed LandSAR software for differential interferometric data processing and application. Built upon the Model-View-Controller (MVC) architectural pattern, LandSAR is coded in C++ for cross-platform and multi-architecture compatibility. Based on the MVC of LandSAR, we carried out white-box testing of model and controller, as well as black-box testing of the view. By testing, we have formed different processing flow, including InSAR、DInSAR and stacking. In order to test the application of LT-1 and LandSAR in different scenarios, we used 6 scenes of 3-meter-resolution single look complex (SLC) images to conduct InSAR and stacking processing around a reservoir. Comparing to the 30-meter-resolution Copernicus DEM, the 10-meter-resolution LT-1 DSM results exhibit more detailed information. Stacking results indicate 7 typical subsidence areas, flagging potential hazards that could threaten the stability of the reservoir. The results proved application potential of the data and the processing capabilities of the software.

articleTitle: JiShiShan Mw 6.2 Earthquake Monitoring by Means of Lutan-1 SAR Data and Optical Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: On December 18, 2023, a 6.2-magnitude earthquake hit Jishishan County, Linxia Prefecture, Gansu Province, followed by several aftershocks. The earthquake caused a large number of house collapses and casualties. Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar technique can obtain multiple dimensional information for geo-hazard management. Lutan-1 SAR satellites with accurate orbit control ability are the first group L-band SAR constellation in China, which provide the potential for deformation monitoring with centimeter even millimeter accuracy. Based on the pre-earthquake and post-earthquake Lutan-1 SAR data and Gaofen-7 optical data, the information of coseismic deformation, debris flow and slope collapse were extracted and analyzed. It provides important data support for post-earthquake rescue and post-disaster reconstruction. The coceismic deformation field characterized the typical deformation induced by the earthquake, and the maximum deformation can reach to 8 cm. The debris flow area showed obvious change on the SAR data and optical data, including spectral information and backscattering information. In combination with the application of Lutan-1 and Gaofen-7 data, the earthquake and secondary disaster can be effectively monitored.

articleTitle: An Efficient and Accurate Asteroid Inversion Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper mainly describes the Adam method under the problem of retrieving asteroid rotation and 3D model from radar 2D images. We improve on the traditional method by introducing computational graph and back propagation algorithm in deep learning to improve the operation speed and calculation accuracy of the gradient, and adopt Adam optimizer to accelerate the convergence speed and avoid local minimum. We compare this method with the existing Gauss-Newton method, Levenberg-Marquardt method, and conclude that the Adam method is better than the Gauss-Newton method and Levenberg-Marquardt method in convergence speed, two-dimensional image fitting accuracy, three-dimensional model fitting accuracy.

articleTitle: Cross-Dataset Pre-Training for Weakly Supervised Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the rising of industries such as autonomous driving and robotics, as well as the maturity of various 3D sensing technologies, the application of processing point cloud data to perceive scenes has become increasingly common. This trend has made 3D point cloud semantic segmentation a hot topic in current research. However, despite the rich semantic information provided by point cloud data, fully annotating such large-scale and unstructured datasets remains highly challenging. To address this issue, weakly supervised learning methods have gained increasing attention, aiming to train networks with fewer labeled data. To further improve the performance of weakly supervised semantic segmentation of point clouds, a method that uses cross-dataset pre-trained models to assist weakly supervised learning is proposed. The Point Transformer architecture is employed for efficient multi-scale feature extraction, while the design of the dual-branch network facilitates the transfer of knowledge from different datasets, improving the performance of the weakly supervised learning process.
