Compared to the SQN weakly supervised learning method, this approach, with only 0.1% of the data labeled, increases the mIoU on the S3DIS dataset from 77.7% to 78.2% and on the Toronto3D dataset from 61.4% to 62.5%, significantly improving the performance of weakly supervised point cloud semantic segmentation.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Quantitatively Measure the Capability of Detection System Based on Information Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: There are a large amount of detection resources in future battlefield. Distributed and networked detection system has become the basic form of future warfare. However, there is no uniform measure and analysis tool for the systematic detection capability. Aiming at the problem, new capability measure method for the detection system is proposed in the paper based on the information theory. With the presented method, the capability of single detection equipment in the detection system is measured based on information entropy. Also, the capability of multiple detection equipments is measured based on joint entropy. In addition, the capability of single equipment’s contribution to detection system is given based on information gain (IG). Meanwhile, these capability measure methods are applied to multi-static radars tracking phase. The results show that the capability measure method is effective and feasible.

articleTitle: Generalized Representation Learning of Azimuth based on Mutual Information for SAR Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Automatic target recognition is of vital importance to SAR image interpretation. Nevertheless, learning-based methods still suffer from severe problems of electromagnetic scattering sensitivity and lack of data. In contrast to many methods synthesizing real-like SAR images or seeking stable features for classification, this paper focuses on the essential azimuth angle of the target, which greatly influences the SAR image due to the electromagnetic scattering mechanism. A method based on mutual information is proposed in order to achieve a balance between representative ability and generalization. The mutual information between the embedding and the azimuth is maximized, while that between the embedding and the input is minimized. Furthermore, a variational framework based on neural networks is introduced to approximate the intractable mutual information. Meanwhile, the azimuth angle is coded by a continuous vector representation to avoid discontinuity. In order to validate the generalization in open environments, a new data split from MSTAR called UTC is proposed, where unseen targets constitute the test set. Extensive experiments show that our method outperforms other discriminant models on MSTAR and exhibits superior generalization capability.

articleTitle: 3D-TF-Spectrum-Based Rotational Parameter Extraction of Extended Target with Vortex Electromagnetic Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Vortex electromagnetic wave radar echoes simultaneously unite the radial and angular information of the target, containing more micro-motion information than traditional radar. By jointly processing the two-dimensional information of radial Doppler and rotational Doppler, more abundant information than traditional plane wave detection can be obtained, providing effective support for accurate target identification. However, most existing rotational parameter extraction methods focus on separating and removing radial Doppler to study the rotational Doppler effect. To address this issue, this paper proposes a method based on time-frequency (TF) analysis and genetic algorithm (GA) optimization to extract micro-motion parameters of rotating extended-target with vortex electromagnetic wave radar.

articleTitle: A SAR Target Recognition Strategy Guided by Electromagnetic Scattering Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: SAR target Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) is indispensable in SAR image interpretation. Recently, deep learning technology has been widely used in SAR target recognition tasks. Most networks achieve incremental improvements in target recognition by modifying their structures to extract visual features of targets. However, due to the unique imaging mechanism, relying solely on visual features often leads to the loss of target information. In contrast, the ASC model, which captures the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of the target, plays a crucial role in target recognition tasks. Unfortunately, traditional parameter estimation methods for extracting the ASC model are computationally expensive and time-consuming, making them impractical for real-world applications. To address these issues, we propose a novel target recognition method based on electromagnetic scattering features in this paper. First, a lightweight network-based feature extraction module is designed. Then, the target ASC image is used as the ground truth for guidance, with image intensity and target structure serving as the loss functions during training. Finally, an ASC model-guided feature fusion network is designed, utilizing the fused features for target recognition. On the MSTAR dataset, a visual assessment experiment demonstrated that the proposed feature extraction module effectively extracts electromagnetic scattering features under various operating conditions. Subsequently, in downstream classification tasks, the inclusion of the proposed module resulted in improved accuracy compared to other networks. Additionally, a visualization analysis of the classification network showed that, under the guidance of electromagnetic scattering features, the network achieved good interpretability.

articleTitle: The Analysis of the tracking performance of Non-Central Random Matrix approach using different Noise Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper analyzes the algorithm of Non-Central Random Matrix filtering. Focusing on the noise model in the algorithm, we discuss the effect of the Noise Matrix on the filtering performance of the Non-Central Random Matrix by changing the noise level and verifiy it with the measured data of phased array radar.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Flight Planning and Jamming Resource Allocation in UAV Swarm against Radar Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper proposes a joint optimization algorithm of flight planning and jamming resource allocation in unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) swarm against radar network. Radar detection probability of the UAV swarm conducting deception jamming is adopted as the performance metric for flight planning and resource allocation strategy. On this basis, a joint optimization model of flight planning and jamming resource allocation in UAV swarm against radar network is established with the objective of minimizing radar detection probability as the optimization goal, and the constraint conditions of flight dynamic, the number of beams and the total power resource. Then, the above optimization model is decomposed into multiple sub problems, and solved sequentially using a combination of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and the interior point method (IPM). Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is effective and reliable.

articleTitle: Cross-Domain Few-Shot SAR Ship Object Detection with Meta-RCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In recent years, the advent of deep learning technology has significantly enhanced the efficacy of ship target detection and recognition in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery. However, in certain specific scenario, SAR ship images are extremely difficult to obtain. Moreover, the data distribution of these samples markedly differs from that of other SAR images, rendering the direct use of other large-scale SAR datasets for model training and generalization impractical. Most Few-shot object detection methods aim to locate and classify targets of novel classes in data-scarce scenerios, but their performance diminishes when confronted with data from unseen domains. To achieve few-shot object detection in images with novel distributions, rather than just novel classes, we meticulously constructed the CrossDomainShipDataset (CDSD), which comprises optical and SAR ship images from widely-used open-source datasets. A limited number of SAR ship images with specific distributions, obtained through our simulations, were used as benchmarks for evaluation. We utilized Meta-RCNN as the base model and integrated a pluggable Class-Domain Prototypes Extraction (CDPE) module to generate prototypes of class and domain at the same time. The model was trained on images from base domains to develop the capacity of learning to learn various distributions during the base training stage, then was fine-tuned with 1, 3, 5, and 10-shot configurations. Benchmark experiments demonstrate the efficacy of our approach for cross-domain few-shot SAR ship object detection.

articleTitle: Two-stage CFAR target detection method based on weighted fusion filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In complex scenes, such as leaf vegetation occlusion and strong reflection from thick branches, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the target echo signal received by the UAV radar is low, and its synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image shows obvious pseudo-target bright spots, which makes it difficult to detect interesting targets based on the image domain and has a high false alarm rate. To solve the above problems, the prerequisite is to filter the SAR image for preprocessing. However, different filters have inconsistent filtering effects on SAR images in different environments and are not universal. Based on the principle of adaptive weighted fusion filtering, a two-stage constant false alarm rate (TSCFAR) detection method is proposed in this work, which comprehensively utilizes the filtering effects of different filters to remove strong interference clutter from SAR images. By retaining more detailed features, a high probability of target detection is achieved. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is verified using measured data.

Author Keywords: Two-stage constant false alarm rate detection (TSCFAR)

articleTitle: Domain Adaptive SAR Ship Detection based on Knowledge Distillation and Transformer Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) ship detection has garnered considerable interest owing to its versatile application in both civilian and military field. Current SAR ship detectors based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) exhibit remarkable detection performance, contingent upon the availability of sufficient labeled SAR samples. However, it is time consuming and artificially expensive to label the training SAR images. Moreover, when the conditions of training data such as sensors, platforms, imaging parameters change, it is inevitable to alter the feature distribution between the source domain and the target domain, leading to the deterioration in detection performance. Consequently, the development of a detector capable of learning domain-invariant features without large-scale labeled samples in target domain remains a significant challenge. In this paper, we construct a semi-supervised domain-adaptive SAR ship detector based on YOLOv5, incorporating the Mean Teacher model with a knowledge distillation framework to capture domain-invariant features and mitigate domain discrepancies. Additionally, we integrate the transformer encoder module and convolutional block attention module into prediction head to enhance the capability of the detector to identify SAR ships of various scales across different domains. Extensive experiments conducted on several SAR ship datasets obtained under diverse conditions validate the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Highly Sensitive Low Reflective Index Waveguide Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This study proposes a high sensitivity waveguide surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor for low refractive index (RI) sensing. By using waveguide with the core RI of 1.38 and cladding RI of 1.374, its sensitivity reaches 11800 nm/RIU for detected RI from 1.33-1.35.

articleTitle: Cross-domain gesture recognition method based on diffusion model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In recent years, radar sensor-based gesture recognition has attracted considerable attention; however, it faces challenges such as limited training data and difficulties in generalizing to new environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes a two-stage domain adaptation approach that integrates diffusion model-based data augmentation with a sophisticated domain adaptation network for gesture recognition. To validate the effectiveness of our method, we conducted radar measurement experiments. The results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves recognition accuracy, underscoring its great capability for radar-based gesture recognition.

articleTitle: Correction of Atmospheric Bending Error for Distributed Astronomical Radar based on NWM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Neutral atmospheric bending error is one of the unfavorable factors that are unneglectable when distributed astronomical radar conducts precise observations in high frequency bands. It is caused by the spatial change of refractivity during electromagnetic propagation. This paper uses high-precision numerical weather model (NWM) data to generate refractivity profiles and estimates neutral atmospheric bending error with ray tracing method. Computer simulation verifies effectiveness of proposed method and analyses impact of error residual on the transmit-coherence performance for distributed astronomical radar.

articleTitle: Generalization Ability Analysis of Through-the-Wall Radar Human Activity Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Through-the-Wall radar (TWR) human activity recognition (HAR) is a technology that uses low-frequency ultra-wideband (UWB) signal to detect and analyze indoor human motion. However, the high dependence of existing end-to-end recognition models on the distribution of TWR training data makes it difficult to achieve good generalization across different indoor testers. In this regard, the generalization ability of TWR HAR is analyzed in this paper. In detail, an end-to-end linear neural network method for TWR HAR and its generalization error bound are first discussed. Second, a micro-Doppler corner representation method and the change of the generalization error before and after dimension reduction are presented. The appropriateness of the theoretical generalization errors is proved through numerical simulations and experiments. The results demonstrate that feature dimension reduction is effective in allowing recognition models to generalize across different indoor testers.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of GEO-LEO SAR ATI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Total surface current velocity vector (TSCV) plays an important role for understanding the dynamic and static sea surface process. Synthetic Aperture Radar Along Track Interferometry (SAR ATI) has its special advantages for high accuracy and large area measurement, thus it becomes a mainstream remote sensing measurement method. The successful launch of GEO SAR gives an opportunity for long time ocean current monitoring and wide area measuring, however, due to the long integration time of GEO SAR, it usually can’t satisfy the limitation of de-correlation time of sea surface. To deal with this problem, a heterogeneous distributed GEO-LEO SAR system has been proposed. To analyze the ATI performance of this system, a new ATI phase model has been derived, velocity resolution, the unambiguous velocity as well as the accuracy are all considered and analyzed by full link ATI simulation. As a result, it can be concluded that GEO-LEO SAR ATI system has the potential to achieve high precision current measurement with 100-meter resolution, and the performance is closely related to the configuration parameters, besides, the influencing factors of accuracy are also showed in the simulation results.

articleTitle: Frequency Control Scheme for Target Tracking under Dynamic Electromagnetic Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper proposes a frequency control (FC) scheme for radar systems that aims to improve target tracking accuracy under dynamic jamming environments. Specifically, the radar must alter the transmit frequency to reduce the impact of jamming. To combat the dynamic jammer, we construct FC as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) within a reinforcement learning framework. By applying a policy iteration technique to the MDP, an optimal strategy can be learned guiding the radar how to choose the transmit frequency at every frame. Since the entire target tracking process is real-time, a trade-off method is to balance the relationship between the model update and FC scheme utilization until online tracking process is over. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method can evidently beat the dynamic jamming and improve the target tracking accuracy.

articleTitle: Security of Integrated Sensing and Communication Systems with Hybrid Eavesdroppers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the joint beamforming design in secure integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, where the active eavesdropper intercepts the transmitted confidential information with an external passive eavesdropper. To improve the sensing performance while preventing the potential eavesdropping, the base station transmits a signal consisting of information symbols and sensing waveform, in which the sensing waveform is also used as artificial noise to interfere with eavesdroppers. Under this setup, we formulate the communication and sensing beamforming design problem, which aims to enhance the transmit beampattern performance, while ensuring the quality of service (QoS) of communication transmission and the secure communication constraint. Furthermore, we propose the semi-definite relaxation (SDR) algorithm to solve the non-convex problem. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme in both sensing and secure communication.

articleTitle: An Imaging Algorithm for High-Squint SAR with Accelerated Trajectory Based on Spectral Regularization and Spectral Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High-squint synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging with accelerated trajectory is significant for target detection and precise guidance. However, seriously space-variant Doppler parameters caused by high-squint angle and acceleration challenges the imaging performance. This paper proposes a precise imaging algorithm for high-squint SAR with accelerated trajectory. At first, coarse sub-image and sub-spectrum are obtained by factorized back-projection (BP) kernel in sub-aperture. Secondly, precise sub-spectrum center and spectrum width are derived corresponding to high-squint angle and acceleration, which are different from traditional imaging model. In the next, the sub-spectrum is corrected and regularized to avoid folding, and fused to generate whole aperture spectrum. Finally, the whole aperture spectrum is transformed into time-domain to obtain focused image. Simulated and measured SAR data experiments validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Single-Epoch Tropospheric Refractivity Tomography using Distributed Spaceborne D-InSAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The three-dimensional (3-D) fine structure of the troposphere is crucial for accurate prediction of meteorological activities. Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (D-InSAR) has become an emerging method for tropospheric monitoring with its high resolution and wide coverage. However, a single satellites can only measure the two-dimensional (2-D) troposphere along the line-of sight direction, and only differential parameters can be inverted, making it difficult to achieve three-dimensional absolute measurements. This paper proposes a distributed spaceborne SAR system scheme, combined with external Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models, to recover absolute delays at a single epoch, and uses distributed multi-angle observations to achieve three-dimensional tomography of the troposphere. The experiment based on the DALES model validate the effectiveness, the inverted refractivity with resolution of sub-kilometer is consistent with the true value, with an RMSE below 20, and the RMSE of the total delay along the zenith direction is around 2mm.

articleTitle: An Effective Parametric Autofocus Algorithm For Earth-based Radar Astronomical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Earth-based radar astronomical imaging is of great significance to planetary science research. With the improvement of imaging resolution, multiple non-ideal effects appear in the earth-based radar astronomical imaging, such as ephemeris error and atmospheric distortion, which seriously degrades the image quality. Due to the low SNR of echoes, the traditional non-parametric autofocus method is no longer suitable, while the traditional parametric autofocus method is inefficient. Therefore, efficient autofocus techniques are required to obtain well-focused SAR images. In this paper, an effective parametric autofocus technology is proposed. First, the phase error is modeled as a polynomial function of slow-time, which reduces the parameter search dimension. Then, sub-patch and sub-aperture division is performed, multiple sub-patches and sub-apertures are selected to perform back-projection imaging, which reduces the computational complexity of imaging. Finally, the phase error parameters are estimated using the Adam gradient descent method. Moreover, point simulation results and lunar experiment results based on an earth-based radar prototype system validate the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on InSAR 3D imaging algorithm based on multi-angle observation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) is not affected by weather conditions and can obtain data in a wide range, which is one of the important ways to obtain digital elevation model (DEM). InSAR phase unwrapped is always the key problem in the whole process. The effect of phase wrapping can be effectively solved by using the correlation of SAR image in multi-angle observation. In this paper, based on the original method, iterative calculation is used to solve the effect of unknown viewing angle on the results, and 3D imaging can be realized without observing the observation information of the scene. Finally, this paper verifies the feasibility and practicability of the proposed algorithm through simulation experiments and actual data processing.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Detection of Moving Targets Using Stepped-Frequency Signal for mmWave FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to perform high-precision velocity measurement and high-resolution range measurement for stepped-frequency millimeter wave (mmWave) radar. To this end, a novel algorithm is developed to iteratively compensate the quadratic phase and measure velocity, while achieving high target peak power to ensure detection performance. Then, motion compensation and inverse fast Fourier transform (IFFT) are performed separately for each chirp signal to obtain high-resolution range measurement results in the slow-time dimension. Finally, numerical simulations demonstrate effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of velocity and range measurements, respectively.

articleTitle: A Novel Estimation of Baroreflex Sensitivity by Using Variational Mode Decomposition and Cross-Wavelet Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: An accurate estimation of baroreflex sensitivity (BRS) supports the diagnosis of hypertension and other cardiovascular diseases. BRS is typically evaluated by analyzing the linear correlation between systolic blood pressure (SBP) and heart rate variability (HRV). In this work, we proposed a novel BRS estimation method that combines variational mode decomposition (VMD) and cross-wavelet transform (XWT) for improvement in BRS assessment. VMD effectively mitigates mode mixing by decomposing signals into intrinsic mode functions, thereby enhancing the accuracy of cardiac and vascular rhythm interplay analysis. XWT offers a time-frequency representation for coherence evaluation, providing a more precise criterion for BRS estimation. The proposed method was then validated by using the EUROBAVAR dataset. Results demonstrate a significantly smaller baroreflex sensitivity during standing position than in supine position in EUROBAVAR subjects. In addition, patients with baroreflex impairment exhibited significantly lower BRS indices than healthy subjects, indicating their weaker ability in regulating blood pressure. The proposed method holds promise in baroreflex impairment diagnosis and dynamic BRS estimation, supporting evaluation of related diseases.

articleTitle: SSMIF: Enhanced Spatial-Spectral Mamba Interactive Fusion Network for Hyperspectral Change Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Change detection (CD) in remote sensing images is a complex task. Recent advancements in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based methods have significantly improved CD accuracy. However, hyperspectral image (HSI) CD remains particularly challenging, especially in terms of change feature extraction and fusion. In this paper, we present an enhanced spatial-spectral mamba interactive fusion (SSMIF) network specifically designed for HSI CD. This network incorporates the state space model (SSM) and flow alignment techniques to extract and fuse features more effectively. In particular, the spatial and spectral mamba (SASM) model is employed to capture spatial and spectral features from bi-temporal HSIs. Furthermore, we introduce a bi-temporal flow alignment (BFA) method to resample images for improved feature alignment. An additional long short-term memory (LSTM) module is used to filter important features and reduce redundancy. Experimental results on HSI CD datasets show that the proposed SSMIF network consistently outperforms several state-of-the-art approaches. The source code of the proposed SSMIF will be released at https://github.com/creativeXin/SSMIF.

articleTitle: Loss-Guided Diffusion For General Controllable Generation With Sequential Monte Carlo
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: There has been a recent surge in employing conditional diffusion models across various applications, primarily owing to their superior generative capabilities. However, training-based conditional generation methods lack flexibility and require costly retraining for new conditions to yield high performance, while training-free methods suffer from inconsistency and instability due to heuristic approximations of the conditional score function. To address these challenges, we propose a novel training-free controllable generation approach for diffusion models based on sequential Monte Carlo (SMC), which implements asymptotically exact loss-guided diffusion sampling. We leverage pre-trained encoders to model the likelihood function based on similarity in feature space and energy-based functions and enable general controllable generation across a broad range of conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in both conditional generation quality and condition alignment and outperforms existing training-free conditional generation techniques.

articleTitle: Sparse SAR Separation Imaging via Exact Observation: Initial Result
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging, modulation of echo by target velocity necessitates more complex approaches for imaging moving targets. Concurrently, the scenes are generally mixed with moving and stationary targets. Achieving simultaneously separated imaging of moving and stationary targets represents a challenge in SAR imaging. In this letter, we proposed a novel separable iterative reweighted algorithm (SIRA), which can achieve separated imaging of moving and stationary targets. First, moving and stationary targets are both considered in the imaging model. Then, by separately applying sparse constraints to stationary and moving targets, the regularization problem is constructed to address the imaging of both moving and stationary targets. Finally, stationary targets are extracted by solving the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions of the problem, and moving targets are obtained through algorithm iteration. Experiments based on simulated data validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Phase Synchronization Network Construction Method Based on Coherent Accumulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To ensure high coherent signal accumulation for distributed space-borne radar, this paper proposes a multi-node phase synchronization network construction method. Firstly, based on the principle of maximum output energy; we derive an objective function to achieve multi-node coherent accumulation optimization. Secondly, the objective function is simplified mathematically combined with the procedure of node to "node to node" phase synchronization and the statistical features of residual phase error. The reduction reveals the internal linkage between the optimal coherent accumulation and the architecture of synchronization topology. Then, the issue is transformed to a network tree hierarchy problem, of which the strategy if to generate a network tree with minimum levels. Finally, the distributed space-borne radar synchronization network is constructed with greedy algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed method is optimal for distributed radar coherent accumulation and improves the radar's target detection capabilities.

articleTitle: A Small Target Detection Method in Sea Clutter Based on Feature Manifold
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Target detection methods based on multidimensional features are often applied to the detection of small targets in sea clutter. However, existing algorithms do not fully utilize the correlation information between features, which to some extent limits their performance. To address this issue, this paper proposes a small target detection method in sea clutter using feature manifolds. By establishing a high-dimensional manifold representation of radar echo feature data, the radar target detection problem is transformed into a discrimination problem between two geometric points on a feature matrix manifold. This method integrates the use of multidimensional features and their correlation information, thereby effectively improving target detection performance. Experimental results on the SDRDSP dataset demonstrate that the proposed detection approach outperforms existing feature-based methods in terms of detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Real-time Refocusing of Spaceborne SAR Images for Ship Targets with Space-variant Motion Based on GPU
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Traditional spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging algorithms are primarily designed for stationary targets. However, in practical scenarios, ship targets are often affected by complex angular motions induced by sea winds and waves, resulting in significant blurring in SAR images. This angular motion is inherently nonlinear and space-variant. This paper proposes a refocusing method tailored for ship targets with complex space-variant motion. The method decomposes the ship target image into multiple subimages and estimates phase errors of each subimage by maximizing image contrast, thereby achieving fine refocusing. Additionally, an acceleration scheme for refocusing processing is designed based on spaceborne hardware platforms, aimed at onboard real-time processing. The effectiveness of both the refocusing method and the acceleration scheme is validated using real spaceborne SAR image data. Experiment results demonstrate that, compared to traditional refocusing methods, the proposed approach improves the imaging quality of ship targets with complex motion. The refocusing processing efficiency is greatly enhanced, meeting the real-time processing requirements.

articleTitle: Improvement of reconstruction accuracy for hardware systems with Finite Rate of Innovation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In classical Finite Rate of Innovation (FRI) theory, signal reconstruction is initially achieved with precision using the zeroing filter algorithm on noiseless pulse signals. However, with the introduction of noise, the zeroing filter algorithm exhibits reduced robustness when handling signals with low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR). This paper introduces the TLS-ESPRIT algorithm, which enhances robustness against noise to some extent. Additionally, building on the development of an FRI reconstruction system based on C-TEM sampling, this work innovatively proposes a cascaded filter phase compensation method. This method mitigates the nonlinear phase effects of analog filters, thereby improving reconstruction accuracy. Ultimately achieving a reduction in sampling rate while improving reconstruction accuracy.

articleTitle: A Novel Keypoint-Based Approach for Occlusion Problem in Cross-View Labelling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Labelling multiple people across various camera views is fundamentally challenging, because of severe occlusion, complex scenes, and changing visibility observed from various viewpoints. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to solve the occlusion problem for cross-view labelling based on pairs of images. To solve the multiple people matching problem while severe occlusion occurs, we introduce a novel keypoint-based correspondence component between different people, in order to overcome the mis-alignment of multi-view geometry and locate the proper cross-view correspondence when occlusion occurs. Based on the keypoint component, correct correspondence can be rectified, thus obtaining accurate multi-view distance. To further enhance the performance for cross-view labelling, we incorporate pre-trained appearance features and multi-view constraints to achieve multiple people matching. Pairwise score strategy is also applied to increase the labelling accuracy. Experimental results verify the superior performance of the proposed method on challenging multi-view multiple people datasets both quantitatively and qualitatively.

articleTitle: PS Point Selection Based on Phase Stability of Time Series Phase Unwrapping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In Time Series SAR interferometry (TS-InSAR) analysis, the screening results of permanent scatterers (PS points) affect the accuracy and efficiency of phase unwrapping of TS-InSAR. In the case of atmospheric effect and random noise, the traditional PS point screening method will lead to incomplete noise removal and loss of key deformation information points. To solve this problem, a phase stability PS point screening method based on the traditional method is proposed in this paper. By analyzing the influence of the noise residual phase on the interference vector distribution, this method proposes a formula for calculating the phase coherence coefficient of a long time series midpoint. By setting a reasonable threshold to screen the phase coherence of global points, PS points that are relatively stable in amplitude and phase can be obtained, and the efficiency of subsequent phase unwinding and the precision of processing results can be improved.

articleTitle: Dual-Angle Radar Image Reconstruction With Geometrical Theory of Diffraction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: When the radar observation angle is sparse and the target is stationary, it is difficult to image by traditional methods. Therefore, we propose a dual-angle radar image reconstruction method to achieve dual-angle radar imaging. Firstly, the scattering centers estimation strategy based on GTD model is used and solved by ADMM to obtain the target scattering center information. Then the scattering center, distance and coefficient information are used to score and match the strong scattering points of the two HRRPs. Finally, the image is reconstructed by tracing the points. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: High Quality Imaging of Automotive Imaging Radar with Co-prime Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In millimeter-wave (mmWave) automotive radar, physical measurements acquired by conventional uniform sampling are often limited by available resources. Sparse sampling can achieve high-quality imaging through sparse reconstruction with limited measurements. However, it often requires cumbersome sampling strategy designs, and the actual manufactured hardware may not meet these requirements well. Therefore, a simpler and easier-to-implement sampling strategy, with less sampling but still structured, along with a corresponding high-quality imaging method, should be explored. In this work, we introduce and explore the technique of co-prime sampling for high-quality imaging of automotive radar. We explore co-prime sensing to obtain more effective samples while reducing the number of physical sampling channels in a structured design. Specifically, we use the second-order statistics of the measured data, namely the covariance matrix, as an alternative for measurements to increase effective measurements. Through this process, we also establish the corresponding imaging forward measurement model of the alternative measurements, and then construct the scene’s sparsity-regularized imaging model. We adopt the first-order proximal gradient algorithm to design the solving method of the imaging model, where background information is specifically reserved for better scene image interpretation while target information is enhanced. Finally, through experimental verification with several sets of measured data, it is proven that high-quality imaging results are obtained with co-prime sampling and the corresponding imaging methods. This paves the way for automotive imaging radar sensing with a less but structured sampling strategy.

articleTitle: GEO SAR Rotated Target Detection based on Edge Enhancement and Feature Alignment Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the advantages of large imaging swath, long observation time and short revisit period, geosynchronous orbit synthetic aperture radar (GEO SAR) plays a significant role in large-scale observation and maritime surveillance. To figure out the issues of low range-resolution, image distortion and target defocus in GEO SAR ship target detection, this paper proposes a GEO SAR rotated target detection method based on edge enhancement and feature alignment convolution. Firstly, the edge features are extracted and fused with context features by channel priority attention mechanism. To register the object with arbitrary pose with the horizontal convolutional kernels, the rotated anchors are predicted by feature alignment convolutional network, where the feature maps are adjusted according to the anchor poses. Finally, the high-precision bounding box and classification results are obtained by a two-stream detection head. In this paper, we produced a simulated GEO SAR ship target detection data set. The experiment shows that the proposed method improves the average precision for 1.8% on focus target and 6.1% on defocus target compared with the traditional methods.

articleTitle: Deformation Inversion Method for Building Structures Based on Cylindrical Aperture Radar Three-Dimensional Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In building structure monitoring scenarios, conventional differential interferometric synthetic aperture radar (DInSAR) is unable to obtain deformation of overlapping targets within observation scenes. This paper proposes a deformation inversion method based on cylindrical aperture radar three-dimensional (3D) imaging. Cylindrical aperture radar, while maintaining traditional resolution capabilities, synthesizes aperture in the elevation direction, enabling acquisition of high-precision 3D images of observation scenes. By performing differential interferometry on 3D radar images before and after target deformation, deformation of each target can be obtained. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through a set of simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Study on the Effects of Phased Array Channel Errors on the Beam Steering Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The effects of antenna array channel phase errors on the beam steering accuracy are investigated in this work. The beam steering errors of a square planar uniform array can be estimated using formula directly. However, this formula cannot be applied to planar arrays in other forms. And the beam errors in two orthogonal planes cannot be determined. The Monte Carlo simulations are conducted to estimate the beam steering errors of a 128-element planar array that is not square. The standard deviations of beam steering errors in two orthogonal planes are calculated and compared with the standard deviation calculated by using formula. In addition, the effects of channel amplitude errors on gain and side-lobe level (SLL) are also discussed.

articleTitle: A study on the relationship between the phenomenon of grating nulls and array configuration of distributed array radars
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The directional pattern of a distributed array has grating lobes. This will lead to a significant decrease in interference suppression performance, which is called the phenomenon of grating nulls. The array configuration has an impact on the phenomenon of grating nulls. In this paper, the relationship between the phenomenon of grating nulls and array configuration of distributed array radars is studied. Through theoretical derivations and simulations, a comparative analysis is conducted on the grating lobe interference suppression performance of distributed arrays with uniform and nonuniform deployments.

articleTitle: Multipath Ghost Suppression Based on Frequency Domain Filtering for Through-the-Wall Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Moving target detection based on unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-borne multichannel through-the-wall radar has found wide applications in military and civilian domains. However, multipath reflections within indoor environments lead to multipath ghost in imaging results, which cause the generation of false alarms. To address this issue, this article proposes a method for suppressing multipath artifacts in UAV-borne multichannel through-the-wall radar based on frequency-domain filtering. In the proposed method, the differences between the multipath echoes and the direct path echoes in the range-Doppler domain are analyzed. Subsequently, a frequency domain filtering method is proposed to filter out multipath echoes. Finally, the back-projection algorithm is used to achieve through-the-wall imaging. Simulations demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Aeroplane Detection using Spaceborne SAR Time-series Images based on low-rank Sparse Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has widely applied in the field of earth monitoring because of its advantages of high-resolution imaging and repeat pass observation. However, the previous SAR target detection algorithms are mainly aimed at stationary and moving targets on land and ocean scenes, and there are relatively few studies on aerial targets detection. Therefore, this paper proposes a detection method for stationary and moving aeroplane using time-series image data. Based on the low-rank sparse decomposition algorithm, this method uses time-series image data to detect stationary targets and severely defocused moving targets. By the above detection results, false alarm suppression and detection of stationary and moving aeroplane can be effectively achieved. The method is verified by Sentinel-1 time-series image data, and the results show that the proposed method is feasible.

articleTitle: Autofocusing Imaging and Medium Parameter Estimation Based on Phase Error for Penetrating Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Penetrating radar has the ability to detect the targets buried inside or hidden behind mediums. Most imaging algorithms are only effective when the medium parameters are known. However, it is difficult to obtain the exact information of the medium in real scenarios. Therefore, the error of unknown parameters leads to defocusing of the obtained image. To solve this problem, an autofocusing imaging and parameter estimation method based on phase error is proposed in this paper. First, the relationship between phase error and medium parameters is derived. Then, by analyzing the linear relationship with respect to the frequency, the phase error and optimal depth are determined. The autofocusing process is realized by compensating the defocused image with the estimated phase error. Finally, the relative permittivity of the medium and depth can be obtained by solving the established function. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated by experiments.

articleTitle: Wide-angle Scanning Irregular Phased Array With Low Sidelobe Level Synthesis Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper aims to minimize the peak sidelobe level (PSLL) via an irregular phased array. An optimization problem based on the minimization of total radiation power (MTRP) problem is constructed. The originally formulated problem is non-convex due to the directivity constraint. Therefore, an alternative minimization method is proposed. Compared with the existing methods, the proposed method can achieve a lower PSLL with high directivity.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of low-orbit satellite broadcast signal receiving and processing terminal spherical crown antenna array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The low-orbit satellite broadcast signal receiving terminal is an important space-based intelligence acquisition and combat command receiving component. The antenna array serves as the first-level module for the receiving terminal to process the received signal. It is responsible for filtering, amplifying the signal, suppressing noise and out-of-band signals. and transmitted to the radio frequency local oscillator board. In the traditional low-orbit reconnaissance satellite reception and processing terminal business process, satellite broadcast signals are difficult to meet the coverage requirements of high-gain and multi-beams. To address this problem, this design is based on HFSS simulation software and uses wide airspace coverage array antenna technology to design the architecture. Based on the characteristics of low-orbit satellite broadcast signal receiving terminals, a 32-element spherical crown array antenna is designed to achieve a reasonable array. Array element architecture selection, array element optimization, and mutual coupling suppression between array elements.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Building Extraction Based on CSAR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Circular synthetic aperture radar (CSAR), as a new imaging model, can be used to image the same scene, obtain scattering information from different azimuth angles, and effectively improve the performance of SAR image interpretation. In the CSAR image, the target of the building has not only the strong scattering characteristic, which is the secondary scattering of the light line that is measured in a certain angle, but also the anisotropic scattering characteristics. Meanwhile, the variation of the scattering amplitude in different angles always obeys certain laws as the Angle of observation changes. The method based on the single feature always only describes part of the target feature and cannot extract the characteristics of the target in a comprehensive way. However, the fusion of excessive characteristics can cause the algorithm complexity to rise dramatically, and the algorithm parameter estimation is more complex based on the fusion of multi-feature. Furthermore, the existing algorithm requires the setting of the super parameter manually. In this paper, a novel method for the extraction of the CSAR image building based on multi-statistical characteristics is proposed, which including the dispersion characteristics of the scattering amplitude as well as the anisotropic scattering characteristics. Moreover, the amplitude and the adjacent domain information are considered simultaneously, which obtains a great opportunity for more accurate extraction of building. By experimenting with the actual measured data of the L band, the proposed method is proved to be better than the existing method. To a certain extent, it suppresses the false alarms generated by other ground targets. Additionally, the method exhibits good extraction performance for buildings of various types and different scenes. In summary, the proposed method has the ability to more effectively extract the scattering characteristics of buildings in CSAR images.

articleTitle: Insect Species Identification Based on Polarimetric Scattering Feature Sequences Using MsRNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This study introduces an original deep learning technique for the classification of insect species, which relies on the analysis of polarimetric scattering feature sequences. Utilizing a multi-scale Recurrent Neural Network (MsRNN) architecture, we achieve high-precision recognition of nine first-class migratory pest species using data collected from a high-resolution fully polarimetric radar. Our method achieves an average identification accuracy of 98.1%, demonstrating significant improvements compared to traditional classification techniques. This high accuracy makes our approach a valuable tool for pest management and agricultural protection, enabling more efficient and accurate monitoring of harmful migratory insect species.

articleTitle: SBSN: Weakly Supervised Image Segmentation Based on Shape Prior
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the domain of multimedia signal processing, shape priors serve as crucial cues for guiding model training. However, many existing techniques struggle to effectively represent complex shape priors in multimedia content. To address this challenge, we introduce a Shape-Based Image Segmentation Network (SBSN) that leverages a Convolutionally Constrained Boltzmann Machine (CRBM) for shape prior extraction from multimedia signals. The SBSN employs CRBM to explicitly model the shape probability distribution through rigorous mathematical formulations and utilizes Wasserstein distance as a metric to quantify the disparity between the segmentation output and the extracted shape prior. For multimedia signal segmentation, SBSN incorporates an advanced feature fusion architecture, utilizing ResNet for hierarchical feature extraction and transposed convolution for signal upsampling and reconstruction. This process culminates in high-resolution, pixel-level segmentation of multimedia content. Notably, SBSN is designed to operate effectively with a limited set of labeled multimedia samples during the training phase. Extensive evaluations were conducted against state-of-the-art weakly-supervised methods across diverse multimedia objects: human figures, horses, airplanes, and surface cracks. The results demonstrate that SBSN achieves a significant 0.8% improvement in average AUROC and secures the second rank in average ABO performance, underscoring its efficacy in processing and analyzing complex multimedia signals.

articleTitle: MARDF:Mining and Reconstructing 4D-Radar Derived Features in Point Cloud for Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Detecting objects plays an essential role in autonomous driving systems. Recently, 4D millimeter-wave radar, which captures spatial information in (x, y, z, v) coordinates along with velocity v, has proven to produce denser point clouds compared to traditional 2+1D radar systems that only provide position and velocity information. While most current point cloud detection techniques are tailored to LiDAR data, they may not be directly applicable to radar data, which is typically sparse, noisy, and includes velocity components. In this work, we propose a novel method to enhance radar-derived point cloud features for object detection, referred to as MARDF. This approach leverages the radar point cloud's density approximation and incorporates point velocities, which boosts the dimensionality of the point cloud features. Experiments conducted using the TJ4DRadSet and VoDataset in various traffic environments indicate that the proposed object detection method outperforms classical point cloud detection methods. Furthermore, this module is adaptable to other detection methods and demonstrates an improvement in accuracy.

articleTitle: Adaptive Nonlinear Causal Quantification for Real-Time Emotion Analysis using EMD-based Causal Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Affective computing, which combines neuroscience and signal processing, plays a critical role in accurately deciphering human emotional states—a key component in various applications. Traditional emotion detection methods often face limitations due to their vulnerability to social influences and reliance on linear models. Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals present a more objective measure by directly reflecting brain activity related to emotional states. This study introduces the EMD-based causal decomposition (CD-EMD) to infer neural causality, which involves decomposing EEGs into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) and capturing instantaneous phase interactions among IMFs. Unlike the traditional Granger causality, which assumes linearity and stationarity, CD-EMD offers an adaptive and nonlinear framework that more accurately represents the complex, time-varying nature of brain dynamics. Based on the DEAP dataset, the graph metrics across various frequency bands are extracted, after CD-EMD constructs the EEG network by quantifying the causal strength (CS) between each two channels. The results show that positive emotions are associated with increased α band centrality and clustering, suggesting enhanced cognitive functions, while negative emotions are linked to heightened β band clustering and longer path lengths, indicating increased stress responses. This research not solely offers new perspectives on the neural dynamics of emotional states, but also demonstrates the superior time efficiency of CD-EMD. Our findings underline the potential of the proposed CD-EMD in enhancing real-time emotion detection and the untangling of emotional brain networks.

articleTitle: MTKD-Det: An Efficient SAR Target Detector Based on Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: As a critical branch of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) interpretation, SAR target detection has many applications in the military and civil fields. Although traditional deep learning methods achieve some satisfactory performance in target detection tasks, they inherently require significant computational resources and interpretation time. Hence, traditional deep learning methods frequently struggle to maintain a balance between high efficiency and precision. It is undoubtedly a huge challenge for target detection tasks. To address this problem, an efficient SAR target detector based on multi-teacher knowledge distillation (MTKD-Det) is proposed in this paper, which can effectively enhance target detection accuracy while reducing inference time. Specifically, a multiple-teacher knowledge distillation strategy is used in the proposed method, which integrates the experiences and methodologies of multiple teachers to collaboratively guide the training and learning of the student network, ultimately enhancing the robustness of the student network. In this work, a novel teacher network is developed to enhance the detection performance of the proposed method specifically for small targets. Furthermore, an attention mechanism is incorporated into the student network to enable it to focus on more critical information, thereby improving overall detection efficacy. Experimental results obtained from a measured SAR target detection dataset convincingly validate the benefits of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Geometric Optimization of Distributed Radar System for TDOA-based Jamming Source Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Accurate localization of jamming sources is essential for developing anti-jamming strategies. This paper proposes a geometric optimization method for distributed radar systems, aimed at enhancing both localization and surveillance performance in jamming source localization based on time difference of arrival measurements. First, evaluation metrics for localization and surveillance performance are established, leading to the formulation of a constrained multi-objective optimization problem. To address the limitations of existing algorithms that often converge to local optima, this paper introduces a randomized relaxation-based multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm. This algorithm effectively balances the sensitivity differences between different optimization metrics by designing new individual best particle update rules, significantly enhancing the search capability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm excels in handling objective functions with optimization sensitivity differences, and the solution sets obtained show significant advantages in both localization and surveillance performance compared to traditional algorithms. Additionally, this algorithm shows strong robustness against variations in jamming source transmission power, indicating its practical application potential.

articleTitle: A lightweight steel surface defect detection model based on YOLOv9
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In addressing the problems of low detection accuracy and high model complexity in current deep learning-based steel surface defect detection algorithms, a steel surface defect detection model based on an improved YOLOv9 is put forward. This model augments the general efficient layer aggregation network by adding four large separable kernel attention modules, thereby enhancing the detection accuracy of minor defects in complex backgrounds. To lower model complexity, an ultra-lightweight dynamic up-sampling operator is integrated, making the network more lightweight and resource-efficient. Moreover, omni-dimensional dynamic convolutions are used to replace traditional convolutions in the YOLOv9 network to further improve defect detection performance. Experimental results show that the proposed model attains a mean average precision (mAP) of 78.9% on the NEU-DET steel defect detection dataset, surpassing the benchmark YOLOv9 model by 4.8%. The detection speed is increased by 5 frames per second (FPS), while model parameters and computational complexity are reduced by 1.1% and 0.6% respectively. These enhancements make our model highly suitable for steel surface defect detection in industrial environments with limited hardware resources.

articleTitle: Fast Super-Resolution DOA Estimation for Unknown Number of Radiation Sources Based on Complex Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To address the high computational complexity of traditional Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation techniques and the limitations of previous neural networks in handling fixed signal sources, a new signal processing model was developed. This model employs sparse representation methods and deep learning through complex convolutional neural networks(CCNN). Focused research on the array’s performance under unknown radiation sources using the complex convolutional neural network algorithm for super-resolution DOA estimation was conducted in a PyTorch environment. The results indicate that the complex convolutional model has a lower DOA computation complexity and higher precision in handling unknown radiation sources. After incorporating sparse representation with sampled data through the CCNN model for DOA estimation, an improvement in estimation accuracy and a reduction in computational complexity were observed compared to methods relying solely on sparse representation. Additionally, this model can effectively detect incoming waves from unknown radiation sources, unlike previous neural networks.

articleTitle: Multi-dimensional super-resolution of off-grid dense multi-targets based on atomic norm minimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Sparse recovery algorithm can achieve super-resolution processing of targets by handling the received signals and dictionary matrix. However, when dealing with dense multitargets that require multi-dimensional super-resolution, the dictionary matrix significantly impacts the recovery results and can lead to grid mismatch issues. Moreover, most existing target recovery methods focus on two-dimensional super-resolution and are prone to off-grid situations. To address these challenges, this paper combines Atomic Norm Minimization (ANM) with the Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL) algorithm to propose a multidimensional target super-resolution algorithm optimized based on atomic norm minimization theory. The simulation results show that this method effectively achieves multi-dimensional super-resolution of off-grid dense multi-targets.

articleTitle: Rapidly Generated Mainlobe Deceptive Jammer Suppression via Matrix Decomposition in FDA-MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The main purpose of this paper is rapidly generated mainlobe deceptive jammer suppression in the framework of a frequency diverse array-multiple-input multiple-output (FDA-MIMO) radar. Particularly, an innovative solution based on the two-low-rank matrix decomposition (2-LRMD) model is proposed. At the stage of signal model formulation, the echo is conformed to the aforementioned model, and it can be separated into two low-rank matrices corresponding to the true target and rapidly generated mainlobe deceptive jammers, also called false targets, respectively. Then, we establish an optimization problem so as to solve the 2-LRMD problem via alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. Moreover, the procedure of residual jammer matrix extraction via truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) is implemented to better recover the signal matrices of true and false targets. Numerical simulation results are presented to attest the effectiveness of our method in mitigating the rapidly generated mainlobe deceptive jammers.

articleTitle: A Bistatic Radar Passive Jamming Identification Method based on HRRP Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The passive jamming put by the ship at sea can deceive the bistatic radar as a decoy false target, which makes it difficult to detect and capture the real target. The HRRP feature, as an important basis for the radar to identify the passive jamming, has been verified on the monostatic radar. In order to explore the performance advantage of HRRP feature in passive jamming identification under bistatic radar, this paper constructs 18 features, based on which the feature differentiation and similarity are comprehensively evaluated based on Relief algorithm and correlation coefficient in order to select highly efficient identification features, and the SVM is used to validate the effect of feature selection. The simulation proves that the selected feature combination under bistatic radar can effectively improve the jamming identification performance.

articleTitle: Patch-based Cross-domain Adaptation for Few-shot Remote Sensing Scene Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Recognizing new classes from a few labeled remote sensing images presents a significant challenge. Existing methodologies assume that training and testing datasets come from identical domains. Collecting training datasets of remote sensing images from each domain is practically unfeasible. To tackle this challenge, we propose a strategy that leverages image patch feature embedding and cross-adaptation mechanism for cross-domain few-shot classification. Initially, the supplied image is segmented into patches of the same size. Subsequently, feature embeddings are extracted and reinforced with prototypical triplet loss to enhance robustness. A unified module then facilitates cross-adaptation between the support and query sets, producing classification features that effectively represent the relationship between them, thus better adapting to few-shot remote sensing classification challenges with domain shifts. Our proposed method’s excellence and generality are confirmed by comprehensive experiments.

articleTitle: A Multipath Signals Recognition Method based on Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Millimeter-wave radar is the primary sensor for enabling autonomous driving and ADAS functions. MIMO technology has demonstrated its effectiveness to deliver precise angular estimation of objects using few antennas, making it a popular choice in automotive radar applications. However, a significant challenge for MIMO systems is multipath reflection. This phenomenon not only degrades angular estimation accuracy by disrupting the integrity of the virtual arrays in MIMO radar, but also impairs detection performance by introducing ghost targets. This paper addresses the issue of ghost target identification in multipath scenarios for vehicle-mounted MIMO radar. A method called DNN-IAA is proposed, which combines Iterative Adaptive Algorithm based on separation of sending and receiving (srt-IAA) with the Deep Neural Network (DNN) to tackle multipath signals recognition in complex scenarios. Firstly, srt-IAA is employed to obtain the two-dimensional angle-frequency spectrum of the target’s Direction of Arrival (DOA) and Direction of Departure (DOD). Subsequently, the DNN is used to extract features from the DOA-DOD spectrum for the classification of multipath signals. Finally, a simulation is conducted to validate the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning-based Radio Frequency Fingerprinting across Receiving Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to the coupling effect of emitter distortion and receiver distortion, the actual received signal contains the information of the current emitter system and the receiving system, which makes the Radio Frequency Fingerprinting (RFF) technology unable to be generalized in cross-receiving system scenarios. To eliminate the effect of receiver, in this paper, a transfer learning-based RFF method across receiving systems is proposed which considers the influence of the receiver as a separate domain. Through the dual-label feature and domain separation adversarial reconstruction method, after trained with multi-receiver data in the source domain, the proposed method can separate domains of transmitting and receiving, extract emitter fingerprint information, which improves the generalization of RFF in scenarios such as cross-receiving system and cross-platform. Compared with the existing cross-receiver RFF methods, the proposed method can truly adapt to the actual unsupervised scenario. And the more the number of source domain receivers participating in the training, the better the domain adaptation effect.

articleTitle: Task Scheduling for Geosynchronous Surveillance Using Radar Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This study proposes a task scheduling method dedicated to fast patrol of geosynchronous surveillance airspace and observation of the satellites inside it using a reflector radar array. Satellite movement time, antenna movement time (point to target) and dwell time (target observation) are considered in modeling, which makes the problem time-dependent. The large surveillance airspace is divided into several sub-airspaces in terms of the distribution of target satellites, while the scheduling of each sub-airspace is performed seriatim following a certain direction. Genetic algorithm (GA) with some modifications is employed to solve the scheduling problem and optimize the patrol time of every single sub-airspace, so as to obtain the optimized total patrol time of the whole surveillance airspace. Simulation is carried out for validation. A notional radar array comprising 5 reflector radars is utilized to conduct a fast patrol of the surveillance airspace that span 20°S~20°N and 110°E~180°E. The results show that: all observation tasks, i.e., the 189 geosynchronous satellites within the surveillance airspace, are evenly distributed to each radar, while the total patrol time is diminished to 490 seconds, which proves the efficacy of the developed scheduling method in geosynchronous surveillance.

articleTitle: A novel multi-ellipsoidal approach to group target tracking using variational approximation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Group target tracking that estimates the position and shape of collective objects is a hotspot area in radar observation. Group targets, such as birds and UAVs, often exhibit complex spatial structures and highly dynamic behaviors. However, traditional multi-ellipsoidal tracking methods rely on a simple random matrix to model sub-object extension, where orientation and extension size are coupled. The initial sub-object model may fail to adapt to dynamic changes in the sub-object state, especially when the sub-object rotates. This paper introduces a modified multi-ellipsoidal tracking method, where the orientation of each sub-object is represented as an independent Gaussian random vector, separate from its extension size. The extension size is described by a diagonal symmetric positive definite matrix, with its elements following inverse Gamma distributions. A variational Bayesian approach is applied to approximate the complex posterior distribution. Real-data experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Detecting Maritime Moving Targets Using Bistatic Radar based on Low-Earth-Orbit Communication Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the accelerated deployment of low Earth orbit (LEO) communication satellites, the integration of distributed communication satellites with passive radar has emerged as a new research domain, offering significant application prospects and value in monitoring remote oceanic regions. However, the complex operational conditions of LEO satellites introduce multiple interference factors in the received signals, including higher-order range migration (RM), higher-order Doppler Frequency migration (DFM), and Doppler ambiguity, which severely impact the effective accumulation of echo energy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a passive radar method for detecting maritime moving targets using LEO communication satellites as the radiation source. The method first estimates the reference values and optimization intervals for the influencing factors and constructs a synchronized matched filter. It then employs a Modified Second-Order Keystone Transform (MSOKT) to process range migration and Doppler ambiguity. Subsequently, a Decoupled Fourier Transform (DcFT) is used to compensate for the remaining Doppler migration in the echo, completing the echo energy accumulation. Finally, the optimal estimates of the influencing factors are used to deduce the target's motion state. Simulation results demonstrate that this method effectively achieves target detection and perception in this scenario. This research is significant for improving the target detection performance of passive radar systems using LEO communication satellites.

articleTitle: Spatiality-Aligned Graph Convolution Hashing for Unsupervised Cross-Modal Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Unsupervised cross-modal retrieval leveraging hash learning has attracted a lot of interest from academics, primarily due to its minimal storage requirements, swift retrieval speeds, and label-free nature, making it a prime candidate for real-world applications. Nevertheless, the inherent "heterogeneous differences" and "semantic gap" within cross-modal data features pose significant challenges. Despite various attempts by scholars to address these issues, the existing solutions often fall short in terms of effectiveness. This can be attributed to several reasons: Firstly, image features, in contrast to text features, possess a plethora of attributes, making it challenging to extract features that possess strong expressive capabilities. Secondly, each modality of data exhibits not only inter-node correlations but also intricate relationships between individual nodes and their neighboring nodes. Consequently, a straightforward semantic correlation matrix is inadequate in capturing the intricate structural relationships within the data. Thirdly, the neglect of internal structural associations results in insufficient representation capabilities of binary hash codes in the Hamming space, hampering the learning of effective hash functions. To address these limitations, we introduce a Spatiality-Aligned Graph Convolution Hashing (SAGCH) algorithm. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our SAGCH method excels in both "image-to-text retrieval" and "text-to-image retrieval" tasks.

articleTitle: Secrecy Performance Analysis of Hybrid RF-FSO Cooperative Satellite-Aerial-Terrestrial Networks with imperfect CSI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This study examines the secrecy outage performance of uplink transmission within a hybrid cooperative satellite-aerial-terrestrial network (SATN) that integrates radio-frequency (RF) and free-space optical (FSO) technologies. Specifically, in the proposed cooperative SATN, a terrestrial source (S) conveys its information to a satellite receiver (D) with the assistance of an aerial relay (R), while a group of eavesdropping aerial terminals (Eves) attempts to intercept the confidential data. RF and FSO transmission methods are employed over the S-R and R-D links, respectively, both subject to imperfect channel state information (CSI). By considering the randomness of R, D, and Eves, and utilizing a stochastic geometry framework, we investigate the secrecy outage performance of the considered SATN. A closed-form analytical expression for the end-to-end secrecy outage probability is derived. Finally, simulations are conducted to validate the accuracy of the analysis.

articleTitle: Gated Recurrent Neural Network with Interaction Model of Multiple Targets for Traffic Radar Tracking
