publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: As urban transportation becomes more intelligent, traffic radar target tracking has emerged as a key research area. In complex traffic environments, clutter or obstacles cause variations in radar measurement data, leading to measurement interruptions or losses that challenge continuous and stable target tracking. Traditional Kalman filter (KF) methods and neural network (NN)-based approaches are limited in their ability to handle these variations. By integrating the strengths of KF and gated recurrent neural networks (GRNN), a novel GRNN is designed to leverage multi-target interaction for robust tracking in traffic scenarios. Specifically, the internal structure of the proposed GRNN is designed based on the computational processes of KF, and a memory factor is introduced to retain historical interaction information to surpass the limitations of traditional first-order Markov tracking methods while integrating the interaction information among multiple targets. The introduction of the KF framework brings excellent interpretability, a lightweight parameter scale, and low training data requirements. Experiments on the real-world dataset show that the proposed method significantly outperforms benchmark KF and advanced NN-based filtering methods in target tracking performance with measurement variations, ensuring continuous and stable tracking.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Detection and Estimation with Distributed FDA-MIMO and EPC-MIMO Radars
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper deals with simultaneous parameter estimation and target detection in a distributed radar system consisting of Frequency Diverse Array Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (FDA-MIMO) and Element-Pulse Coding MIMO (EPC-MIMO) radars. For each local radar station, a binary hypothesis detection problem is formulated with unknown target parameters, and detectors are developed leveraging Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) criterion. Under the hypothesis of target presence, the Coordinate Descent (CD) algorithm is leveraged to estimate the range and angle information of the target. Subsequently, the multiple sets of the local test statistics are fused at the Fusion Center (FC) for the ultimate decision, where the global test statistic can be constructed by taking the logarithm sum of local test statistics. At the analysis stage, the effectiveness of the devised method is evaluated in terms of Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Probability of Detection (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>), where comparisons among different radar frameworks, including the distributed radar composed of traditional phased arrays, monostatic EPC-MIMO, and FDA-MIMO radars are carried out. Numerical results verify the superiorities of the proposed approach for simultaneous target detection and parameter estimation.

articleTitle: Cancer Subtype Classification Based on Graph Convolutional Network with Enhanced Structural Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) are biased toward local data information during training while neglecting global structural feature. Therefore, this paper investigates a cancer subtype classification method based on a GCN with enhanced structural feature. Aiming at genomics and transcrip-tomes datasets for stomach adenocarcinoma samples obtained from the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), the proposed approach relies on a weighted autoencoder with a shared hidden layer to integrate multi-omics data feature. Subsequently, a Self-Organizing Mapping network is employed to learn the global structural feature of samples based on Geodesic distance. The integrated multi-omics feature and global structural feature serve as feature inputs for the GCN. At the same time, the input graph for the GCN is generated through Similarity Network Fusion algorithm. Finally, the classification of cancer samples is accomplished after training. Comparative experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms several popular algorithms in cancer subtype classification, achieving the highest accuracy. This is because enhancing global structural feature allows the model to capture the samples’ local and global structural feature, leading to more reasonable classification results.

articleTitle: Boosted Spectral Perception via Synergistic Vision for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Hyperspectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Cross-domain few-shot learning (CDFSL) hyper-spectral image classification (HSIC) techniques have significantly enhanced the performance of HSIC under a few annotations. Due to the scattered spatial distribution of HSI and limited labels, the spatial information of the HSI sample is restricted, which means the spectral information may contain more discriminative category features than spatial information. However, most existing CDFSL HSIC methods lack targeted spectral discriminative feature extraction and struggle to capture spectral subtleties. To address this, a Human Eye-like Dual-Branch Network (HEDB-Net) is proposed, comprising a central branch and a peripheral branch. The central branch focuses on extracting core features from complete spectral dimension HSI patches. Simultaneously, these patches are input into the peripheral branch via random sampling and reintegration of spectral bands, enabling the model to perceive initially dispersed spectral information. These two branches represent the model’s central and peripheral vision for the spectrum, allowing it to focus on different levels of feature information and significantly boosting spectral perception capabilities. To fully leverage the advantages of synergistic vision, a consistency constraint is applied to align their category probability prediction distributions, which helps ensure consistency in classification decisions between the two branches. Experimental results on the PaviaU dataset demonstrate that HEDBNet outperforms other advanced algorithms in terms of overall accuracy(OA), average accuracy(AA), and Kappa coefficient. This proves that HEDBNet can simultaneously focus on primary and secondary spectral features, thus significantly boosting classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Image Segmentation Algorithm of Ischemic Stroke based on Wavelet Pooling Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Ischemic stroke is a high-risk brain disease that causes disability or death in adults worldwide. Rapid diagnosis and treatment, as well as segmentation of ischemic lesions from stroke medical images so that doctors can evaluate and develop treatment plans, are crucial to reducing brain damage. Currently, doctors’ manual segmentation of lesions is time-consuming and labor-intensive and prone to missed or misdiagnosed diagnoses, delaying the best time for treatment. A well-trained neural network is considered as an effective aid for image segmentation tasks. However, in the traditional neural network down-sampling process, the pooling layer loses feature information, and the lost information significantly impacts the edge regions. While for medical images, edge regions are crucial features in the segmentation process. Therefore, to address the above issues, in this paper we improve upon the existing stroke lesion segmentation algorithm U-net, we design a segmentation network based on wavelet pooling and attention mechanisms. The network was tested on ISLES 2018 and ISLES 2022 datasets, and the Dice coefficient improved by 2.13% and 1.93% compared to baseline network, respectively.

articleTitle: Shallow Sea Bathymetry Mapping from Satellite SAR Observations Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This study proposes a deep-learning model to map underwater topography from spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. For the model development, 18 high-resolution Sentinel-1 dual-polarization SAR images covering the southern Cape Cod area from 2014 to 2022 are collected, among which twelve images were used for model training, while the rest were used for testing. In order to facilitate the model learning complex and nonlinear relations among various parameters, the model input is designed to consist of 8 variables, which involve radar backscatter coefficient, radar observation geometry, geography information and marine dynamic environmental parameters. The deep learning network consists of a convolutional layer, two residual blocks, and a fully connected layer, facilitating feature extraction and regression prediction. The final model performances in retrieving shallow water depth are shown as follows: For the training set, the model achieved a root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.02 m and a relative error of 4.32%, with the maximum detectable water depth reaching 48.17 m. For testing, the best performance of the model presented with an RMSE of 1.59 m and a relative error of 5.29%, while the worst performance corresponds to an RMSE of 4.53 m with a relative error of 15.61%. Thus, the proposed model has the capacity of detecting the shallow water depth up to 50 meters with high precision.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation SAR Target Recognition Based on Evidential Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target recognition based on deep learning has yielded superior results. However, these methods typically necessitate large-scale labeled SAR data, which is challenging to acquire. Therefore, investigating the knowledge transfer from easily generated simulated SAR data to unlabeled real SAR data is of significant importance. The distribution difference between simulated SAR data and real SAR data can impact recognition performance. To align the distribution of simulated SAR data with that of real SAR data, this paper proposes an unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) SAR target recognition algorithm based on evidential deep learning (EDL). The algorithm employs an adversarial-based method for domain-level alignment between the simulated and real domains, while also filtering pseudo-labels to achieve finer class-level alignment. To obtain reliable pseudo-labels, the algorithm utilizes EDL with a second-order distribution model based on the Dirichlet distribution, enabling the model to represent decision uncertainty, which integrates model uncertainty and data uncertainty. Experimental results indicate that the algorithm can achieve excellent recognition performance.

articleTitle: Improved Deep Matrix Factorization for Signal Recovery in Random Frequency Diversity Array Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Motivated by the success of recent deep learning researches on radar, we consider a deep learning based matrix factorization method for suppressing the high range-angle side-lobes in random frequency diversity array (FDA) radars. While the existing deep matrix factorization approach is designed for real-valued situations and signals of FDA radars are complex-valued cases, we propose two methods to extend the existing approach into complex-valued framework: 1) adjusting the neural network structures and activation functions for complex-valued operations, and 2) constructing a real-valued representation of the original complex-valued input. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed methods outperform traditional ones in multi-target scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on Dataset Preparation and Registration Methods for Multi-Temporal Airport SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) offers high-resolution imaging capabilities that are unaffected by weather and lighting conditions, making it ideal for complex environments. Recent advancements in spaceborne SAR technology have provided diverse high-resolution, multi-temporal SAR data, crucial for applications like airport monitoring. Despite these advancements, there is a notable lack of multi-temporal airport SAR datasets for research. This study addresses this gap by presenting a method to create a multi-temporal airport SAR image dataset. Utilizing known latitude and longitude information, the method converts geographic coordinates to image projection coordinates to locate airports in SAR images, followed by image conversion and alignment to construct the dataset. Additionally, this study introduces a registration method named SAR-SURF for multi-temporal SAR images, employing a SURF-based Feature Points Detector and an improved Fast Sample Consensus (FSC) algorithm. The experimental results demonstrate that this method effectively reduces speckle noise, ensures matching accuracy, and minimizes processing time, enabling rapid and precise registration of multi-temporal airport SAR images.

articleTitle: Clustering Model-based Analysis of Sales in Vegetable Categories for Supermarkets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The development of effective vegetable sales strategies is crucial for enhancing supermarket profitability, and these strategies are heavily reliant on a nuanced understanding of the sales volume distribution patterns across different vegetable categories. However, most existing studies fail to thoroughly analyze these distribution patterns, often neglecting factors such as sales volume magnitude and fluctuations. To address this gap, we first propose a comprehensive framework based on a K-means++ clustering model and Spearman correlation coefficient to analyze the sales data. Firstly, we normalize the data to eliminate the impact of differing dimensions across vegetable categories. Next, we analyze the sales data from both quarterly and daily perspectives. Data visualization is performed utilizing line charts, followed by a descriptive analysis of the sales volume distribution considering both magnitude and fluctuation. Furthermore, we utilize a K-means++ clustering model and the Spearman correlation coefficient to further explore the distribution patterns and interrelationships among different vegetable categories. The results of the experiments reveal the daily and quarterly sales distribution patterns of various vegetable categories, providing valuable insights to support the development of effective vegetable sales strategies for supermarkets.

articleTitle: LR-Contrast: Accurate Multi-modal Brain Tumor Segmentation based on Local-Region Supervised Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Early detection and accurate segmentation of brain tumors is of paramount importance for diagnosis and treatment. Due to the abundant information in multi-modal data, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has become the primary basis for brain tumor image segmentation. The existing deep learning-based segmentation methods mainly focus on refining the internal structure of deep networks, most of them employ Dice loss and Cross-Entropy loss to guide model learning. However, due to the limitations of these two losses in detailed areas, the discriminative ability and the segmentation accuracy of the model for these areas is not enough. To address this issue, we propose a multi-modal brain tumor segmentation method based on local-region supervised contrastive learning (LR-Contrast). The proposed method comprises an Anchor Selector Module (ASM), a Contrastive Sample Selector Module (CSSM) and a Supervised Contrastive Loss. ASM is designed to effectively pinpoint the detailed regions that are most suitable for contrastive learning. CSSM aims to identify efficient contrastive samples. Contrastive Loss is designed for improving the discriminative ability of features using contrastive samples in the detailed areas obtained by ASM. Extensive experiments on two public datasets (BraTS2020 and ISBI) indicate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in the Dice Score and 95% Hausdorff Distance (HD95) metrics compared to several state-of-the-art methods, making it more suitable for accurate segmentation of brain tumors.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Graph Convolutional Networks for EEG-Based Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Emotion recognition is a critical task in understanding human affective states and their impact on interactions with products, services, and brands. In this study, we introduce a novel spatiotemporal graph convolutional network (GCN) framework for EEG-based emotion recognition. Unlike conventional CNN and RNN models that struggle with non-Euclidean data structures, our approach leverages the spatial and temporal relationships between EEG channels, captured using advanced GCN techniques. The proposed framework includes spatial and spatiotemporal models, each further divided based on different feature inputs, including Differential Entropy (DE) and Power Spectral Density (PSD). We validate our models on the DEAP dataset, where the spatiotemporal model achieved a valence classification accuracy of 79.7% and an arousal classification accuracy of 68.2%. These results demonstrate that the optimal model configuration significantly enhances emotion classification accuracy, particularly in the recognition of both valence and arousal states. The findings suggest that incorporating GCNs into emotion recognition systems can effectively address the challenges posed by the complex, non-Euclidean structure of EEG data.

articleTitle: An Unsupervised Spatial-Temporal-Spectral Fusion Model for Hyperspectral Images Using a Global Shared Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSI) are renowned for their high spectral resolution and extensive wavelength coverage, but they often suffer from limited spatial and temporal resolution due to imaging sensor constraints. This may make it difficult for hyperspectral images to play a role in the acquisition of fine surface information and the observation of continuity of time scales. Spatial-temporal-spectral fusion (STSF) has the purpose of synthesizing different information which from multisource satellite data which has the advantage in temporal, spatial, and spectral aspect respectively to reconstruct HSI with high spatial resolution and high temporal resolution. However most existing spatial-temporal-spectral fusion methods are restricted to the assumption of linear relationship of space temporal and spectrum. Furthermore, the spatial-temporal-spectral fusion methods mostly cannot directly process the current hyperspectral data which has a lower temporal resolution based on Landsat and MODIS. This paper proposed an unsupervised STSF model for hyperspectral images using a global shared convolutional neural network (UGSCNN). The proposed method has two models: 1) Spatial-spectral down model: combine spectral linear theory with deep learning to down sample the space and the spectrum; 2) Spectral up model: utilize the shared global information to up sample the spectrum. To verify the proposed method, we compared it with others using simulated and real on-board data, proving its effectiveness and practical fusion results.

articleTitle: DCUNet: Deformable Convolutional UNet for Multi-frame Infrared Small Target Super-resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The objective of infrared multi-frame super-resolution for small targets is to enhance the target's resolution by leveraging complementary information from multiple frames. However, the presence of motion variations and scale changes in infrared small targets introduces discontinuities in information between frames, posing challenges for super-resolution. To address the above challenges, we propose a multi-frame infrared small target super-resolution network based on deformable UNet. Specifically, the network takes multi-frame sequential infrared images as input and divides the input into reference frames and current frames. It utilizes deformable convolutions to align the frames to enhance the target features of the current frame. Additionally, the encoding structure of the UNet network is employed to extract multiscale features from the sequential images. By leveraging skip connections and a decoding structure, the network achieves the enhancement of target detail information and the fusion of multiscale features, ultimately outputting the super-resolved image. We conducted experiments on the IRDST and NUDT-MIRSDT datasets, and the results validate the practicality of our designed network.

articleTitle: Multi-function Radar Cognitive Interference Decision-making Based on Improved DQN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The emergence of multi-function radar (MFR) has brought unprecedented challenges to the field of electronic reconnaissance and interference. In response to the problems of data redundancy and poor interpretability in traditional signal description methods for characterizing complex and variable MFR signals, we propose a joint representation method for radar state based on existing multi-level signal models. In response to the overestimation problem of the original Deep Q Network (DQN) algorithm in evaluating the value of interference actions, we apply three improved DQNs: DQN with target network, Double DQN, and Dueling DQN to the interference decision-making. Finally, we conduct simulation experiments using the operation modes of the Mercury Radar and common interference patterns as algorithm inputs to verify the performance of the improved algorithms, and optimize some parameters of the Dueling DQN. The simulation results show that the improved algorithms can effectively solve the overestimation problem of DQN, and significantly improve the convergence speed and decision performance of the algorithm.

articleTitle: DNN-based Intelligent Target Detection for MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper investigates intelligent target detection for Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar in complex clutter and noise environments. In the modeling phase, the detection problem is formulated as a binary hypothesis testing scenario. To handle the detection problem, adaptive detectors based on Deep Neural Network (DNN) are developed resorting to the Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) and Adaptive Matched Filter (AMF) criteria by constructing a network architecture comprising input layers, multiple hidden layers, dropout layers, and output layers. Specifically, a supervised learning method based on DNN is developed, where the DNN is represented as a parametric function, mapping inputs to outputs through consecutive hidden layers. In the analysis phase, the proposed DNN-based detectors are compared with traditional GLRT and AMF-based counterparts. Numerical findings confirm the efficiency of the devised DNN-based strategies.

articleTitle: Radiometric Resolution Measurement for TerraSAR-X Sensor by Realizing Man-Made Homogeneous Regions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A homogeneous region exhibiting a stable and high backscattering coefficient is crucial for the radiometric calibration and performance evaluation of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems. However, creating such a region in practice presents significant challenges. This study presents a new method for creating a uniform region with consistent backscattering, defined by a known backscattering coefficient, using specially designed metal grids. This method is applied to evaluate the radiometric resolution of the TerraSAR-X sensor.The proposed man-made grid-structured target, referred to as the metal grid, is constructed from aluminum. The backscattering coefficients of this grid were measured across various incident angles and frequencies in a microwave anechoic chamber. Radar cross-section (RCS) measurements confirm the target's strong backscattering properties. Using this designed target, homogeneous regions with high backscattering were created at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, China. Two spaceborne experiments conducted by the TerraSAR-X satellite over the test area were carried out to assess the radiometric resolution of the SAR sensor. The experimental results demonstrate that the radiometric resolution values derived from the TerraSAR-X images closely align with the reference values provided in the product specifications. Additionally, the developed strong backscattering homogeneous region proves to be highly effective and well-suited for SAR radiometric calibration and other related applications.

articleTitle: A Dual Network Approach with Enhanced Feature Guidance for SAR-to-Optical Image Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images own dominant merits, such as all-weather and all-day working conditions, but it is difficult for unprofessional people to interpret SAR images. Translating SAR images into optical images to assist interpretation can facilitate the transformation of SAR data into usable information. Therefore, an advanced SAR to Optical (S2O) image translation method utilizing a parallel Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) framework was proposed. This method incorporates an optical image reconstruction network alongside the S2O translation network, enhancing the fidelity and color consistency of the translated images. By employing a domain alignment module and a deep supervision feature loss module, the network effectively utilizes abundant optical image features to overcome the scarcity of SAR-optical image pairs. Experiments conducted on the SEN1-2 dataset demonstrate superior performance over existing methods, particularly in preserving detailed structural information in images.

articleTitle: Cramér-Rao Bound Optimization for STAR-RIS Enabled ISAC System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: We consider a simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) enabled integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system. The whole space is divided into sensing and communication subspaces by the STAR-RIS. The Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for the estimation of the direction of arrival (DoA) of the radar echo is derived. By simultaneously optimizing the transmit beamforming at the base station and the reflection and transmission vectors of the STAR-RIS, a CRB minimization problem is formulated while the minimal signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) at the communication user equipment is used as a constraint. In this context, the original problem is decomposed using an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm, and two subproblems are alternately optimized using the semi-definite relaxation (SDR) and successive convex approximation (SCA) techniques until the final solution converges. Finally, simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: DCTracker: Differential Motion Compensation Based Multi-Object Tracking in Satellite Videos
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multi-object tracking (MOT) in satellite videos is a vital technique in Earth observation, serving various purposes such as smart city management and military target reconnaissance. However, satellite videos face several challenges, including wide observation ranges, low target pixel proportions, and significant background interference such as cloud drift and lighting changes. Relying solely on appearance features from single-frame videos is insufficient for fully identifying targets; extracting target motion information across multiple frames is also necessary for assistance.This paper introduces an innovative integrated real-time architecture for multi-object tracking, named DCTracker. Specifically, to address the loss of target motion information and the issue of weak targets being easily obscured by noise, we designed a differential compensation module to enhance discrimination between targets and noise by analyzing the motion characteristics of targets across consecutive video frames. Experimental results show that DCTracker achieves advanced performance, with an accuracy score of 61.3% on the VISO dataset, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling complex tracking scenarios.

articleTitle: Registration Error-resistant Track-to-track Association for Multiple Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The process of Multi-sensor Track-to-Track Association (MTTA) involves the association of tracks observed by multiple sensors, which are of the same target. This process serves as a foundation for enhancing track continuity and refining state estimation via the fusion of multi-sensor information. Predominantly, the existing methods employ statistical modeling of target motion to devise association gates between tracks. However, these methods encounter a decrease in association accuracy when faced with unknown registration errors. To address this challenge, a data-driven approach is proposed, which reconfigures track association into a classification problem. This approach harnesses target kinematic characteristics and track trajectory features extracted at the track level. Subsequently, these features are employed in constructing a track association algorithm based on decision trees. Experiments are conducted on a publicly available dataset, Multi-source Track Association Dataset (MTAD) derived from real data. The results have demonstrated superior association performance, particularly under conditions of inadequate system registration.

articleTitle: An Insect Swarm Segmentation Algorithm Based on Two-dimensional Spatiotemporal Aggregation Pattern Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Radar observations have identified a phenomenon where insects exhibit collective migratory behavior, characterized by uniform flight times, altitudes, and directions. Radar-detected insect swarms display aggregation in both spatial and temporal dimensions, with indistinct boundaries and varied shapes. Different swarms often merge into a single entity, making it challenging to accurately extract individual swarms using simple multi-parameter segmentation methods. To address these issues, this paper proposes an insect swarm segmentation method based on a two-dimensional spatiotemporal aggregation pattern attention mechanism. Building upon the Mask R-CNN architecture, this method leverages spatial attention mechanisms and circular soft nonmaximum suppression algorithms to enhance spatial position sensitivity and reduce occlusion effects between adjacent swarms. This approach transforms the two-dimensional clustering problem into an image instance segmentation problem and demonstrates its effectiveness in the automatic segmentation of insect swarms.

articleTitle: A Fast Iterative Adaptive Algorithm for Direction of Arrival Estimation of Millimeter-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Iterative Adaptive Algorithm (IAA) is a super-resolution algorithm widely applied for highly accurate estimation of Direction of Arrival (DOA) in millimeter-wave radar. However, traditional IAA encounters challenges related to algorithmic complexity and computational delay, making it unsuitable for applications requiring real-time performance. In order to reduce the angle estimation errors caused by the mismatch between the target location and the grid dictionary, a common approach is to refine the grid. However, it will further exacerbate the slow computation problem of IAA. To tackle this problem, a Fast Iterative Adaptive Algorithm (FIAA) is proposed in this paper. Built upon the traditional IAA, the FIAA adopts a hierarchical grid refinement approach to iteratively calculate target angles. Initially, a coarse grid division is implemented across the entire spatial domain and the potential regions of real target location are identified by utilizing the IAA. Subsequently, within these potential regions, a refined grid division is executed, accompanied by updates to the signal direction matrix. Ultimately, the IAA, incorporating a regularized covariance matrix, is employed to attain highly accurate estimations of the target angles. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed FIAA can effectively circumvent scanning and computation in non-signal potential regions, reducing computational time to at least 4% of that required by IAA. Moreover, the computational accuracy of FIAA is nearly identical to that of IAA when the SNR exceeds 10 dB, making it suitable for high-real-time, high-accuracy DOA estimation in millimeter-wave radar applications.

articleTitle: A Nonlinear Frequency Modulation Agile Waveform Optimization Algorithm for Pulse Doppler Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Traditional pulse Doppler radar faces limitations such as range ambiguity and clutter folding when detecting long-range slow-moving small targets in strong clutter backgrounds. The agile waveform technique aims to suppress these issues by varying the parameters of the transmitted waveform between pulses within the coherent processing interval (CPI). However, due to the differing range sidelobes produced by the matched filtering output of the agile waveform, range sidelobe modulation (RSM) effect occurs after Doppler processing, resulting in higher sidelobes in the Doppler domain. To address these challenges, a nonlinear frequency modulation (NLFM) agile waveform optimization algorithm for Pulse Doppler radar is proposed in this paper. First, the spectrum of NLFM waveforms is initially mathematically formulated by using a cosine series representation. Then, considering the RSM effect and waveform orthogonality, with the optimization objectives being the similarity and orthogonality of the agile waveforms. Finally, the Genetic Algorithm-Particle Swarm Optimization (GA-PSO) algorithm is employed to solve the optimization objectives, resulting in a set of NLFM waveforms with improved performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can strike a good balance between the RSM suppression and waveform orthogonality. The designed waveforms, when filtered by mismatched filters, effectively reduces the signal-to-noise ratio loss(SNRL) relative to the initial waveforms.

articleTitle: Spoofing Detection Algorithm for Tightly Coupled INS/GNSS Integration Model with robust Averaging Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) are susceptible to external signal interference.The GNSS-INS tightly coupled model exhibits high robustness and can avoid some interference; however, it is ineffective against spoofing interference, especially slow-changing spoofing interference. This paper proposes a robust detection algorithm based on measurement averaging and the IGG-III weighting function to effectively identify and mitigate such interference. By constructing a detection statistic from the measurement-averaged innovation, we theoretically demonstrate its nature as a zero-mean white noise process and design a corresponding adaptive detection strategy. Compared with traditional spoofing interference detection methods, simulation experiments using an open-source dataset show that the proposed algorithm significantly improves the detection rate of slowly varying spoofing signals while maintaining a low false alarm rate, validating its effectiveness and robustness in tightly coupled INS/GNSS systems.

articleTitle: Interference Suppression for FMCW Radars with EMD Enhanced Sparse Matrix Recovery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper deals with the issue of long-time interference suppression for frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radars. Conventionally, the sparse matrix recovery-based method is used to suppress the interference with the assumption that the interference is sparse enough. However, the sparse assumption cannot be fulfilled when the interference widely spreads over the time domain. We hereby propose an interference suppression method based on empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and sparse matrix recovery. Firstly, the EMD is applied to decompose the received echo signals of the FMCW radar, resulting in a series of intrinsic mode functions (IMF). The cumulative mean squared error (CMSE) is then performed to specifically reorganize the IMF components, which not only improves the initial signal-to-noise ratio, but enhances sparsity of the interference in the echo signals greatly. Then, the sparsity enhanced echo signals are transformed into a low-rank Hankel matrix and the robust principal component analysis (RPCA) method can be performed to recover the echo efficiently. Extensive simulations demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method with long interference signal periods and strong interference intensity in comparison with state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Attention-based Multi-Target Shadow Tracking for Video SAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Achieving high-precision and reliable tracking in complex target motion, low shadow quality, occlusion, blurring, and other scenarios is the main problem of multi-target tracking in Video SAR. This paper presents an enhanced multi-target tracking algorithm that adds attention mechanisms to improve target feature extraction and matching, performs preliminary object detection and tracking based on the TraDes model, and first preprocesses the image sequence for enhancement and denoising. With the model focused on the region of interest and improved inter-frame similarity, the improved algorithm shows higher tracking accuracy and robustness, effectively improving multi-target tracking performance under complex conditions like limited representation ability and noise interference caused by unclear shadow appearance features. It provides a lot of advantages over conventional techniques. This offers fresh concepts for the advancement of multi-target tracking video SAR technology. According to the experimental results using the Sandia National Laboratory (SNL) dataset, our technique outperformed JDE (33.56%), FairMOT (39.18%), and CenterTrack (40.72%) with the highest MOTA score (46.33%) in the video SAR test sequence, which was 12.77%, 7.15%, and 5.61% higher.

articleTitle: Radar HRRP Recognition Model Based on Pyramid Large Kernel Convolutional Attention and Stacked Transformer Encoders
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Facing the challenge of radar high-resolution range profiles (HRRP) target recognition tasks with many target categories and limited training samples, existing radar HRRP target recognition models struggle to effectively capture and delineate the decision boundaries in the feature space of radar signals. Our paper proposes a radar HRRP recognition model based on pyramid large kernel convolutional attention (PLKC-Attention) and stacked transformer encoders (STE). The pyramid large kernel convolutional attention module captures multi-scale features from local to global levels, effectively extracting the details and structural characteristics of various HRRP target samples in a few-shot scenario. The stacked transformer encoders module constructs a deep encoders network that iteratively synthesizes the relationships between low-level details and structural characteristics, progressively resolving the high-level features corresponding to each class of targets, thereby enhancing the model's discrimination ability in scenarios with minor target class differences. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to other deep learning models, the model proposed in this paper exhibits superior recognition balance and accuracy in radar HRRP target recognition.

articleTitle: Demand prediction of earthquake emergency materials using CBR optimized weight distribution by GT-SAGA-AHP algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper presents a case-based reasoning (CBR) optimised weight distribution by GT-SAGA-AHP algorithm for earthquake emergency materials demand forecasting, aiming to improve the accuracy of emergency resources demand prediction. The approach sets the number of disaster-affected population as the prediction target, selects seven seismic hazard indicators such as earthquake magnitude, depth of hypocenter, time, population density, number of collapsed buildings, seismic fortification level, earthquake intensity as research factors to accurately predict the disaster-affected population. Combined with the theory of safety inventory, developing an earthquake emergency materials demand forecasting model to calculate the demand for all kinds of emergency supplies after the earthquake. The experiment results show that the prediction model optimized by GT-SAGA-AHP algorithm achieves a smaller mean relative error (MRE) of the predicted values compared to the models optimized by the GA and SAGA algorithms, with reductions of 89.57% and 87.51%, respectively. This signifies that the feature weight distribution refined through the GT-SAGA-AHP is more rational, and the CBR-based prediction model exhibits greater accuracy.

articleTitle: Range-forming for FMCW Radar Vital Sign Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the radar vital sign monitoring, compared with continuous wave radar (CW), frequency modulated radar (such as FMCW and UWB) can effectively distinguish the target from the clutter in terms of distance. Through the range Fourier transform, the heartbeat and breathing signals of the target can be extracted from different distance intervals,thereby improving the monitoring accuracy. The range FFT widely used in the literature has some defects: first, the breathing amplitude of the subject may cross the boundary of the range bin and affect the integrity of the signal. Secondly, the breathing movement of the subject will cause amplitude modulation of the physiological signal, which is not conducive to the waveform recovery of the vital sign signal. Third, in muti-subject scenario, the sidelobe leakage of the energy of the close targets will affect the extraction of the signal of the farther target. Based on the above reasons, we proposed an algorithm architecture based on range-forming. For the above three situations, the algorithm performance was evaluated in simulation and experiment. Simulation and experimental show that when the target across the range bin, the proposed method can effectively suppress amplitude modulation, thereby accurately restoring phase information and accurately tracking heart beat intervals. And in the dual-target scenario, the proposed method is also better than the traditional range FFT method.

articleTitle: Online Identification Technology for Aircraft Power Failure Based on LSTM Neural Network and Inertial Information
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper discusses a typical thrust fault online identification method for aircraft during flight, based on the aircraft motion information of the control system and the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network. Aimed at the typical power failure mode of liquid main engine thrust decline, the paper studies the technology of typical power failure identification, and completes the demonstration and verification of key technologies through flight tests using an aircraft. On the basis of limited flight computing power, the paper completes the research on fault identification methods based on neural network methods. By using the inertial guidance information of the flight, it identifies the problem of flight failure caused by non-fatal power failures. It further enhances the autonomous adaptability and intelligent level of the aircraft.

articleTitle: Fusion of Image and Pointcloud Data for 3D Object Detection with 4D Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: 3D object detection aims to extract the spatial positions of objects from sensor data, thereby improving environmental awareness and comprehension. With the advancement of radar technology, the 4D imaging radar offers greater robustness in adverse weather conditions compared to LiDAR sensors, thus expanding its potential applications. However, due to the relative scarcity of 4D imaging radar datasets and the inherent sparsity of the radar point clouds, traditional point cloud-based 3D detection models perform suboptimally when applied directly. This paper focuses on the 3D object detection task with multimodal sensors, exploring the integration of RGB image features and 4D imaging radar point cloud features. We propose an innovative multi-modal detection fusion algorithm that markedly enhances detection accuracy on the VoD dataset.

articleTitle: A Two-step Signal Registration Algorithm for Distributed Radar with Censored Observations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In a distributed radar system, a signal fusion-based target detection algorithm can yield better detection performance compared to traditional decision fusion-based algorithm, thus has drawn considerable attention. In practice, however, signal fusion-based detection algorithm for distributed radar encounters two primary challenges: one is excessive communication cost and the other is difficult to fuse locally unregistered signals which is usually ignored by existing researches. To resolve these challenges, this paper presents a two-step signal registration algorithm with locally censored observations. Specifically, only local signals exceeding an initial threshold are sent to a fusion center for signal registration. At the first step of this algorithm, Mahalanobis Distance is employed as a metric to identify physically admissible observations, referred to as candidate observations. At the second step, the maximum likelihood estimation criterion is applied to eliminate potential false alarms among these candidate observations, thus determining the final set of registered observations for signal fusion. Numerical results indicate that the algorithm presented herein is capable of efficiently tackling the signal registration problem as well as alleviating communication burden. Furthermore, it achieves nearly lossless detection performance in comparison with its unregistered counterpart. This algorithm can be applied to practical engineering applications, since the simulation parameters are aligned with real radar scenarios.

articleTitle: FANM: Fuzzy-Aware Nested Mamba for Infrared Dense Small Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The task of infrared dense small target detection aims to accurately locate densely distributed thermal radiation targets in complex scenes. However, in complex scenes, dense small targets often suffer from occlusion, shadows, and blurriness, leading to unclear detection bounding boxes and inaccurate localization. To address the aforementioned issues, this paper introduces an innovative approach for infrared dense small target detection, termed the Fuzzy-Aware Nested Mamba (FANM) network. Specifically, the network takes a single-frame infrared image as its input and leverages shallow, middle, and deep Mamba networks to fully exploit and integrate local and global multi-scale features. The extracted features are subsequently passed to a feature pyramid network (FPN) to balance the spatial resolution and semantic information of each feature map layer, ensuring that feature maps of different scales can be effectively utilized. Then, the output features at each level are fed into the detection head, which consists of two branches: one for regressing the positions of arbitrarily distributed bounding boxes, and the other for predicting the quality of the bounding boxes. The proposed fuzzy perceptual loss function is used to optimize these branches, ultimately outputting images with accurately detected target bounding boxes. Experiments were performed on the DMIST dataset, which includes images with varying numbers of targets, and the results validate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Extended Target Localization in Distributed MIMO Radars Employing One-Bit ADCs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Low-complexity distributed MIMO radars can be achieved by implementing one-bit quantization in each receiver, significantly reducing data volume and hardware cost. Previous research typically assumes point targets, where each target contains a single scatterer, thus limiting their applicability to extended target scenarios. In this study, we propose a sparse reconstruction method tailored for locating extended targets in distributed MIMO radars with one-bit ADCs. The proposed method relies on the sparse Bayesian learning framework, simultaneously addressing the non-linear quantization effect and the pattern-coupled block sparse structure resulting from extended targets. Our numerical experiments demonstrate that our method achieves high accuracy in localizing extended targets compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: SAR Target Data Generation Method with Integrated Scattering Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is widely used in military and civilian fields. However, the difficulty in obtaining high-quality measured data limits the availability of existing SAR vehicle target datasets. As a result, deep learning-based data generation is frequently utilized for SAR target augmentation because of its affordability and simplicity of use. For SAR targets, scattering features are the most important information that discriminates the targets. However, the state-of-the-art methods do not adequately account for the target scattering information in SAR data generation. Furthermore, the scattering feature distribution of the generated data differs much from that of the real SAR data, making it difficult to effectively represent the scattering features of the target. Aiming at the above problems, we propose a SAR vehicle target generation method that fuses scattering features. The attributed scattering center (ASC) of the target is extracted by the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) method, which is computationally efficient. Then, a multidimensional feature representation is constructed by combining the original SAR data, fully utilizing the scattering features of SAR images. We improve the CycleGAN by adding a converter module, so that the network model can learn more information in the multidimensional features. It aims to enhance the ability of model to capture and learn the scattering mechanisms of SAR targets, enabling the generation of data that closely aligns with these scattering features. Finally, to validate the effectiveness of our method, extensive experiments are conducted using the MSTAR and SAMPLE datasets, demonstrating its superiority over existing techniques. The proposed method can supplement SAMPLE dataset by filling in missing target data, thereby enriching the dataset with additional target categories and increasing its sample amount. At the same time, the proposed method provides a new direction for the high-quality generation of SAR ship and aircraft targets.

articleTitle: Towards Discriminative Feature Learning for Multi-object Tracking in UAV Captured Videos
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Recently, multi-object tracking (MOT) based on unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platform has become an important topic. However, in aerial photography scenes, the lack of object’s appearance texture remains a challenge, as trackers are prone to confuse objects with similar appearances and lead to ID switches. Nonetheless, most of the existing methods mainly model appearance features using short-time clues, and such limited information makes it difficult to distinguish similar objects. To address this issue, we propose a novel Discriminative Multi-object Tracker (DistMOT), aiming to utilize high-quality long-term templates to mine distinctive object appearance, and further leverage the richer information of historical templates to distinguish similar objects. To this end, a Selective Memory Bank (SMB) is introduced to store multi-view historical templates; meanwhile, the Uncertainty-augmented Contrastive Learning (UACL) strategy is proposed to focus more attention on hard samples in the SMB, thereby forcing the model to highlight inter-object differential features and intra-object invariant features. Finally, the historical template differences of similar objects are considered for more accurate discrimination. Extensive experiments on the VisDrone-MOT and UAVDT datasets demonstrate the superiority of our method. Code is available at https://github.com/JackWoo0831/DistMOT

articleTitle: A novel strategy of estimating the GNSS ray-tracing tropospheric delay based on the satellite clustering areas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The tropospheric delay is a natural error source that occurs when objects, including radio signals, pass through the lower atmosphere at altitudes below 70 km. It needs to be carefully adjusted in numerous scientific research endeavors, e.g., remote sensing satellite-based Earth observation, aircraft precise positioning, and active radar surveillance system. Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) has become a popular tropospheric delay generating technique thanks to its facilitating approach, high precision estimation, and low-cost receiving devices. However, the existing GNSS data processing methodology allows for the estimation of zenith tropospheric delay by considering the physical characteristics of the troposphere and employing a simplified functional model. Therefore, the accuracy of ray-tracing tropospheric delay would be compromised when converting the zenith delay to the slant direction using a mapping function. This manuscript proposes a novel GNSS data processing strategy which can directly estimate the ray-tracing tropospheric delay. The hemispherical observable space is divided into several regions based on different azimuth and elevation angles, and GNSS satellites that belong to the same region are considered to experience the identical tropospheric delay due to the tropospheric physical characteristics. In this case, the ray tracing tropospheric delay can be calculated, and the corresponding estimation precision can be guaranteed, as an individual delay may incorporate observables from multiple satellites. The estimation precision could be further improved once additional GNSS receivers are involved in the data processing. Furthermore, this manuscript analyzes the impact of multiple GNSS receivers on ray-tracing tropospheric delays, considering that the signal paths may not be strictly identical for the receivers. Among which, potential signal blockage impacts, horizontal distance impacts and altitude variation impacts between each receiver are regarded as the main factor in the precision evaluation. This manuscript also considers compensating the tropospheric delay for radar as a case study, and the theoretical precision in regard to GNSS receiver locations are presented. The simulation results reveal theoretical precision can achieve 2.4 mm; while the experimental results achieve an accuracy of 9.98 mm compared to a water vapor radiometer in the usage of 4 GNSS receivers, demonstrating the availability of the proposed tropospheric delay estimation method.

articleTitle: Design of Satellite Constellations for Maximizing Regional Coverage Time Using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The satellite's payload collects and transmits information only within its field of view. To accomplish the detection mission, a satellite constellation of a certain scale needs to be designed. In this paper, a genetic algorithm is used to optimize the satellite combination on a fixed orbit to maximize the coverage time of the target area. The interconnection between MATLAB and STK is implemented through the COM interface, and a hash table is introduced to eliminate duplicate calculations, significantly improving the algorithm's performance. Simulation results show that this method has potential for application in large-scale satellite network coverage optimization.

articleTitle: Relation Aware Network for Multi-View SAR Target Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) has unique advantages and plays an important role in the field of remote sensing, which makes the research of SAR Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) very hot. In recent years, due to the rapid development of deep learning networks and hardware computing power, the deep learning based ATR algorithm for SAR has gradually become the mainstream. Compared with the single-view based recognition, multi-view SAR target recognition tends to better utilize the target scattering information of different azimuth angles. In this paper, we propose a Multi-View Relation Aware (MVRA) network for SAR ATR, which can capture the latent relationships between multiple input views, achieving better recognition accuracy than single-view recognition. Additionally, to enable the network to more accurately capture the contour information of SAR image targets, the Laplacian pyramid is applied for SAR image preprocessing. The proposed MVRA network shows a significant improvement in recognition accuracy on the public dataset MSTAR compared to other multi-view SAR target recognition algorithms. Furthermore, on the new Ground Military Vehicle Target (GMVT) dataset constructed by Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics (NUAA), the proposed MVRA network demonstrates excellent generalization performance even in the scenarios with relatively strong background clutter interference.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Object Detection in SAR images via Gaussian Flow Class-Balanced Differential Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Currently, few-shot object detection (FSOD) methods for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images are severely understudied. The high confidentiality and scarcity of SAR data, coupled with the susceptibility of targets in SAR images to significant changes in orientation, make existing models sensitive to variations in novel class examples. This sensitivity leads to challenges in extracting class prototypes and accurately estimating class centers for novel classes. To solve the above issues, we propose a few-shot object detection algorithm for SAR images via Gaussian Flow Class-Balanced Differential Aggregation. Specifically, we first design a class-balanced difference feature aggregation module to solve the problems of difficult class distribution estimation and inaccurate class center estimation of novel classes in SAR images. Second, the contextual information perception module is designed to extract the most representative support features into fine-grained prototypes and aggregate them with the query features using the matching paradigm to solve the imbalance between foreground targets and background in SAR images. Finally, experimental results on MSAR-AIR dataset indicate that our model realizes the best detection properties on SAR images compared to existing models.

articleTitle: Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling for Dynamic Tasks with Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based methods for scheduling Earth observation satellites (EOSs), which use DRL to accept or reject dynamic tasks, are limited in their ability to adaptively adjust satellite schedules, leading to suboptimal performance and inadequate handling of dynamically arriving tasks. To overcome this limitation, this study introduces a novel DRL-based method for the EOS scheduling problem in scenarios with dynamic tasks, called dynamic satellite scheduling (DSS). Unlike existing DRL-based methods, the proposed DSS method allows for modifying satellite schedules in response to dynamic tasks, transforming the EOS scheduling problem into a decision-making problem that determines which tasks the satellites will perform, thus enabling better handling of dynamic tasks. The proposed DSS method incorporates the long short-term memory network into the decision-making network to achieve dynamic updates of decision results. Experimental results show that our proposed method significantly enhances scheduling performance compared with existing methods, achieving higher rewards in scenarios with dynamic tasks.

articleTitle: Adaptive Subspace Detection of Range-Distributed Targets in Compound Gaussian Clutter with Generalized Inverse Gaussian Texture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper addresses adaptive subspace detection of range-distributed targets in compound Gaussian clutter with Generalized Inverse Gaussian (GIG) texture. Novel adaptive subspace detectors are developed based on the generalized likelihood ratio, Rao, and Wald test criteria, employing two-step design strategies that incorporate the persymmetric covariance structure and the GIG texture distribution to enhance detection performance. Furthermore, to achieve full adaptivity, a novel method is proposed for adaptively estimating the clutter texture parameters. The effectiveness of the proposed adaptive detectors, combined with this new texture parameter estimation method, is validated via numerical examples in various non-Gaussian clutter environments, demonstrating superior detection performance compared to several existing methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive Manifold Discriminative Regression for Multi-view Radar HRRP Target Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High-resolution range profiles (HRRP) is an important tool for automatic recognition of targets in radar systems. However, single-view HRRP is sensitive to the angle of aspect and provides limited information of target scattering feature, leading to unsatisfying recognition accuracy in practice. Multi-view HRRP from multiple radars or multiple scans appears promising for alleviating these problems and promoting recognition performance. In this paper, a novel adaptive discriminative regression algorithm based on manifold learning is advanced for multi-view radar HRRP target recognition. By using the adaptive locality preserving projection, our method can explore the geometric distribution and angular patterns of the data. Then, a novel cost based adaptive weighted multi-view least squares regression is proposed with the l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,1</inf> norm regularization to facilitate multi-view fusion and enhance feature selection capabilities. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that the presented algorithm remarkably enhances target recognition accuracy compared with existing methods.

articleTitle: Indoor CSI Identity Recognition Based on Residual Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Identity recognition has been extensively studied over the years, with traditional methods like camera and iris recognition becoming less favored due to their vulnerability to ambient light and privacy concerns. Recently, there has been a shift towards using CSI (channel state information) from wireless devices, such as commercial wireless cards, for identity recognition. This approach has applications in various fields, including smart homes and virtual reality. However, to achieve high identification accuracy, it is crucial to mitigate random noise from indoor environments. This paper proposes using dwt (discrete wavelet transform) to reduce noise in CSI data. Additionally, to extract robust high-level features from CSI data and ensure precise identity recognition, it is essential to deepen the training network. This often leads to challenges like gradient vanishing and explosion. To address these issues, this paper employs the ResNet18 (Residual Network) for feature extraction and identification of pre-processed CSI data, effectively preventing non-convergence and enhancing identification accuracy.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Unmixing via Multi-scale Representation by CNN-BiLSTM and Transformer Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) is a powerful technique to solve the challenge associated with mixed pixels that widely exist in hyperspectral images (HSIs). HU can obtain the pure signature of ground objects (endmembers) and their constituent proportion (abundances) within mixed pixels. Recently, deep learning techniques, with their powerful feature extraction capabilities, have significantly advanced the development of new HU technologies. A HU network based on an autoencoder, which combines a multi-branch convolutional neural network (CNN), a bidirectional long and short-term memory (BiLSTM) network, and transformers is proposed to enhance the spectral and spatial feature extraction ability of the network in this paper. Given the complex distribution of ground objects observed in hyperspectral remote sensing images, we employ a multi-branch CNN and a BiLSTM to extract multi-scale spatial features and spectral features respectively to address the issue that the transformer is not sensitive to low-level features. Then, the joint features are input into the transformer encoder to extract non-local features. Finally, the decoder reconstructs the HSI, estimating both endmembers and abundances. The efficacy of the proposed method is validated through one synthetic hyperspectral dataset, in addition to three real hyperspectral datasets: Samson, Jasper, and Apex.

articleTitle: High Concealment Bionic Communication (HCBC) Algorithm based on Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, a high concealability bionic communication algorithm is proposed. The algorithm imbedded a confusing signal in each layer of the wavelet, and only the people who communicate with each other know which layer of the wavelet signal contains the target information. The algorithm can enhance the concealability of the signal, but the multi-layer embedding of confusing information will lead to poor bionic performance of the signal. In this paper, an objective function is set up to find the balance between them, and an optimization algorithm is used to solve the objective function. To realize highly concealed bionic communication in complex Marine environment.

articleTitle: Near-Field Sensing of mmWave XL-MIMO Systems through Joint Parabolic Interpolation and Barycenter Calibration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The pursuit of higher data rates in next-generation mobile communications necessitates the use of higher frequency bands and larger antenna arrays. These shifts will extend the Rayleigh distance, resulting in near-field effects, where traditional far-field algorithms for source sensing yield considerable errors. Moreover, near-field spatial spectrum estimation algorithms require multi-dimensional spectral peak searches, which lead to high computational complexity and necessitate a trade-off between sensing accuracy and real-time performance. To address these issues, we propose the joint parabolic interpolation and barycenter calibration (PI-BC) algorithm, a calibration method for near-field spectral peak searches. The joint PI-BC algorithm significantly boosts sensing accuracy while maintaining low computational complexity, thus providing a real-time, efficient solution for near-field sensing.

articleTitle: A Dual-Branch Network Based on ViT and Mamba for Semantic Segmentation of Remote Sensing Image
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Semantic segmentation of remote sensing images has significant applications across various scenarios. The prevailing frameworks include Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Transformer. However, CNN is limited by the receptive field of convolutions, while the Transformer is constrained by computational complexity, which restricts attention calculations to local windows and fails to effectively address long-range dependency modeling. The efficient Mamba architecture, characterized by linear complexity, offers a promising solution to these challenges. Inspired by Mamba, we propose a dual-branch network based on ViT and Mamba. The Vision Transformer (ViT) branch incorporates the Swin Transformer to model spatial details while maintaining computational complexity within acceptable bounds. Complementarily, the Mamba branch efficiently captures global context and long-range dependencies. Additionally, to suppress noise and conflicting information arising from the fusion of features from different frameworks, we design the Cross-Model Fusion Module (CMFM) and the Cross-Model Relevance Loss (CMRLoss) to achieve semantic consistency in the fusion process. The comprehensive experimental findings on the commonly utilized GaoFen-2 and iSAID datasets clearly illustrate the advantages of our proposed approach compared to the leading methods in the field.

articleTitle: An Anchor-free Method for Aircraft Detection in SAR Images Based on Density Map
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The accurate detection of aircraft targets in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery is pivotal for aviation safety monitoring and military strategic planning. This paper addresses the challenges in detecting densely arranged aircraft targets within SAR images by introducing a novel detection network based on aircraft density map prediction. Initially, we propose a method for predicting the aircraft density map, which incorporates an innovative coding and decoding approach for aircraft targets, effectively mitigating the issue of overlapping target labels caused by dense distributions. Subsequently, we devise an aircraft density loss function, tailored specifically for the aircraft density map. This method abandons the reliance on preset anchor boxes and significantly enhances the model’s detection performance in scenarios with high-density targets. Comprehensive experimental validation on the SADD public dataset demonstrates that the proposed method exhibits high detection efficiency and accuracy when dealing with small-sized and densely distributed aircraft targets.

articleTitle: Long-term Radar Echo Extrapolation Method Based on Optical Flow and Deep Learning Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Radar echo extrapolation plays a crucial role in nowcasting. With the advancement of deep learning techniques in recent years, numerous advanced models for radar echo extrapolation have been introduced, resulting in great improvement in results and performance metrics. However, the extrapolation results of many existing LSTM-based networks tend to become increasingly blurred over time, losing precipitation details and failing to meet the requirements for refined forecasting. The complexity of network models also results in high memory consumption, which limits the size of input data and sequence length. Therefore, this paper proposes a radar echo extrapolation model that integrates the optical flow method with deep learning to address these issues. Within the 0-1 hour range, radar echoes, as spatiotemporal sequences, allow neural networks to extract more detailed features, thus enhancing performance. For the 1-2 hour range, the optical flow method, which consumes less memory, is used to avoid excessively blurred extrapolation results. Experimental results show that this hybrid model outperforms single models in the long-term radar echo extrapolation task within 0-2 hours.

articleTitle: GCGR-Net: Road Extraction Model Based on Graph-Convolution Global Reasoning Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The task of road extraction in remote sensing is subjected to pronounced challenges, which arise from a variety of converging factors. To increase road extraction accuracy, road extraction model based on graph-convolution global reasoning network is introduced in this study. Firstly, by utilizing deformable convolution, the DEFB module is proposed to capture local road features, conduct feature extraction at different scales, integrate richer contextual information, and enhance the expression capability of local features. Subsequently, the spatial information of the road feature is extracted in the channel domain using depth-wise separable convolution. Furthermore, spatial features of road nodes are captured in a global context using graph convolution, so that the model obtains comprehensive road topology information. Finally, a global reasoning method is adopted to efficiently capture long-range dependencies between road semantic information. The proposed method outperforms the compared models in the mean intersection over union (mIoU) scores of 80.24% and 79.18% on the respective datasets. The proposed model has been proved to be effective in addressing the problems of inaccurate and incomplete road extraction that arise from object shadows, vegetation occlusions, as well as challenges "same-spectrum-different-object".

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Radar for Non-Contact Detection of Respiratory and Cardiac Signals: A Comparative Study of Signal Decomposition Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The advancement of non-contact physiological signal monitoring technology is becoming increasingly important. This study combines millimeter-wave radar and advanced signal processing methods to accurately detect heart and respiratory signals. Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), Dynamic Bandwidth Variational Mode Decomposition (DB-VMD), Fast Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (fEEMD), and band-pass filters were employed to decompose radar signals into respiratory and cardiac components. The findings demonstrate that VMD and its variants outperform other methods, maintaining high accuracy across different distances and monitoring durations. Experimental results show that DB-VMD can effectively isolate vital signals even in noisy environments, making it well-suited for non-contact health monitoring applications. This study contributes to the development of reliable and user-friendly monitoring systems, enhancing patient comfort.

articleTitle: RGB-Guided Spatial-Spectral Fusion for Microscopic Hyperspectral Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Tumor segmentation in histopathological images is crucial for clinical cancer diagnosis and treatment. Digital imaging of pathology sections can simultaneously capture microscopic hyperspectral images (MHSIs) and RGB images. MHSIs, with their combined spatial and spectral information, are popular in many emerging methods. However, the corresponding RGB images, which contain richer spatial morphological information such as textures and colors, are often overlooked. In this study, we propose using RGB data as an auxiliary modality to enhance tumor segmentation by providing detailed spatial features that complement the spatial-spectral features of MHSIs. To facilitate effective inter-modal feature fusion between MHSIs and RGB images and bridge the modality differences between 3D and 2D data, we design a spatial-guided alignment module (SGAM). It derives spatial guidance weights and enhanced details from RGB images, which are fused with MHSIs to obtain discriminative spatial-spectral features for tumor identification. Additionally, we develop a hybrid loss function to balance pixel predictions between tumour and background regions, and encourage the model to focus on boundary areas. Experiments on a public histopathology dataset show that our approach can identify tumors with high accuracy and outperform several state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods using one modality.

articleTitle: Research on Single-Trial ErrP Decoding Algorithm and Cognitive Enhancement Paradigm Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The Error-Related Potential (ErrP) is is a subtle indicator of erroneous behavior.
