This paper discusses the application value of ErrP and proposes a cognitive enhancement paradigm, using a visual stimulation paradigm that combines steady-state stimuli with rapid visual presentation. Data collection experiments in this paper were conducted based on this paradigm, and a study on single-trial ErrP classification algorithms was carried out. Improvements were made to the Discriminative Canonical Pattern Matching (DCPM) algorithm. Comparison of the participants' behavioral data and EEG classification results indicates that Gamma rhythmic background stimuli positively modulate the participants' discriminative cognitive processes. Under this paradigm, the participants' judgment efficiency and performance of the classification algorithm were significantly better than those under traditional paradigms, thus effectively improving the quality and data utilization rate of ErrP data collection. Meanwhile, the improved DCPM proposed in this paper shows better decoding capability for ErrP components compared to the original DCPM and other mainstream event-related potential decoding algorithms. In the dataset collected from 20 participants, the decoding balance accuracy increased by 3.7% to 79.6%, and the true positive rate increased by 8.2% to 87.5%.

articleTitle: A Novel Channel Error Calibration Algorithm for Multichannel High-Resolution and Wide-Swath SAR Imaging Based on the Oblique Projection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The Azimuth multichannel synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can achieve the high resolution and wide swath (HRWS) imaging of the ground observation scene. However, the inevitable channel phase error will lead to azimuth ambiguities, i.e., the appearance of "ghost" points, which will degrade the SAR imaging quality. To address this issue, a novel channel error calibration method based on the oblique projection is proposed in this article. First, the optimal weight of each Doppler ambiguity component is calculated by the oblique projection. Then, the optimization function is constructed based on the power maximization method, from which the channel phase error can be estimated. Finally, the HRWS-SAR imaging can be precisely accomplished after performing the channel error calibration. The real-measured multichannel SAR data with azimuth ambiguity is provided to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Visual-Tiered LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper proposes a quality-guided LiDAR-Inertial-Visual odometry. Visual feature matching frequently suffers from mismatches and interference from dynamic objects. Existing visual odometry methods typically discard low-quality visual information, which can lead to insufficient information and reduced diversity. In visual-assisted odometry systems, high-quality visual features improve localization accuracy, while the impact of low-quality information on odometry performance depends on its distribution. This paper introduces a quality-filtered multi-hypothesis visual-inertial localization method, which retains visual features of varying quality levels and evaluates the reliability of these multi-hypothesis visual-inertial odometry models using laser localization results, enabling adaptive mode selection. By modeling the information from various sensors as error factors and considering sensor failures, we develop a factor-graph based LiDAR-Inertial-Visual odometry. The proposed method’s performance is validated using public datasets and our own constructed dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to the LVI-SAM algorithm, the proposed method achieves superior odometry accuracy.

articleTitle: Keynote Speeches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)

articleTitle: Near-Field Integrated Sensing and Communications: Unlocking Potentials and Shaping the Future
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The advent of sixth generation (6G) communication networks introduces integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) technologies, which are transforming base stations (BSs) and terminals. A key enabler of this evolution is the Extremely Large-Scale Antenna Array (ELAA), which plays a central role in the 6G ecosystem. ELAAs ability to cover vast near-field regions gives rise to unique spherical wave characteristics, enhancing both communication and sensing capabilities. This paper systematically explores the immense potential of near-field ISAC technology, starting with the foundational principles of near-field propagation and its benefits for both communication and sensing. We then investigate the technological frameworks supporting near-field ISAC, highlighting recent advances. Through comprehensive case simulations, we demonstrate the significant advantages of near-field ISAC, positioning it as a transformative paradigm in the 6G era. Finally, we address the open challenges and propose future research directions for near-field ISAC.

articleTitle: Global Information Edge Augmentation Network for Remote Sensing Image Continuous Super-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The continuous-scale super-resolution (SR) method for remote sensing (RS) images has the potential to achieve flexible scale SR with a single network, representing a significant research area in the field of RS. However, the majority of prevailing methods learn features from localization, thereby neglecting the global semantic coherence of RS images. This results in unbalanced SR outcomes. Furthermore, the optimization strategy based on the multilayer perceptron (MLP) utilized in the implicit neural representation (INR) method results in blurred reconstructed image edges. To address these issues, a novel continuous-scale SR method for RS images, a global information edge augmentation network (GIEAN), is proposed. Initially, the global state space model (GSSM) aggregates the global information of the image from diverse perspectives and learns the contextual interactions at disparate locations of the image globally. Subsequently, the dual edge enhancement module (DEEM) learns the image body and edges independently through the main branch and edge branch, respectively, with the objective of enhancing the edge component of the SR results. Extensive experimental evaluation on the UCMerced dataset demonstrates the superiority of GIEAN over existing continuous-scale SR techniques.

articleTitle: Phase-coded Waveform Optimization of Spaceborne Sliding Spotlight SAR with Low Sidelobe
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Spaceborne sliding spotlight synthetic aperture radar (3S-SAR) has achieved long-duration and high-resolution observations of targets, playing a vital role in remote sensing. However, strong scattering targets in SAR imagery exhibit high two-dimensional sidelobes, which would degrade image quality and obscure critical targets. To address this issue, we propose a phase-coded waveform optimization of 3S-SAR with low sidelobe. Firstly, we establish that the SAR imagery sidelobes are equivalent to the autocorrelation sidelobes. Next, we formulate the waveform optimization as a minimization problem aimed at reducing the discrete integrated autocorrelation sidelobe. Finally, we apply the majorization-minimization method to solve this optimization. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Non-Contact Sleep Apnea Monitoring System Based on Multi-Point Scattering Model and Multi-Scale Fusion Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Sleep Apnea (SA) is a common disorder that can lead to decreased blood oxygen saturation and is closely associated with the development of numerous cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. Early screening is crucial for timely intervention. However, the complexity and discomfort of traditional polysomnography (PSG) limit its applicability in large-scale screening and prognosis tracking. This study proposes a non-contact sleep apnea monitoring method based on Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar. The method is built upon a multi-point scattering model of the human body, using FMCW radar to capture chest and abdominal respiratory movements. A multi-scale fusion convolutional neural network is then employed to achieve high-precision identification of sleep apnea events. We collected synchronized radar and PSG data from 35 subjects for system training and validation. Experimental results demonstrate that the system achieves a classification accuracy of 91.37%. This system can be deployed in sleep laboratories or home environments, providing a convenient and non-intrusive solution for large-scale screening and prognosis tracking of sleep apnea.

articleTitle: Choroidal Thickness Estimation based on Fundus images with Uncertainty Quantification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Choroidal thickness estimation is a crucial step in monitoring the progression of choroid-related diseases. With the resurgence of deep learning technology, researchers begin to explore choroidal thickness estimation methods using fundus images based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Nonetheless, existing methods face challenges such as low accuracy and robustness. To improve the prediction accuracy and reliability of choroidal thickness estimation task using fundus images, a deep ensemble method with uncertainty quantification is proposed.. In general, the network architectures in ensemble methods are designed by hand, but hand-tuned network architectures which is time consuming and requires abundant experience. In this paper, we propose a novel choroidal thickness estimation method with network architecture search (NAS) guided by uncertainty quantification. By regulating the search direction, the proposed method aims to search the high accuracy and robustness models. Additionally, a selection method is proposed to select some of the searched models from all the searched models to make a balance between the performance in accuracy and robustness. Extensive experimental results show that the proposed method improves prediction accuracy and exhibits excellent uncertainty quantification performance for choroidal thickness estimation.

articleTitle: SAR Target Recognition Network Based on Time-Frequency Domain Channel Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper introduces a Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) target recognition network based on the time-frequency domain channel attention mechanism (DSN-DCT). Traditional SAR target recognition networks utilize the ResNet model to extract time-domain and frequency-domain features from SAR images. However, these networks suffer from low utilization rates of frequency-domain channels, leading to insufficient extraction of feature information and relatively low recognition accuracy. To address this issue, we have integrated a Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) based time-frequency domain channel attention mechanism module into the existing deep network architecture. This module is capable of extracting the most significant top N high-frequency components in the spectral space, effectively capturing detailed information such as edges and textures in SAR images, which is crucial for a deeper understanding of SAR imagery. Furthermore, considering the overfitting issues associated with DCT when applied to small datasets, and to ensure that the model maintains high recognition accuracy in the presence of complex noise, we employ data augmentation techniques. Specifically, we add Gaussian noise to SAR images and integrate the noisy image features with the corresponding generated spectral features. These enhanced features are then input into the target recognition network for training and prediction. Ultimately, on the Sentinel-1 dataset, we have improved the accuracy from 91.25% to 93.44%, and on the OpenSARShip_1 dataset, we have increased the accuracy from 72.80% to 76.60%. These results substantiate the effectiveness and generalizability of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Entropy of Nocturnal Breathing from Wearable Devices to Assess Post-Discharge Outcome Differences in ADHF Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The nighttime breathing of acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) patients may be closely related to their health status and disease progression. However, there is currently no consistent and widely accepted approach for processing, analyzing, and extracting the potential value of respiratory signals obtained from wearable devices. In this study, a reference approach was proposed for ADHF patients, involving the processing and analysis of respiratory signals obtained from a wearable continuous physiological parameter monitoring system, as well as clinical application validation. The study included 62 ADHF patients, among whom 17 experienced readmission or death within six months after discharge, as well as 56 healthy subjects. The nighttime respiratory signals of ADHF patients and healthy subjects were selected and processed by removing motion artifacts, filtering, and quality assessment. High-quality respiratory segments were used to calculate parameters such as respiratory cycle, respiratory amplitude, chest-abdominal coordination, and respiratory entropy, validating the feasibility of quantifying respiratory features using wearable devices. A subgroup analysis was conducted to investigate the occurrence of adverse events after discharge in ADHF patients. Compared to the non-adverse event group, the group that experienced adverse events exhibited higher multiscale sample entropy of respiratory rate. This study has proposed a comprehensive approach for processing and quantifying respiratory signals obtained from wearable devices, improving the signal processing methods in the field of medical signal analysis. The study has also explored the potential clinical application value of these respiratory quantification measures, particularly in the context of home monitoring. This approach holds promise for widespread utilization and implementation in home-based monitoring settings.

articleTitle: A Class Incremental Learning Method Based on Class Rebalancing and Old Knowledge Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Real-world scenarios are inherently dynamic where new objects constantly emerge. Class incremental learning (CIL), which learns to classify new classes by updating old classification model, has been proposed for object classification problems in real world. Current CIL approaches typically retain a few exemplars from old classes in a size-constrained memory and replay them when updating the model with new class data. However, such an update mode faces two serious issues: catastrophic forgetting and class imbalance, leading to the loss of discriminative knowledge among old classes and the tendency to misclassify old class data towards new classes, respectively. As a result, the performance of old classes after updating will be destroyed. In this paper, we propose a CIL method based on class rebalancing and old knowledge transfer that can alleviate catastrophic forgetting and class imbalance in CIL. In detail, the proposed method is mainly composed of two modules: feature-relation knowledge distillation (FRKD) and prototypical metric rebalancing (PMR). FRKD copes with catastrophic forgetting, transferring the learned discriminative knowledge among old classes by encouraging the updated model to reproduce similar feature topologies with the old model. PMR addresses class imbalance by employing prototypical metric learning to adjust the model tendency towards new classes, thereby enhancing the distinguishability between old and new class features. With the FRKD and PMR techniques, our method adequately retains the performance on old classes when learning new classes. Experiments on benchmark datasets show the superiority of our method compared to the state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: An Interactive Multiple Model Based Deep Learning State Fusion Approach to Target Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The rapid development of the deep learning technology has provided novel, data-driven solutions to the classic maneuvering target tracking problems. Based on the celebrated interactive multiple model (IMM) approach, this paper proposes a deep learning state fusion target tracking algorithm, termed IMM-LSTM, which combines the advantages of the IMM algorithm and long short-term memory (LSTM) network. The algorithm assigns a separate target motion model for each of the LSTM trackers that are run in parallel. Further on, an LSTM-based classifier is employed to determine the weights for each motion model of the target and the final estimate is given by the weighted average of the estimates of these individual trackers. Simulation results have shown that our algorithm yields better tracking accuracy and robustness in scenarios where the a-priori target information is deficient.

articleTitle: Radar Echo Modeling and Doppler Characteristic Fitting Method for UAVs Based on Multi-Scattering Point Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The radar echo characteristics of unmanned aerial vehicles provide important information for identification. The radar echoes of various types of UAVs are modeled by the multi-scattering point modeling method. A Doppler characteristic modeling method for unmanned aerial vehicles based on the mixture Gaussian algorithm is proposed, in which the slow-time dimension data are extracted from the Range- Doppler and fitted by the mixture Gaussian algorithm. The parameters of the Gaussian distribution components representing the unmanned aerial vehicle's Doppler spread characteristics are obtained using the algorithm. The simulated radar echoes of the multi-rotor unmanned aerial vehicle and the flapping-wing unmanned aerial vehicle are used for analysis. The performance of the fitting is acceptable and the way in which various parameters affect the Doppler characteristics is discussed and concluded.

articleTitle: SAR Target Zero-Shot Recognition with Optical Image Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Most synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target recognition (ATR) methods focus on closed set conditions, which assumes that the testing set shares the same label space with the training set. However, new targets inevitably appear in practical testing phase. Closed-set SAR target recognition methods will misclassify those unseen new targets as the known targets in training phase, causing decision errors. Zero-shot recognition (ZSR) is an effective way to make predictions for unknown classes. Existing ZSR methods, which are primarily designed for optical images, typically construct an attribute knowledge base shared among known and unknown targets, and then learn the feature-attribute mapping using only known class data, which is subsequently applied to predict attributes of unknowns during testing and achieve class judgment. Unfortunately, the optical ZSR methods do not perform well in SAR data, due to the huge difficulty in the learning of feature-attribute mapping caused by the less accurate target representation of SAR images than the optical images. To overcome this problem, this paper proposes a ZSR method of SAR target with optical image assistance. In detail, on the basis of attribute knowledge base construction, the proposed method maps the known optical and SAR training data to the feature space through their respective feature extraction network, and uses feature aggregation loss to ensure that optical and SAR image features from the same category are close to each other, while those from different categories remain far apart. Based on the alignment of optical and SAR features, the feature-attribute mapping is learned using both SAR and optical data, leveraging the advantages of optical images in the easier and more accurate learning of feature-attribute mapping to promote the learning of SAR images. In testing phase, the learned SAR feature extraction network and feature-attribute mapping are used to predict unknown targets’ attributes. Ultimately, the unknown class prediction is realized by measuring the similarities between the predicted attributes and true attributes from all unknown targets which can be obtained according to the prior knowledge. Experiments on measured ship dataset demonstrate that our method achieves superior recognition performance compared to existing ZSR methods using only SAR data.

articleTitle: Improving Nighttime Flare Removal with Subspace Basic Projection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Flare is an imaging issue caused by optical refraction in the lens. The imaging hazards caused by flares are more pronounced at night due to the large difference in intensity between the light source and the background. Since it is difficult to infer a flare-free scene from a flare-corrupted image, recovering textures under nighttime flare remains a challenging problem. In this paper, we propose a novel nighttime flare removal framework based on subspace projection and a jet map mask-based crossattention mechanism to remove nighttime flare and recover the scene under the flare, termed FBNet. On one hand, we propose subspace projection as a function of the flare basis network to better separate the flare from the scene. On the other hand, we found that the binarized threshold segmentation result obtained by using the jet map as a threshold segmentation condition is remarkably effective in extracting the flare as an input feature to the cross-attention mechanism. Therefore, we came out with a jet map-based transformer cross-attention block that uses a binary mask as a priori to achieve optimal recovery in the flare region Extensive evaluations on synthetic benchmarks and the real-world datasets Flare7K and Flare7pp highlight the superiority of our approach compared to the previous state-of-the-art methods for flare removal. All proposed methods improve the nighttime flare removal performance.

articleTitle: An Interference Elimination and Coherent Accumulation Method for Narrowband Aiming Jamming Based on FCM-IAA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Narrowband aiming jammer interferes with the normal work of the radar by transmitting high-power noise signals to realize the suppression of the target echo signal. Frequency agile signals with random inter-pulse carrier frequency hopping can reduce the coverage of narrowband aiming jamming on the target echo effectively, and exhibit strong anti-jamming capability. However, due to its inter-pulse carrier frequency hopping, the traditional phase reference accumulation method is difficult to apply. Aiming at the above problems, this paper proposes an interference elimination and coherent accumulation method for narrowband aiming jamming based on Fuzzy C-means and Iterative Adaptive Approach (FCM-IAA) algorithm. For the frequency agile signal interfered by narrowband aiming jamming, pulse compression is used at first and then extract the mean and variance characteristics based on the pulse compression results. Subsequently, the Fuzzy C-means (FCM) algorithm is employed to determine whether each pulse echo is affected by jamming and eliminate any jammed pulses accordingly. For frequency agile signals with frequency points missing, we use the Iterative Adaptive Approach (IAA) to realize super-resolution estimation of target range-velocity two-dimensional parameters, and solve the problem of coherent processing caused by inter-pulse carrier frequency agile. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that compared with traditional algorithms, the proposed algorithm offers a lower coherence processing floor which can achieve weak target detection and have a higher detection probability in the case of low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and high Jamming Coverage Rate (JCR).

articleTitle: Hybrid Integration Segment Strategy for Fluctuating Target Based on Bistatic Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The echo of high-speed maneuvering targets is prone to the phenomenon of Across Range-Doppler units (ARDU) and fluctuations in echo amplitude and phase. Traditional processing algorithms sacrifice time and computing resources in exchange for integration performance, which is not conducive to engineering applications. This paper proposes a long-time hybrid integration strategy suitable for fluctuating targets. First, based on the bistatic radar scenario, the fluctuating target is modeled considering the motion errors. Then, the influencing factors of the segmentation strategy in long-time hybrid integration are analyzed. It is proposed that under the condition of known prior information of the target, the correlation time can be obtained by traversal search. Let the length of each segment be equal to the smaller of the correlation time and the maximum time without ARDU phenomenon, then the accumulation time can be divided into several sub-segments. The simulation results show that this method can effectively realize accumulation and significantly improve the detection performance, providing ideas for further research.

articleTitle: An Anti-Jamming Beam and Power Allocation Strategy for Multistatic Radar System via Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multistatic radar system (MRS) has the potential to achieve excellent detection performance in electronic warfare thanks to the ability of mutual support among different radars. In this paper, we propose a novel joint beam and power allocation method for the MRS in a multiple target tracking scenario, where each target is equipped with a jamming device. We formulate the problem in a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning manner. To solve the proposed problem, we express the hybrid action of each radar with continuous values and employ multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) method to solve the joint beam and power allocation strategy efficiently. Numerical simulations show that the MRS achieves better tracking performance with the beam and power strategy provided by MADDPG.

articleTitle: Lightweight CNN for Radar HRRP Recognition Using NAS-Based Pruning and Multi-Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Deep convolutional neural network (CNN) has been widely studied in radar target high resolution range profile (HRRP) recognition. However, the CNN with deep structure requires high storage and computational capabilities, thus restricting its applications with limited resources. In this paper, we propose a differentiable neural architecture search (NAS)-based channel pruning and multi-knowledge distillation (MKD) to prune and fine-tune the CNN for lightweight. In the pruning stage, NAS method is used to automatically find the good-performance pruning structure by optimizing channel preserve scores. After the search process, these scores are used for global pruning to derive the pruned model. In the fine-tuning stage, MKD method combine the physical scattering knowledge with the category knowledge from pretrained model to restore the pruned model performance. Experimental results on VGG-16 with HRRP dataset inversed from the MSTAR show that the recognition accuracy of the proposed method decreases 1.52% by using 5% model parameters.

articleTitle: Asteroid Spin State Determination with Ground-Based Radar Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Spin states are crucial physical parameters of asteroids. Ground-based radar observations serve as a significant technique for determining asteroid spin information. This review provides a succinct overview of three principal signal processing methods utilized in radar astronomy for spin state determination: Doppler broadening, SHAPE and radar speckle tracking. Key research findings in this domain are summarized. Additionally, we compare these radar-based methods with alternative techniques for spin measurement, evaluating their respective strengths and limitations, and discussing future prospects for their advancement.

articleTitle: A Joint Optimization Method of Pulse Transmission and Range-Doppler Reconstruction for Pulse-Doppler Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To obtain a large unambiguous sensing range, traditional single-channel pulse-Doppler (PD) radar requires a large pulse repetition interval between adjacent pulses. However, due to the Nyquist sampling theorem, the pulse repetition frequency must be larger than the range of the Doppler domain, otherwise, aliasing in the Doppler domain will affect the range-Doppler (RD) reconstruction quality. Existing methods have designed non-uniform pulse transmission patterns to realize unambiguous range extension or develop compressive sensing-based algorithms to obtain high-quality RD reconstruction. However, the design of existing pulse transmission patterns and the RD reconstruction algorithms are often separated, which degrades the aliasing removal capability of non-uniform transmission. To solve this issue, this article introduces a data-driven joint optimization method that couples the learnable pulse transmission pattern and RD reconstruction algorithm, with the final RD reconstruction quality taken as the joint optimization objective. Specifically, we propose a learnable pulse transmission pattern and optimize the pulse transmission intervals in a random parameter freeze way. In addition, we propose a deep unfolding network for high-quality RD reconstruction based on approximate observations named MF-ISTA-Net. Experiments verify that the proposed method achieves superior RD reconstruction quality with the maintaining unambiguous sensing range extension in comparison with existing methods.

articleTitle: Optimization of Station Deployment Based on AHP-PSO Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this article, the problem of station deployment in passive localization system is studied with the aim of guaranteeing the performance of both specific and general areas. A set of metrics is first proposed to give a comprehensive assessment of the system performance, after which analytic hierarchy process (AHP) is employed to acquire the fitness value. Subsequently, a station deployment optimization scheme is proposed exploiting particle swarm optimization (PSO) techniques. Furthermore, chaotic disturbance and adaptive population particle swarm optimization (CD-AP-PSO) and dynamic adaptive population particle swarm optimization (DAP-PSO) are introduced in the process, which greatly benefit the reduction of computational complexity, as well as the avoidance of the local optima. Simulation results demonstrate that the system performance reaches a balance between specific and general areas, and that a higher convergence speed is achieved with lower complexity compared to the traditional PSO.

articleTitle: One-Bit Quantization with Sub-Nyquist Sampling: A Low-Complexity Receiver Design in ISAC System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, a low-complexity receiver is designed for low-priced hardware implementation in the integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system. The receiving antennas are sparsely located, and the signal is sampled with low-resolution and low-sampling rate analog-to-digital converters (ADCs). An orthogonal frequency division multiplexing-based ISAC waveform is considered where preambles are used for target sensing. Range, Doppler and direction-of-arrival are estimated via a block-sparse quantized orthogonal matching pursuit (BS-QOMP) method. Numerical results show that the estimation performance of the proposed scheme degrades 8.5 dB compared with the conventional design, while having a 74 dB reduction in power consumption. And the localization error under the practical base station (BS) setting is 0.2 m for the target located 400 m away from the BS.

articleTitle: Improved Polar Format Algorithm for Maritime Ship Target Imaging in Spaceborne-Maneuvering Platform Bistatic SAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Spaceborne-maneuvering platform bistatic SAR (BiSAR) can not only make the high-speed maneuvering platform have the advantages of electromagnetic silence and anti-jamming, but also have the ability of high-resolution imaging of the ship targets in front of the flight, which has an important civil and military value. Due to the characteristics of non-cooperation of the movement of ship target, the imaging of ship target will have serious defocusing problem, and the degree of defocusing of the spaceborne-maneuvering platform bistatic SAR are not the same for ship target under different sea conditions. To solve the problem of defocusing, in this paper, the improved polar format algorithm is proposed for different sea conditions. Firstly, the defocusing problem of moving ship target under different sea conditions are analysed. And, the envelope alignment and particular point method are used to compensate the signal for translational motion. Secondly, when the ship target is in a low sea condition, the polar format algorithm can used for imaging directly, and it can focus well. While in high sea conditions, the defocusing problem will become serious. Thus, this paper process the resulting signal in the wave number domain, and fits the two-dimensional wave number as a third-order polynomial, then extracts the higher-order polynomial that affects the focusing to get the space-variant phase. Then the particle swarm optimization (PSO) is adopted to search for these space-variant phase parameters. Finally, compensating for the space-variant phase by the estimated parameters, and then obtain the focusing image of ship target. The effectiveness of the proposed Algorithm is verified through simulation data.

articleTitle: Low false alarm radar detection for low altitude weak target based on multi-dimensional clustering extended features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Low-altitude flying objects, such as small rotary-wing drones and birds, pose significant safety risks to both national defense and civil aviation. Due to its all-weather and all-day capabilities, radar has become a crucial tool for detecting low-altitude flying targets, enabling critical tasks such as drone early warning and airport bird monitoring. However, the detection challenges posed by diverse and intense ground clutter often result in the loss of target location information, making it difficult for airports and military forces to take appropriate actions. Traditional algorithms are prone to high miss detection rates, making low-altitude radar detection a persistent challenge. Therefore, this paper first statistically analyzes the amplitude distribution of clutter using a high-resolution Ku-band bio-radar dataset, which includes various rotary-wing drones, aerial creatures, and multiple types of clutter, and identifies the most fitting probability distribution. Subsequently, an extended target detector based on amplitude priors and DBSCAN clustering is designed to achieve low false alarm radar detection of drones and aerial creatures under strong low-altitude clutter conditions. The results from processing real-world data demonstrate that the proposed algorithm not only successfully detects low-altitude targets but also reduces the false alarm rate to one percent of that produced by traditional methods.

articleTitle: Decoupled Lateral and Longitudinal Local Path Planning Method Based on LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The use of autonomous driving technology to improve mining efficiency and safety is currently a focal point of development. This paper addresses the issue of local path planning for unmanned trucks tasked with transportation between loading and unloading points in mining areas. It proposes a method for collision-free, smooth, and efficient path planning based on the decoupling of longitudinal and lateral movements. Initially, the vehicle is transformed from the Cartesian coordinate system to the Frenet coordinate system, and the problem is decomposed into two independent subproblems: longitudinal and lateral. In the longitudinal aspect, the global path from the cloud control platform is captured as the planning result. For lateral planning, a quintic polynomial model parametrized by longitudinal displacement is established. Obstacle information is acquired through the lateral system, and planning results are derived using numerical optimization. Subsequently, the system converts back to the Cartesian coordinate system, where B-spline curve smoothing is applied, and a collision detection function based on the occupied grid lookup table is established to determine the optimal local path.

articleTitle: Multimodal Slot Vision Transformer for SAR Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In recent years, deep learning network models, particularly Vision Transformer (ViT), have achieved remarkable progress in the domain of computer vision. Radar remote sensing has garnered attention due to its all-weather operational capabilities; However, due to limitations in imaging mechanisms, radar data is susceptible to noise interference, affecting data quality and interpretation accuracy. Hyperspectral data, on the other hand, is known for its extensive spectral coverage. To effectively utilize the modal features of both and promote information exchange between different modalities, addressing the shortcomings of single-modal data and solving the issue of feature indistinguishability in multimodal networks, a ViT network based on slot attention encoder, referred to as SLViT, is proposed. To better achieve feature decoupling, parallel branches are employed to handle remote sensing image blocks from various modalities, while position-based weight sharing is applied, providing a new means to simultaneously leverage spatial information and specific modal information. Meanwhile, unlike traditional multimodal fusion methods, attention mechanisms are employed for feature fusion, and a depthwise separable convolution module is introduced for processing remote sensing image blocks.

articleTitle: Multipath Ghost Suppression Based on Doppler Velocity Estimation in Traffic Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (MMW) radar has been widely applied in road traffic target detection and tracking. However, targets and strong reflective surfaces such as static road guardrails can lead to multipath ghosts during the propagation of electromagnetic (EM) waves in these complex scenarios. The multipath phenomenon causes interference and many errors. To reduce the probability of false alarms for real target detection, we propose a method based on radar point clouds for multipath ghost recognition and suppression. This method utilizes a multipath propagation geometric model and reflection boundary information to obtain the Doppler velocity of multipath ghosts and implement velocity filtering. Furthermore, experimental results shows that our algorithm can efficiently recognize and suppress multipath ghosts in complex road scenarios with multiple targets, significantly reducing the false alarm rate of real target detection.

articleTitle: A Polarimetric Target Decomposition Algorithm for Grassland Area with Orthogonal Scattering Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: As an essential component of terrestrial ecosystems, grassland ecosystems cover a large portion of the Earth's surface and provide significant benefits, including soil and water conservation as well as biodiversity preservation. They play an irreplaceable role in maintaining ecological balance and supporting human society. However, among the existing polarimetric decomposition algorithms, there is a lack of decomposition algorithms built for grassland characteristics. To address this problem, this paper proposes a polarimetric SAR data decomposition algorithm based on two mutually orthogonal rank-1 scattering models, enabling better separation of the corresponding scattering mechanisms. On this basis, the commonly used uniformly oriented dipole model is replaced with a volume scattering model of dual dominant-oriented dipoles, tailored to the characteristics of grassland structures, such as houses. This adjustment results in decomposition outcomes that are more consistent with real-world scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method not only provides more accurate decomposition results but also has the advantage of reducing negative power components.

articleTitle: Efficient Vision Mamba with Dynamic Feature Fusion for Remote Sensing Image Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The improvement in imaging resolution and the increase in imaging swath of remote sensing satellites have enabled the acquisition of vast and complex remote sensing image data. Effectively and comprehensively extracting target information to enhance segmentation accuracy and interpretation efficiency has become a research hotspot in the field of remote sensing semantic segmentation. Although current segmentation algorithms based on CNN and Transformer frameworks have made significant progress in performance, achieving a good balance between segmentation accuracy and computational complexity remains challenging, limiting their widespread application in practical tasks to a certain extent. To address this issue, this paper introduces a state-space model and proposes an efficient vision Mamba for remote sensing image semantic segmentation, abbreviated as EVMDNet. By designing an efficient vision state space block (EVSSBlock), the method effectively integrates local and non-local features while improving computational efficiency through efficient 2D scanning (ES2D) strategy. Furthermore, to avoid the insufficient utilization of features and weak discriminative ability caused by the direct addition of skip connections, a dynamic feature fusion block (DFFBlock) is designed to adaptively adjust the weights of different features for efficient feature fusion. Experimental results on classical remote sensing image datasets demonstrate that the proposed method not only improves segmentation accuracy but also reduces computational complexity to a certain extent, outperforming existing state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms.

articleTitle: Biomechanical analysis of gait based on surface electromyography signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Human walking is a fundamental and complex action. Through analysis, we can understand its basic mechanism and provide a foundation for the treatment and rehabilitation of related gait disorders. This article conducts biomechanical analysis of human gait walking based on surface electromyographic signals, which enables accurate estimation of internal physiological parameters and dynamic tracking of physiological activities during walking. Firstly, based on the optical capture markers, a human lower limb musculoskeletal model was constructed. Secondly, using the Hill model and introducing muscle damping viscosity elements, and considering the submaximally activated conditions, a static parameter optimization algorithm was designed to accurately estimate the force of lower limb muscles. Finally, we calculated joint torque and established a lower limb dynamics model. The simulated joint torque was input into the lower limb rigid body model to obtain the various joint movements of the human body. The correlation coefficient and root mean square error of joint torque are 0.975 and 7.822Nm respectively. This work has successfully completed the dynamic biomechanical analysis.

articleTitle: A Differentiable Framework for Image-Based SAR Target Reconstruction with 3D Gaussian Splatting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Image-based synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction is an important application for extracting target information from high-resolution two-dimensional (2D) SAR images. However, due to the complex mechanism of SAR imaging, developing a data-driven, fully automated 3D reconstruction framework with explicit physical constraints is very difficult. Thus, this paper proposes a differentiable framework for image-based SAR target reconstruction with 3D Gaussian Splatting, which can automatically realize the 3D target reconstruction from multi-view SAR images. Specifically, the proposed differentiable framework accumulates and generates simulated SAR images according to the SAR imaging geometry and projection during the forward simulation stage. By calculating the loss between the simulated and ground truth SAR images and backpropagating, the spatial positions of the 3D Gaussians are continuously adjusted until convergence, generating the 3D point cloud model of the target. The experiment is conducted on the constructed T72 SAR image dataset and the reconstruction results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Partially-Connected Hybrid Precoder Design for ISAC via Joint Grouping and Precoding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the spectrum resources becoming overwhelmingly scarce, Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) based on the multi-input-multi-output (MIMO) array is regarded as a pivotal approach for alleviating the spectrum congestion. Current researches on MIMO based ISAC predominantly focus on the design of the precoding matrix, while overlooking the potential performance improvement brought by the precoder structure. In light of this, we propose the partially-connected hybrid precoder design for ISAC via joint grouping and pre-coding optimization in this work. A fully digital approximation is applied to design the precoding matrices, incorporating the grouping structure optimization between radio frequency (RF) chains and transmit antennas via antenna selection. We consider two partially-connected hybrid precoder structures via overlapped and non-overlapped grouping, respectively. To address the coupling between antenna grouping and precoding, we propose to decompose the original problem into distinct subproblems using an alternating minimization (AM) method, and provide effective methods of tackling each of them. Experimental results demonstrate that grouping optimization significantly enhances the performance of the partially-connected hybrid precoder in both overlapped and non-overlapped grouping, validating the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Modeling and Verification of Processing Engines in SAR Imaging SoC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the development of real-time requirements for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging technology, SAR imaging processing SoC (System on Chip) has become an important research field at present. The subsystem for SAR imaging processing in the SAR imaging SoC needs to be fully verified during the development process. This article designs a UVM-based random verification environment, focusing on the verification requirements of key computing engines and interaction engines in the SAR imaging processing SoC. At the same time, a modeling method for computing engines and interaction engines is proposed, which can quickly and accurately describe the functions and behaviors of processing engines. Collaborating with the verification environment and the reference C model, the design under test achieves satisfactory coverage results. Consequently, the functionality of the processing engines within the subsystem can be comprehensively and effectively verified. The content studied in this article has certain value for the engineering verification implementation of SAR imaging algorithms in the SoC.

articleTitle: Dual-Band HRRP Recognition via Wavelet Packet Decomposition and Redundancy Reduction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High resolution range profiles (HRRP) is widely used in radar automatic target recognition. Due to aspect sensitivity, HRRP of different targets can be similar under certain aspects, making it difficult for recognition via traditional methods. One way to mitigate it is to increase the frequency dimension, utilizing the differences of target frequency response to extract inter-class discriminative information. Therefore, we propose a HRRP recognition model based on redundancy reduction criterion and wavelet packet decomposition. Specifically, we use deep wavelet packet decomposition to perform multi-level decomposition of dual-band HRRP and adaptively extract discriminative features of sub-wavelets; we use redundancy reduction layer to cluster intra-class features and expand inter-class features, thereby reducing feature heterogeneity. Furthermore, we propose a deep discriminative correlation analysis for joint analysis and transformation of dual-band features to fuse complementary information. Experimental results show that proposed method has excellent recognition performance. Additionally, analysis study also verify the effectiveness of each submodule.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Sensing Targets in OTFS-ISAC: Challenges and Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space-integrated sensing and communication (OTFS-ISAC) has recently emerged as a focal point of research within the development of sixth generation (6G) networks, due to its unique advantages in high mobility scenarios. In this article, we focus on the parameter estimation problem of sensing targets in the OTFS-ISAC system. Firstly, we introduce the system framework of OTFS-ISAC. Then, a review is conducted on the parameter estimation methods of sensing targets in OTFS-ISAC. Furthermore, technical challenges that OTFS-ISAC may face are outlined, as well as the future research directions. Finally, we provide several emerging applications for OTFS-ISAC and make statements on the parameter estimation of sensing targets in these scenarios.

articleTitle: FeatureSeries: An explainable neural network for financial marketing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Financial marketing models often struggle with interpretability due to the complexity and high dimensionality of features. This paper introduces FeatureSeries, an explainable neural network designed to address these challenges in financial marketing scenarios. Our model tackles two primary issues: feature selection from vast repositories and effective feature ranking. To improve feature selection, we incorporate an orthogonality loss function during model training, which mitigates collinearity among selected features. For feature ranking, we innovatively apply Wasserstein distance combined with Sobol coefficients, enabling more accurate importance assessment of behavioral and potentially redundant features common in financial marketing. FeatureSeries demonstrates superior performance in both predictive accuracy and model explainability compared to existing methods. We optimize Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) through our novel approach, resulting in more interpretable output features and enhanced model performance. Our experiments on real-world financial marketing tasks, including customer segmentation and product recommendation, validate the effectiveness of FeatureSeries. This paper contributes to the field by presenting a model that not only improves the interpretability of complex financial marketing models but also maintains high predictive power. The insights provided on applying FeatureSeries to various financial marketing scenarios offer practical value for industry professionals and researchers alike.

articleTitle: A Target Recognition Method for High-Resolution Range Profiles in Imbalanced Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Traditional high-resolution range profile (HRRP) recognition methods face challenges in automatically extracting targets’ temporal and spatial information and demonstrate low recognition accuracy on multi-class imbalanced datasets. We propose an HRRP target recognition approach based on a lightweight Transformer and fully convolutional network (FCN) model to address these challenges. The Transformer's encoder and the FCN are utilized to extract deep temporal correlation features and deep spatial structural features of HRRP, respectively. An adaptive weight matrix is introduced at the decision level to enhance the expression capabilities of temporal features and spatial features. To address the class imbalance issue, we design an adaptive focal loss function combined with a label smoothing strategy, which enhances the model's sensitivity to minority classes and improves its generalization ability. Extensive experiments conducted on the MSTAR dataset validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The model demonstrates superior recognition performance on both balanced and imbalanced datasets, and the proposed loss function outperforms other methods.

articleTitle: GPU-based real-time estimation of phase and delay of PCAL signal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to meet the requirement of high-efficiency phase delay estimation of PCAL signal in the digital baseband converter (DBBC) equipment link for deep space measurement and control, we propose a GPU-based PCAL signal phase delay estimation method with parallel computing technology, combining the method with FFT and FFT to solve the problem of low computational efficiency in the traditional PCAL signal phase delay estimation method based on the fast Fourier transform (FFT), and then propose a graphics processing unit(GPU)-based PCAL signal phase delay estimation method with parallel computing technology. Firstly, to address the problem of low computational efficiency in the traditional fast Fourier transform (FFT)-based phase delay estimation of PCAL signals, a GPU-based phase delay estimation method for PCAL signals is proposed by combining this method with parallel computing technology. Experimental validation of the method is carried out, and a large number of experimental results show that the GPU-based PCAL signal phase delay estimation method improves the acceleration ratio by at least one order of magnitude, and realizes the real-time estimation of the phase delay of PCAL signals with bandwidths of 32 MHz or less, signal intervals of 1 MHz, and quantization bit number of 8 bit. In addition, the designed real-time system is also applicable to the link calibration of other inverter devices.

articleTitle: A Unified Tensor-Based Joint Communication and Sensing Parameter Estimation for ISAC with Large-Scale User Access
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The combination of active user detection (AUD) and integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) can be utilized to realize communication and sensing functionalities over one hardware platform in the ultra-massive machine-type communications (umMTC). However, due to the received signals are typically coupled in both AUD and ISAC, it is hard to obtain the communication and sensing parameters. To solve this problem, the actual channel model is first converted into a unified form through CANDECOMP/PARAFAC decomposition (CPD) to mitigate the interference between communication and radar signals. Then, by utilizing the matrix subspace-based method, the factor matrices are accurately estimated, where the equivalent path parameters can be extracted. Furthermore, to estimate the coupled path parameters, an alternating iterative estimation algorithm is proposed. Simulation results verify the superiority of our proposed joint communication and sensing parameter estimation algorithm in AUD, channel estimation, and radar sensing.

Author Keywords: joint communication and sensing parameter estimation

articleTitle: Multi-Source Remote Sensing Image Registration Method Based on Nonlinear Scale Space and Phase Congruency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to differences in sensor characteristics, imaging conditions, and time among multi-source remote sensing images, nonlinear changes in image radiance intensity occur, increasing the difficulty of image registration. Existing techniques often face challenges in the robustness and accuracy of feature matching when addressing these nonlinear radiance variations. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a phase congruency remote sensing image registration method based on nonlinear scale space. This method constructs a nonlinear scale space of the image using an improved anisotropic diffusion filter, effectively suppressing noise while preserving the edges and detailed features of the image. It calculates the edge strength and corner strength of the image at different scales using a phase congruency model and extracts feature points from the edge strength map and corner strength map. Multi-scale, multi-direction descriptors are constructed using the response values generated by the Log-Gabor filter to enhance the robustness of feature extraction, thereby achieving precise registration of multi-source remote sensing images. Experimental results show that this method significantly suppresses image noise and nonlinear radiance differences, and outperforms traditional algorithms and other improved registration algorithms regarding the number of correctly matched point pairs and robustness.

articleTitle: Sea Surface Small Target Tracking Method with Integrated Dynamic Wave Prediction Information
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Tracking small targets on the sea surface has always been a challenging issue in the field of maritime target monitoring. Traditional methods typically rely on specific dynamic equations to establish the motion state model of the target (such as CV, CA, and CT models or their combinations), which struggle to accurately represent the motion states of small targets under complex sea conditions. We propose a method that incorporates deep learning to predict the dynamic fluctuations of sea waves, integrating real-time wave state information into the target state model. This method, which fuses sea wave dynamic prediction information, aims to improve the tracking of small sea surface targets. Firstly, we simulate various sea conditions based on the Elfouhaily wave spectrum to establish a database of small target motion trajectories on the sea surface. Then, we employ an LSTM network with a dual-stage attention mechanism to predict wave heights, which are subsequently fed into the state transition model. We utilize the Extended Kalman Filter for tracking. Simulation results demonstrate that with the assistance of sea wave dynamic prediction information, the proposed method enhances target tracking accuracy by approximately 14% compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Open Set Radar HRRP Recognition Using Confidence through Neural Weight Proximity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: High-resolution range profiles (HRRP) have become increasingly important in radar automatic target recognition (RATR) due to their ability to capture detailed structural features of targets. In practical RATR scenarios, the operational environment is open and dynamic, often exposing models to targets belonging to previously unseen categories. This underscores the necessity for open-set recognition (OSR) methods that can effectively distinguish both known and unknown targets. Theoretically, there exists a distributional discrepancy between the feature representations of known and unknown categories in deep learning models. By designing a suitable confidence calculation method that leverages this discrepancy, it becomes possible to accurately identify whether a given sample belongs to a known or an unknown category. Inspired by the Neural Collapse theory, we observe that deep features representing known categories tend to cluster tightly around the weight vectors of the final layer, whereas features from unknown categories are typically more scattered and lie farther away. Building on this observation, we propose a confidence measure that is determined by the proximity of a feature to the weight vectors of the final classification layer. Samples with confidence values below a defined threshold are classified as unknown, which forms the fundamental mechanism of our open-set detector. Our approach is versatile, making it applicable to a variety of network architectures and adaptable to different feature distance metrics. Extensive experiments conducted on HRRP data confirm the efficacy of our proposed method for open-set recognition, demonstrating its ability to reliably distinguish between known and unknown targets under diverse conditions.

articleTitle: USIFnet: A convolutional neural network for spatial downscaling of satellite-based SIF
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Satellite-based chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) offers substantial potential for applications in carbon cycle assessment and ecosystem monitoring. However, the utility of satellite-based SIF data is constrained by its coarse spatial resolution, spatial gaps, and significant noise interference, posing challenges for its use in fine-scale ecosystem studies. Building on previous downscaling studies, this research presents a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based model aimed at addressing issues in SIF data and overcoming the constraints of current models. We utilized this model to generate a 0.005° and 16-day resolution downscaled SIF product based on the 0.05° TROPOMI data across China, achieving validation metrics of R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> = 0.9216, RMSE = 0.0671 mW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/nm/sr, and a no intercept regression slope of 0.987. Furthermore, we compared the model’s performance with previous CNN model using original TROPOMI SIF and tower-based SIF measurements, confirming its effectiveness and improvements in accuracy, spatial detail, and reduction of artifacts. This work provides a promising tool for reconstructing high-resolution SIF data and demonstrates the potential of CNN-based methods in SIF downscaling applications.

articleTitle: STAW-Net: Spatio-Temporal Attentional Windmill Network for Tropical Cyclone Intensity Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Tropical cyclone (TC) intensity prediction using remote sensing images plays an important role in weather forecast and disaster prevention. Though having achieved great success in image analysis, deep learning methods lack feature extractors specifically designed for TC structures, resulting in limited representation capabilities for TC structure. Moreover, most of these methods overlook that TC is a temporal system with strong time dependencies. To this end, we propose a spatiotemporal attentional windmill network (STAW-Net) for TC intensity prediction. Specifically, we extract temporal-spatial-spectral features from multi-temporal TC multispectral images (MSIs). Notably, we design a novel Windmill Convolution (WMConv) to simulate the dynamic characteristics of TC occurrence and to extract structural features related to the TC eye region. Finally, we combine these temporal-spatial-spectral features with structural features to predict the maximum sustained wind (MSW) speed. Experimental results show that STAW-Net outperforms many baselines and state-of-the-art methods on various cyclone datasets. The errors of 24-hours MSW prediction by STAW-Net can be as low as 6.37m/s and 5.64m/s for the TCIR and the HURSAT-B1 datasets, respectively.

articleTitle: Unleashing the Potential of Beamspace Modulation in Near-Field MIMO: Opportunities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The principal distinction in transitioning from far-field multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems to near-field MIMO configurations lies in the notable augmentation of spatial degrees of freedom (DoF). This increase is not static; rather, it dynamically fluctuates in response to user mobility. A critical challenge emerges in effectively leveraging this significantly enhanced and continuously evolving spatial DoF, particularly when constrained by a limited and energy-intensive array of radio frequency (RF) chains. This article presents an exhaustive review of the current methodologies for exploring spatial DoF in MIMO systems, with a particular emphasis on the near-field context. Central to this review is the exploration of beamspace modulation, a technique that ingeniously capitalizes on the increased and dynamic spatial DoFs inherent in near-field MIMO systems. This strategic exploitation is demonstrated to yield significant enhancements in both spectral efficiency and system reliability. Furthermore, the article delves into a detailed analysis of the multifaceted challenges associated with implementing this technology. Through this comprehensive evaluation, the work provides crucial insights into ongoing efforts to navigate these challenges and suggests potential pathways for future research in this rapidly evolving field.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation and User Localization Assisted by Hybrid RIS with 1-Bit ADCs in MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper investigates the deployment of Hybrid Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (HRIS) equipped with analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) with one-bit quantization in multiple-input multiple-output systems to address the inherent limitations of passive elements in traditional RIS. The integration of one-bit ADCs into the HRIS simplifies the system architecture while reducing both cost and energy consumption. For channel estimation and user localization, we jointly leverage the one-bit data received at the HRIS and the reflected signals at the Base Station (BS). The atomic norm minimization method is utilized to substantially enhance the accuracy of channel estimation, while Vandermonde decomposition of a two-level Toeplitz matrix is applied to derive the Angle of Arrival (AoA) information of the User Terminals (UTs). To further optimize the HRIS configuration, we develop a Cramér-Rao Bound-based algorithm. Our simulation results show that the method we propose can improve the performance of both channel estimation and user localization.

articleTitle: Tiny Target Detection with Adaptive Weighted Feature Fusion in UAV Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the development of drones, imaging lenses and other equipment, effective and accurate detection of tiny targets in drone remote sensing images has become a hotspot. However, the features of tiny targets are weak and difficult to extract. Most existing methods enhance the target feature expression by directly superimposing and fusing multi-scale feature maps. Only the features with stronger responses in adjacent feature maps can be enhanced, while the targets with weaker responses may be diluted. For this reason, an adaptive weighted fusion small target detection algorithm is designed. To enhance the proportion of small targets in feature maps of different resolutions, a bidirectional feature pyramid network is designed. The adaptive weights are set according to the feature density in the feature map, and they will be used to perform bidirectional fusion on feature maps to reduce the interference of background and large targets on the features of small targets. Besides, we design multi-scale dilated convolution, which is injected into the feature fusion network. In this way, we successfully enhance the expression of small target feature. Finally, we test the algorithm via the public dataset VisDrone, the results show that our methods significantly improve the accuracy of small target detection.

articleTitle: NNC: A Nearest Neighbors Constraint-based Metric Learning for Multivariate Time Series Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multivariate time series (MTS) classification has gained significant attention as a prominent research area in recent years. Studies using Mahalanobis distance-based dynamic time warping along with metric learning algorithms have reported significant results. Existing metric learning approaches, such as large margin nearest neighbor, seek to optimize a loss function with two components: one that reduces the distance between samples with the same label and another that increases the distance between samples with different labels. However, these two terms play an opposite role in some situations and it is difficult to explore a way to balance such two competitive terms. In this paper, we introduce a nearest neighbors constraint (NNC) model designed for MTS classification. In NNC, a data-adaptive Mahalanobis distance-based dynamic time warping distance metric is designed to compute the distance between two MTS. To learn the Mahalanobis distance, a concise and effective loss function is developed. Instead of scanning all triplets, NNC only employs the triplets which violate the rule that an MTS's k nearest neighbors should share the same label with it to learn the Mahalanobis distance. Experiments on 9 public MTS datasets demonstrate that the proposed model achieves competitive performance.

articleTitle: Enhanced 2D-DOA Estimation for Monostatic EMVS-MIMO Radar via Phase Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) sparse electromagnetic vector sensor (EMVS) arrays offer enhanced flexibility and resolution in signal processing. This study presents an improved PARAFAC-based algorithm for angle estimation in monostatic MIMO radar with arbitrary EMVS arrays. By leveraging the array data multidimensional structure and using PARAFAC decomposition for factor matrix estimation, followed by vector cross product and phase compensation techniques, the proposed method achieves super-resolution while maintaining low computational complexity. Numerical simulations confirm the superiority of the proposed method over existing algorithms.

articleTitle: Multi-attentional Action Recognition Method for Captive Giant Panda based on Surveillance Video
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The actions of giant pandas are important indicators of their physical and mental health, and understanding their actions helps to improve animal welfare and refine the management. In this paper, we present a Multi-Attentional Action Recognition (MAAR) method, which includes spatial-temporal, motion and channel attentions, for giant pandas based on surveillance videos. The Region of Interest (ROI) video clips, which are generated by YOLOv7 model, are processed by our MAAR model to identify action labels. We also created a giant panda action recognition dataset based on the surveillance video, which includes 7 types of actions with 49,689 video clips with each label. Experimental results indicate that our proposed method achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 81.75%, which outperforms ACTION-Net with a 3.58% improvement.

articleTitle: Research on Fast Frequency Hopping Technology Based on Signal Processing Microsystems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to meet the needs of miniaturization and lightweight of communication equipment such as drones, this paper designs a high-density integrated signal processing microsystem. The microsystem is designed with ABF (Ajinomoto Build-up Film) substrate, realizing the integrated high-density integration of 8 heterogeneous chips of 5 process nodes, supporting independent RF transceiver with 4 receive and 4 transmit, and supporting independent switching of local oscillators and fast ping-pong switching on the chip. In order to improve the anti-interference ability of the communication system, this paper proposes a fast frequency hopping anti-interference scheme based on the signal processing microsystem. The simulation verification shows that the fast frequency hopping technology has better performance in the signal processing microsystem and has good Hamming auto-correlation and Hamming cross-correlation. The actual test verification shows that when the dual-channel ping-pong frequency point is switched in the signal processing microsystem, the serial instruction sending time is 17us, and the instruction execution and signal stabilization time is only 6us, which can meet the application of analog frequency hopping 4000Hops hopping speed. After adopting the fast frequency hopping anti-interference scheme, the hybrid frequency hopping application with a hopping speed of at least 10000Hops can be achieved in actual applications, which provides favorable guidance for frequency hopping communication applications.

articleTitle: Deployment Optimization for XL-IRS Assisted Multi-User Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we study the deployment optimization for an extremely large-scale intelligent reflecting surface (XL-IRS) assisted multi-user communication system, within which the channels between the XL-IRS and the BS (or user) are modeled by the near-field spherical wavefronts. To draw some valuable insights, we first consider the single-user case, where an alternating optimization (AO) based algorithm is devised to maximize the received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at the user. To address the high computational complexity issue incurred by the AO based algorithm, three approximate received SNR expressions are obtained to yield useful insights, corresponding to the upper bound, approximate expression, and closed-form. It is demonstrated that the XL-IRS ought to be positioned near the user (rather than the BS) to obtain a higher beamforming gain. Then, for the multi-user scenario, an efficient algorithm is proposed to obtain a high-quality XL-IRS placement solution by using the AO and successive convex approximation (SCA) techniques. Furthermore, the effective degree of freedom (DoF) of the BS-IRS channel is provided, which indicates that the additional effective DoF can be leveraged to improve multi-user spatial multiplexing. Last, numerical results confirm the existence of a trade-off between near-field beam-focusing gain and multiplexing gain.

articleTitle: Radio Interferometer with UAV and SDR Payload for Direction-Finding of Non-Coherent Emitter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Direction-finding of non-coherent target emitters with unknown waveform using small receive-only UAVs is a challenging task. The traditional passive SAR techniques cannot be directly applied without prior information about the target waveform. Here, a new scheme of radio interferometer based on UAVs and SDR payloads is introduced. Large synthetic aperture is obtained through coherent processing of data collected by both stationary and moving SDR receivers. Then the DOA of emitter can be estimated accurately. In this work, synchronization and positioning methods for UAV-based receivers are proposed considering the vibrations of UAV platforms as well as drifts of distributed frequency sources. Extensive simulations and experiments are implemented to validate the proposed radio interferometer scheme and synchronization methods. The performances of DOA estimation are also evaluated.

articleTitle: Physically Plausible Spectral Reconstruction in Remote Sensing Using Multispectral Image
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging technology offers significant advantages in remote sensing, capturing richer and more detailed spectral information in narrower bands compared to multispectral images. This makes it highly effective for land cover classification, crop monitoring, and environmental monitoring. However, the high cost, low spatial resolution, and complexity of data acquisition limit its widespread application. This study proposes a novel and flexible framework for spectral reconstruction designed to overcome these challenges. Our framework incorporates radiometric calibration, atmospheric correction, classification, spectral unmixing, and thermal infrared super-resolution, all of which can be replaced with the latest high-performance algorithms. Additionally, the physically plausible framework considers actual optical transmission processes, ensuring accurate representation of both reflective and radiative properties. This adaptable approach facilitates cost-effective and scalable acquisition of hyperspectral data. Experimental results demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method, with reconstructed images showing high consistency with measured data, both in spectral curve shapes and radiance levels, underscoring its significant application potential.
